Prove Lemma 3.5.

***Problem 3.8***

Let *u* be an element  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk](images/c03_256.png). Prove that:

1.   <math alttext="a equals u Superscript left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis slash 2 Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>u</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![a equals u Superscript left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis slash 2 Baseline](images/c03_257.png) is a square root of 1
2.   <math alttext="u Superscript left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis slash 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>u</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![u Superscript left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis slash 2](images/c03_258.png) is 1 or  <math alttext="negative 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![negative 1](images/c03_259.png).

***Problem 3.9***

Prove the following lemma:

*Given two distinct primes p and q, p*(*p^(\-1) mod q*) + *q*(*q^(\-1) mod p*) = *pq* + 1

## 3.2 Basic Algebraic Structures

### 3.2.1 Groups and Rings and Their Properties

#### *3.2.1.1 Groups and Rings*

***Definition 3.18 Group****: a group, denoted*  <math alttext="left-parenthesis upper G comma normal o right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis upper G comma normal o right-parenthesis](images/c03_260.png)*, is a set equipped with an operation*  <math alttext="normal o" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></math> ![normal o](images/c03_261.png)*, which is usually the addition or the multiplication modulo* *n, satisfying the following properties for all elements*  <math alttext="x comma y comma z element-of upper G" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>z</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow></math> ![x comma y comma z element-of upper G](images/c03_262.png):

1.  *Closeness: the group operation* ο *is closed. That is*:  <math alttext="x normal o y equals c comma c element-of upper G" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow></math> ![x normal o y equals c comma c element-of upper G](images/c03_263.png)
2.  *Neutral element (also called identity): there exists an element e in* *G* *such that*  <math alttext="e normal o x equals x normal o e equals x" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>e</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>e</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> ![e normal o x equals x normal o e equals x](images/c03_264.png)
3.  *Inverse: for every*  <math alttext="x element-of upper G" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow></math> ![x element-of upper G](images/c03_265.png) *there exists* <math alttext="x prime element-of upper G" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi>G</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![x prime element-of upper G](images/c03_266.png)*such that*  <math alttext="x normal o x prime equals x prime normal o x equals e" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow></math> ![x normal o x prime equals x prime normal o x equals e](images/c03_267.png)
4.  *Associativity of operation*  <math alttext="normal o colon x o left-parenthesis y o z right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis x o y right-parenthesis o z" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mo>:</mo><mi>x</mi><mtext>&#160;o&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mtext>&#160;o&#160;</mtext><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mtext>&#160;o&#160;</mtext><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>o&#160;</mtext><mi>z</mi></mrow></math> ![normal o colon x o left-parenthesis y o z right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis x o y right-parenthesis o z](images/c03_268.png)

***Definition 3.19 Abelian group****: a group* *G* *is said to be abelian (or commutative) if*  <math alttext="x normal o y equals y normal o x comma for-all x element-of upper G comma for-all y element-of upper G" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>y</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8704;</mo><mi>x</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi>G</mi><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8704;</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>G</mi></mrow></math> ![x normal o y equals y normal o x comma for-all x element-of upper G comma for-all y element-of upper G](images/c03_269.png).

***Definition 3.20 Subgroup***: *H, a subset of a group* *G, is called a subgroup of* *G* *if* *H* *is a group with respect to the operation*  <math alttext="normal o" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></math> ![normal o](images/c03_270.png) *over* *G*.

***Definition 3.21 Additive*** *and* ***multiplicative groups****: if a group* *G* *is equipped with the addition operation (+), it is called additive group* *and denoted*  <math alttext="left-parenthesis upper G comma plus right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>,</mo><mo>+</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis upper G comma plus right-parenthesis](images/c03_271.png) *and its neutral element is* 0*. If a group* *G* *is equipped with the multiplication operation*  <math alttext="left-parenthesis normal x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis normal x right-parenthesis](images/c03_272.png),[⁸](#c03.xhtml#c03-note-0008) *it is called multiplicative group* *and denoted*  <math alttext="left-parenthesis upper G comma normal x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis upper G comma normal x right-parenthesis](images/c03_273.png) *and its neutral element is* 1.

***Definition 3.22 Order of a group****: the order of a group* *G, denoted*  <math alttext="StartAbsoluteValue upper G EndAbsoluteValue" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>G</mi><mo>&#124;</mo></mrow></math> ![StartAbsoluteValue upper G EndAbsoluteValue](images/c03_274.png)*, is the number of elements in* *G. A group* *G* *is infinite if*  <math alttext="StartAbsoluteValue upper G EndAbsoluteValue" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>G</mi><mo>&#124;</mo></mrow></math> ![StartAbsoluteValue upper G EndAbsoluteValue](images/c03_275.png) *is infinite*.

**Example 3.20**

*   – ℝ (the set of real numbers) is a group under the addition operation as well as under the multiplication operation. Any number  <math alttext="x element-of double-struck upper R" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi>&#8477;</mi></mrow></math> ![x element-of double-struck upper R](images/c03_276.png) has an additive inverse (i.e.  <math alttext="negative x element-of double-struck upper R" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi>&#8477;</mi></mrow></math> ![negative x element-of double-struck upper R](images/c03_277.png)) and a multiplicative inverse (i.e.  <math alttext="x Superscript negative 1 Baseline element-of double-struck upper R" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi>&#8477;</mi></mrow></math> ![x Superscript negative 1 Baseline element-of double-struck upper R](images/c03_278.png)).
*   – ℕ (the set of positive integers) is neither a group under the addition operation nor a group under multiplication operation, because additive inverses are negatives and multiplicative inverses of most integers are not integers.
*   – ℤ[p] (the set of integers modulo *p*) is a group under the addition operation, but it is not a group under multiplication operation, because some multiplicative inverses do not exist in ℤ[p] when *p* is not prime.

***Definition 3.23 Order of element****: the order of an element*  <math alttext="a element-of upper G" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow></math> ![a element-of upper G](images/c03_279.png)*, denoted*  <math alttext="o r d left-parenthesis a right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>o</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![o r d left-parenthesis a right-parenthesis](images/c03_280.png)*, is the smallest positive integer* *k* *such that*  <math alttext="a Superscript k Baseline equals a o a o ellipsis o a identical-to e" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mtext>&#160;o&#160;</mtext><mi>a</mi><mtext>&#160;o</mtext><mo>&#8230;</mo><mtext>o&#160;</mtext><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow></math> ![a Superscript k Baseline equals a o a o ellipsis o a identical-to e](images/c03_281.png)*, where* *e* *is the neutral element of* *G. If no such* *k* *exists, the element* *a* *is said to have an infinite order*.

Theorem 3.8 is very useful to compute modular exponentiation. For example, one can immediately find that  <math alttext="2 Superscript 6 Baseline equals 64 identical-to 1 m o d 9" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>6</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn></mrow></math> ![2 Superscript 6 Baseline equals 64 identical-to 1 m o d 9](images/c03_286.png). However, finding  <math alttext="2 Superscript 66666666666666 Baseline m o d 9" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>66666666666666</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![2 Superscript 66666666666666 Baseline m o d 9](images/c03_287.png) is more complex without using Theorem 3.8. Indeed, since the exponent is a multiple of 6 and  <math alttext="2 Superscript 6 Baseline m o d 9" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>6</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn></mrow></math> ![2 Superscript 6 Baseline m o d 9](images/c03_288.png) is known, by the previous theorem, one can easily find that  <math alttext="2 Superscript 66666666666666 Baseline m o d 9 equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>66666666666666</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![2 Superscript 66666666666666 Baseline m o d 9 equals 1](images/c03_289.png).

**Example 3.21**

*   – Let  <math alttext="left-parenthesis double-struck upper Z 7 comma plus right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>7</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>+</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis double-struck upper Z 7 comma plus right-parenthesis](images/c03_290.png) denote the group over the set  <math alttext="StartSet 0 comma 1 comma 2 comma 3 comma 4 comma 5 comma 6 EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>6</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![StartSet 0 comma 1 comma 2 comma 3 comma 4 comma 5 comma 6 EndSet](images/c03_291.png) equipped with the addition operation.  <math alttext="left-parenthesis double-struck upper Z 7 comma plus right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>7</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>+</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis double-struck upper Z 7 comma plus right-parenthesis](images/c03_292.png) is a finite group. Its cardinality is  <math alttext="StartAbsoluteValue double-struck upper Z 7 EndAbsoluteValue equals 7" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mrow><msub><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>7</mn></msub></mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></math> ![StartAbsoluteValue double-struck upper Z 7 EndAbsoluteValue equals 7](images/c03_293.png). The order of element 4 is 3, because  <math alttext="4 asterisk 4 asterisk 4 equals 1 m o d 7" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn></mrow></math> ![4 asterisk 4 asterisk 4 equals 1 m o d 7](images/c03_294.png).
*   – Let *S* denote the set  <math alttext="StartSet 1 comma 2 comma 3 comma 4 comma 5 comma 6 comma 7 comma 8 EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></math> ![StartSet 1 comma 2 comma 3 comma 4 comma 5 comma 6 comma 7 comma 8 EndSet](images/c03_295.png). Let us check if *S* is a finite group under the multiplication operation. We have to check if all elements have inverses:
    
     <math alttext="1 asterisk 1 identical-to 1 m o d 9" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn></mrow></math> ![1 asterisk 1 identical-to 1 m o d 9](images/c03_296.png)   <math alttext="2 asterisk 5 identical-to 1 m o d 9" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn></mrow></math> ![2 asterisk 5 identical-to 1 m o d 9](images/c03_297.png)   <math alttext="4 asterisk 7 identical-to 1 m o d 9" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn></mrow></math> ![4 asterisk 7 identical-to 1 m o d 9](images/c03_298.png)
    
     <math alttext="5 asterisk 2 identical-to 1 m o d 9" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn></mrow></math> ![5 asterisk 2 identical-to 1 m o d 9](images/c03_299.png)   <math alttext="7 asterisk 4 identical-to 1 m o d 9" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn></mrow></math> ![7 asterisk 4 identical-to 1 m o d 9](images/c03_300.png)   <math alttext="8 asterisk 8 identical-to 1 m o d 9" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn></mrow></math> ![8 asterisk 8 identical-to 1 m o d 9](images/c03_301.png)
    
    Elements 3 and 6 have no multiplicative inverses. Therefore, the set *S* is not a finite group under the multiplication operation, while  <math alttext="upper S prime equals StartSet 1 comma 2 comma 4 comma 5 comma 7 comma 8 EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>8</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper S prime equals StartSet 1 comma 2 comma 4 comma 5 comma 7 comma 8 EndSet](images/c03_302.png) is.
    
*   – Let  <math alttext="upper G equals StartSet 1 comma 2 comma 4 comma 5 comma 7 comma 8 EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>8</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper G equals StartSet 1 comma 2 comma 4 comma 5 comma 7 comma 8 EndSet](images/c03_303.png) be a finite group under the multiplication operation. We check if all element orders are finite:
    
       <math alttext="o r d left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>o</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![o r d left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis equals 1](images/c03_304.png), because  <math alttext="1 asterisk 1 equals 1 m o d 9" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn></mrow></math> ![1 asterisk 1 equals 1 m o d 9](images/c03_305.png)
    
       <math alttext="o r d left-parenthesis 2 right-parenthesis equals 6" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>o</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></math> ![o r d left-parenthesis 2 right-parenthesis equals 6](images/c03_306.png), because  <math alttext="2 asterisk 2 asterisk 2 asterisk 2 asterisk 2 asterisk 2 equals 1 m o d 9" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn></mrow></math> ![2 asterisk 2 asterisk 2 asterisk 2 asterisk 2 asterisk 2 equals 1 m o d 9](images/c03_307.png)
    
       <math alttext="o r d left-parenthesis 4 right-parenthesis equals 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>o</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> ![o r d left-parenthesis 4 right-parenthesis equals 3](images/c03_308.png), because  <math alttext="4 asterisk 4 asterisk 4 equals 1 m o d 9" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn></mrow></math> ![4 asterisk 4 asterisk 4 equals 1 m o d 9](images/c03_309.png)
    
       <math alttext="o r d left-parenthesis 5 right-parenthesis equals 6" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>o</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></math> ![o r d left-parenthesis 5 right-parenthesis equals 6](images/c03_310.png), because  <math alttext="5 asterisk 5 asterisk 5 asterisk 5 asterisk 5 asterisk 5 equals 1 m o d 9" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn></mrow></math> ![5 asterisk 5 asterisk 5 asterisk 5 asterisk 5 asterisk 5 equals 1 m o d 9](images/c03_311.png)
    
       <math alttext="o r d left-parenthesis 7 right-parenthesis equals 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>o</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> ![o r d left-parenthesis 7 right-parenthesis equals 3](images/c03_312.png), because  <math alttext="7 asterisk 7 asterisk 7 equals 1 m o d 9" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn></mrow></math> ![7 asterisk 7 asterisk 7 equals 1 m o d 9](images/c03_313.png)
    
       <math alttext="o r d left-parenthesis 8 right-parenthesis equals 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>o</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![o r d left-parenthesis 8 right-parenthesis equals 2](images/c03_314.png), because  <math alttext="8 asterisk 8 equals 1 m o d 9" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn></mrow></math> ![8 asterisk 8 equals 1 m o d 9](images/c03_315.png)
    
    Therefore, all the elements of the group have an order less or equal to 6, which is the order of the group.
    

***Definition 3.24 Ring****: a ring, denoted*  <math alttext="left-parenthesis upper R comma plus comma times right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>,</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>,</mo><mo>&#215;</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis upper R comma plus comma times right-parenthesis](images/c03_316.png)*, is a set* *R* *equipped with two operations, addition and multiplication, satisfying the following properties*:

1.   <math alttext="less-than upper R comma plus ampersand gt semicolon" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#60;</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>,</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>&#38;gt;</mo></mrow></math> ![less-than upper R comma plus ampersand gt semicolon](images/c03_317.png) *is an abelian group*
2.  *Associativity of operation*  <math alttext="times colon a times left-parenthesis b times normal c right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis a times b right-parenthesis times c" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#215;</mo><mo>:</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></math> ![times colon a times left-parenthesis b times normal c right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis a times b right-parenthesis times c](images/c03_318.png)
3.  *Distributivity*:  <math alttext="a times left-parenthesis b plus c right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis a times b right-parenthesis plus left-parenthesis a times c right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![a times left-parenthesis b plus c right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis a times b right-parenthesis plus left-parenthesis a times c right-parenthesis](images/c03_319.png) *and*  <math alttext="left-parenthesis b plus c right-parenthesis times a equals left-parenthesis b times a right-parenthesis plus left-parenthesis c times a right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis b plus c right-parenthesis times a equals left-parenthesis b times a right-parenthesis plus left-parenthesis c times a right-parenthesis](images/c03_320.png)
4.  *Multiplicative identity: there exists an element*  <math alttext="1 element-of upper R vertical-bar a times 1 equals 1 times a equals a" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></math> ![1 element-of upper R vertical-bar a times 1 equals 1 times a equals a](images/c03_321.png).

***Definition 3.25 Commutative ring****: a commutative ring, denoted*  <math alttext="left-parenthesis upper R comma plus comma times right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>,</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>,</mo><mo>&#215;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis upper R comma plus comma times right-parenthesis](images/c03_322.png)*, is a ring satisfying the following property: Commutativity of operation*  <math alttext="times colon a times b equals b times a" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#215;</mo><mo>:</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>a</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></math> ![times colon a times b equals b times a](images/c03_323.png)*, for all*  <math alttext="a comma b element-of upper R" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow></math> ![a comma b element-of upper R](images/c03_324.png).

#### *3.2.1.2 Cyclic Groups*

***Definition 3.26 Cyclic group****: a cyclic group is a finite group that is generated by a single element* *g, called* ***generator*** *(or* ***primitive*** ***element****) of the group*.

*   ***Properties of elements of a cyclic group***

Let *g* be a generator of a cyclic group *G* with elements in ℤ[p]. Each element  <math alttext="a element-of upper G" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow></math> ![a element-of upper G](images/c03_325.png) can be written:

1.  as a multiple of *g* in  <math alttext="left-parenthesis double-struck upper Z Subscript p Baseline comma plus right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>+</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis double-struck upper Z Subscript p Baseline comma plus right-parenthesis](images/c03_326.png) group:
    
     <math alttext="for-all a element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript p Baseline comma there-exists k left-parenthesis k element-of double-struck upper N right-parenthesis vertical-bar k asterisk g identical-to a m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8704;</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msub><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8707;</mo><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi>&#8469;</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>a</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![for-all a element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript p Baseline comma there-exists k left-parenthesis k element-of double-struck upper N right-parenthesis vertical-bar k asterisk g identical-to a m o d p](images/c03_327.png)
    
    Alternatively, we can write:
    
     <math alttext="upper G equals StartSet a identical-to k asterisk g m o d p comma 0 less-than-or-equal-to k less-than-or-equal-to phi left-parenthesis p right-parenthesis minus 1 right-parenthesis EndSet equals StartSet 0 comma g comma 2 g comma 3 g comma left-parenthesis phi left-parenthesis p right-parenthesis minus 1 right-parenthesis g EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>g</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>2</mn><mi>g</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>3</mn><mi>g</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper G equals StartSet a identical-to k asterisk g m o d p comma 0 less-than-or-equal-to k less-than-or-equal-to phi left-parenthesis p right-parenthesis minus 1 right-parenthesis EndSet equals StartSet 0 comma g comma 2 g comma 3 g comma left-parenthesis phi left-parenthesis p right-parenthesis minus 1 right-parenthesis g EndSet](images/c03_328.png)
    
2.  as a power of  <math alttext="g element-of left-parenthesis double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk Baseline comma asterisk right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>g</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8712;</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mo>\*</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![g element-of left-parenthesis double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk Baseline comma asterisk right-parenthesis](images/c03_329.png) group, i.e. with the multiplication operation:
    
     <math alttext="for-all a element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk Baseline there-exists k left-parenthesis k element-of double-struck upper N right-parenthesis vertical-bar g Superscript k Baseline identical-to a m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8704;</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup><mo>&#8707;</mo><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi>&#8469;</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>a</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![for-all a element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk Baseline there-exists k left-parenthesis k element-of double-struck upper N right-parenthesis vertical-bar g Superscript k Baseline identical-to a m o d p](images/c03_330.png)
    
    Alternatively, we can write:
    
     <math alttext="upper G equals left-brace g Superscript k Baseline identical-to a m o d p comma 0 less-than-or-equal-to k less-than-or-equal-to phi left-parenthesis p right-parenthesis minus 1 right-parenthesis right-brace equals StartSet 1 comma g comma g squared comma ellipsis comma g Superscript phi left-parenthesis p right-parenthesis minus 1 Baseline EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>{</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>a</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>}</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![upper G equals left-brace g Superscript k Baseline identical-to a m o d p comma 0 less-than-or-equal-to k less-than-or-equal-to phi left-parenthesis p right-parenthesis minus 1 right-parenthesis right-brace equals StartSet 1 comma g comma g squared comma ellipsis comma g Superscript phi left-parenthesis p right-parenthesis minus 1 Baseline EndSet](images/c03_331.png)
    

*   ***Property of a generator of a multiplicative group***

If *p* is a prime and *g* is a prime and a generator of the group  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk](images/c03_332.png), then  <math alttext="g Superscript p minus 1 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![g Superscript p minus 1 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d p](images/c03_333.png). Such a property is a result of Fermat’s little theorem.

***Definition 3.27 Primitive root modulo***  <math alttext="bold-italic n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">n</mi></math> ![bold-italic n](images/c03_334.png): *a number* α *is called primitive root modulo* *n, if every number coprime to* *n* *is congruent to a power of* α *modulo* *n. Formally*, α *is a primitive root if for any integer* *a* *such that*  <math alttext="normal upper G normal upper C normal upper D left-parenthesis a comma n right-parenthesis equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">G</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![normal upper G normal upper C normal upper D left-parenthesis a comma n right-parenthesis equals 1](images/c03_335.png)*, there exists an integer* *k* *such that*  <math alttext="alpha Superscript k Baseline identical-to a m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>&#945;</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>a</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![alpha Superscript k Baseline identical-to a m o d n](images/c03_336.png).

*   ***Properties of cyclic group***  <math alttext="left-parenthesis double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk Baseline comma bold-italic asterisk right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#160;</mi><mo>\*</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk Baseline comma bold-italic asterisk right-parenthesis](images/c03_347.png)

1.  If *g* is a generator of a cyclic group *G*, then the order of *g* is equal to the cardinality of group *G*. Formally:  <math alttext="o r d left-parenthesis g right-parenthesis equals StartAbsoluteValue upper G EndAbsoluteValue" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>o</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>G</mi><mo>&#124;</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![o r d left-parenthesis g right-parenthesis equals StartAbsoluteValue upper G EndAbsoluteValue](images/c03_348.png).
2.  For any element *a* in a cyclic group *G*:  <math alttext="a Superscript StartAbsoluteValue upper G EndAbsoluteValue Baseline identical-to 1 m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>G</mi><mo>&#124;</mo></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![a Superscript StartAbsoluteValue upper G EndAbsoluteValue Baseline identical-to 1 m o d p](images/c03_349.png).
3.  Any generator of a cyclic group  <math alttext="upper G equals less-than double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk Baseline comma bold-italic asterisk ampersand gt semicolon" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>&#60;</mo><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#160;</mi><mo>\*</mo><mo>&#38;gt;</mo></mrow></math> ![upper G equals less-than double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk Baseline comma bold-italic asterisk ampersand gt semicolon](images/c03_350.png) is a primitive root  <math alttext="m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![m o d p](images/c03_351.png).
4.  For any element  <math alttext="a element-of upper G" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow></math> ![a element-of upper G](images/c03_352.png), the set of powers of *a* forms a group *H*, which is a subgroup of *G*:  <math alttext="upper H equals StartSet b equals a Superscript i Baseline comma 0 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than-or-equal-to o r d left-parenthesis a right-parenthesis minus 1 EndSet equals StartSet 1 comma a comma a squared comma ellipsis comma a Superscript o r d left-parenthesis a right-parenthesis minus 1 Baseline EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>o</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>o</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>}</mo></mrow></math> ![upper H equals StartSet b equals a Superscript i Baseline comma 0 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than-or-equal-to o r d left-parenthesis a right-parenthesis minus 1 EndSet equals StartSet 1 comma a comma a squared comma ellipsis comma a Superscript o r d left-parenthesis a right-parenthesis minus 1 Baseline EndSet](images/c03_353.png).
5.  For any element *a* in a cyclic group *G*:  <math alttext="o r d left-parenthesis a right-parenthesis d i v i d e s StartAbsoluteValue upper G EndAbsoluteValue" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>o</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>s</mi><mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>G</mi><mo>&#124;</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![o r d left-parenthesis a right-parenthesis d i v i d e s StartAbsoluteValue upper G EndAbsoluteValue](images/c03_354.png).
6.  Every cyclic group is an abelian group.
7.  Every finitely generated abelian group is a direct product of cyclic groups. The direct product is an operation that takes two groups  <math alttext="upper G 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>G</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper G 1](images/c03_355.png) and  <math alttext="upper G 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>G</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper G 2](images/c03_356.png) and constructs a new group *G*, such that  <math alttext="upper G equals upper G 1 times upper G 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>G</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>&#215;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>G</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper G equals upper G 1 times upper G 2](images/c03_357.png).
8.  Every cyclic group of prime order is a group, which cannot be broken down into smaller groups. Cyclic groups of prime order (also called elementary groups) are the building blocks from which all groups can be built.

***Corollary* 3.1**  <math alttext="for-all a element-of upper G comma o r d left-parenthesis a right-parenthesis divides StartAbsoluteValue upper G EndAbsoluteValue" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8704;</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi>G</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>o</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;divides&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>G</mi><mo>&#124;</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![for-all a element-of upper G comma o r d left-parenthesis a right-parenthesis divides StartAbsoluteValue upper G EndAbsoluteValue](images/c03_360.png).

***Corollary* 3.2** If  <math alttext="StartAbsoluteValue upper G EndAbsoluteValue" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>G</mi><mo>&#124;</mo></mrow></math> ![StartAbsoluteValue upper G EndAbsoluteValue](images/c03_361.png) is prime, then  <math alttext="for-all a element-of upper G comma a not-equals e comma o r d left-parenthesis a right-parenthesis equals StartAbsoluteValue upper G EndAbsoluteValue" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8704;</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi>G</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8800;</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>o</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>G</mi><mo>&#124;</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![for-all a element-of upper G comma a not-equals e comma o r d left-parenthesis a right-parenthesis equals StartAbsoluteValue upper G EndAbsoluteValue](images/c03_362.png).

columnalign="left"><mrow><mtext>ord</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;because&#160;</mtext><msup><mn>9</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;mod&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>11</mn></mrow></mtd><mtd columnalign="left"><mrow><mtext>ord</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;because&#160;</mtext><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;mod</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>11</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></math> Hence, the orders of the elements of  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 11 Superscript asterisk Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mrow><mn>11</mn></mrow><mo>\*</mo></msubsup><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 11 Superscript asterisk Baseline](images/c03_374.png) are all dividers of  <math alttext="StartAbsoluteValue double-struck upper Z 11 Superscript asterisk Baseline EndAbsoluteValue" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mrow><mn>11</mn></mrow><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo>&#124;</mo></mrow></math> ![StartAbsoluteValue double-struck upper Z 11 Superscript asterisk Baseline EndAbsoluteValue](images/c03_375.png). It should be noticed that the elements  <math alttext="2 comma 6 comma 7" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn></mrow></math> ![2 comma 6 comma 7](images/c03_376.png), and 8 have an order of 10 (which is equal to  <math alttext="StartAbsoluteValue double-struck upper Z 11 Superscript asterisk Baseline EndAbsoluteValue" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mrow><mn>11</mn></mrow><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo>&#124;</mo></mrow></math> ![StartAbsoluteValue double-struck upper Z 11 Superscript asterisk Baseline EndAbsoluteValue](images/c03_377.png)). So, they are all generators of  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 11 Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mrow><mn>11</mn></mrow><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 11 Superscript asterisk](images/c03_378.png).

### 3.2.2 Fields

***Definition 3.28 Field****: a field* *F* *is a set of elements*[⁹](#c03.xhtml#c03-note-0009) *together with two operations, Addition (+) and Multiplication (*×*), satisfying the following properties*:

1.   <math alttext="left-parenthesis upper F comma plus right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>F</mi><mo>,</mo><mo>+</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis upper F comma plus right-parenthesis](images/c03_379.png) *is an abelian group with a neutral element denoted* 0 *such that*  <math alttext="a plus b equals b plus a" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></math> ![a plus b equals b plus a](images/c03_380.png) *and*  <math alttext="a plus 0 equals a comma for-all a comma for-all b element-of upper F" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8704;</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8704;</mo><mi>b</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi>F</mi></mrow></math> ![a plus 0 equals a comma for-all a comma for-all b element-of upper F](images/c03_381.png).
2.   <math alttext="left-parenthesis upper F minus StartSet 0 EndSet comma times right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mo>&#215;</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis upper F minus StartSet 0 EndSet comma times right-parenthesis](images/c03_382.png) *is a commutative group under the multiplication operation with an identity element*  <math alttext="1 colon a times b equals b times a" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>:</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>a</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></math> ![1 colon a times b equals b times a](images/c03_383.png) *and*  <math alttext="a times 1 equals a comma for-all a comma for-all b element-of upper F period upper F minus StartSet 0 EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8704;</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8704;</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi>F</mi><mo>.</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>F</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![a times 1 equals a comma for-all a comma for-all b element-of upper F period upper F minus StartSet 0 EndSet](images/c03_384.png) *is often denoted*  <math alttext="upper F Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>F</mi><mo>\*</mo></msup></mrow></math> ![upper F Superscript asterisk](images/c03_385.png).
3.  *Associativity*:  <math alttext="left-parenthesis a plus b right-parenthesis plus c equals a plus left-parenthesis b plus c right-parenthesis comma left-parenthesis a times b right-parenthesis times c equals a times left-parenthesis b times c right-parenthesis comma for-all a comma for-all b comma for-all c element-of upper F" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8704;</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8704;</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8704;</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi>F</mi></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis a plus b right-parenthesis plus c equals a plus left-parenthesis b plus c right-parenthesis comma left-parenthesis a times b right-parenthesis times c equals a times left-parenthesis b times c right-parenthesis comma for-all a comma for-all b comma for-all c element-of upper F](images/c03_386.png).
4.  *Distributivity*:  <math alttext="a times left-parenthesis b plus c right-parenthesis equals a times b plus a times c comma for a comma b comma c element-of upper F" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;for&#160;</mtext><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi>F</mi></mrow></math> ![a times left-parenthesis b plus c right-parenthesis equals a times b plus a times c comma for a comma b comma c element-of upper F](images/c03_387.png).
5.  *Every nonzero element*  <math alttext="a element-of upper F" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi>F</mi></mrow></math> ![a element-of upper F](images/c03_388.png) *has a multiplicative inverse*  <math alttext="a Superscript negative 1 Baseline element-of upper F vertical-bar a times a Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi>F</mi><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![a Superscript negative 1 Baseline element-of upper F vertical-bar a times a Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 1](images/c03_389.png).

In other words, a commutative ring where all nonzero elements have multiplicative inverses is a field.

#### *3.2.2.1 Prime Finite Fields*

***Definition 3.29 Finite field****: a finite field* *F[p], also called* ***Galois*** *field and denoted*  <math alttext="upper G upper F left-parenthesis p right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>G</mi><mi>F</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper G upper F left-parenthesis p right-parenthesis](images/c03_390.png)*, is a field with a finite number of elements* *p. It is a set with two operations, addition (*+*) and multiplication (*×*), which are both commutative and associative*.

*Notations*:

Finite field with prime *p* is denoted *F[p]*,  <math alttext="upper F left-parenthesis p right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>F</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper F left-parenthesis p right-parenthesis](images/c03_391.png), or  <math alttext="upper G upper F left-parenthesis p right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>G</mi><mi>F</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper G upper F left-parenthesis p right-parenthesis](images/c03_392.png).

Finite field with prime power *p^m* is denoted  <math alttext="upper F Subscript p Sub Superscript m Subscript Baseline comma upper F left-parenthesis p Superscript m Baseline right-parenthesis or upper G upper F left-parenthesis p Superscript m Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>F</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;or&#160;</mtext><mi>G</mi><mi>F</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript p Sub Superscript m Subscript Baseline comma upper F left-parenthesis p Superscript m Baseline right-parenthesis or upper G upper F left-parenthesis p Superscript m Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c03_393.png).

 <math alttext="upper F Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>F</mi><mo>\*</mo></msup></mrow></math> ![upper F Superscript asterisk](images/c03_394.png) is the set of nonzero elements of finite  <math alttext="upper F" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>F</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![upper F](images/c03_395.png)(i.e. <math alttext="upper F Superscript asterisk Baseline equals upper F minus StartSet 0 EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>F</mi><mtext>\*</mtext></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>F</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper F Superscript asterisk Baseline equals upper F minus StartSet 0 EndSet](images/c03_396.png)).

***Definition 3.30 Prime field****: any field* *F[p], also denoted*[^(10)](#c03.xhtml#c03-note-0010) ℤ[p]*,with prime* *p, is unique and called prime field*.

*   ***Operations over prime finite fields***

Let *a*, *b*, *c*, and  <math alttext="h" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow></math> ![h](images/c03_398.png) be elements of *F[p]*.

*   Addition and subtraction modulo *p* 
    *     <math alttext="a plus b equals c m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![a plus b equals c m o d p](images/c03_399.png)
    *     <math alttext="a minus b m o d p delta-equals a plus left-parenthesis negative b right-parenthesis m o d p equals d" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>b</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8796;</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></math> ![a minus b m o d p delta-equals a plus left-parenthesis negative b right-parenthesis m o d p equals d](images/c03_400.png): subtraction is defined as an addition of the negative of *b*
*   Multiplication:  <math alttext="a asterisk b equals h m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>h</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![a asterisk b equals h m o d p](images/c03_401.png)
*   Division:  <math alttext="StartFraction a Over b EndFraction m o d p delta-equals a asterisk b Superscript negative 1 Baseline m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mfrac><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi></mfrac><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8796;</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![StartFraction a Over b EndFraction m o d p delta-equals a asterisk b Superscript negative 1 Baseline m o d p](images/c03_402.png), where  <math alttext="b Superscript negative 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![b Superscript negative 1](images/c03_403.png) is the inverse of *b*. Division is defined as a multiplication by the inverse.

**Note**. Theorem 3.14 is very useful to quickly compute multiplicative inverses.

**Example 3.23**

*   –  <math alttext="3 minus 5 m o d 7 equals 3 plus 2 equals 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>5</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![3 minus 5 m o d 7 equals 3 plus 2 equals 5](images/c03_407.png), because  <math alttext="negative 5 identical-to 2 m o d 7" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>2</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn></mrow></math> ![negative 5 identical-to 2 m o d 7](images/c03_408.png)
*   –  <math alttext="three-fifths m o d 7 equals 3 times left-parenthesis 5 Superscript negative 1 Baseline right-parenthesis equals 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>&#215;</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![three-fifths m o d 7 equals 3 times left-parenthesis 5 Superscript negative 1 Baseline right-parenthesis equals 2](images/c03_409.png), because 3 is the multiplicative inverse of  <math alttext="5 m o d 7" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn></mrow></math> ![5 m o d 7](images/c03_410.png).

**Example 3.24**  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 7" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>7</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 7](images/c03_411.png), under the usual addition and multiplication operations + and \* is a finite field, because:

*   – The number of elements of  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 7" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>7</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 7](images/c03_412.png) is finite.
*   –  <math alttext="left-parenthesis double-struck upper Z 7 comma plus right-parenthesis and left-parenthesis double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk Baseline comma asterisk right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>7</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>+</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>and&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mo>\*</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis double-struck upper Z 7 comma plus right-parenthesis and left-parenthesis double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk Baseline comma asterisk right-parenthesis](images/c03_413.png) are commutative groups.
*   – Each nonzero element of  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 7" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>7</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 7](images/c03_414.png) has its multiplicative inverse in  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 7" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>7</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 7](images/c03_415.png). Below is the table of computations for  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 7" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>7</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 7](images/c03_416.png):

![](images/c03_417.png)

**Example 3.25**

*   –  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 100" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>&#8484;</mi><mrow><mn>100</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 100](images/c03_419.png), with the usual addition and multiplication operations + and \*, is not a finite field, because some elements (i.e. even elements and multiples of 5) have no multiplicative inverse  <math alttext="m o d 100" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>100</mn></mrow></math> ![m o d 100](images/c03_420.png). Recall that the multiplicative inverse of  <math alttext="a element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msub><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![a element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript p](images/c03_421.png) exists only if  <math alttext="normal upper G normal upper C normal upper D left-parenthesis a comma p right-parenthesis equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">G</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![normal upper G normal upper C normal upper D left-parenthesis a comma p right-parenthesis equals 1](images/c03_422.png).
*   –  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>8</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 8](images/c03_423.png), with the usual addition and multiplication operations + and \* is not a finite field, because even elements (i.e.  <math alttext="2 comma 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>4</mn></mrow></math> ![2 comma 4](images/c03_424.png), and 6) have no multiplicative inverse  <math alttext="m o d 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>8</mn></mrow></math> ![m o d 8](images/c03_425.png). However,  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>8</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 8](images/c03_426.png) can be written as  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 cubed Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 cubed Baseline](images/c03_427.png) and by Theorem 3.12,  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>8</mn></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 8](images/c03_428.png) should be a field. To make  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>8</mn></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 8](images/c03_429.png) a field, we need to redefine addition and multiplication (see [Section 3.2.3](#c03.xhtml#c03-sec-0049)).

**Example 3.26**

Elements of the field  <math alttext="upper F 23" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mn>23</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F 23](images/c03_430.png) are  <math alttext="StartSet 0 comma 1 comma 2 comma 3 comma ellipsis comma 21 comma 22 EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>21</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>22</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></math> ![StartSet 0 comma 1 comma 2 comma 3 comma ellipsis comma 21 comma 22 EndSet](images/c03_431.png). Example of inverse calculation based on the generator of  <math alttext="upper F 23" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mn>23</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F 23](images/c03_435.png):

 <math alttext="6 Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 4 m o d 23 comma since 6 asterisk 4 equals 1 m o d 23 period" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>6</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>23</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;since&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>6</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>23.</mn></mrow></math> ![6 Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 4 m o d 23 comma since 6 asterisk 4 equals 1 m o d 23 period](images/c03_436.png) Since 5 is a generator of  <math alttext="upper F 23" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mn>23</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F 23](images/c03_437.png) and  <math alttext="5 Superscript 18 Baseline equals 6 m o d 23 comma 6 Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 5 Superscript 23 minus 18 minus 1 Baseline equals 5 Superscript 4 Baseline equals 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mrow><mn>18</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>6</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>23</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mn>6</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mrow><mn>23</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>18</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></math> ![5 Superscript 18 Baseline equals 6 m o d 23 comma 6 Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 5 Superscript 23 minus 18 minus 1 Baseline equals 5 Superscript 4 Baseline equals 4](images/c03_438.png).

*   ***Properties of prime fields***

1.  The set of elements of field  <math alttext="upper F Subscript p Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript p Baseline](images/c03_439.png) is  <math alttext="StartSet 0 comma 1 comma 2 comma ellipsis comma p minus 1 EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></math> ![StartSet 0 comma 1 comma 2 comma ellipsis comma p minus 1 EndSet](images/c03_440.png).
2.  The order of field *F[p]*, with prime *p*, is the number of the elements in the field and it is denoted  <math alttext="StartAbsoluteValue upper F Subscript p Baseline EndAbsoluteValue" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><mo>&#124;</mo></mrow></math> ![StartAbsoluteValue upper F Subscript p Baseline EndAbsoluteValue](images/c03_441.png) and it is equal to *p*.
3.  Adding *p* copies of any element of *F[p]* results in zero, i.e. for any  <math alttext="a element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msub><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![a element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript p](images/c03_442.png),  <math alttext="p asterisk a identical-to 0 m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>0</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![p asterisk a identical-to 0 m o d p](images/c03_443.png).
4.  Every nonzero element in  <math alttext="upper F Subscript p Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript p Baseline](images/c03_444.png) has a multiplicative inverse in *F[p]*.
5.   <math alttext="upper F Subscript p Baseline minus 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript p Baseline minus 0](images/c03_445.png), denoted  <math alttext="upper F Subscript p Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript p Superscript asterisk](images/c03_446.png), is a cyclic group of order  <math alttext="p minus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![p minus 1](images/c03_447.png).

### 3.2.3 Extension Fields  <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>F</mi><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>m</mi></msup></msub></math> ![F subscript p to the power of m end subscript](images/c03_448a.png)

***Definition 3.31 Extension field****: a field* *F* *is said to be an extension of a field* *E*, *if* *E* *is a subfield of*  <math alttext="upper F" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>F</mi></mrow></math> ![upper F](images/c03_448.png)*. That is denoted*  <math alttext="upper F slash upper E or upper F o v e r upper E" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>E</mi><mtext>&#160;or&#160;</mtext><mi>F</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>v</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>E</mi></mrow></math> ![upper F slash upper E or upper F o v e r upper E](images/c03_449.png)*. An extension field also is called extended field*.

***Definition 3.32 Characteristic of extension field***: if  <math alttext="upper F Subscript p Sub Superscript m" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript p Sub Superscript m](images/c03_450.png) *is an extension of field* *F[p], it has a characteristic of* *p. That is, adding* *p* *copies of any elements of*  <math alttext="upper F Subscript p Sub Superscript m" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript p Sub Superscript m](images/c03_451.png) *results in adding the neutral element* 0.

**Example 3.27**

*   – ℝ, the set of real numbers, is an extension of ℚ, the set of rational numbers, and ℚ is an extension of ℤ, the set of integers.
*   –  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 cubed Baseline equals StartSet 0 comma 1 comma 2 comma 3 comma 4 comma 5 comma 6 comma 7 EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 cubed Baseline equals StartSet 0 comma 1 comma 2 comma 3 comma 4 comma 5 comma 6 comma 7 EndSet](images/c03_452.png) is an extension field of  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 2](images/c03_453.png). It has a characteristic of 2. Hence,  <math alttext="for-all a element-of upper F Subscript 2 cubed Baseline comma a plus a equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8704;</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![for-all a element-of upper F Subscript 2 cubed Baseline comma a plus a equals 0](images/c03_454.png), because addition is done  <math alttext="m o d u l o 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>o</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![m o d u l o 2](images/c03_455.png).
*   –  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 3 squared Baseline equals StartSet 0 comma 1 comma 2 comma 3 comma 4 comma 5 comma 6 comma 7 comma 8 EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 3 squared Baseline equals StartSet 0 comma 1 comma 2 comma 3 comma 4 comma 5 comma 6 comma 7 comma 8 EndSet](images/c03_456.png) is an extension field of  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 3](images/c03_457.png). It has a characteristic of 3. Hence, <math alttext="for-all a element-of upper F Subscript 3 squared Baseline comma a plus a plus a equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8704;</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![for-all a element-of upper F Subscript 3 squared Baseline comma a plus a plus a equals 0](images/c03_458.png), because addition is done  <math alttext="m o d u l o 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>o</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> ![m o d u l o 3](images/c03_459.png).

To do operations on elements of extension fields  <math alttext="upper F Subscript p Sub Superscript m" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript p Sub Superscript m](images/c03_460.png), we need to represent them as polynomials. That is, any element of an extension field is a polynomial with coefficients in a subfield *F[p]*.

#### *3.2.3.1 Basics of Modular Polynomial Arithmetic*

***Definition 3.33 Polynomial***: *a polynomial*  <math alttext="upper P left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo **Example 3.28**

Let  <math alttext="upper A left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x cubed plus x squared plus x plus 1 and upper B left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x squared plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;and&#160;</mtext><mi>B</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![upper A left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x cubed plus x squared plus x plus 1 and upper B left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x squared plus 1](images/c03_466.png).
