    3.  Iteration 3: <math alttext="t" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> ![t](images/c03_1299.png) is equal to 1. Thus, return  <math alttext="r equals 87" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>87</mn></mrow></math> ![r equals 87](images/c03_1300.png).
        
        Hence, the solutions to  <math alttext="111 m o d 113" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>111</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>113</mn></mrow></math> ![111 m o d 113](images/c03_1301.png) are 87 and 26 (i.e.  <math alttext="negative 87 m o d 113" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>87</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>113</mn></mrow></math> ![negative 87 m o d 113](images/c03_1302.png)).
        

#### 3.3.5.2 Finding Square Roots of Multiple Primes

This subsection considers the following problem:

Find the solutions to  <math alttext="y squared identical-to a m o d upper N" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>a</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> ![y squared identical-to a m o d upper N](images/c03_1303.png), with *N* a multiple of two or more primes.

##### *3.3.5.2.1 Case of Two Primes*

Let us start with the following example: find solutions to  <math alttext="r squared identical-to 29 m o d 35" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>29</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>35</mn></mrow></math> ![r squared identical-to 29 m o d 35](images/c03_1304.png).

In such a scenario,  <math alttext="upper N equals 35" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>35</mn></mrow></math> ![upper N equals 35](images/c03_1305.png) is a product of two primes 5 and 7.

By Lemma 3.2, if there exists *r* such that  <math alttext="r squared identical-to 29 m o d 35" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>29</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>35</mn></mrow></math> ![r squared identical-to 29 m o d 35](images/c03_1306.png), then  <math alttext="r squared identical-to 29 m o d 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>29</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![r squared identical-to 29 m o d 5](images/c03_1307.png) and  <math alttext="r squared identical-to 29 m o d 7" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>29</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn></mrow></math> ![r squared identical-to 29 m o d 7](images/c03_1308.png).

 <math alttext="r squared identical-to 29 m o d 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>29</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![r squared identical-to 29 m o d 5](images/c03_1309.png) is equivalent to  <math alttext="r squared identical-to 4 m o d 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>4</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![r squared identical-to 4 m o d 5](images/c03_1310.png).

 <math alttext="r squared identical-to 29 m o d 7" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>29</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn></mrow></math> ![r squared identical-to 29 m o d 7](images/c03_1311.png) is equivalent to  <math alttext="r squared identical-to 1 m o d 7" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn></mrow></math> ![r squared identical-to 1 m o d 7](images/c03_1312.png).

 <math alttext="4 m o d 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>4</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![4 m o d 5](images/c03_1313.png) has two quadratic squares: 2 and 3.

 <math alttext="1 m o d 7" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn></mrow></math> ![1 m o d 7](images/c03_1314.png) has two quadratic squares: 1 and 6.

Thus, there are four congruence systems to solve:

 <math alttext="upper S 1 colon equals StartLayout Enlarged left-brace 1st Row x identical-to 2 m o d 5 2nd Row x identical-to 1 m o d 7 EndLayout" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>:</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mtable><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>2</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper S 1 colon equals StartLayout Enlarged left-brace 1st Row x identical-to 2 m o d 5 2nd Row x identical-to 1 m o d 7 EndLayout](images/c03_1315.png)    <math alttext="upper S 2 colon equals StartLayout Enlarged left-brace 1st Row x identical-to 2 m o d 5 2nd Row x identical-to 6 m o d 7 EndLayout" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>:</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mtable><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>2</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>6</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper S 2 colon equals StartLayout Enlarged left-brace 1st Row x identical-to 2 m o d 5 2nd Row x identical-to 6 m o d 7 EndLayout](images/c03_1316.png)

 <math alttext="upper S 3 colon equals left-brace StartLayout 1st Row x identical-to 3 m o d 5 2nd Row x identical-to 1 m o d 7 EndLayout" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>:</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtable><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>3</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper S 3 colon equals left-brace StartLayout 1st Row x identical-to 3 m o d 5 2nd Row x identical-to 1 m o d 7 EndLayout](images/c03_1317.png)    <math alttext="upper S 4 colon equals StartLayout Enlarged left-brace 1st Row x identical-to 3 m o d 5 2nd Row x identical-to 6 m o d 7 EndLayout" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>:</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mtable><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>3</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>6</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper S 4 colon equals StartLayout Enlarged left-brace 1st Row x identical-to 3 m o d 5 2nd Row x identical-to 6 m o d 7 EndLayout](images/c03_1318.png)

Recall that the commonly used method to solve congruence systems is Gauss’s algorithm. Below are calculations to solve  <math alttext="upper S 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper S 1](images/c03_1319.png) system:

The constants of the congruence equation system are:  <math alttext="n 1 equals 5 comma n 2 equals 7 comma a 1 equals 2 comma a 2 equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![n 1 equals 5 comma n 2 equals 7 comma a 1 equals 2 comma a 2 equals 1](images/c03_1320.png).

Common modulus is  <math alttext="upper N equals 5 asterisk 7 equals 35" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>35</mn></mrow></math> ![upper N equals 5 asterisk 7 equals 35](images/c03_1321.png)

 <math alttext="upper N 1 equals StartFraction 35 Over 5 EndFraction equals 7 comma upper N 2 equals StartFraction 35 Over 7 EndFraction equals 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>35</mn></mrow><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>35</mn></mrow><mn>7</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![upper N 1 equals StartFraction 35 Over 5 EndFraction equals 7 comma upper N 2 equals StartFraction 35 Over 7 EndFraction equals 5](images/c03_1322.png).

Multiplicative inverses:  <math alttext="upper N 1 Superscript negative 1 Baseline asterisk upper N 1 identical-to 1 m o d 5 right double arrow upper N 1 Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>\*</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn><mo>&#8658;</mo><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> ![upper N 1 Superscript negative 1 Baseline asterisk upper N 1 identical-to 1 m o d 5 right double arrow upper N 1 Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 3](images/c03_1323.png)

 <math alttext="upper N 2 Superscript negative 1 Baseline asterisk upper N 2 identical-to 1 m o d 7 right double arrow upper N 2 Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>\*</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn><mo>&#8658;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> ![upper N 2 Superscript negative 1 Baseline asterisk upper N 2 identical-to 1 m o d 7 right double arrow upper N 2 Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 3](images/c03_1324.png)

 <math alttext="x equals left-parenthesis left-parenthesis 2 asterisk 7 asterisk 3 right-parenthesis plus left-parenthesis 1 asterisk 5 asterisk 3 right-parenthesis right-parenthesis m o d 35 equals 22" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>35</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>22</mn></mrow></math> ![x equals left-parenthesis left-parenthesis 2 asterisk 7 asterisk 3 right-parenthesis plus left-parenthesis 1 asterisk 5 asterisk 3 right-parenthesis right-parenthesis m o d 35 equals 22](images/c03_1325.png).

Applying Gauss’s algorithm to the four congruence systems yields the following:

 <math alttext="x equals 22" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>22</mn></mrow></math> ![x equals 22](images/c03_1326.png) is a solution to <math alttext="upper S 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper S 1](images/c03_1327.png)

 <math alttext="x equals 27" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>27</mn></mrow></math> ![x equals 27](images/c03_1328.png) is a solution to  <math alttext="upper S 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper S 2](images/c03_1329.png)

 <math alttext="r squared identical-to a m o d p comma when p identical-to 1 m o d 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>a</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;when&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>4</mn></mrow></math> ![r squared identical-to a m o d p comma when p identical-to 1 m o d 4](images/c03_1330.png) is a solution to  <math alttext="upper S 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper S 3](images/c03_1331.png)

 <math alttext="x equals 13" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>13</mn></mrow></math> ![x equals 13](images/c03_1332.png) is a solution to  <math alttext="upper S 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper S 4](images/c03_1333.png)

Now, check that the values are square roots of  <math alttext="29 m o d 35" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>29</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>35</mn></mrow></math> ![29 m o d 35](images/c03_1334.png)

 <math alttext="x equals 22 colon 22 squared equals 484 identical-to 29 m o d 35" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>22</mn><mo>:</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mrow><mn>22</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>484</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>29</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>35</mn></mrow></math> ![x equals 22 colon 22 squared equals 484 identical-to 29 m o d 35](images/c03_1335.png)

 <math alttext="x equals 27 colon 27 squared equals 729 identical-to 29 m o d 35" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>27</mn><mo>:</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mrow><mn>27</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>729</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>29</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>35</mn></mrow></math> ![x equals 27 colon 27 squared equals 729 identical-to 29 m o d 35](images/c03_1336.png)

 <math alttext="x equals 8 colon 8 squared equals 64 identical-to 29 m o d 35" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>:</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mn>8</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>29</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>35</mn></mrow></math> ![x equals 8 colon 8 squared equals 64 identical-to 29 m o d 35](images/c03_1337.png)

 <math alttext="x equals 13 colon 13 squared equals 169 identical-to 29 m o d 35" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>13</mn><mo>:</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mrow><mn>13</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>169</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>29</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>35</mn></mrow></math> ![x equals 13 colon 13 squared equals 169 identical-to 29 m o d 35](images/c03_1338.png)

Thus,  <math alttext="29 m o d 35" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>29</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>35</mn></mrow></math> ![29 m o d 35](images/c03_1339.png) has four square roots.

##### *3.3.5.2.2 General Case (2 or More Primes)*

When *n* is a product of *k* primes denoted  <math alttext="n 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![n 1](images/c03_1340.png),  <math alttext="n 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![n 2](images/c03_1341.png), …,  <math alttext="n Subscript k" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![n Subscript k](images/c03_1342.png), the commonly used method to find the square roots of  <math alttext="a m o d upper N" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> ![a m o d upper N](images/c03_1343.png) is composed of two steps:

*   Step 1: Find the square roots of prime moduli
    
    1.  From congruence  <math alttext="a m o d upper N" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> ![a m o d upper N](images/c03_1344.png), derive congruences  <math alttext="a 1 m o d n 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![a 1 m o d n 1](images/c03_1345.png), …,  <math alttext="a Subscript k Baseline m o d n Subscript k Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![a Subscript k Baseline m o d n Subscript k Baseline](images/c03_1346.png), where  <math alttext="a Subscript i Baseline identical-to a m o d n Subscript i Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>a</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![a Subscript i Baseline identical-to a m o d n Subscript i Baseline](images/c03_1347.png), for  <math alttext="1 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than-or-equal-to k" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></math> ![1 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than-or-equal-to k](images/c03_1348.png).
    2.  Then, find the square roots to each of congruences  <math alttext="a Subscript i Baseline m o d n Subscript i Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![a Subscript i Baseline m o d n Subscript i Baseline](images/c03_1349.png),  <math alttext="1 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than-or-equal-to k" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></math> ![1 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than-or-equal-to k](images/c03_1350.png). The result is a set of *k* pairs  <math alttext="left-parenthesis r Subscript i Baseline comma minus r Subscript i Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis r Subscript i Baseline comma minus r Subscript i Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c03_1351.png), where  <math alttext="r Subscript i Baseline squared identical-to a Subscript i Baseline m o d zero width space n Subscript i Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><msup><mrow><mtext>&#8201;</mtext></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#8203;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![r Subscript i Baseline squared identical-to a Subscript i Baseline m o d zero width space n Subscript i Baseline](images/c03_1352.png),  <math alttext="1 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than-or-equal-to k" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></math> ![1 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than-or-equal-to k](images/c03_1353.png). At this step, depending on each  <math alttext="n Subscript i" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![n Subscript i](images/c03_1354.png), either Lemma 3.5 or Tonelli-Shanks algorithm should be used to find square roots to  <math alttext="r Subscript i Baseline squared identical-to a Subscript i Baseline m o d n Subscript i Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><msup><mrow><mtext>&#8201;</mtext></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![r Subscript i Baseline squared identical-to a Subscript i Baseline m o d n Subscript i Baseline](images/c03_1355.png).
*   Step 2: Solve a set of congruence systems
    
    *   iii) Build a set of  <math alttext="r squared identical-to a mod p comma zero width space w h e n zero width space p identical-to 1 zero width space mod 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>a</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>mod</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#8203;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>w</mi><mi>h</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mtext>&#8203;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8203;</mtext><mi>mod</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>4</mn></mrow></math> ![r squared identical-to a mod p comma zero width space w h e n zero width space p identical-to 1 zero width space mod 4](images/c03_1356.png) distinct congruence systems denoted  <math alttext="upper S 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper S 1](images/c03_1357.png),  <math alttext="upper S 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper S 2](images/c03_1358.png), …,  <math alttext="upper S Subscript 2 Sub Superscript k" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>k</mi></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper S Subscript 2 Sub Superscript k](images/c03_1359.png) such that each congruence system is composed of exactly *k* congruences (a congruence for each of the *k* primes) as follows:
        
         <math alttext="upper S 1 equals StartSet r 1 m o d n 1 comma r 2 m o d n 2 comma ellipsis comma r Subscript k minus 1 Baseline m o d n Subscript k minus 1 Baseline comma r Subscript k Baseline m o d n Subscript k Baseline EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper S 1 equals StartSet r 1 m o d n 1 comma r 2 m o d n 2 comma ellipsis comma r Subscript k minus 1 Baseline m o d n Subscript k minus 1 Baseline comma r Subscript k Baseline m o d n Subscript k Baseline EndSet](images/c03_1360.png)
        
         <math alttext="upper S 2 equals StartSet r 1 m o d n 1 comma r 2 m o d n 2 comma ellipsis comma r Subscript k minus 1 Baseline m o d n Subscript k minus 1 Baseline comma minus r Subscript k Baseline m o d n Subscript k Baseline EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper S 2 equals StartSet r 1 m o d n 1 comma r 2 m o d n 2 comma ellipsis comma r Subscript k minus 1 Baseline m o d n Subscript k minus 1 Baseline comma minus r Subscript k Baseline m o d n Subscript k Baseline EndSet](images/c03_1361.png)
        
         <math alttext="upper S 3 equals StartSet r 1 m o d n 1 comma r 2 m o d n 2 comma ellipsis comma minus r Subscript k minus 1 Baseline m o d n Subscript k minus 1 Baseline comma r Subscript k Baseline m o d n Subscript k Baseline EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper S 3 equals StartSet r 1 m o d n 1 comma r 2 m o d n 2 comma ellipsis comma minus r Subscript k minus 1 Baseline m o d n Subscript k minus 1 Baseline comma r Subscript k Baseline m o d n Subscript k Baseline EndSet](images/c03_1362.png)
        
        …
        
         <math alttext="upper S Subscript 2 Sub Superscript k Baseline equals StartSet minus r 1 m o d n 1 comma minus r 2 m o d n 2 comma ellipsis comma minus r Subscript k minus 1 Baseline m o d n Subscript k minus 1 Baseline comma minus r Subscript k Baseline m o d n Subscript k Baseline EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>k</mi></msup></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper S Subscript 2 Sub Superscript k Baseline equals StartSet minus r 1 m o d n 1 comma minus r 2 m o d n 2 comma ellipsis comma minus r Subscript k minus 1 Baseline m o d n Subscript k minus 1 Baseline comma minus r Subscript k Baseline m o d n Subscript k Baseline EndSet](images/c03_1363.png)
        
    *   iv) Use Gauss’s algorithm to find the solutions to each of the  <math alttext="2 Superscript k" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>k</mi></msup></mrow></math> ![2 Superscript k](images/c03_1364.png) congruence systems. The  <math alttext="2 Superscript k" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>k</mi></msup></mrow></math> ![2 Superscript k](images/c03_1365.png) found solutions represent the square roots to  <math alttext="a m o d upper N" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> ![a m o d upper N](images/c03_1366.png).

### 3.3.6 Test of Irreducibility

In cryptography, before using a polynomial  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c03_1367.png) of degree *m* over a field *F[p]* as a reduction polynomial to construct a field  <math alttext="upper F Subscript p Sub Superscript m" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript p Sub Superscript m](images/c03_1368.png), one must first check that *p* is prime and  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c03_1369.png) is irreducible over *F[p]*. Hence, algorithms for testing irreducibility are needed in cryptography. There exist two approaches to test if a polynomial  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c03_1370.png) of degree *m* over a finite field *F[p]* is irreducible: naïve approach and Rabin’s test for irreducibility.

#### 3.3.6.1 Naïve Approach

Take each element in  <math alttext="StartSet 0 comma 2 comma ellipsis comma p minus 1 EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></math> ![StartSet 0 comma 2 comma ellipsis comma p minus 1 EndSet](images/c03_1371.png) and check if  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis 0 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis 0 right-parenthesis](images/c03_1372.png),  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis](images/c03_1373.png), …,  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis](images/c03_1374.png) is equal to 0. When the first element *a* such that  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis a right-parenthesis equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis a right-parenthesis equals 0](images/c03_1375.png) is found, stop testing, because there exists at least a root of  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c03_1376.png) and  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c03_1377.png) can be factorized as  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis x minus a right-parenthesis asterisk q left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo><mi>q</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis x minus a right-parenthesis asterisk q left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c03_1378.png), with  <math alttext="q left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>q</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![q left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c03_1379.png) a polynomial of degree less than *m*, and consequently  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c03_1380.png) is reducible.

**Example 3.44** Test irreducibility of  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x squared plus x plus 1 over upper F 2 colon" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;over&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>:</mo></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x squared plus x plus 1 over upper F 2 colon](images/c03_1381.png)

 <math alttext="upper F 2 equals StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper F 2 equals StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet](images/c03_1382.png). Thus, the check is:

 <math alttext="f left-parenthesis 0 right-parenthesis equals 0 Superscript 4 Baseline plus 0 squared plus 0 plus 1 m o d 2 equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis 0 right-parenthesis equals 0 Superscript 4 Baseline plus 0 squared plus 0 plus 1 m o d 2 equals 1](images/c03_1383.png)   <math alttext="f left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis equals 1 Superscript 4 Baseline plus 1 squared plus 1 plus 1 m o d 2 equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis equals 1 Superscript 4 Baseline plus 1 squared plus 1 plus 1 m o d 2 equals 0](images/c03_1384.png).

Therefore,  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c03_1385.png) is reducible and can be expressed as  <math alttext="left-parenthesis x plus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis x cubed plus x squared plus 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis x plus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis x cubed plus x squared plus 1 right-parenthesis](images/c03_1386.png).

Irreducibility test of  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x cubed plus x plus 1 over upper F 5 colon" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;over&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>5</mn></msub><mo>:</mo></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x cubed plus x plus 1 over upper F 5 colon](images/c03_1387.png)

 <math alttext="upper F 5 equals left-brace 0 comma 1 comma 2 comma 3 comma 4 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>5</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![upper F 5 equals left-brace 0 comma 1 comma 2 comma 3 comma 4 right-parenthesis](images/c03_1388.png). Thus, the check is:

 <math alttext="f left-parenthesis 0 right-parenthesis equals 0 Superscript 4 Baseline plus 0 cubed plus 0 plus 1 m o d 5 equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis 0 right-parenthesis equals 0 Superscript 4 Baseline plus 0 cubed plus 0 plus 1 m o d 5 equals 1](images/c03_1389.png)   <math alttext="f left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis equals 1 Superscript 4 Baseline plus 1 cubed plus 1 plus 1 m o d 5 equals 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis equals 1 Superscript 4 Baseline plus 1 cubed plus 1 plus 1 m o d 5 equals 4](images/c03_1390.png)

 <math alttext="f left-parenthesis 2 right-parenthesis equals 2 Superscript 4 Baseline plus 2 cubed plus 2 plus 1 m o d 5 equals 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis 2 right-parenthesis equals 2 Superscript 4 Baseline plus 2 cubed plus 2 plus 1 m o d 5 equals 2](images/c03_1391.png)    <math alttext="f left-parenthesis 3 right-parenthesis equals 3 Superscript 4 Baseline plus 3 cubed plus 3 plus 1 m o d 5 equals 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis 3 right-parenthesis equals 3 Superscript 4 Baseline plus 3 cubed plus 3 plus 1 m o d 5 equals 2](images/c03_1392.png)

 <math alttext="f left-parenthesis 4 right-parenthesis equals 4 Superscript 4 Baseline plus 4 cubed plus 4 plus 1 m o d 5 equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis 4 right-parenthesis equals 4 Superscript 4 Baseline plus 4 cubed plus 4 plus 1 m o d 5 equals 0](images/c03_1393.png).

Hence,  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c03_1394.png) is reducible and can be expressed as  <math alttext="left-parenthesis x minus 4 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis x cubed plus 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis x minus 4 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis x cubed plus 1 right-parenthesis](images/c03_1395.png), which is the same as  <math alttext="left-parenthesis x plus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis x cubed plus 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis x plus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis x cubed plus 1 right-parenthesis](images/c03_1396.png) over  <math alttext="upper F 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>5</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F 5](images/c03_1397.png).

Such a naïve method is easy to understand and implement. Unfortunately, it suffers two weaknesses: 1) it does not scale (remember that in cryptography very large numbers are used) and 2) a polynomial may be reducible even if it has no roots. For example, in field  <math alttext="upper F 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F 3](images/c03_1398.png),  <math alttext="x Superscript 4 Baseline plus 2 x squared plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![x Superscript 4 Baseline plus 2 x squared plus 1](images/c03_1399.png) can be written as a product  <math alttext="left-parenthesis x squared plus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis x squared plus 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis x squared plus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis x squared plus 1 right-parenthesis](images/c03_1400.png). Therefore, it is reducible, but it has no roots in  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 3](images/c03_1401.png), because  <math alttext="left-parenthesis x squared plus 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis x squared plus 1 right-parenthesis](images/c03_1402.png) has no roots in  <math alttext="upper F 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F 3](images/c03_1403.png).

#### 3.3.6.2 Efficient Approach (Rabin’s Test of Irreducibility)

One of well-known algorithms for testing the irreducibility of polynomials over ℤ[p] is the Rabin’s test \[[11](#c03.xhtml#c03-bib-0011)\], which results from the following theorem:

Pseudocode of Rabin’s test of irreducibility is as follows:

**Example 3.45**

*   – Check of irreducibility of  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x squared plus x plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x squared plus x plus 1](images/c03_1421.png) over  <math alttext="upper F 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F 2](images/c03_1422.png)
    
     <math alttext="m equals 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></math> ![m equals 4](images/c03_1423.png), so the prime divider of *m* is 2.
    
     <math alttext="p 1 equals four-halves equals 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![p 1 equals four-halves equals 2](images/c03_1424.png)
    
    *Iteration #1 (test of prime divider 2, i.e*.  <math alttext="p 1 equals 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![p 1 equals 2](images/c03_1425.png)*)*:
    
     <math alttext="x Superscript 2 squared Baseline equals x Superscript 4 Baseline identical-to x squared plus x plus 1 m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![x Superscript 2 squared Baseline equals x Superscript 4 Baseline identical-to x squared plus x plus 1 m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c03_1426.png)
    
     <math alttext="h left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x squared plus x plus 1 minus x m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x squared plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>x</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![h left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x squared plus x plus 1 minus x m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x squared plus 1](images/c03_1427.png)
    
     <math alttext="g left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals normal upper G normal upper C normal upper D left-parenthesis f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis comma h left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis right-parenthesis equals x plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">G</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![g left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals normal upper G normal upper C normal upper D left-parenthesis f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis comma h left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis right-parenthesis equals x plus 1](images/c03_1428.png)
    
     <math alttext="g left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis not-equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8800;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![g left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis not-equals 1](images/c03_1429.png); thus,  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c03_1430.png) is irreducible over  <math alttext="upper F 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F 2](images/c03_1431.png) as it was checked by the naïve method (see Example [3.44](#c03.xhtml#c03-mthst-0044)). Stop the algorithm.
    
*   – Check of irreducibility of  <math alttext="x cubed plus x plus 1 over upper F 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;over&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![x cubed plus x plus 1 over upper F 2](images/c03_1432.png)
    
     <math alttext="m equals 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> ![m equals 3](images/c03_1433.png) is a prime. Thus, the prime divider of *m* is 3.
    
     <math alttext="p 1 equals three-thirds equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![p 1 equals three-thirds equals 1](images/c03_1434.png)
    
    *Iteration #1 (test of prime divider 3, i.e*.  <math alttext="p 1 equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![p 1 equals 1](images/c03_1435.png)*)*:
    
      <math alttext="h left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x squared minus x m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x squared plus x" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>x</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> ![h left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x squared minus x m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x squared plus x](images/c03_1436.png)
    
      <math alttext="g left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals upper G upper C upper D left-parenthesis f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis comma h left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis right-parenthesis equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>G</mi><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![g left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals upper G upper C upper D left-parenthesis f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis comma h left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis right-parenthesis equals 1](images/c03_1437.png)
    
      <math alttext="g left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![g left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals 1](images/c03_1438.png)*;* hence, the algorithm continues.
    
    *Second step of the algorithm*
    
     <math alttext="g left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 2 cubed Baseline minus x equals x Superscript 8 Baseline plus x m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>8</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![g left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 2 cubed Baseline minus x equals x Superscript 8 Baseline plus x m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals 0](images/c03_1439.png).
    
    Thus,  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c03_1440.png) is irreducible.

## 3.4 Birthday Paradox and Its Generalization

First of all, it is worth noticing that Birthday paradox is used to find the complexity of some attacks against cryptographic algorithms that will be discussed in next chapters.

*Birthday paradox*, also referred to as *Birthday problem*, is relating to the probability that, in a set of *n* randomly chosen people, a pair of them will have the same birthday. In a group of 23 people, the probability of a same birthday exceeds 50%, while a group of 70 has a 99.9% chance of a same birthday. Birthday problem is a paradox, because it first appears counterintuitive that with 23 people, there is 50% chance that two people share the same birthday.

*Proof*:

It is assumed that all 365 birthdays have the same probability of occurrence.

Let  <math alttext="upper P left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis represent the probability that at least a pair among the n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;represent&#160;the&#160;probability&#160;that&#160;at&#160;least&#160;a&#160;pair&#160;among&#160;the&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper P left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis represent the probability that at least a pair among the n](images/c03_1463.png) people have the same birthday.

 <math alttext="ModifyingAbove upper P With bar left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis equals 1 minus upper P left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>&#175;</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![ModifyingAbove upper P With bar left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis equals 1 minus upper P left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis](images/c03_1464.png) represents the probability that no pair among the *n* people have the same birthday. It is obvious to deduce that  <math alttext="ModifyingAbove upper P With bar left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>&#175;</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![ModifyingAbove upper P With bar left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis equals 0](images/c03_1465.png).

Let us consider  <math alttext="n less-than 365" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mn>365</mn></mrow></math> ![n less-than 365](images/c03_1467.png):

Without loss of generality, assume that persons are numbered from  <math alttext="1 to n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;to&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![1 to n](images/c03_1468.png).

The generalization of the birthday paradox to any set of *M* values with a uniform distribution is relating to the probability that two values among *n* values from the set *M* are equal. Such a probability is

 <math alttext="upper P left-parenthesis n comma upper M right-parenthesis equals 1 minus StartFraction upper M factorial Over upper M Superscript n Baseline left-parenthesis upper M minus n right-parenthesis factorial EndFraction period" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>!</mo></mrow><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>M</mi><mi>n</mi></msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>!</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> ![upper P left-parenthesis n comma upper M right-parenthesis equals 1 minus StartFraction upper M factorial Over upper M Superscript n Baseline left-parenthesis upper M minus n right-parenthesis factorial EndFraction period](images/c03_1478.png)

In cryptography field,  <math alttext="p left-parenthesis n comma upper M right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> ![p left-parenthesis n comma upper M right-parenthesis](images/c03_1479.png) is called *collision probability*.

*   ***Approximation and bounds to collision probability***

The following two approximations are proposed in literature to compute the number *n* of required people given *M*, the size of the population, and the expected probability of success  <math alttext="upper P left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper P left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis](images/c03_1480.png):

*    <math alttext="n almost-equals StartRoot 2 asterisk upper M asterisk upper P left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis EndRoot" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8776;</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></msqrt></mrow></math> ![n almost-equals StartRoot 2 asterisk upper M asterisk upper P left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis EndRoot](images/c03_1481.png), which works well for  <math alttext="upper P left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper P left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis](images/c03_1482.png) less or equal to 0.5.
*    <math alttext="n almost-equals StartRoot 2 asterisk upper M asterisk l n left-parenthesis StartFraction 1 Over 1 minus upper P left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis EndFraction right-parenthesis EndRoot" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8776;</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>l</mi><mi>n</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></msqrt></mrow></math> ![n almost-equals StartRoot 2 asterisk upper M asterisk l n left-parenthesis StartFraction 1 Over 1 minus upper P left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis EndFraction right-parenthesis EndRoot](images/c03_1483.png), where  <math alttext="l n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>l</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![l n](images/c03_1484.png) is the napierian logarithm.

Using the approximation below, to have 50% chance that at least a pair of persons have the same birthday,  <math alttext="n almost-equals StartRoot 2 asterisk 365 asterisk one-half EndRoot almost-equals 20 and n almost-equals StartRoot 2 asterisk 365 asterisk l n left-parenthesis 2 right-parenthesis EndRoot almost-equals 23" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8776;</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>365</mn><mo>\*</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></msqrt><mo>&#8776;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>20</mn><mtext>&#160;and&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8776;</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>365</mn><mo>\*</mo><mi>l</mi><mi>n</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></msqrt><mo>&#8776;</mo><mn>23</mn></mrow></math> ![n almost-equals StartRoot 2 asterisk 365 asterisk one-half EndRoot almost-equals 20 and n almost-equals StartRoot 2 asterisk 365 asterisk l n left-parenthesis 2 right-parenthesis EndRoot almost-equals 23](images/c03_1485.png) for the first and second approximations, respectively.

If  <math alttext="upper P left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis equals 0.5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow></math> ![upper P left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis equals 0.5](images/c03_1486.png), the first approximation results in  <math alttext="n almost-equals StartRoot upper M EndRoot" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8776;</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>M</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow></math> ![n almost-equals StartRoot upper M EndRoot](images/c03_1487.png) and the second in  <math alttext="n almost-equals StartRoot 2 asterisk upper M asterisk l n left-parenthesis 2 right-parenthesis EndRoot almost-equals 1.18 StartRoot upper M EndRoot" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8776;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>l</mi><mi>n</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></msqrt><mo>&#8776;</mo><mn>1.18</mn><msqrt><mrow><mi>M</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow></math> ![n almost-equals StartRoot 2 asterisk upper M asterisk l n left-parenthesis 2 right-parenthesis EndRoot almost-equals 1.18 StartRoot upper M EndRoot](images/c03_1488.png).

In \[[12](#c03.xhtml#c03-bib-0012)\] and other references in literature, the following bounds have been proven to delimit the collision probability  <math alttext="upper P left-parenthesis n comma upper M right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper P left-parenthesis n comma upper M right-parenthesis](images/c03_1489.png). The first upper bound is as follows:

 <math alttext="upper P left-parenthesis n comma upper M right-parenthesis less-than-or-equal-to StartFraction n left-parenthesis n minus 1 right-parenthesis Over 2 upper M EndFraction" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8804;</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>n</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>M</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> ![upper P left-parenthesis n comma upper M right-parenthesis less-than-or-equal-to StartFraction n left-parenthesis n minus 1 right-parenthesis Over 2 upper M EndFraction](images/c03_1490.png)

If is large, may  <math alttext="n is large comma n squared minus n may be approximated by n squared" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mtext>&#160;is&#160;large</mtext><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>n</mi><mtext>&#160;may&#160;be&#160;approximated&#160;by&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math> ![n is large comma n squared minus n may be approximated by n squared](images/c03_1491.png). Thus, a second upper bound is used:

 <math alttext="upper P left-parenthesis n comma upper M right-parenthesis less-than-or-equal-to StartFraction n squared Over 2 upper M EndFraction period" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8804;</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>M</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> ![upper P left-parenthesis n comma upper M right-parenthesis less-than-or-equal-to StartFraction n squared Over 2 upper M EndFraction period](images/c03_1492.png)

The upper bound to probability of no collision  <math alttext="ModifyingAbove upper P With bar left-parenthesis n comma upper M right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>&#175;</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![ModifyingAbove upper P With bar left-parenthesis n comma upper M right-parenthesis](images/c03_1493.png) is

 <math alttext="ModifyingAbove upper P With bar left-parenthesis n comma upper M right-parenthesis less-than-or-equal-to e Superscript minus StartFraction q left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis Over 2 upper N EndFraction Baseline period" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>&#175;</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8804;</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mfrac><mrow><mi>q</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>N</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> ![ModifyingAbove upper P With bar left-parenthesis n comma upper M right-parenthesis less-than-or-equal-to e Superscript minus StartFraction q left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis Over 2 upper N EndFraction Baseline period](images/c03_1494.png)

Thus, the lower bound to  <math alttext="upper P left-parenthesis n comma upper M right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper P left-parenthesis n comma upper M right-parenthesis](images/c03_1495.png) becomes

 <math alttext="1 minus e Superscript minus StartFraction q left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis Over 2 upper N EndFraction Baseline less-than-or-equal-to upper P left-parenthesis n comma upper M right-parenthesis period" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>q</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>N</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></msup><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![1 minus e Superscript minus StartFraction q left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis Over 2 upper N EndFraction Baseline less-than-or-equal-to upper P left-parenthesis n comma upper M right-parenthesis period](images/c03_1496.png)

The following property holds for any real number  <math alttext="x element-of left-bracket 0 comma 1 right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![x element-of left-bracket 0 comma 1 right-bracket](images/c03_1497.png):

 <math alttext="left-parenthesis 1 minus e Superscript negative 1 Baseline right-parenthesis asterisk x less-than-or-equal-to 1 minus e Superscript negative x Baseline less-than-or-equal-to x period" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>\*</mo><mi>x</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8804;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 1 minus e Superscript negative 1 Baseline right-parenthesis asterisk x less-than-or-equal-to 1 minus e Superscript negative x Baseline less-than-or-equal-to x period](images/c03_1498.png)

Finally, using the property above, the lower bound to  <math alttext="upper P left-parenthesis n comma upper M right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper P left-parenthesis n comma upper M right-parenthesis](images/c03_1499.png) can be approximated as:

 <math alttext="0.316 asterisk StartFraction q left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis Over upper N EndFraction less-than-or-equal-to upper P left-parenthesis n comma upper M right-parenthesis period" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0.316</mn><mo>\*</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>q</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![0.316 asterisk StartFraction q left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis Over upper N EndFraction less-than-or-equal-to upper P left-parenthesis n comma upper M right-parenthesis period](images/c03_1500.png)

### 3.5 Solutions to Exercises and Problems

***Exercise*** ***3.1***

Pro perties of Euler’s totient function are given by Theorem 3.1.

1.   <math alttext="upper N equals 17" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>17</mn></mrow></math> ![upper N equals 17](images/c03_1501.png) is a prime. Hence, all the 16 integers in range  <math alttext="left-bracket 1 comma 16 right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></math> ![left-bracket 1 comma 16 right-bracket](images/c03_1502.png) are coprime to 17.  <math alttext="17 i s p r i m e right double arrow phi left-parenthesis 17 right-parenthesis equals 17 minus 1 equals 16" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>17</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>i</mi><mi>s</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>m</mi><mi>e</mi><mo>&#8658;</mo><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>17</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>17</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow></math> ![17 i s p r i m e right double arrow phi left-parenthesis 17 right-parenthesis equals 17 minus 1 equals 16](images/c03_1503.png).
    
2.   <math alttext="upper N equals 42" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>42</mn></mrow></math> ![upper N equals 42](images/c03_1504.png):
    
    12 integers, which are coprime to 42, are:  <math alttext="1 comma 5 comma 11 comma 13 comma 17 comma 19 comma 23 comma 25 comma 29 comma 31 comma 37 comma 41" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>11</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>13</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>17</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>19</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>23</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>25</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>29</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>31</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>37</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>41</mn></mrow></math> ![1 comma 5 comma 11 comma 13 comma 17 comma 19 comma 23 comma 25 comma 29 comma 31 comma 37 comma 41](images/c03_1505.png).
    
     <math alttext="42 equals 7 asterisk 3 asterisk 2 right double arrow phi left-parenthesis 42 right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis 7 minus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis 3 minus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis 2 minus 1 right-parenthesis equals 12 period" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>42</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>&#8658;</mo><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>42</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> ![42 equals 7 asterisk 3 asterisk 2 right double arrow phi left-parenthesis 42 right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis 7 minus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis 3 minus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis 2 minus 1 right-parenthesis equals 12 period](images/c03_1506.png)
    
3.   <math alttext="upper N equals 25" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow></math> ![upper N equals 25](images/c03_1507.png):
    
    20 integers, which are coprime to 25, are:  <math alttext="1 comma 2 comma 3 comma 4 comma 6 comma 7 comma 8 comma 9 comma 11 comma 12 comma 13 comma 14 comma 16 comma 17 comma 18 comma 19 comma 21 comma 22 comma 23 comma 24" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>11</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>12</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>13</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>14</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>16</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>17</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>18</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>19</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>21</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>22</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>23</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>24</mn></mrow></math> ![1 comma 2 comma 3 comma 4 comma 6 comma 7 comma 8 comma 9 comma 11 comma 12 comma 13 comma 14 comma 16 comma 17 comma 18 comma 19 comma 21 comma 22 comma 23 comma 24](images/c03_1508.png)
    
     <math alttext="25 equals 5 squared right double arrow phi left-parenthesis 25 right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis 5 squared minus 5 right-parenthesis equals 20" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8658;</mo><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>25</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow></math> ![25 equals 5 squared right double arrow phi left-parenthesis 25 right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis 5 squared minus 5 right-parenthesis equals 20](images/c03_1509.png).
    

***Exercise*** ***3.2***

1.
