More generally,  <math alttext="a prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></math> ![a prime](images/c03_1510.png) is the additive inverse of *a* modulo *p* if  <math alttext="a prime plus a identical-to 0 m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>0</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![a prime plus a identical-to 0 m o d p](images/c03_1511.png) and  <math alttext="a Superscript negative 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![a Superscript negative 1](images/c03_1512.png) is the multiplicative inverse of *a* modulo *p* if  <math alttext="a asterisk a Superscript negative 1 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![a asterisk a Superscript negative 1 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d p](images/c03_1513.png). The additive inverse of 27 is 73, because if  <math alttext="27 plus 73 identical-to 0 m o d 100" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>27</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>73</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>0</mn><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>100</mn></mrow></math> ![27 plus 73 identical-to 0 m o d 100](images/c03_1514.png) and its multiplicative inverse is 63, because if  <math alttext="27 asterisk 63 equals 1701 identical-to 1 m o d p period" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>27</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>63</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1701</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> ![27 asterisk 63 equals 1701 identical-to 1 m o d p period](images/c03_1515.png)
2.  By properties of Euler’s phi function (Theorem 3.1): 
    *   101 is prime. Thus,  <math alttext="phi left-parenthesis 101 right-parenthesis equals 100" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>101</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow></math> ![phi left-parenthesis 101 right-parenthesis equals 100](images/c03_1516.png)
    *    <math alttext="102 equals 2 asterisk 3 asterisk 17" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>102</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>17</mn></mrow></math> ![102 equals 2 asterisk 3 asterisk 17](images/c03_1517.png). Thus,  <math alttext="phi left-parenthesis 102 right-parenthesis equals phi left-parenthesis 2 right-parenthesis asterisk phi left-parenthesis 3 right-parenthesis asterisk phi left-parenthesis 17 right-parenthesis equals 1 asterisk 2 asterisk 16 equals 32" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>102</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>17</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow></math> ![phi left-parenthesis 102 right-parenthesis equals phi left-parenthesis 2 right-parenthesis asterisk phi left-parenthesis 3 right-parenthesis asterisk phi left-parenthesis 17 right-parenthesis equals 1 asterisk 2 asterisk 16 equals 32](images/c03_1518.png)
    *    <math alttext="500 equals 2 squared asterisk 5 cubed" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>500</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>\*</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></math> ![500 equals 2 squared asterisk 5 cubed](images/c03_1519.png). Thus,  <math alttext="phi left-parenthesis 500 right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis 2 squared minus 2 Superscript 1 Baseline right-parenthesis left-parenthesis 5 cubed minus 5 squared right-parenthesis equals 200" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>500</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>1</mn></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>200</mn></mrow></math> ![phi left-parenthesis 500 right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis 2 squared minus 2 Superscript 1 Baseline right-parenthesis left-parenthesis 5 cubed minus 5 squared right-parenthesis equals 200](images/c03_1520.png).

***Exercise*** ***3.3***

1.  Find *x* such that  <math alttext="3 Superscript x Baseline identical-to 13 m o d 17" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>13</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>17</mn></mrow></math> ![3 Superscript x Baseline identical-to 13 m o d 17](images/c03_1521.png): we can use a trial-and-error method and find  <math alttext="x equals 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></math> ![x equals 4](images/c03_1522.png).
    
     <math alttext="3 Superscript 4 Baseline equals 81 equals 4 asterisk 17 plus 13 right double arrow 3 Superscript 4 Baseline 13 m o d 17" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>81</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>17</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>13</mn><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8658;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>13</mn><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>17</mn></mrow></math> ![3 Superscript 4 Baseline equals 81 equals 4 asterisk 17 plus 13 right double arrow 3 Superscript 4 Baseline 13 m o d 17](images/c03_1523.png)
2.  If  <math alttext="x less-than-or-equal-to 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8804;</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![x less-than-or-equal-to 5](images/c03_1524.png), there is no solution to  <math alttext="4 Superscript x Baseline identical-to 5 m o d 31" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>5</mn><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>31</mn></mrow></math> ![4 Superscript x Baseline identical-to 5 m o d 31](images/c03_1525.png), because  <math alttext="4 Superscript 1 Baseline comma 4 squared comma 4 cubed comma 4 Superscript 4 Baseline comma a n d 4 Superscript 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>1</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>a</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>5</mn></msup></mrow></math> ![4 Superscript 1 Baseline comma 4 squared comma 4 cubed comma 4 Superscript 4 Baseline comma a n d 4 Superscript 5](images/c03_1526.png) are not congruent to  <math alttext="5 m o d 31" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>5</mn><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>31</mn></mrow></math> ![5 m o d 31](images/c03_1527.png). In particular,  <math alttext="4 Superscript 5 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 31" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>31</mn></mrow></math> ![4 Superscript 5 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 31](images/c03_1528.png).
    
    If *x* is greater than 5, it can be written as  <math alttext="x equals 5 k plus x prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></mrow></math> ![x equals 5 k plus x prime](images/c03_1529.png), for some positive integer *k* and  <math alttext="x prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></math> ![x prime](images/c03_1530.png), an integer less than 5. Thus,
    
     <math alttext="4 Superscript x Baseline m o d 31 identical-to left-parenthesis 4 Superscript 5 Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript k Baseline left-parenthesis 4 right-parenthesis Superscript x prime Baseline m o d 31 identical-to left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis Superscript k Baseline left-parenthesis 4 right-parenthesis Superscript x prime Baseline m o d 31 identical-to 4 Superscript x prime Baseline m o d 31" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>31</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>5</mn></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>k</mi></msup><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>31</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>k</mi></msup><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>31</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mn>4</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>31</mn></mrow></math> ![4 Superscript x Baseline m o d 31 identical-to left-parenthesis 4 Superscript 5 Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript k Baseline left-parenthesis 4 right-parenthesis Superscript x prime Baseline m o d 31 identical-to left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis Superscript k Baseline left-parenthesis 4 right-parenthesis Superscript x prime Baseline m o d 31 identical-to 4 Superscript x prime Baseline m o d 31](images/c03_1531.png).
    
    Since  <math alttext="x prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![x prime](images/c03_1532.png) is less than 5,  <math alttext="4 Superscript x prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![4 Superscript x prime](images/c03_1533.png)  <math alttext="not-identical-to 5 m o d 31" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>&#8802;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>31</mn></mrow></math> ![not-identical-to 5 m o d 31](images/c03_1534.png). Therefore, there does not exist *x* such that  <math alttext="4 Superscript x Baseline identical-to 5 m o d 31" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>5</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>31</mn></mrow></math> ![4 Superscript x Baseline identical-to 5 m o d 31](images/c03_1535.png).
    
3.  In general, the modular exponentiation is an invertible function. It is what is called Discrete Logarithm Problem.

***Exercise*** ***3.4***

By definition of multiplicative inverse, *a* has an inverse modulo *n*, if and only if  <math alttext="GCD left-parenthesis a comma n right-parenthesis equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>GCD</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![GCD left-parenthesis a comma n right-parenthesis equals 1](images/c03_1536.png). Thus,  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 9 Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>9</mn><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 9 Superscript asterisk](images/c03_1537.png) has only six elements;  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 9 Superscript asterisk Baseline equals StartSet 1 comma 2 comma 4 comma 5 comma 7 comma 8 EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>9</mn><mo>\*</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>8</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 9 Superscript asterisk Baseline equals StartSet 1 comma 2 comma 4 comma 5 comma 7 comma 8 EndSet](images/c03_1538.png).

Euler’s theorem (Theorem 3.4 states that if  <math alttext="a element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript n Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![a element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript n Superscript asterisk](images/c03_1539.png), then  <math alttext="a Superscript phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis Baseline identical-to 1 m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![a Superscript phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis Baseline identical-to 1 m o d n](images/c03_1540.png), which can be written as  <math alttext="a asterisk a Superscript phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis minus 1 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![a asterisk a Superscript phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis minus 1 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d n](images/c03_1541.png). Using the definition of multiplicative inverse, we deduce that  <math alttext="a Superscript phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis minus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![a Superscript phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis minus 1](images/c03_1542.png) is the inverse of *a*.

By definition of Euler’s totient (Theorem 3.1),  <math alttext="phi left-parenthesis 9 right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis 3 cubed minus 3 right-parenthesis equals 6" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></math> ![phi left-parenthesis 9 right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis 3 cubed minus 3 right-parenthesis equals 6](images/c03_1543.png). Therefore, using Euler’s theorem, the inverses are computed and checked as follows:

   <math alttext="1 Superscript negative 1 Baseline identical-to 1 Superscript 5 Baseline m o d 9 identical-to 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mn>1</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![1 Superscript negative 1 Baseline identical-to 1 Superscript 5 Baseline m o d 9 identical-to 1](images/c03_1544.png). Check:  <math alttext="1 asterisk 1 identical-to 1 m o d 9" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn></mrow></math> ![1 asterisk 1 identical-to 1 m o d 9](images/c03_1545.png)

   <math alttext="2 Superscript negative 1 Baseline identical-to 2 Superscript 5 Baseline m o d 9 identical-to 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![2 Superscript negative 1 Baseline identical-to 2 Superscript 5 Baseline m o d 9 identical-to 5](images/c03_1546.png). Check:  <math alttext="2 asterisk 5 equals 10 identical-to 1 m o d 9" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn></mrow></math> ![2 asterisk 5 equals 10 identical-to 1 m o d 9](images/c03_1547.png)

   <math alttext="4 Superscript negative 1 Baseline identical-to 4 Superscript 5 Baseline m o d 9 identical-to 7" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></math> ![4 Superscript negative 1 Baseline identical-to 4 Superscript 5 Baseline m o d 9 identical-to 7](images/c03_1548.png). Check:  <math alttext="4 asterisk 7 equals 28 identical-to 1 m o d 9" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>28</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn></mrow></math> ![4 asterisk 7 equals 28 identical-to 1 m o d 9](images/c03_1549.png)

   <math alttext="5 Superscript negative 1 Baseline identical-to 5 Superscript 5 Baseline m o d 9 identical-to 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![5 Superscript negative 1 Baseline identical-to 5 Superscript 5 Baseline m o d 9 identical-to 2](images/c03_1550.png). Check:  <math alttext="5 asterisk 2 equals 10 identical-to 1 m o d 9" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn></mrow></math> ![5 asterisk 2 equals 10 identical-to 1 m o d 9](images/c03_1551.png)

   <math alttext="7 Superscript negative 1 Baseline identical-to 7 Superscript 5 Baseline m o d 9 identical-to 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>7</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mn>7</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></math> ![7 Superscript negative 1 Baseline identical-to 7 Superscript 5 Baseline m o d 9 identical-to 4](images/c03_1552.png). Check:  <math alttext="7 asterisk 4 equals 28 identical-to 1 m o d 9" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>28</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn></mrow></math> ![7 asterisk 4 equals 28 identical-to 1 m o d 9](images/c03_1553.png)

   <math alttext="8 Superscript negative 1 Baseline identical-to 8 Superscript 5 Baseline m o d 9 identical-to 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>8</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mn>8</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>8</mn></mrow></math> ![8 Superscript negative 1 Baseline identical-to 8 Superscript 5 Baseline m o d 9 identical-to 8](images/c03_1554.png). Check:  <math alttext="8 asterisk 8 equals 64 identical-to 1 m o d 9" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn></mrow></math> ![8 asterisk 8 equals 64 identical-to 1 m o d 9](images/c03_1555.png).

Let us try to find  <math alttext="3 Superscript negative 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![3 Superscript negative 1](images/c03_1556.png) using Euler’s theorem:

 <math alttext="3 Superscript negative 1 Baseline identical-to 3 Superscript 5 Baseline m o d 9 identical-to 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![3 Superscript negative 1 Baseline identical-to 3 Superscript 5 Baseline m o d 9 identical-to 0](images/c03_1557.png), which is incongruous, since 0 is not the inverse of any other integer. Therefore, Euler’s theorem is applicable only if *a* and *n* are coprime.

***Exercise*** ***3.5***

If  <math alttext="n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![n](images/c03_1558.png) is prime and  <math alttext="n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![n](images/c03_1559.png) and *a* are coprime, then Fermat’s little theorem states that  <math alttext="a Superscript n minus 1 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![a Superscript n minus 1 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d n](images/c03_1560.png), which can be rewritten as  <math alttext="a asterisk a Superscript n minus 2 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![a asterisk a Superscript n minus 2 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d n](images/c03_1561.png). Using the definition of inverse, we deduce that  <math alttext="a Superscript n minus 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![a Superscript n minus 2](images/c03_1562.png) is the inverse of *a*. Euler’s theorem states that if  <math alttext="a element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript n Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![a element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript n Superscript asterisk](images/c03_1563.png), then  <math alttext="a Superscript phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis Baseline identical-to 1 m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![a Superscript phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis Baseline identical-to 1 m o d n](images/c03_1564.png), which can be written as  <math alttext="a asterisk a Superscript phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis minus 1 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![a asterisk a Superscript phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis minus 1 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d n](images/c03_1565.png). Using the definition of inverse, we deduce that  <math alttext="a Superscript phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis minus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![a Superscript phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis minus 1](images/c03_1566.png) is the inverse of *a*.

1.   <math alttext="a equals 6" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></math> ![a equals 6](images/c03_1567.png),  <math alttext="n equals 7" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></math> ![n equals 7](images/c03_1568.png):
    
    7 is prime and coprime to 6. Thus, Fermat’s little theorem is applicable.
    
     <math alttext="6 Superscript negative 1 Baseline identical-to 6 Superscript 5 Baseline m o d 7 identical-to 6" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>6</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mn>6</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></math> ![6 Superscript negative 1 Baseline identical-to 6 Superscript 5 Baseline m o d 7 identical-to 6](images/c03_1569.png). Check:  <math alttext="6 asterisk 6 identical-to 1 m o d 7" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn></mrow></math> ![6 asterisk 6 identical-to 1 m o d 7](images/c03_1570.png).
    
2.   <math alttext="a equals 7" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></math> ![a equals 7](images/c03_1571.png),  <math alttext="n equals 15 colon" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>:</mo></mrow></math> ![n equals 15 colon](images/c03_1572.png)
    
    15 is not prime. Thus, Fermat’s little theorem is not applicable. We use Euler’s theorem.
    
    By Theorem 3.1,  <math alttext="phi left-parenthesis 15 right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis 5 minus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis 3 minus 1 right-parenthesis equals 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>15</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></math> ![phi left-parenthesis 15 right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis 5 minus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis 3 minus 1 right-parenthesis equals 8](images/c03_1573.png)
    
     <math alttext="7 Superscript negative 1 Baseline identical-to 7 Superscript 8 minus 1 Baseline m o d 15 identical-to 13" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>7</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mn>7</mn><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>15</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>13</mn></mrow></math> ![7 Superscript negative 1 Baseline identical-to 7 Superscript 8 minus 1 Baseline m o d 15 identical-to 13](images/c03_1574.png).
    
    Check:  <math alttext="7 asterisk 13 m o d 15 identical-to 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>13</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>15</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![7 asterisk 13 m o d 15 identical-to 1](images/c03_1575.png)
    
3.   <math alttext="a equals 19" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>19</mn></mrow></math> ![a equals 19](images/c03_1576.png),  <math alttext="n equals 101" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>101</mn></mrow></math> ![n equals 101](images/c03_1577.png):
    
    101 is prime and coprime to 19. Thus, Fermat’s little theorem is applicable.
    
     <math alttext="19 Superscript negative 1 Baseline identical-to 19 Superscript 99 Baseline m o d 101" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>19</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mrow><mn>19</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>99</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>101</mn></mrow></math> ![19 Superscript negative 1 Baseline identical-to 19 Superscript 99 Baseline m o d 101](images/c03_1578.png)
    
     <math alttext="19 Superscript negative 1 Baseline identical-to left-parenthesis 19 Superscript 3 asterisk 25 Baseline right-parenthesis left-parenthesis 19 Superscript 19 Baseline right-parenthesis left-parenthesis 19 Superscript 5 Baseline right-parenthesis m o d 10 identical-to 1 asterisk 5 asterisk 84 m o d 101 identical-to 16" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>19</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>19</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>19</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>19</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>19</mn></mrow><mn>5</mn></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>10</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>84</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>101</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>16</mn></mrow></math> ![19 Superscript negative 1 Baseline identical-to left-parenthesis 19 Superscript 3 asterisk 25 Baseline right-parenthesis left-parenthesis 19 Superscript 19 Baseline right-parenthesis left-parenthesis 19 Superscript 5 Baseline right-parenthesis m o d 10 identical-to 1 asterisk 5 asterisk 84 m o d 101 identical-to 16](images/c03_1579.png)
    
    Check:  <math alttext="19 asterisk 16 m o d 101 identical-to 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>19</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>16</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>101</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![19 asterisk 16 m o d 101 identical-to 1](images/c03_1580.png)
    
4.   <math alttext="a equals 97" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>97</mn></mrow></math> ![a equals 97](images/c03_1581.png),  <math alttext="n equals 100 colon" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>:</mo></mrow></math> ![n equals 100 colon](images/c03_1582.png)
    
    100 is not prime. Thus, Fermat’s little theorem is not applicable. We use Euler’s theorem.
    
    By theorem 3.1,  <math alttext="phi left-parenthesis 100 right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis 25 minus 5 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis 4 minus 2 right-parenthesis equals 40" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>100</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>40</mn></mrow></math> ![phi left-parenthesis 100 right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis 25 minus 5 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis 4 minus 2 right-parenthesis equals 40](images/c03_1583.png)
    
     <math alttext="97 Superscript negative 1 Baseline identical-to 97 Superscript 39 Baseline m o d 100 identical-to left-parenthesis 97 Superscript 20 Baseline asterisk 97 Superscript 19 Baseline right-parenthesis m o d 100 identical-to 33" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>97</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mn>97</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>39</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>100</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>97</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>20</mn></mrow></msup><mo>\*</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mrow><mn>97</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>19</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>100</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>33</mn></mrow></math> ![97 Superscript negative 1 Baseline identical-to 97 Superscript 39 Baseline m o d 100 identical-to left-parenthesis 97 Superscript 20 Baseline asterisk 97 Superscript 19 Baseline right-parenthesis m o d 100 identical-to 33](images/c03_1584.png).
    
    Check:  <math alttext="97 asterisk 33 m o d 100 identical-to 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>97</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>33</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>100</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![97 asterisk 33 m o d 100 identical-to 1](images/c03_1585.png)
    

***Exercise*** ***3.6***

1.   <math alttext="x identical-to 4 Superscript 100 Baseline m o d 17" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mn>4</mn><mrow><mn>100</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>17</mn></mrow></math> ![x identical-to 4 Superscript 100 Baseline m o d 17](images/c03_1586.png)
    
     <math alttext="4 squared identical-to negative 1 mod 17" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;mod&#160;</mtext><mn>17</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![4 squared identical-to negative 1 mod 17](images/c03_1587.png)
    
    Thus,  <math alttext="4 Superscript 100 Baseline identical-to m o d 17 identical-to 4 Superscript 2 asterisk 50 Baseline m o d 17 identical-to left-parenthesis negative 1 right-parenthesis Superscript 50 Baseline m o d 17 identical-to 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mrow><mn>100</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>17</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mn>4</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>17</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>50</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>17</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![4 Superscript 100 Baseline identical-to m o d 17 identical-to 4 Superscript 2 asterisk 50 Baseline m o d 17 identical-to left-parenthesis negative 1 right-parenthesis Superscript 50 Baseline m o d 17 identical-to 1](images/c03_1588.png).
    
    Therefore,  <math alttext="x equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![x equals 1](images/c03_1589.png).
    
2.   <math alttext="9 Superscript x Baseline identical-to 13 m o d 17" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>9</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>13</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>17</mn></mrow></math> ![9 Superscript x Baseline identical-to 13 m o d 17](images/c03_1590.png)
    
     <math alttext="9 squared identical-to 13 m o d 17" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>9</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>13</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>17</mn></mrow></math> ![9 squared identical-to 13 m o d 17](images/c03_1591.png). Therefore,  <math alttext="x equals 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![x equals 2](images/c03_1592.png)
    
3.   <math alttext="5 Superscript x Baseline identical-to 13 m o d 17" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>13</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>17</mn></mrow></math> ![5 Superscript x Baseline identical-to 13 m o d 17](images/c03_1593.png)
    
     <math alttext="5 squared identical-to 8 m o d 17" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>8</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>17</mn></mrow></math> ![5 squared identical-to 8 m o d 17](images/c03_1594.png)
    
     <math alttext="left-parenthesis 5 squared right-parenthesis asterisk left-parenthesis 5 squared right-parenthesis identical-to 8 asterisk 8 m o d 17 equals 13" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>8</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>8</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>17</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>13</mn></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 5 squared right-parenthesis asterisk left-parenthesis 5 squared right-parenthesis identical-to 8 asterisk 8 m o d 17 equals 13](images/c03_1595.png). Therefore,  <math alttext="x equals 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></math> ![x equals 4](images/c03_1596.png)
    
4.   <math alttext="7 Superscript x Baseline identical-to 11 m o d 13" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>7</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>11</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>13</mn></mrow></math> ![7 Superscript x Baseline identical-to 11 m o d 13](images/c03_1597.png)
    
     <math alttext="left-parenthesis 7 squared right-parenthesis asterisk left-parenthesis 7 squared right-parenthesis asterisk left-parenthesis 7 Superscript 1 Baseline right-parenthesis identical-to 10 asterisk 10 asterisk 7 m o d 13 equals 9 asterisk 7 m o d 13 equals 11" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mn>7</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mn>7</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mn>7</mn><mn>1</mn></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>7</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>13</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>7</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>13</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>11</mn></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 7 squared right-parenthesis asterisk left-parenthesis 7 squared right-parenthesis asterisk left-parenthesis 7 Superscript 1 Baseline right-parenthesis identical-to 10 asterisk 10 asterisk 7 m o d 13 equals 9 asterisk 7 m o d 13 equals 11](images/c03_1598.png).
    
    Therefore,  <math alttext="x equals 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![x equals 5](images/c03_1599.png).
    

***Exercise*** ***3.7***

By definition, the order of a group is the number of the group elements.

1.   <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 7 Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>7</mn><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 7 Superscript asterisk](images/c03_1600.png): 7 is prime. Thus,  <math alttext="StartAbsoluteValue double-struck upper Z 7 Superscript asterisk Baseline EndAbsoluteValue equals 7" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>7</mn><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></math> ![StartAbsoluteValue double-struck upper Z 7 Superscript asterisk Baseline EndAbsoluteValue equals 7](images/c03_1601.png).
2.   <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 101 Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mrow><mn>101</mn></mrow><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 101 Superscript asterisk](images/c03_1602.png): 101 is prime. Thus,  <math alttext="StartAbsoluteValue double-struck upper Z 101 Superscript asterisk Baseline EndAbsoluteValue equals 101" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mrow><mn>101</mn></mrow><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>101</mn></mrow></math> ![StartAbsoluteValue double-struck upper Z 101 Superscript asterisk Baseline EndAbsoluteValue equals 101](images/c03_1603.png).
3.   <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 18 Superscript asterisk Baseline colon 18" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mrow><mn>18</mn></mrow><mo>\*</mo></msubsup><mo>:</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>18</mn></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 18 Superscript asterisk Baseline colon 18](images/c03_1604.png) is not prime. Thus, we need to identify the invertible elements that belong to  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 18 Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mrow><mn>18</mn></mrow><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 18 Superscript asterisk](images/c03_1605.png). In general, an integer  <math alttext="a element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript n Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![a element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript n Superscript asterisk](images/c03_1606.png), if and only if  <math alttext="normal upper G normal upper C normal upper D left-parenthesis a comma n right-parenthesis equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">G</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![normal upper G normal upper C normal upper D left-parenthesis a comma n right-parenthesis equals 1](images/c03_1607.png). Thus,  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 18 Superscript asterisk Baseline equals StartSet 1 comma 5 comma 7 comma 11 comma 13 comma 17 EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mrow><mn>18</mn></mrow><mo>\*</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>11</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>13</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>17</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 18 Superscript asterisk Baseline equals StartSet 1 comma 5 comma 7 comma 11 comma 13 comma 17 EndSet](images/c03_1608.png) and  <math alttext="StartAbsoluteValue double-struck upper Z 18 Superscript asterisk Baseline EndAbsoluteValue equals 6" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mrow><mn>18</mn></mrow><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></math> ![StartAbsoluteValue double-struck upper Z 18 Superscript asterisk Baseline EndAbsoluteValue equals 6](images/c03_1609.png).

***Exercise*** ***3.8***

1.  By definition, the order of an element  <math alttext="a element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript n Superscript asterisk Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![a element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript n Superscript asterisk Baseline](images/c03_1610.png) is the smallest integer *k* such that  <math alttext="a Superscript k Baseline identical-to 1 m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![a Superscript k Baseline identical-to 1 m o d n](images/c03_1611.png).
2.   <math alttext="2 Superscript 12 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 13" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>12</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>13</mn></mrow></math> ![2 Superscript 12 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 13](images/c03_1612.png). Thus,  <math alttext="o r d left-parenthesis 2 right-parenthesis equals 12" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>o</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow></math> ![o r d left-parenthesis 2 right-parenthesis equals 12](images/c03_1613.png).
3.   <math alttext="5 Superscript 4 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 13" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>13</mn></mrow></math> ![5 Superscript 4 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 13](images/c03_1614.png). Thus,  <math alttext="o r d left-parenthesis 5 right-parenthesis equals 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>o</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></math> ![o r d left-parenthesis 5 right-parenthesis equals 4](images/c03_1615.png).
4.   <math alttext="3 cubed identical-to 1 m o d 13" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>13</mn></mrow></math> ![3 cubed identical-to 1 m o d 13](images/c03_1616.png). Thus,  <math alttext="o r d left-parenthesis 3 right-parenthesis equals 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>o</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> ![o r d left-parenthesis 3 right-parenthesis equals 3](images/c03_1617.png).

***Exercise*** ***3.9***

1.  Calculate  <math alttext="two-fifths" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mrow></math> ![two-fifths](images/c03_1618.png) in  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 8 Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>8</mn><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 8 Superscript asterisk](images/c03_1619.png)
    
     <math alttext="two-fifths equals 2 asterisk 5 Superscript negative 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![two-fifths equals 2 asterisk 5 Superscript negative 1](images/c03_1620.png)
    
     <math alttext="5 asterisk 5 identical-to 1 m o d 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>8</mn></mrow></math> ![5 asterisk 5 identical-to 1 m o d 8](images/c03_1621.png); hence,  <math alttext="5 Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mn>5</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![5 Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 5](images/c03_1622.png)
    
    Hence,  <math alttext="two-fifths equals 2 asterisk 5 equals 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![two-fifths equals 2 asterisk 5 equals 2](images/c03_1623.png) in  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 8 Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>8</mn><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 8 Superscript asterisk](images/c03_1624.png).
    
2.  Is  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 6 Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>6</mn><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 6 Superscript asterisk](images/c03_1625.png) a cyclic group?
    
    Recall that an integer *b* has a multiplicative inverse  <math alttext="m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![m o d p](images/c03_1626.png) if and only if  <math alttext="normal upper G normal upper C normal upper D left-parenthesis b comma p right-parenthesis equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">G</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![normal upper G normal upper C normal upper D left-parenthesis b comma p right-parenthesis equals 1](images/c03_1627.png). Thus,  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 6 Superscript asterisk Baseline equals StartSet 1 comma 5 EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>6</mn><mo>\*</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 6 Superscript asterisk Baseline equals StartSet 1 comma 5 EndSet](images/c03_1628.png).
    
    Recall that a cyclic group is a finite group that is generated by a single element *g*, called generator.
    
     <math alttext="5 Superscript 0 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 6" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>0</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>6</mn></mrow></math> ![5 Superscript 0 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 6](images/c03_1629.png),   <math alttext="5 Superscript 1 Baseline identical-to 5 m o d 6" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>1</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>5</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>6</mn></mrow></math> ![5 Superscript 1 Baseline identical-to 5 m o d 6](images/c03_1630.png).
    
    Hence, 5 is a generator for  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 6 Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>6</mn><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 6 Superscript asterisk](images/c03_1631.png). Therefore,  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 6 Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>6</mn><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 6 Superscript asterisk](images/c03_1632.png) is a cyclic group.
    
3.  Is  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 8 Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>8</mn><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 8 Superscript asterisk](images/c03_1633.png) a cyclic group?
    
     <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 8 Superscript asterisk Baseline equals StartSet 1 comma 3 comma 5 comma 7 EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>8</mn><mo>\*</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 8 Superscript asterisk Baseline equals StartSet 1 comma 3 comma 5 comma 7 EndSet](images/c03_1634.png)
    
     <math alttext="3 Superscript 0 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>0</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>8</mn></mrow></math> ![3 Superscript 0 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 8](images/c03_1635.png),   <math alttext="3 Superscript 1 Baseline identical-to 3 m o d 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>1</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>3</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>8</mn></mrow></math> ![3 Superscript 1 Baseline identical-to 3 m o d 8](images/c03_1636.png)   <math alttext="3 squared identical-to 1 m o d 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>8</mn></mrow></math> ![3 squared identical-to 1 m o d 8](images/c03_1637.png)   <math alttext="3 cubed identical-to 3 m o d 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>3</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>8</mn></mrow></math> ![3 cubed identical-to 3 m o d 8](images/c03_1638.png) …
    
     <math alttext="5 Superscript 0 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>0</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>8</mn></mrow></math> ![5 Superscript 0 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 8](images/c03_1639.png),   <math alttext="5 Superscript 1 Baseline identical-to 5 m o d 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>1</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>5</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>8</mn></mrow></math> ![5 Superscript 1 Baseline identical-to 5 m o d 8](images/c03_1640.png)   <math alttext="5 squared identical-to 1 m o d 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>8</mn></mrow></math> ![5 squared identical-to 1 m o d 8](images/c03_1641.png)   <math alttext="5 cubed identical-to 5 m o d 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>5</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>8</mn></mrow></math> ![5 cubed identical-to 5 m o d 8](images/c03_1642.png) …
    
     <math alttext="7 Superscript 0 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>7</mn><mn>0</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>8</mn></mrow></math> ![7 Superscript 0 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 8](images/c03_1643.png),   <math alttext="7 Superscript 1 Baseline identical-to 7 m o d 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>7</mn><mn>1</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>7</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>8</mn></mrow></math> ![7 Superscript 1 Baseline identical-to 7 m o d 8](images/c03_1644.png)   <math alttext="7 squared identical-to 1 m o d 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>7</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>8</mn></mrow></math> ![7 squared identical-to 1 m o d 8](images/c03_1645.png)   <math alttext="7 cubed identical-to 7 m o d 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>7</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>7</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>8</mn></mrow></math> ![7 cubed identical-to 7 m o d 8](images/c03_1646.png) …
    
    No element in  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 8 Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>8</mn><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 8 Superscript asterisk](images/c03_1647.png) can generate  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 8 Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>8</mn><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 8 Superscript asterisk](images/c03_1648.png). Therefore,  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 8 Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>8</mn><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 8 Superscript asterisk](images/c03_1649.png) is not a cyclic group.
    

***Exercise*** ***3.10***

 <math alttext="99 Superscript 707 Super Superscript 411 Superscript Baseline m o d 100 equals left-parenthesis 100 minus 1 right-parenthesis Superscript 707 Super Superscript 411 Superscript Baseline m o d 100" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>99</mn></mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>707</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>411</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>100</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>707</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>411</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>100</mn></mrow></math> ![99 Superscript 707 Super Superscript 411 Superscript Baseline m o d 100 equals left-parenthesis 100 minus 1 right-parenthesis Superscript 707 Super Superscript 411 Superscript Baseline m o d 100](images/c03_1650.png)

By Lemma 3.1, for integers *a*, *m*, and *n*,  <math alttext="a Superscript m Baseline m o d n equals left-parenthesis a m o d n right-parenthesis Superscript m Baseline m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mi>m</mi></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![a Superscript m Baseline m o d n equals left-parenthesis a m o d n right-parenthesis Superscript m Baseline m o d n](images/c03_1651.png).

Thus,  <math alttext="4 Superscript 100 Baseline identical-to m o d 17 identical-to 4 Superscript 2 asterisk 50 Baseline m o d 17 identical-to left-parenthesis negative 1 right-parenthesis Superscript 50 Baseline m o d 17 identical-to 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mrow><mn>100</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>17</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mn>4</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>17</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>50</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>17</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![4 Superscript 100 Baseline identical-to m o d 17 identical-to 4 Superscript 2 asterisk 50 Baseline m o d 17 identical-to left-parenthesis negative 1 right-parenthesis Superscript 50 Baseline m o d 17 identical-to 1](images/c03_1652.png)

The exponent  <math alttext="707 Superscript 411" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>707</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>411</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![707 Superscript 411](images/c03_1653.png) is odd. Thus, there exists *k* such that  <math alttext="707 Superscript 411 Baseline equals 2 k plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>707</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>411</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![707 Superscript 411 Baseline equals 2 k plus 1](images/c03_1654.png).

 <math alttext="99 Superscript 707 Super Superscript 411 Superscript Baseline m o d 100 equals left-parenthesis negative 1 right-parenthesis Superscript 2 k Baseline asterisk left-parenthesis negative 1 right-parenthesis m o d 100 equals 99" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>99</mn></mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>707</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>411</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>100</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>100</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>99</mn></mrow></math> ![99 Superscript 707 Super Superscript 411 Superscript Baseline m o d 100 equals left-parenthesis negative 1 right-parenthesis Superscript 2 k Baseline asterisk left-parenthesis negative 1 right-parenthesis m o d 100 equals 99](images/c03_1655.png).

***Exercise*** ***3.11***

More generally (by Theorem 3.9), if  <math alttext="4 Superscript 100 Baseline identical-to m o d 17 identical-to 4 Superscript 2 asterisk 50 Baseline m o d 17 identical-to left-parenthesis negative 1 right-parenthesis Superscript 50 Baseline m o d 17 identical-to 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mrow><mn>100</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>17</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mn>4</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>17</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>50</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>17</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![4 Superscript 100 Baseline identical-to m o d 17 identical-to 4 Superscript 2 asterisk 50 Baseline m o d 17 identical-to left-parenthesis negative 1 right-parenthesis Superscript 50 Baseline m o d 17 identical-to 1](images/c03_1656.png) is a prime number, then  <math alttext="upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>Z</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk](images/c03_1657.png) has  <math alttext="phi left-parenthesis phi left-parenthesis p right-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#966;</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>&#966;</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![phi left-parenthesis phi left-parenthesis p right-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c03_1658.png) generators (also called primitive roots), where  <math alttext="phi left-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#966;</mi><mo>(</mo><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![phi left-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c03_1659.png) is the Euler’s totient function.

By Theorem 3.1, since 29 is prime,  <math alttext="phi left-parenthesis 29 right-parenthesis equals 28" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#981;</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>29</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>28</mn></mrow></math> ![phi left-parenthesis 29 right-parenthesis equals 28](images/c03_1660.png). Integers between 1 and 28, which are coprime with 28, are  <math alttext="StartSet 1 comma 3 comma 5 comma 9 comma 11 comma 13 comma 15 comma 17 comma 19 comma 23 comma 25 comma 27 EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>11</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>13</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>15</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>17</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>19</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>23</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>25</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>27</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></math> ![StartSet 1 comma 3 comma 5 comma 9 comma 11 comma 13 comma 15 comma 17 comma 19 comma 23 comma 25 comma 27 EndSet](images/c03_1661.png). Thus,  <math alttext="phi left-parenthesis 28 right-parenthesis equals 12" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#981;</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>28</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow></math> ![phi left-parenthesis 28 right-parenthesis equals 12](images/c03_1662.png). Therefore, by Theorem 3.9,  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 29 Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mrow><mn>29</mn></mrow><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 29 Superscript asterisk](images/c03_1663.png) has 12 generators.

***Exercise*** ***3.12***

In general, to build the multiplication table of a finite field  <math alttext="upper F Subscript p Sub Superscript m" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript p Sub Superscript m](images/c03_1664.png) with an irreducible polynomial  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c03_1665.png):

1.  associate with each element  <math alttext="i element-of upper F Subscript p Sub Superscript m Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![i element-of upper F Subscript p Sub Superscript m Baseline](images/c03_1666.png) a polynomial  <math alttext="upper P Subscript i Baseline left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![upper P Subscript i Baseline left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c03_1667.png) of degree *m* and with coefficients in *F[p]*.
2.  compute  <math alttext="upper R Subscript i comma j Baseline left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis identical-to left-parenthesis upper P Subscript i Baseline left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis asterisk upper P Subscript j Baseline left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis right-parenthesis m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8801;</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper R Subscript i comma j Baseline left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis identical-to left-parenthesis upper P Subscript i Baseline left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis asterisk upper P Subscript j Baseline left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis right-parenthesis m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c03_1668.png) for all pairs of elements *i* and *j* in  <math alttext="upper F Subscript p Superscript m" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>m</mi></msubsup></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript p Superscript m](images/c03_1669.png).
3.  Let  <math alttext="i asterisk j equals sigma-summation Underscript k equals 0 Overscript m Endscripts left-parenthesis p Superscript k Baseline asterisk r Subscript i comma j comma k Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msubsup><mo>&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><mo>\*</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></mstyle></mrow></math> ![i asterisk j equals sigma-summation Underscript k equals 0 Overscript m Endscripts left-parenthesis p Superscript k Baseline asterisk r Subscript i comma j comma k Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c03_1670.png) be the multiplication table of 8 rows by 8 columns.  <math alttext="r Subscript i comma j comma k" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![r Subscript i comma j comma k](images/c03_1671.png)  <math alttext="k equals 0 comma ellipsis m comma" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo></mrow></math> ![k equals 0 comma ellipsis m comma](images/c03_1672.png), are the binary coefficients of the polynomial  <math alttext="upper R Subscript i comma j Baseline left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper R Subscript i comma j Baseline left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c03_1673.png).

Now, build the multiplication table of field  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 cubed" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 cubed](images/c03_1674.png) with the irreducible polynomial  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x cubed plus x squared plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x cubed plus x squared plus 1](images/c03_1675.png):

 <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 cubed Baseline equals StartSet 0 comma 1 comma 2 comma 3 comma 4 comma 5 comma 6 comma 7 EndSet period" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 cubed Baseline equals StartSet 0 comma 1 comma 2 comma 3 comma 4 comma 5 comma 6 comma 7 EndSet period](images/c03_1676.png)

Polynomial representation of field elements:

 <math alttext="upper P 0 left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![upper P 0 left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals 0](images/c03_1677.png)         <math alttext="upper P 1 left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![upper P 1 left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals 1](images/c03_1678.png)      <math alttext="upper P 2 left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> ![upper P 2 left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x](images/c03_1679.png)   <math alttext="upper P 3 left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![upper P 3 left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x plus 1](images/c03_1680.png)    <math alttext="upper P 4 left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x squared" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math> ![upper P 4 left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x squared](images/c03_1681.png)

 <math alttext="upper P 5 left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x squared plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>5</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![upper P 5 left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x squared plus 1](images/c03_1682.png)     <math alttext="upper P 6 left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x squared plus x" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> ![upper P 6 left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x squared plus x](images/c03_1683.png)   <math alttext="upper P 7 left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x squared plus x plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>7</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![upper P 7 left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x squared plus x plus 1](images/c03_1684.png)

 <math alttext="upper P Subscript i Baseline left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper P Subscript i Baseline left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c03_1685.png) denotes the polynomial associated with element *i* of  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 cubed" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 cubed](images/c03_1686.png).

Recall that the multiplication is commutative in finite fields.
