    By Lemma 3.1:
    
     <math alttext="113 Superscript 72 000 000 000 013 Baseline m o d 5 identical-to left-parenthesis 3 right-parenthesis Superscript 72 000 000 000 013 Baseline m o d 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>113</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>72</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>013</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>72</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>013</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![113 Superscript 72 000 000 000 013 Baseline m o d 5 identical-to left-parenthesis 3 right-parenthesis Superscript 72 000 000 000 013 Baseline m o d 5](images/c03_1994.png)
    
     <math alttext="identical-to left-parenthesis 3 Superscript 1 Baseline right-parenthesis asterisk left-parenthesis 3 Superscript 4 Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript StartFraction 72 000 000 000 012 Over 4 EndFraction Baseline m o d 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>1</mn></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>72</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>012</mn></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![identical-to left-parenthesis 3 Superscript 1 Baseline right-parenthesis asterisk left-parenthesis 3 Superscript 4 Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript StartFraction 72 000 000 000 012 Over 4 EndFraction Baseline m o d 5](images/c03_1995.png)
    
     <math alttext="identical-to 3 asterisk left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis Superscript StartFraction 72 000 000 000 012 Over 4 EndFraction Baseline m o d 5 equals 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>3</mn><mo>\*</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>72</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>012</mn></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![identical-to 3 asterisk left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis Superscript StartFraction 72 000 000 000 012 Over 4 EndFraction Baseline m o d 5 equals 3](images/c03_1996.png) (because  <math alttext="3 Superscript 4 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![3 Superscript 4 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 5](images/c03_1997.png))
    
*    <math alttext="113 identical-to 1 m o d 7" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>113</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn></mrow></math> ![113 identical-to 1 m o d 7](images/c03_1998.png).
    
    By Lemma 3.1:
    
     <math alttext="113 Superscript 72 000 000 000 013 Baseline m o d 7 identical-to left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis Superscript 72 000 000 000 013 Baseline m o d 7 equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>113</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>72</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>013</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>72</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>013</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![113 Superscript 72 000 000 000 013 Baseline m o d 7 identical-to left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis Superscript 72 000 000 000 013 Baseline m o d 7 equals 1](images/c03_1999.png).
    
*   Thus, we have the following congruences:
    
     <math alttext="113 Superscript 72 000 000 000 013 Baseline identical-to 2 m o d 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>113</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>72</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>013</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>2</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>3</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![113 Superscript 72 000 000 000 013 Baseline identical-to 2 m o d 3](images/c03_2000.png)
    
     <math alttext="113 Superscript 72 000 000 000 013 Baseline identical-to 3 m o d 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>113</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>72</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>013</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>3</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![113 Superscript 72 000 000 000 013 Baseline identical-to 3 m o d 5](images/c03_2001.png)
    
     <math alttext="113 Superscript 72 000 000 000 013 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 7" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>113</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>72</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>013</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![113 Superscript 72 000 000 000 013 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 7](images/c03_2002.png).
    
    There exist two positive integers *k* and  <math alttext="x less-than 105" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mn>105</mn></mrow></math> ![x less-than 105](images/c03_2003.png), such that  <math alttext="113 Superscript 72 000 000 000 013 Baseline equals k asterisk 105 plus x" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>113</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>72</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>013</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>\*</mo><mn>105</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> ![113 Superscript 72 000 000 000 013 Baseline equals k asterisk 105 plus x](images/c03_2004.png). Thus, from the congruences above, we derive the following congruence equation system:
    
     <math alttext="upper S equals left-brace StartLayout 1st Row x identical-to 2 m o d 3 2nd Row x identical-to 3 m o d 5 3rd Row x identical-to 1 m o d 7 EndLayout" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtable columnalign="left"><mtr columnalign="left"><mtd columnalign="left"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>2</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>3</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr columnalign="left"><mtd columnalign="left"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>3</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr columnalign="left"><mtd columnalign="left"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper S equals left-brace StartLayout 1st Row x identical-to 2 m o d 3 2nd Row x identical-to 3 m o d 5 3rd Row x identical-to 1 m o d 7 EndLayout](images/c03_2005.png)
    
    The constant of the congruence system above are:  <math alttext="n 1 equals 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> ![n 1 equals 3](images/c03_2006.png),  <math alttext="n 2 equals 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![n 2 equals 5](images/c03_2007.png),  <math alttext="n 3 equals 7" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></math> ![n 3 equals 7](images/c03_2008.png),  <math alttext="a 1 equals 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![a 1 equals 2](images/c03_2009.png),  <math alttext="a 2 equals 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> ![a 2 equals 3](images/c03_2010.png), and  <math alttext="a 3 equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![a 3 equals 1](images/c03_2011.png). All moduli are pairwise coprime and  <math alttext="a Subscript i Baseline less-than n Subscript i" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>&#60;</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![a Subscript i Baseline less-than n Subscript i](images/c03_2012.png), for  <math alttext="i equals 1 comma 2 comma 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> ![i equals 1 comma 2 comma 3](images/c03_2013.png). Therefore, the conditions to use the Chinese remainder theorem are met. Hence, according to the CRT there exists a unique value of  <math alttext="x m o d 3 asterisk 5 asterisk 7" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>3</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></math> ![x m o d 3 asterisk 5 asterisk 7](images/c03_2014.png) that satisfies the three congruences. The solution to the congruence equation system is as follows:
    
     <math alttext="upper N identical-to 3 asterisk 5 asterisk 7 equals 105" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>105</mn></mrow></math> ![upper N identical-to 3 asterisk 5 asterisk 7 equals 105](images/c03_2015.png)
    
     <math alttext="upper N 1 equals 5 asterisk 7 equals 35" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>35</mn></mrow></math> ![upper N 1 equals 5 asterisk 7 equals 35](images/c03_2016.png)   <math alttext="upper N 2 equals 3 asterisk 7 equals 21" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>21</mn></mrow></math> ![upper N 2 equals 3 asterisk 7 equals 21](images/c03_2017.png)   <math alttext="upper N 3 equals 3 asterisk 5 equals 15" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow></math> ![upper N 3 equals 3 asterisk 5 equals 15](images/c03_2018.png)
    
     <math alttext="upper N 1 Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![upper N 1 Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 2](images/c03_2019.png)       <math alttext="upper N 2 Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![upper N 2 Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 1](images/c03_2020.png)         <math alttext="upper N 3 Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mn>3</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![upper N 3 Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 1](images/c03_2021.png)
    
     <math alttext="x equals left-parenthesis left-parenthesis 2 asterisk 35 asterisk 2 right-parenthesis plus left-parenthesis 3 asterisk 21 asterisk 1 right-parenthesis plus left-parenthesis 1 asterisk 15 asterisk 1 right-parenthesis right-parenthesis m o d 105 equals 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>35</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>21</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>105</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></math> ![x equals left-parenthesis left-parenthesis 2 asterisk 35 asterisk 2 right-parenthesis plus left-parenthesis 3 asterisk 21 asterisk 1 right-parenthesis plus left-parenthesis 1 asterisk 15 asterisk 1 right-parenthesis right-parenthesis m o d 105 equals 8](images/c03_2022.png).
    

***Exercise*** ***3.27***

1.  First, use the Euler’s criterion (Theorem 3.7) to test if  <math alttext="37 m o d 43" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>37</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>43</mn></mrow></math> ![37 m o d 43](images/c03_2023.png) has a solution.
    
     <math alttext="37 Superscript left-parenthesis 43 minus 1 right-parenthesis slash 2 Baseline identical-to 42 m o d 43 equals negative 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>37</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>43</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>42</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>43</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![37 Superscript left-parenthesis 43 minus 1 right-parenthesis slash 2 Baseline identical-to 42 m o d 43 equals negative 1](images/c03_2024.png). Therefore, no solution exists.
    
2.  First, use the Euler’s criterion to test if  <math alttext="36 m o d 43" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>36</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>43</mn></mrow></math> ![36 m o d 43](images/c03_2025.png) has a solution.
    
     <math alttext="36 Superscript left-parenthesis 43 minus 1 right-parenthesis slash 2 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 43" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>36</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>43</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>43</mn></mrow></math> ![36 Superscript left-parenthesis 43 minus 1 right-parenthesis slash 2 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 43](images/c03_2026.png). Thus, two solutions exist.
    
    The steps of Tonelli-Shanks algorithm are as follows:
    
     <math alttext="43 equals 2 Superscript 1 Baseline asterisk 21 plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>43</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>1</mn></msup><mo>\*</mo><mn>21</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![43 equals 2 Superscript 1 Baseline asterisk 21 plus 1](images/c03_2027.png). Thus,  <math alttext="s equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![s equals 1](images/c03_2028.png) and  <math alttext="q equals 21" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>21</mn></mrow></math> ![q equals 21](images/c03_2029.png).
    
    Find a square nonresidue modulo  <math alttext="43 period u equals 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>43.</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![43 period u equals 2](images/c03_2030.png) is a square nonresidue.
    
    Initialization:  <math alttext="m equals 1 semicolon c equals 2 Superscript 21 Baseline m o d 43 equals 42 semicolon t equals 36 Superscript 21 Baseline m o d 43 equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>21</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>43</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>42</mn><mo>;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mn>36</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>21</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>43</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![m equals 1 semicolon c equals 2 Superscript 21 Baseline m o d 43 equals 42 semicolon t equals 36 Superscript 21 Baseline m o d 43 equals 1](images/c03_2031.png)
    
            <math alttext="upper R equals 36 Superscript left-parenthesis 21 plus 1 right-parenthesis slash 2 Baseline m o d 43 equals 6 period" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mn>36</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>21</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>43</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> ![upper R equals 36 Superscript left-parenthesis 21 plus 1 right-parenthesis slash 2 Baseline m o d 43 equals 6 period](images/c03_2032.png)
    
    Loop: the algorithm stops at the first iteration, because  <math alttext="t equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![t equals 1](images/c03_2033.png), and returns  <math alttext="r equals 6" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></math> ![r equals 6](images/c03_2034.png).
    
    Check:  <math alttext="left-parenthesis plus-or-minus 6 right-parenthesis squared identical-to 36 m o d 43" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>&#177;</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>36</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>43</mn></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis plus-or-minus 6 right-parenthesis squared identical-to 36 m o d 43](images/c03_2035.png).
    
3.  First, use the Euler’s criterion to test if  <math alttext="53 m o d 97" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>53</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>97</mn></mrow></math> ![53 m o d 97](images/c03_2036.png) has a solution.
    
     <math alttext="53 Superscript left-parenthesis 97 minus 1 right-parenthesis slash 2 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 97" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>53</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>97</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>97</mn></mrow></math> ![53 Superscript left-parenthesis 97 minus 1 right-parenthesis slash 2 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 97](images/c03_2037.png). Thus, two solutions exist.
    
    The steps of Tonelli-Shanks algorithm are as follows:
    
     <math alttext="97 equals 2 Superscript 5 Baseline asterisk 3 plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>97</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><mo>\*</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![97 equals 2 Superscript 5 Baseline asterisk 3 plus 1](images/c03_2038.png). Thus,  <math alttext="s equals 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![s equals 5](images/c03_2039.png) and  <math alttext="q equals 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> ![q equals 3](images/c03_2040.png).
    
    Find a square nonresidue modulo  <math alttext="97 colon u equals 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>97</mn><mo>:</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![97 colon u equals 5](images/c03_2041.png) is a square nonresidue.
    
    Initialization:  <math alttext="m equals 5 semicolon c equals 5 cubed m o d 97 equals 28 semicolon t equals 53 cubed m o d 97 equals 79" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>97</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>28</mn><mo>;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mn>53</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>97</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>79</mn></mrow></math> ![m equals 5 semicolon c equals 5 cubed m o d 97 equals 28 semicolon t equals 53 cubed m o d 97 equals 79](images/c03_2042.png)
    
           <math alttext="upper R equals 53 Superscript left-parenthesis 3 plus 1 right-parenthesis slash 2 Baseline m o d 97 equals 93 period" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mn>53</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>97</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>93</mn><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> ![upper R equals 53 Superscript left-parenthesis 3 plus 1 right-parenthesis slash 2 Baseline m o d 97 equals 93 period](images/c03_2043.png)
    
    Loop:
    
    ![](images/c03_2044.png)
    
    Check:  <math alttext="left-parenthesis plus-or-minus 76 right-parenthesis squared equals 53 m o d 97" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>&#177;</mo><mn>76</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>53</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>97</mn></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis plus-or-minus 76 right-parenthesis squared equals 53 m o d 97](images/c03_2064.png).
    

***Exercise*** ***3.28***

Find the solution(s) to  <math alttext="y squared identical-to 3 m o d 143" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>3</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>143</mn></mrow></math> ![y squared identical-to 3 m o d 143](images/c03_2065.png).

143 has two prime factors 13 and 11.

Step 1: Find the square roots of prime moduli.

  From congruence  <math alttext="3 m o d 143" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>3</mn><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>143</mn></mrow></math> ![3 m o d 143](images/c03_2066.png), two congruences are derived using Lemma 3.1:

   <math alttext="3 m o d 11" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>3</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>11</mn></mrow></math> ![3 m o d 11](images/c03_2067.png) and  <math alttext="3 m o d 13" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>3</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>13</mn></mrow></math> ![3 m o d 13](images/c03_2068.png).

   <math alttext="3 m o d 11" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>3</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>11</mn></mrow></math> ![3 m o d 11](images/c03_2069.png) has two square roots:  <math alttext="r 1 equals 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![r 1 equals 5](images/c03_2070.png) and  <math alttext="minus r 1 equals 6" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></math> ![minus r 1 equals 6](images/c03_2071.png)

   <math alttext="3 m o d 13" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>3</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>13</mn></mrow></math> ![3 m o d 13](images/c03_2072.png) has two square roots:  <math alttext="r 2 equals 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></math> ![r 2 equals 4](images/c03_2073.png) and  <math alttext="minus r 2 equals 9" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></math> ![minus r 2 equals 9](images/c03_2074.png).

Step 2: Solve a set of congruence systems.

  Build a set of  <math alttext="2 squared" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math> ![2 squared](images/c03_2075.png) distinct congruence systems denoted  <math alttext="upper S 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper S 1](images/c03_2076.png),  <math alttext="upper S 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper S 2](images/c03_2077.png),  <math alttext="upper S 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper S 3](images/c03_2078.png), and  <math alttext="upper S 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper S 4](images/c03_2079.png) as follows:

   <math alttext="upper S 1 colon equals StartLayout Enlarged left-brace 1st Row x identical-to 5 m o d 11 2nd Row x identical-to 4 m o d 13 EndLayout" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>:</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mtable><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>5</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>11</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>4</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>13</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper S 1 colon equals StartLayout Enlarged left-brace 1st Row x identical-to 5 m o d 11 2nd Row x identical-to 4 m o d 13 EndLayout](images/c03_2080.png)   <math alttext="upper S 2 colon equals StartLayout Enlarged left-brace 1st Row x identical-to 5 m o d 11 2nd Row x identical-to 9 m o d 13 EndLayout" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>:</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mtable><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>5</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>11</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>9</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>13</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper S 2 colon equals StartLayout Enlarged left-brace 1st Row x identical-to 5 m o d 11 2nd Row x identical-to 9 m o d 13 EndLayout](images/c03_2081.png)

   <math alttext="upper S 3 colon equals StartLayout Enlarged left-brace 1st Row x identical-to 6 m o d 11 2nd Row x identical-to 4 m o d 13 EndLayout" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>:</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mtable><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>6</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>11</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>4</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>13</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper S 3 colon equals StartLayout Enlarged left-brace 1st Row x identical-to 6 m o d 11 2nd Row x identical-to 4 m o d 13 EndLayout](images/c03_2082.png)   <math alttext="upper S 4 colon equals StartLayout Enlarged left-brace 1st Row x identical-to 6 m o d 11 2nd Row x identical-to 9 m o d 13 EndLayout" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>:</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mtable><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>6</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>11</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>9</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>13</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper S 4 colon equals StartLayout Enlarged left-brace 1st Row x identical-to 6 m o d 11 2nd Row x identical-to 9 m o d 13 EndLayout](images/c03_2083.png).

  Use Gauss’s algorithm to find the solutions to each of the four congruence systems. Below, only the calculations to solve  <math alttext="upper S 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper S 1](images/c03_2084.png) are included.

The constants of congruence equation system  <math alttext="upper S 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper S 1](images/c03_2085.png) are:  <math alttext="n 1 equals 11" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>11</mn></mrow></math> ![n 1 equals 11](images/c03_2086.png),  <math alttext="n 2 equals 13" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>13</mn></mrow></math> ![n 2 equals 13](images/c03_2087.png),  <math alttext="a 1 equals 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![a 1 equals 5](images/c03_2088.png),  <math alttext="a 2 equals 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></math> ![a 2 equals 4](images/c03_2089.png).

Common modulus is  <math alttext="upper N equals 11 asterisk 13 equals 143" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>13</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>143</mn></mrow></math> ![upper N equals 11 asterisk 13 equals 143](images/c03_2090.png).

 <math alttext="upper N 1 equals StartFraction 11 asterisk 13 Over 11 EndFraction equals 13" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>11</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>13</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>11</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>13</mn></mrow></math> ![upper N 1 equals StartFraction 11 asterisk 13 Over 11 EndFraction equals 13](images/c03_2091.png),  <math alttext="upper N 2 equals StartFraction 11 asterisk 13 Over 13 EndFraction equals 11" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>11</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>13</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>13</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>11</mn></mrow></math> ![upper N 2 equals StartFraction 11 asterisk 13 Over 13 EndFraction equals 11](images/c03_2092.png).

Multiplicative inverses:  <math alttext="upper N 1 Superscript negative 1 Baseline asterisk upper N 1 identical-to 1 m o d 11 right double arrow upper N 1 Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 6" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>\*</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>11</mn><mo>&#8658;</mo><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></math> ![upper N 1 Superscript negative 1 Baseline asterisk upper N 1 identical-to 1 m o d 11 right double arrow upper N 1 Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 6](images/c03_2093.png)

 <math alttext="upper N 2 Superscript negative 1 Baseline asterisk upper N 2 identical-to 1 m o d 13 right double arrow upper N 2 Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 6" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>\*</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>13</mn><mo>&#8658;</mo><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></math> ![upper N 2 Superscript negative 1 Baseline asterisk upper N 2 identical-to 1 m o d 13 right double arrow upper N 2 Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 6](images/c03_2094.png)

 <math alttext="x equals left-parenthesis left-parenthesis 5 asterisk 13 asterisk 6 right-parenthesis plus left-parenthesis 4 asterisk 11 asterisk 6 right-parenthesis right-parenthesis m o d 143 equals 82" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>13</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>143</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>82</mn></mrow></math> ![x equals left-parenthesis left-parenthesis 5 asterisk 13 asterisk 6 right-parenthesis plus left-parenthesis 4 asterisk 11 asterisk 6 right-parenthesis right-parenthesis m o d 143 equals 82](images/c03_2095.png).

Applying Gauss’s algorithm to the four congruence systems yields the following:

  <math alttext="x equals 82" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>82</mn></mrow></math> ![x equals 82](images/c03_2096.png) is a solution to <math alttext="upper S 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper S 1](images/c03_2097.png)

  <math alttext="x equals 126" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>126</mn></mrow></math> ![x equals 126](images/c03_2098.png) is a solution to  <math alttext="upper S 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper S 2](images/c03_2099.png)

  <math alttext="x equals 17" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>17</mn></mrow></math> ![x equals 17](images/c03_2100.png) is a solution to  <math alttext="upper S 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper S 3](images/c03_2101.png)

  <math alttext="x equals 61" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>61</mn></mrow></math> ![x equals 61](images/c03_2102.png) is a solution to  <math alttext="upper S 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper S 4](images/c03_2103.png).

Now, check that the four values are square roots of  <math alttext="3 m o d 143" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>3</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>143</mn></mrow></math> ![3 m o d 143](images/c03_2104.png)

  <math alttext="x equals 82 colon" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>82</mn><mo>:</mo></mrow></math> ![x equals 82 colon](images/c03_2105.png)  <math alttext="82 squared equals 6724 identical-to 3 m o d 143" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>82</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>6724</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>3</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>143</mn></mrow></math> ![82 squared equals 6724 identical-to 3 m o d 143](images/c03_2106.png)

  <math alttext="x equals 126 colon" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>126</mn><mo>:</mo></mrow></math> ![x equals 126 colon](images/c03_2107.png)  <math alttext="126 squared equals 15876 identical-to 3 m o d 143" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>126</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>15876</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>3</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>143</mn></mrow></math> ![126 squared equals 15876 identical-to 3 m o d 143](images/c03_2108.png)

  <math alttext="x equals 17 colon" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>17</mn><mo>:</mo></mrow></math> ![x equals 17 colon](images/c03_2109.png)  <math alttext="17 squared equals 289 identical-to 3 m o d 143" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>17</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>289</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>3</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>143</mn></mrow></math> ![17 squared equals 289 identical-to 3 m o d 143](images/c03_2110.png)

  <math alttext="x equals 61 colon" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>61</mn><mo>:</mo></mrow></math> ![x equals 61 colon](images/c03_2111.png)  <math alttext="61 squared equals 2304 identical-to 3 m o d 143" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>61</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>2304</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>3</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>143</mn></mrow></math> ![61 squared equals 2304 identical-to 3 m o d 143](images/c03_2112.png).

Thus,  <math alttext="3 m o d 143" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>3</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>143</mn></mrow></math> ![3 m o d 143](images/c03_2113.png) has four square roots.

***Exercise*** ***3.29***

Find the solution(s) to  <math alttext="y squared identical-to 421 m o d 693" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>421</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>693</mn></mrow></math> ![y squared identical-to 421 m o d 693](images/c03_2114.png).

Since  <math alttext="693 equals 7 asterisk 9 asterisk 11" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>693</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>11</mn></mrow></math> ![693 equals 7 asterisk 9 asterisk 11](images/c03_2115.png) is a product of three primes, there should exist  <math alttext="2 cubed" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></math> ![2 cubed](images/c03_2116.png) square roots. Procedure to find the square roots in case of multiple primes is composed of two steps:

*   *Step 1*: *Find the square roots of prime factors*.
    
    By Lemma 3.2:
    
     <math alttext="x identical-to 421 m o d 693 left-brace StartLayout 1st Row x identical-to 421 m o d 7 right double arrow x identical-to 1 m o d 7 2nd Row x identical-to 421 m o d 9 right double arrow x identical-to 7 m o d 9 3rd Row x identical-to 421 m o d 11 right double arrow x identical-to 3 m o d 11 EndLayout" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>421</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>693</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtable><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>421</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn><mo>&#8658;</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>421</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn><mo>&#8658;</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>7</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>421</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>11</mn><mo>&#8658;</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>3</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>11</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow></mrow></math> ![x identical-to 421 m o d 693 left-brace StartLayout 1st Row x identical-to 421 m o d 7 right double arrow x identical-to 1 m o d 7 2nd Row x identical-to 421 m o d 9 right double arrow x identical-to 7 m o d 9 3rd Row x identical-to 421 m o d 11 right double arrow x identical-to 3 m o d 11 EndLayout](images/c03_2117.png)
    
    *Find square roots for each of the three congruences above*:
    
     <math alttext="1 m o d 7" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn></mrow></math> ![1 m o d 7](images/c03_2118.png) has two square roots: <math alttext="r 1 equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![r 1 equals 1](images/c03_2119.png) and  <math alttext="minus r 1 equals 6" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></math> ![minus r 1 equals 6](images/c03_2120.png).
    
     <math alttext="7 m o d 9" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>7</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn></mrow></math> ![7 m o d 9](images/c03_2121.png) has two square roots:  <math alttext="r 2 equals 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></math> ![r 2 equals 4](images/c03_2122.png) and  <math alttext="minus r 2 equals 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![minus r 2 equals 5](images/c03_2123.png).
    
     <math alttext="3 m o d 11" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>3</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>11</mn></mrow></math> ![3 m o d 11](images/c03_2124.png) has two square roots:  <math alttext="r 3 equals 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![r 3 equals 5](images/c03_2125.png) and  <math alttext="minus r 3 equals 6" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></math> ![minus r 3 equals 6](images/c03_2126.png).
    
*   *Step 2*: *Find solutions to congruence systems*.

From the squares roots of the primes factoring 693, eight congruence systems are derived:

Gauss’s algorithm is used to find solutions to the eight congruence systems. Below are calculations to solve  <math alttext="upper S 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper S 1](images/c03_2135.png) system:

The constants of the congruence equation system are  <math alttext="n 1 equals 7 comma n 2 equals 9 comma n 3 equals 11 comma a 1 equals 1 comma a 2 equals 4 comma a 2 equals 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![n 1 equals 7 comma n 2 equals 9 comma n 3 equals 11 comma a 1 equals 1 comma a 2 equals 4 comma a 2 equals 5](images/c03_2136.png).

Common modulus is  <math alttext="upper N equals 7 asterisk 9 asterisk 11" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>11</mn></mrow></math> ![upper N equals 7 asterisk 9 asterisk 11](images/c03_2137.png)

 <math alttext="upper N 1 equals StartFraction 7 asterisk 9 asterisk 11 Over 7 EndFraction equals 99 comma upper N 2 equals StartFraction 7 asterisk 9 asterisk 11 Over 9 EndFraction equals 77 comma upper N 3 equals StartFraction 7 asterisk 9 asterisk 11 Over 11 EndFraction equals 63 period" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>11</mn></mrow><mn>7</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>11</mn></mrow><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>77</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>11</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>11</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>63</mn><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> ![upper N 1 equals StartFraction 7 asterisk 9 asterisk 11 Over 7 EndFraction equals 99 comma upper N 2 equals StartFraction 7 asterisk 9 asterisk 11 Over 9 EndFraction equals 77 comma upper N 3 equals StartFraction 7 asterisk 9 asterisk 11 Over 11 EndFraction equals 63 period](images/c03_2138.png)

Multiplicative inverses:

Finally, notice that

 <math alttext="negative 148 m o d 693 equals 545" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>148</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>693</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>545</mn></mrow></math> ![negative 148 m o d 693 equals 545](images/c03_2176.png)   <math alttext="negative 545 m o d 693 equals 148" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>545</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>693</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>148</mn></mrow></math> ![negative 545 m o d 693 equals 148](images/c03_2177.png)

 <math alttext="negative 589 m o d 693 equals 104" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>589</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>693</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>104</mn></mrow></math> ![negative 589 m o d 693 equals 104](images/c03_2178.png)   <math alttext="negative 104 m o d 693 equals 589" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>104</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>693</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>589</mn></mrow></math> ![negative 104 m o d 693 equals 589](images/c03_2179.png)

 <math alttext="negative 50 m o d 693 equals 643" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>50</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>693</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>643</mn></mrow></math> ![negative 50 m o d 693 equals 643](images/c03_2182.png)    <math alttext="negative 643 m o d 693 equals 50" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>643</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>693</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow></math> ![negative 643 m o d 693 equals 50](images/c03_2183.png).

Thus,  <math alttext="421 m o d 693" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>421</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>693</mn></mrow></math> ![421 m o d 693](images/c03_2184.png) has exactly eight square roots: four roots and their negatives.

***Exercise*** ***3.30***

Note that to do computations with large numbers, a tool implementing the polynomial extended Euclidean algorithm is required.

In the following,  <math alttext="minus a x m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>x</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![minus a x m o d p](images/c03_2185.png) is replaced by  <math alttext="left-parenthesis p minus a right-parenthesis x m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo><mi>x</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis p minus a right-parenthesis x m o d p](images/c03_2186.png).

Check the irreducibility of  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 10 Baseline plus x cubed plus 1 over upper F 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;over&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 10 Baseline plus x cubed plus 1 over upper F 2](images/c03_2187.png).

Degree of  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c03_2188.png) is  <math alttext="m equals 10" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></math> ![m equals 10](images/c03_2189.png). The prime dividers of 10 are 5 and 2.

 <math alttext="p 1 equals StartFraction 10 Over 5 EndFraction equals 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![p 1 equals StartFraction 10 Over 5 EndFraction equals 2](images/c03_2190.png),  <math alttext="p 2 equals StartFraction 10 Over 2 EndFraction equals 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![p 2 equals StartFraction 10 Over 2 EndFraction equals 5](images/c03_2191.png).

*Iteration #1 (test of prime divider 5, i.e*.  <math alttext="p 1 equals 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![p 1 equals 2](images/c03_2192.png)*)*:

 <math alttext="x Superscript 2 squared Baseline identical-to x Superscript 4 Baseline m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![x Superscript 2 squared Baseline identical-to x Superscript 4 Baseline m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c03_2193.png)

 <math alttext="h left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 4 Baseline minus x m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>x</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> ![h left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 4 Baseline minus x m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x](images/c03_2194.png)

 <math alttext="g left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals GCD left-parenthesis f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis comma h left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis right-parenthesis equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mtext>GCD</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![g left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals GCD left-parenthesis f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis comma h left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis right-parenthesis equals 1](images/c03_2195.png)  <math alttext="g left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![g left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals 1](images/c03_2196.png); hence, the algorithm continues.

*Iteration #2 (test of prime divider 2, i.e*.  <math alttext="p 2 equals 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![p 2 equals 5](images/c03_2197.png)*)*:

*Second step of the algorithm*

 <math alttext="g left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 2 Super Superscript 10 Superscript Baseline minus x m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>x</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![g left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 2 Super Superscript 10 Superscript Baseline minus x m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals 0](images/c03_2202.png).

Thus,  <math alttext="x Superscript 10 Baseline plus x cubed plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![x Superscript 10 Baseline plus x cubed plus 1](images/c03_2203.png) is irreducible over  <math alttext="upper F 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F 2](images/c03_2204.png).

***Exercise*** ***3.31***

Note that to do computations with large numbers, a tool implementing the polynomial extended Euclidean algorithm is required.

In the following,  <math alttext="minus a x m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>x</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![minus a x m o d p](images/c03_2205.png) is replaced by  <math alttext="left-parenthesis p minus a right-parenthesis x m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo><mi>x</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis p minus a right-parenthesis x m o d p](images/c03_2206.png).

Let  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 5 Baseline plus x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x cubed plus x squared plus x minus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>5</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 5 Baseline plus x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x cubed plus x squared plus x minus 1](images/c03_2207.png).

First, notice that, over  <math alttext="upper F 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F 3](images/c03_2208.png),  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis 0 right-parenthesis equals 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis 0 right-parenthesis equals 2](images/c03_2209.png),  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis equals 1](images/c03_2210.png), and  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis 2 right-parenthesis equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis 2 right-parenthesis equals 1](images/c03_2211.png). Hence,  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c03_2212.png) has no roots in  <math alttext="upper F 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F 3](images/c03_2213.png). Since  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c03_2214.png) is of degree 5, we cannot conclude that  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c03_2215.png) is irreducible. Thus, let us check  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c03_2216.png) irreducibility using Rabin’s test.

The given polynomial is of degree 5. Thus, only one prime divider is to be considered.

 <math alttext="p 1 equals five-fifths equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![p 1 equals five-fifths equals 1](images/c03_2217.png).

*Iteration #1 (test of prime divider 5, i.e*.  <math alttext="p 1 equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![p 1 equals 1](images/c03_2218.png)*)*:

 <math alttext="x Superscript 3 Super Superscript 1 Superscript Baseline equals x cubed identical-to x cubed m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>1</mn></msup></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![x Superscript 3 Super Superscript 1 Superscript Baseline equals x cubed identical-to x cubed m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c03_2219.png)

 <math alttext="h left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x cubed minus x m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x cubed plus 2 x m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>x</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![h left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x cubed minus x m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x cubed plus 2 x m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c03_2220.png)

 <math alttext="GCD left-parenthesis f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis comma h left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>GCD</mtext><mo>(</mo><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![GCD left-parenthesis f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis comma h left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals 1](images/c03_2221.png).

Hence, the algorithm continues.

*Second step of the algorithm*

 <math alttext="g left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 3 Super Superscript 5 Superscript Baseline minus x m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals 2 x squared plus 2 x plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>5</mn></msup></mrow></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>x</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![g left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 3 Super Superscript 5 Superscript Baseline minus x m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals 2 x squared plus 2 x plus 1](images/c03_2222.png)

Thus,  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 5 Baseline plus x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x cubed plus x squared plus x minus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>5</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 5 Baseline plus x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x cubed plus x squared plus x minus 1](images/c03_2223.png) is irreducible over  <math alttext="upper F 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F 3](images/c03_2224.png).

Indeed,  <math alttext="x Superscript 5 Baseline plus x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x cubed plus x squared plus x plus 2 equals left-parenthesis x squared plus 2 x plus 2 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis x cubed plus 2 x squared plus x plus 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>5</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![x Superscript 5 Baseline plus x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x cubed plus x squared plus x plus 2 equals left-parenthesis x squared plus 2 x plus 2 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis x cubed plus 2 x squared plus x plus 1 right-parenthesis](images/c03_2225.png).

***Problem*** ***3.1*** (Proof of Lemma 3.1)

Lemma 3.1 states that if *a*, *n*, and *k* are positive integers, then  <math alttext="a Superscript k Baseline m o d n identical-to left-parenthesis a m o d n right-parenthesis Superscript k Baseline m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![a Superscript k Baseline m o d n identical-to left-parenthesis a m o d n right-parenthesis Superscript k Baseline m o d n](images/c03_2226.png).

By definition, for any integers *a* and *b*:  <math alttext="a asterisk b m o d n identical-to left-parenthesis a m o d n right-parenthesis asterisk left-parenthesis b m o d n right-parenthesis m o d n period" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>b</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> ![a asterisk b m o d n identical-to left-parenthesis a m o d n right-parenthesis asterisk left-parenthesis b m o d n right-parenthesis m o d n period](images/c03_2227.png)

Thus,  <math alttext="a asterisk a m o d n identical-to left-parenthesis a m o d n right-parenthesis squared m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>a</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![a asterisk a m o d n identical-to left-parenthesis a m o d n right-parenthesis squared m o d n](images/c03_2228.png).

Then,  <math alttext="a asterisk a asterisk a m o d n identical-to left-parenthesis a m o d n right-parenthesis cubed m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>a</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![a asterisk a asterisk a m o d n identical-to left-parenthesis a m o d n right-parenthesis cubed m o d n](images/c03_2229.png), which may be generalized to  <math alttext="a Superscript k Baseline m o d n identical-to left-parenthesis a m o d n right-parenthesis Superscript k Baseline m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![a Superscript k Baseline m o d n identical-to left-parenthesis a m o d n right-parenthesis Superscript k Baseline m o d n](images/c03_2230.png) for any integer  <math alttext="k ampersand gt semicolon 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>&#38;gt;</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![k ampersand gt semicolon 2](images/c03_2231.png).

***Problem*** ***3.2*** (Proof of Lemma 3.2)

Let  <math alttext="upper N Subscript i Baseline equals StartFraction u asterisk upper N Over n Subscript i Baseline EndFraction" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> ![upper N Subscript i Baseline equals StartFraction u asterisk upper N Over n Subscript i Baseline EndFraction](images/c03_2234.png), for  <math alttext="1 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than-or-equal-to k" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></math> ![1 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than-or-equal-to k](images/c03_2235.png).  <math alttext="upper N Subscript i" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![upper N Subscript i](images/c03_2236.png) is an integer because  <math alttext="n Subscript i" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![n Subscript i](images/c03_2237.png) is a factor of *N*.

*x* can be expressed as  <math alttext="x equals a plus upper N Subscript i Baseline asterisk n Subscript i" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>\*</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![x equals a plus upper N Subscript i Baseline asterisk n Subscript i](images/c03_2238.png), for  <math alttext="1 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than-or-equal-to k" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></math> ![1 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than-or-equal-to k](images/c03_2239.png).

 <math alttext="a plus upper N Subscript i Baseline asterisk n Subscript i Baseline identical-to a m o d n Subscript i Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>\*</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>a</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![a plus upper N Subscript i Baseline asterisk n Subscript i Baseline identical-to a m o d n Subscript i Baseline](images/c03_2240.png) ⇒  <math alttext="x identical-to a m o d n Subscript i Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>a</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![x identical-to a m o d n Subscript i Baseline](images/c03_2241.png) for  <math alttext="1 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than-or-equal-to k" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></math> ![1 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than-or-equal-to k](images/c03_2242.png).

***Problem*** ***3.3*** **(***Proof of Lemma* 3.3)

By definition,  <math alttext="phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis](images/c03_2243.png) is the number of elements of ℤ[n], which are coprime with *n*. By Theorem 3.3, all the  <math alttext="phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis](images/c03_2244.png) elements have multiplicative inverse  <math alttext="m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![m o d n](images/c03_2245.png). Therefore, they are elements of  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript n Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript n Superscript asterisk](images/c03_2246.png). Hence,  <math alttext="StartAbsoluteValue double-struck upper Z Subscript n Superscript asterisk Baseline EndAbsoluteValue equals phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![StartAbsoluteValue double-struck upper Z Subscript n Superscript asterisk Baseline EndAbsoluteValue equals phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis](images/c03_2247.png).
