***Problem*** ***3.4***

1.  By definition of multiplicative inverse, given two elements *x* and  <math alttext="x prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![x prime](images/c03_2248.png) of  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk](images/c03_2249.png), if  <math alttext="x prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![x prime](images/c03_2250.png) is a multiplicative inverse of *x*, then  <math alttext="x asterisk x prime identical-to 1 m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>'</mo><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![x asterisk x prime identical-to 1 m o d p](images/c03_2251.png).
    
    Let *a* be an even integer less than *p*. There exists a positive integer *m* such that  <math alttext="a equals 2 m" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></mrow></math> ![a equals 2 m](images/c03_2252.png).  <math alttext="a prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></math> ![a prime](images/c03_2253.png), the multiplicative inverse of *a*, does not exist because the condition  <math alttext="a asterisk a Superscript prime Baseline identical-to 1 m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![a asterisk a Superscript prime Baseline identical-to 1 m o d p](images/c03_2254.png) cannot be satisfied, if *p* is even, which is proven as follows:
    
    If  <math alttext="a prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></math> ![a prime](images/c03_2255.png) was the multiplicative inverse of *a*, then:
    
     <math alttext="a asterisk a Superscript prime Baseline identical-to 1 m o d p right double arrow there-exists k vertical-bar 2 m asterisk a Superscript prime Baseline equals k asterisk p plus 1 period" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8658;</mo><mo>&#8707;</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>&#124;</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1.</mn></mrow></math> ![a asterisk a Superscript prime Baseline identical-to 1 m o d p right double arrow there-exists k vertical-bar 2 m asterisk a Superscript prime Baseline equals k asterisk p plus 1 period](images/c03_2256.png)(a) 
    
    Since *p* is even, there exists *q* such that  <math alttext="p equals 2 q" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> ![p equals 2 q](images/c03_2257.png).
    
    Statement (a) becomes:
    
     <math alttext="a asterisk a Superscript prime Baseline identical-to 1 m o d p right double arrow there-exists k vertical-bar 2 m asterisk a Superscript prime Baseline equals k asterisk 2 q plus 1" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8658;</mo><mo>&#8707;</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>&#124;</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>\*</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>q</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![a asterisk a Superscript prime Baseline identical-to 1 m o d p right double arrow there-exists k vertical-bar 2 m asterisk a Superscript prime Baseline equals k asterisk 2 q plus 1](images/c03_2258.png) <math alttext="2 left-parenthesis m asterisk a prime right-parenthesis equals 2 left-parenthesis k asterisk q right-parenthesis plus 1 period" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1.</mn></mrow></math> ![2 left-parenthesis m asterisk a prime right-parenthesis equals 2 left-parenthesis k asterisk q right-parenthesis plus 1 period](images/c03_2259.png)(b) 
    
    Statement (b) cannot hold because the left side of equality is even while the right one is odd. Thus, no even integer is an element of  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk](images/c03_2260.png) if *p* is even.
    
2.   <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript 2 Sub Superscript m Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript 2 Sub Superscript m Superscript asterisk](images/c03_2261.png) means  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk](images/c03_2262.png) with  <math alttext="p equals 2 Superscript m" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow></math> ![p equals 2 Superscript m](images/c03_2263.png). Since *p* is even,  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk](images/c03_2264.png) does not include any even elements, because their multiplicative inverses do not exist in  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript 2 Sub Superscript m Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript 2 Sub Superscript m Superscript asterisk](images/c03_2265.png). Thus,  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript 2 Sub Superscript m Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript 2 Sub Superscript m Superscript asterisk](images/c03_2266.png) includes only odd elements. Hence, its cardinality can be at most  <math alttext="StartFraction 2 Superscript m Baseline Over 2 EndFraction equals 2 Superscript m minus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![StartFraction 2 Superscript m Baseline Over 2 EndFraction equals 2 Superscript m minus 1](images/c03_2267.png).

 Thus, five (i.e.  <math alttext="StartFraction 11 minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>11</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></math> ![StartFraction 11 minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction](images/c03_2281.png)) of elements in  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 11 Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mrow><mn>11</mn></mrow><mtext>\*</mtext></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 11 Superscript asterisk](images/c03_2282.png) are square residues and five elements are square nonresidues.

***Problem*** ***3.6*** (Proof of Lemma 3.4)

 <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk Baseline equals StartSet 1 comma 2 comma ellipsis comma p minus 1 EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk Baseline equals StartSet 1 comma 2 comma ellipsis comma p minus 1 EndSet](images/c03_2283.png).

Since *p* is a prime greater than 2, the number of elements of  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk](images/c03_2284.png) is even.

By definition of  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk](images/c03_2285.png), if  <math alttext="negative a element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![negative a element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk](images/c03_2286.png), then  <math alttext="negative a element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![negative a element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk](images/c03_2287.png) (i.e. any element and its additive inverse are elements of  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk](images/c03_2288.png)). Any element of  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk](images/c03_2289.png) has one and only one additive inverse.

 <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk Baseline equals StartSet 1 comma 2 comma ellipsis comma p minus 1 EndSet equals StartSet 1 comma 2 comma ellipsis comma StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction comma StartFraction p plus 1 Over 2 EndFraction comma ellipsis comma p minus 2 comma p minus 1 EndSet period" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>}</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk Baseline equals StartSet 1 comma 2 comma ellipsis comma p minus 1 EndSet equals StartSet 1 comma 2 comma ellipsis comma StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction comma StartFraction p plus 1 Over 2 EndFraction comma ellipsis comma p minus 2 comma p minus 1 EndSet period](images/c03_2290.png)

By definition of the additive inverse (or negative):

 <math alttext="negative 1 equals p minus 1 m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![negative 1 equals p minus 1 m o d p](images/c03_2291.png),    <math alttext="negative 2 equals p minus 2 m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![negative 2 equals p minus 2 m o d p](images/c03_2292.png), …, <math alttext="minus StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction equals p minus StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction m o d p equals StartFraction p plus 1 Over 2 EndFraction" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></math> ![minus StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction equals p minus StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction m o d p equals StartFraction p plus 1 Over 2 EndFraction](images/c03_2293.png)

Thus,  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk Baseline equals StartSet 1 comma 2 comma ellipsis comma p minus 1 EndSet equals StartSet 1 comma 2 comma ellipsis comma StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction comma minus StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction comma ellipsis comma negative 2 comma negative 1 EndSet period" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>}</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk Baseline equals StartSet 1 comma 2 comma ellipsis comma p minus 1 EndSet equals StartSet 1 comma 2 comma ellipsis comma StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction comma minus StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction comma ellipsis comma negative 2 comma negative 1 EndSet period](images/c03_2294.png)

right-parenthesis squared" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis minus StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction right-parenthesis squared](images/c03_2301.png). Since  <math alttext="for-all a element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk Baseline comma a squared equals left-parenthesis negative a right-parenthesis squared" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8704;</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math> ![for-all a element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk Baseline comma a squared equals left-parenthesis negative a right-parenthesis squared](images/c03_2302.png), there exist  <math alttext="StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></math> ![StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction](images/c03_2303.png) distinct squares. It is easy to prove that if *a* and *b* are two distinct elements in  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk](images/c03_2304.png), with  <math alttext="b not-equals negative a" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>&#8800;</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></math> ![b not-equals negative a](images/c03_2305.png), then  <math alttext="a squared m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![a squared m o d p](images/c03_2306.png) and  <math alttext="b squared m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![b squared m o d p](images/c03_2307.png) are two distinct elements. By definition, an element  <math alttext="a element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![a element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk](images/c03_2308.png) is a quadratic residue if there exists  <math alttext="y element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![y element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk](images/c03_2309.png) such that  <math alttext="y squared identical-to a m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>a</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![y squared identical-to a m o d p](images/c03_2310.png). Since there are exactly  <math alttext="StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></math> ![StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction](images/c03_2311.png) distinct squares in  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk](images/c03_2312.png), the number of square residues is  <math alttext="StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></math> ![StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction](images/c03_2313.png). Hence, the remaining  <math alttext="StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></math> ![StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction](images/c03_2314.png) elements are square nonresidues.

***Problem*** ***3.7*** *(Proof of Lemma* 3.5)

Since *a* is a quadratic residue of *p*, we know by Euler’s criterion (Theorem 3.7) that  <math alttext="a Superscript StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction Baseline identical-to 1 m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![a Superscript StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction Baseline identical-to 1 m o d p](images/c03_2315.png). Thus, if  <math alttext="r equals a Superscript StartFraction p plus 1 Over 4 EndFraction" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![r equals a Superscript StartFraction p plus 1 Over 4 EndFraction](images/c03_2316.png), then

 <math alttext="r squared equals a Superscript StartFraction p plus 1 Over 2 EndFraction Baseline equals a asterisk a Superscript StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction Baseline right double arrow r squared identical-to a asterisk left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis m o d p equals a" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup><mo>&#8658;</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></math> ![r squared equals a Superscript StartFraction p plus 1 Over 2 EndFraction Baseline equals a asterisk a Superscript StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction Baseline right double arrow r squared identical-to a asterisk left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis m o d p equals a](images/c03_2317.png).□

***Problem*** ***3.8***

By definition,  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk Baseline equals StartSet a element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript p Baseline vertical-bar GCD left-parenthesis a comma p right-parenthesis equals 1 EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mo>{</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msub><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#124;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>GCD</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk Baseline equals StartSet a element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript p Baseline vertical-bar GCD left-parenthesis a comma p right-parenthesis equals 1 EndSet](images/c03_2318.png).

Let *u* be any element of  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk](images/c03_2319.png).

*    <math alttext="a equals u Superscript left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis slash 2 Baseline right double arrow a squared equals u Superscript left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>u</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8658;</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>u</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![a equals u Superscript left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis slash 2 Baseline right double arrow a squared equals u Superscript left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis](images/c03_2320.png).
    
    By Fermat’s little theorem (Theorem 3.5),  <math alttext="u Superscript left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline identical-to 1 m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>u</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![u Superscript left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline identical-to 1 m o d p](images/c03_2321.png).
    
    Thus,  <math alttext="a squared identical-to 1 m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![a squared identical-to 1 m o d p](images/c03_2322.png). Hence, *a* is a square root of  <math alttext="1 period" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1.</mn></mrow></math> ![1 period](images/c03_2323.png)
    
*   From answer to question 1, we know that  <math alttext="u Superscript left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis slash 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>u</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![u Superscript left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis slash 2](images/c03_2324.png) is a square root of  <math alttext="1 m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![1 m o d p](images/c03_2325.png). Thus,  <math alttext="u Superscript left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis slash 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>u</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![u Superscript left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis slash 2](images/c03_2326.png) is 1 or  <math alttext="negative 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![negative 1](images/c03_2327.png) in modulo *p*.

***Problem*** ***3.9***

Prove that: g*iven two distinct primes*  <math alttext="p a n d q" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>a</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> ![p a n d q](images/c03_2328.png):

***Problem*** ***3.10***

Let *q* be the order of  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk](images/c03_2343.png) and 1 its neutral element.

If  <math alttext="g" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow></math> ![g](images/c03_2344.png) is a generator of  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk](images/c03_2345.png), then elements of  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk](images/c03_2346.png) can be expressed as powers of *g*:

 <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk Baseline equals StartSet 1 comma g comma g squared comma ellipsis comma g Superscript q minus 1 Baseline EndSet period" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk Baseline equals StartSet 1 comma g comma g squared comma ellipsis comma g Superscript q minus 1 Baseline EndSet period](images/c03_2347.png)

Since *g* is a generator of  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk](images/c03_2348.png) and  <math alttext="StartAbsoluteValue double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk Baseline EndAbsoluteValue equals q" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> ![StartAbsoluteValue double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk Baseline EndAbsoluteValue equals q](images/c03_2349.png),  <math alttext="g Superscript q Baseline identical-to 1 m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>g</mi><mi>q</mi></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![g Superscript q Baseline identical-to 1 m o d p](images/c03_2350.png).

By definition of multiplicative inverse:  <math alttext="g asterisk g Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![g asterisk g Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 1](images/c03_2351.png).

Then,  <math alttext="left-parenthesis g asterisk g Superscript negative 1 Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript q Baseline equals 1 right double arrow g Superscript q Baseline asterisk left-parenthesis g Superscript negative 1 Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript q Baseline equals 1 right double arrow 1 asterisk left-parenthesis g Superscript negative 1 Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript q Baseline equals 1 right double arrow left-parenthesis g Superscript negative 1 Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript q Baseline equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>q</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8658;</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mi>q</mi></msup><mo>\*</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>q</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8658;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>\*</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>q</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8658;</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>q</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis g asterisk g Superscript negative 1 Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript q Baseline equals 1 right double arrow g Superscript q Baseline asterisk left-parenthesis g Superscript negative 1 Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript q Baseline equals 1 right double arrow 1 asterisk left-parenthesis g Superscript negative 1 Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript q Baseline equals 1 right double arrow left-parenthesis g Superscript negative 1 Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript q Baseline equals 1](images/c03_2352.png).

Since the order of  <math alttext="g Superscript negative 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![g Superscript negative 1](images/c03_2353.png) is *q*,  <math alttext="g Superscript negative 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![g Superscript negative 1](images/c03_2354.png) is a generator of  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk](images/c03_2355.png).

***Problem*** ***3.11*** *(Proof of Lemma* 3.6)

To prove that Lemma 3.6 is correct, we need to prove that the statement “any irreducible polynomial of degree *m* can generate all the elements of field  <math alttext="upper F Subscript p Sub Superscript m" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript p Sub Superscript m](images/c03_2356.png)” is false. The two following scenarios are counterexamples to the statement above.

1.  Let  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x squared plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x squared plus 1](images/c03_2357.png) and α its root over field  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 3 squared" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 3 squared](images/c03_2358.png).
    
    Since α is a root of  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c03_2359.png), then  <math alttext="alpha squared plus 1 equals 0 right double arrow alpha squared equals negative 1 equals 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#945;</mi><msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8658;</mo><mi>&#945;</mi><msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![alpha squared plus 1 equals 0 right double arrow alpha squared equals negative 1 equals 2](images/c03_2360.png).
    
    Let us see how powers of α generate elements of field  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 3 squared" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 3 squared](images/c03_2361.png):
    
     <math alttext="alpha Superscript 0 Baseline equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>&#945;</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![alpha Superscript 0 Baseline equals 1](images/c03_2362.png)   <math alttext="alpha Superscript 1 Baseline equals alpha" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#945;</mi><msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>&#945;</mi></mrow></math> ![alpha Superscript 1 Baseline equals alpha](images/c03_2363.png)
    
     <math alttext="alpha squared equals 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>&#945;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![alpha squared equals 2](images/c03_2364.png)   <math alttext="alpha cubed equals alpha left-parenthesis alpha squared right-parenthesis equals 2 alpha" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>&#945;</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>&#945;</mi><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>&#945;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>&#945;</mi></mrow></math> ![alpha cubed equals alpha left-parenthesis alpha squared right-parenthesis equals 2 alpha](images/c03_2365.png)
    
     <math alttext="alpha Superscript 4 Baseline equals alpha left-parenthesis 2 alpha right-parenthesis equals 2 alpha squared equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#945;</mi><msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>&#945;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>&#945;</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>&#945;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![alpha Superscript 4 Baseline equals alpha left-parenthesis 2 alpha right-parenthesis equals 2 alpha squared equals 1](images/c03_2366.png)
    
     <math alttext="alpha Superscript 5 Baseline equals alpha left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis equals alpha" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#945;</mi><msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>&#945;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>&#945;</mi></mrow></math> ![alpha Superscript 5 Baseline equals alpha left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis equals alpha](images/c03_2367.png)   <math alttext="alpha Superscript 6 Baseline equals alpha left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis equals 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>&#945;</mi><mn>6</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>&#945;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![alpha Superscript 6 Baseline equals alpha left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis equals 2](images/c03_2368.png).
    
    Thus, α cannot generate all the eight nonzero elements of  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 3 squared" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 3 squared](images/c03_2369.png). Hence, α, which represents the element 3, is not a primitive element in  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 3 squared" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 3 squared](images/c03_2370.png).
    
2.  Let  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x cubed plus 2 x plus 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x cubed plus 2 x plus 2](images/c03_2371.png) and α its root over field  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 3 cubed" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 3 cubed](images/c03_2372.png).
    
    ![](images/c03_2373.png)
    
    Root α can generate only 12 nonzero elements among the 26 nonzero elements of  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 3 cubed" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 3 cubed](images/c03_2408.png).
    
    Both examples above prove (by counterexamples) that not all polynomials of degree  <math alttext="normal m" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> ![normal m](images/c03_2409.png) and irreducible over field *F[p]* have a root α that can generate all elements of a field  <math alttext="upper F Subscript p Sub Superscript m" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript p Sub Superscript m](images/c03_2410.png).

***Problem*** ***3.12***

1.  If  <math alttext="g Subscript i" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![g Subscript i](images/c03_2411.png) is a generator, then its multiplicative inverse  <math alttext="g Subscript i Superscript negative 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></math> ![g Subscript i Superscript negative 1](images/c03_2412.png) also is a generator.
    
    By definition of multiplicative inverse:  <math alttext="g Subscript i Baseline asterisk g Subscript i Superscript negative 1 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>\*</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![g Subscript i Baseline asterisk g Subscript i Superscript negative 1 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d p](images/c03_2413.png).
    
    Let *q* be the number of generators of  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk](images/c03_2414.png) and *G* the set of  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk](images/c03_2415.png) generators denoted  <math alttext="StartSet g 1 comma g 2 comma ellipsis comma g Subscript q Baseline EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>{</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>}</mo></mrow></math> ![StartSet g 1 comma g 2 comma ellipsis comma g Subscript q Baseline EndSet](images/c03_2416.png). Each element in  <math alttext="upper G" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>G</mi></mrow></math> ![upper G](images/c03_2417.png) has its multiplicative inverse in  <math alttext="upper G" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>G</mi></mrow></math> ![upper G](images/c03_2418.png). Without loss of generality, assume that, if *q* is even, the set  <math alttext="upper G" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>G</mi></mrow></math> ![upper G](images/c03_2419.png) is organized into two halves such that  <math alttext="g Subscript k" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![g Subscript k](images/c03_2420.png),  <math alttext="1 less-than-or-equal-to k less-than-or-equal-to StartFraction q Over 2 EndFraction" display="inline"     The product  <math alttext="product Underscript i equals 1 Overscript i equals k Endscripts g Subscript i Baseline equals g 1 asterisk g 2 asterisk dot dot dot asterisk g Subscript q" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msubsup><mo>&#8719;</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>\*</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>\*</mo><mo>&#8901;</mo><mo>&#8901;</mo><mo>&#8901;</mo><mo>\*</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>q</mi></msub></mrow></mstyle></mrow></math> ![product Underscript i equals 1 Overscript i equals k Endscripts g Subscript i Baseline equals g 1 asterisk g 2 asterisk dot dot dot asterisk g Subscript q](images/c03_2424.png) may be rewritten as
    
     <math alttext="product Underscript i equals 1 Overscript i equals k Endscripts g Subscript i Baseline equals left-parenthesis g 1 asterisk g 1 Superscript negative 1 Baseline right-parenthesis asterisk left-parenthesis g 2 asterisk g 2 Superscript negative 1 Baseline right-parenthesis asterisk ellipsis asterisk left-parenthesis g Subscript StartFraction q Over 2 EndFraction Baseline asterisk g Subscript StartFraction q Over 2 EndFraction Superscript negative 1 Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msubsup><mo>&#8719;</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>\*</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>\*</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mfrac><mi>q</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></msub><mo>\*</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mfrac><mi>q</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mstyle></mrow></math> ![product Underscript i equals 1 Overscript i equals k Endscripts g Subscript i Baseline equals left-parenthesis g 1 asterisk g 1 Superscript negative 1 Baseline right-parenthesis asterisk left-parenthesis g 2 asterisk g 2 Superscript negative 1 Baseline right-parenthesis asterisk ellipsis asterisk left-parenthesis g Subscript StartFraction q Over 2 EndFraction Baseline asterisk g Subscript StartFraction q Over 2 EndFraction Superscript negative 1 Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c03_2425.png).
    
    Thus,  <math alttext="product Underscript i equals 1 Overscript i equals k Endscripts g Subscript i Baseline identical-to 1 asterisk 1 asterisk ellipsis asterisk 1 identical-to 1 m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msubsup><mo>&#8719;</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>\*</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>\*</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></mstyle></mrow></math> ![product Underscript i equals 1 Overscript i equals k Endscripts g Subscript i Baseline identical-to 1 asterisk 1 asterisk ellipsis asterisk 1 identical-to 1 m o d p](images/c03_2426.png)
    
    If *q* is odd, *G* is organized as  <math alttext="StartSet g 1 comma g 2 comma ellipsis period comma g Subscript StartFraction q minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction Baseline comma g Subscript StartFraction q plus 1 Over 2 EndFraction Baseline comma g Subscript StartFraction q minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction Superscript negative 1 Baseline comma g 2 Superscript negative 1 Baseline comma g 1 Superscript negative 1 Baseline EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></math> ![StartSet g 1 comma g 2 comma ellipsis period comma g Subscript StartFraction q minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction Baseline comma g Subscript StartFraction q plus 1 Over 2 EndFraction Baseline comma g Subscript StartFraction q minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction Superscript negative 1 Baseline comma g 2 Superscript negative 1 Baseline comma g 1 Superscript negative 1 Baseline EndSet](images/c03_2427.png). Since, the elements in the subset of *G* on the right of  <math alttext="g Subscript StartFraction q plus 1 Over 2 EndFraction" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![g Subscript StartFraction q plus 1 Over 2 EndFraction](images/c03_2428.png) and the elements on its left are pairwise inverses,  <math alttext="g Subscript StartFraction q plus 1 Over 2 EndFraction Baseline equals g Subscript StartFraction q plus 1 Over 2 EndFraction Superscript negative 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></math> ![g Subscript StartFraction q plus 1 Over 2 EndFraction Baseline equals g Subscript StartFraction q plus 1 Over 2 EndFraction Superscript negative 1](images/c03_2429.png). Hence,  <math alttext="product Underscript i equals 1 Overscript i equals k Endscripts g Subscript i Baseline identical-to 1 asterisk ellipsis 1 ellipsis asterisk 1 identical-to 1 m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msubsup><mo>&#8719;</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>\*</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>\*</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></mstyle></mrow></math> ![product Underscript i equals 1 Overscript i equals k Endscripts g Subscript i Baseline identical-to 1 asterisk ellipsis 1 ellipsis asterisk 1 identical-to 1 m o d p](images/c03_2430.png).
    
2.  Let *F[p]* be a prime field. Thus,  <math alttext="upper F Subscript p Baseline equals StartSet 0 comma 1 2 comma ellipsis comma p minus 1 EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript p Baseline equals StartSet 0 comma 1 2 comma ellipsis comma p minus 1 EndSet](images/c03_2431.png). Each element  <math alttext="u element-of upper F Subscript p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![u element-of upper F Subscript p](images/c03_2432.png) has one and only one additive inverse  <math alttext="u prime element-of upper F Subscript p Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>'</mo><mo>&#8712;</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![u prime element-of upper F Subscript p Baseline](images/c03_2433.png), such that  <math alttext="u plus u Superscript prime Baseline equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>u</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![u plus u Superscript prime Baseline equals 0](images/c03_2434.png). The elements of *F[p]* can be organized as follows:  <math alttext="StartSet 0 comma 1 comma negative 1 comma 2 comma negative 2 comma ellipsis comma StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction comma minus left-parenthesis StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction right-parenthesis EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></math> ![StartSet 0 comma 1 comma negative 1 comma 2 comma negative 2 comma ellipsis comma StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction comma minus left-parenthesis StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction right-parenthesis EndSet](images/c03_2435.png). Therefore,
    
     <math alttext="sigma-summation Underscript u element-of upper F Subscript p Baseline Endscripts u Superscript zero width space Baseline identical-to left-parenthesis 0 right-parenthesis plus left-parenthesis 1 minus 1 right-parenthesis plus left-parenthesis 2 minus 2 right-parenthesis plus ellipsis plus left-parenthesis StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction minus StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction right-parenthesis m o d p equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mstyle displaystyle="true" mathsize="140%"><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msub><mo>&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mi>u</mi></mstyle></mrow></mstyle><mtext>&#8203;</mtext></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>&#8722;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> ![sigma-summation Underscript u element-of upper F Subscript p Baseline Endscripts u Superscript zero width space Baseline identical-to left-parenthesis 0 right-parenthesis plus left-parenthesis 1 minus 1 right-parenthesis plus left-parenthesis 2 minus 2 right-parenthesis plus ellipsis plus left-parenthesis StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction minus StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction right-parenthesis m o d p equals 0](images/c03_2436.png)
    

***Problem*** ***3.13***

 <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 4 equals StartSet 0 comma 1 comma 2 comma 3 EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 4 equals StartSet 0 comma 1 comma 2 comma 3 EndSet](images/c03_2437.png) is not a field, because 0 and 2 have no multiplicative inverse in  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>&#8484;</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 4](images/c03_2438.png).

***Problem*** ***3.14***

Consider field  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 5](images/c03_2439.png) with reduction polynomial  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 5 Baseline plus x squared plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>5</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 5 Baseline plus x squared plus 1](images/c03_2440.png). Show that  <math alttext="g equals x" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> ![g equals x](images/c03_2441.png) is a generator of  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 5](images/c03_2442.png).

The set of elements of  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 5](images/c03_2443.png) is  <math alttext="StartSet 0 comma 1 comma 2 comma ellipsis comma 30 comma 31 EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>30</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>31</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></math> ![StartSet 0 comma 1 comma 2 comma ellipsis comma 30 comma 31 EndSet](images/c03_2444.png).

By definition, if *g* is a generator of a field  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript m" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript m](images/c03_2445.png), then every nonzero element of  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript m" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript m](images/c03_2446.png) can be uniquely written is a power of *g*. That is:  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript m Subscript Superscript asterisk Baseline equals upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript m Subscript Baseline minus StartSet 0 EndSet equals StartSet 2 Superscript m Baseline comma 0 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than-or-equal-to 2 Superscript m Baseline minus 2 EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow><mo>\*</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow></msub><mo>&#8722;</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>&#8804;</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript m Subscript Superscript asterisk Baseline equals upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript m Subscript Baseline minus StartSet 0 EndSet equals StartSet 2 Superscript m Baseline comma 0 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than-or-equal-to 2 Superscript m Baseline minus 2 EndSet](images/c03_2447.png).

 <math alttext="g equals x" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> ![g equals x](images/c03_2448.png) is it a generator of  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 5](images/c03_2449.png)?

In this problem  <math alttext="2 Superscript m Baseline equals 32" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow></math> ![2 Superscript m Baseline equals 32](images/c03_2450.png). Thus, we have to check the powers of *x* from 0 to 30.

 <math alttext="x Superscript 4 Baseline m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 4 Baseline equals left-parenthesis 10000 right-parenthesis equals 16" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>10000</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow></math> ![x Superscript 4 Baseline m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 4 Baseline equals left-parenthesis 10000 right-parenthesis equals 16](images/c03_2455.png)   <math alttext="x Superscript 5 Baseline m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x squared plus 1 equals left-parenthesis 00101 right-parenthesis equals 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>5</mn></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>00101</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![x Superscript 5 Baseline m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x squared plus 1 equals left-parenthesis 00101 right-parenthesis equals 5](images/c03_2456.png).
