***Problem*** ***3.15***

Let  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x plus 1](images/c03_2495.png) be an irreducible polynomial over  <math alttext="upper F 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F 2](images/c03_2496.png).  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c03_2497.png) is used for computations over field  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 4](images/c03_2498.png). Solve the following linear equations:

1.   <math alttext="3 y equals 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></math> ![3 y equals 4](images/c03_2499.png)
    
     <math alttext="y equals 4 asterisk 3 Superscript negative 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>\*</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![y equals 4 asterisk 3 Superscript negative 1](images/c03_2500.png).
    
    Operations are done using polynomial representation.
    
     <math alttext="3 Superscript negative 1 Baseline colon left-parenthesis x plus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis x cubed plus x squared plus x right-parenthesis m o d left-parenthesis x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x plus 1 right-parenthesis equals 1 right double arrow 3 Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 14" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>:</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8658;</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>14</mn></mrow></math> ![3 Superscript negative 1 Baseline colon left-parenthesis x plus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis x cubed plus x squared plus x right-parenthesis m o d left-parenthesis x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x plus 1 right-parenthesis equals 1 right double arrow 3 Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 14](images/c03_2501.png)
    
     <math alttext="4 asterisk 3 Superscript negative 1 Baseline colon left-parenthesis x squared right-parenthesis left-parenthesis x cubed plus x squared plus x right-parenthesis m o d left-parenthesis x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x plus 1 right-parenthesis equals x cubed plus x squared plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>\*</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>:</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![4 asterisk 3 Superscript negative 1 Baseline colon left-parenthesis x squared right-parenthesis left-parenthesis x cubed plus x squared plus x right-parenthesis m o d left-parenthesis x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x plus 1 right-parenthesis equals x cubed plus x squared plus 1](images/c03_2502.png).
    
    Hence,  <math alttext="y equals 13" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>13</mn></mrow></math> ![y equals 13](images/c03_2503.png)
    
2.   <math alttext="9 y plus 3 equals 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>9</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![9 y plus 3 equals 2](images/c03_2504.png)
    
     <math alttext="y equals left-parenthesis 2 minus 3 right-parenthesis asterisk 9 Superscript negative 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo><msup><mn>9</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![y equals left-parenthesis 2 minus 3 right-parenthesis asterisk 9 Superscript negative 1](images/c03_2505.png).
    
    Operations are done with polynomial representation.
    
     <math alttext="2 minus 3 colon x minus x minus 1 equals negative 1 equals 15" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>:</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow></math> ![2 minus 3 colon x minus x minus 1 equals negative 1 equals 15](images/c03_2506.png)
    
     <math alttext="9 Superscript negative 1 Baseline colon left-parenthesis x cubed plus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis m o d left-parenthesis x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x plus 1 right-parenthesis equals 1 right double arrow 9 Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>9</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>:</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8658;</mo><msup><mn>9</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![9 Superscript negative 1 Baseline colon left-parenthesis x cubed plus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis m o d left-parenthesis x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x plus 1 right-parenthesis equals 1 right double arrow 9 Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 2](images/c03_2507.png)
    
     <math alttext="left-parenthesis 2 minus 3 right-parenthesis asterisk 9 Superscript negative 1 Baseline colon 15 x m o d left-parenthesis x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x plus 1 right-parenthesis equals 15 x equals negative x" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>\*</mo><msup><mn>9</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>:</mo><mn>15</mn><mi>x</mi><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 2 minus 3 right-parenthesis asterisk 9 Superscript negative 1 Baseline colon 15 x m o d left-parenthesis x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x plus 1 right-parenthesis equals 15 x equals negative x](images/c03_2508.png)
    
    Hence,  <math alttext="y equals negative 2 equals 14" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>14</mn></mrow></math> ![y equals negative 2 equals 14](images/c03_2509.png).
    

***Problem*** ***3.16***

 <math alttext="147 Superscript 155 Baseline m o d 23 identical-to question-mark" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>147</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>155</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>23</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mo>?</mo></mrow></math> ![147 Superscript 155 Baseline m o d 23 identical-to question-mark](images/c03_2510.png)

1.  Fermat’s little theorem states that given two positive integers *m* and *p*, such that *p* is prime and *m* is not divisible by *p*, then  <math alttext="m Superscript p minus 1 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>m</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![m Superscript p minus 1 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d p](images/c03_2511.png).
    
    In this problem  <math alttext="m equals 147" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>147</mn></mrow></math> ![m equals 147](images/c03_2512.png) and  <math alttext="p equals 23" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>23</mn></mrow></math> ![p equals 23](images/c03_2513.png). *m* and *p* are coprime. Thus, Fermat’s little theorem is applicable. Thus,  <math alttext="147 Superscript 22 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 23" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>147</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>22</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>23</mn></mrow></math> ![147 Superscript 22 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 23](images/c03_2514.png) is used to reduce the computations as follows:
    
     <math alttext="147 Superscript 155 Baseline m o d 23 identical-to 147 Superscript 7 asterisk 22 plus 1 Baseline m o d 23 identical-to left-parenthesis 147 Superscript 22 Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript 7 Baseline asterisk left-parenthesis 147 right-parenthesis m o d 23" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>147</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>155</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>23</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mn>147</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>22</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>23</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>147</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>22</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>7</mn></msup><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>147</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>23</mn></mrow></math> ![147 Superscript 155 Baseline m o d 23 identical-to 147 Superscript 7 asterisk 22 plus 1 Baseline m o d 23 identical-to left-parenthesis 147 Superscript 22 Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript 7 Baseline asterisk left-parenthesis 147 right-parenthesis m o d 23](images/c03_2515.png)
    
     <math alttext="identical-to left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis Superscript 7 Baseline asterisk left-parenthesis 147 right-parenthesis m o d 23 identical-to 9" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>7</mn></msup><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>147</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>23</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></math> ![identical-to left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis Superscript 7 Baseline asterisk left-parenthesis 147 right-parenthesis m o d 23 identical-to 9](images/c03_2516.png).
    
2.  To use the right-to-left binary exponentiation method, we need to represent the exponent as a sum of powers of 2:
    
     <math alttext="155 equals 128 plus 16 plus 8 plus 2 plus 1 equals 2 Superscript 7 Baseline plus 2 Superscript 4 Baseline plus 2 cubed plus 2 Superscript 1 Baseline plus 2 Superscript 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>155</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>128</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>7</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>1</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>0</mn></msup></mrow></math> ![155 equals 128 plus 16 plus 8 plus 2 plus 1 equals 2 Superscript 7 Baseline plus 2 Superscript 4 Baseline plus 2 cubed plus 2 Superscript 1 Baseline plus 2 Superscript 0](images/c03_2517.png).
    
    The number of iterations of the right-to-left binary exponentiation method depends on the rank of the leftmost significant bit of the exponent. If the exponent is 155, the number of iterations of the algorithm is 8 (i.e. 7+1). Consequently, when applicable, Fermat’s little theorem is a very fast method to perform modular exponentiation.
    

***Problem*** ***3.17***

1.  We need to prove that  <math alttext="t asterisk upper R equals upper T m o d upper N" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>T</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> ![t asterisk upper R equals upper T m o d upper N](images/c03_2518.png),  <math alttext="0 less-than-or-equal-to t less-than upper N" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> ![0 less-than-or-equal-to t less-than upper N](images/c03_2519.png) (because a residue is less than the modulus), and *t* is an integer.
    
     <math alttext="t asterisk upper R equals upper T m o d upper N question-mark" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>T</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>N</mi><mo>?</mo></mrow></math> ![t asterisk upper R equals upper T m o d upper N question-mark](images/c03_2520.png)(a) 
    
    In line 2,  <math alttext="t equals left-parenthesis upper T plus m asterisk upper N right-parenthesis slash upper R right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>/</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![t equals left-parenthesis upper T plus m asterisk upper N right-parenthesis slash upper R right-parenthesis](images/c03_2521.png). Multiplying both sides by *R* yields  <math alttext="t asterisk upper R equals left-parenthesis upper T plus m asterisk upper N right-parenthesis right-parenthesis identical-to upper T m o d upper N" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>T</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> ![t asterisk upper R equals left-parenthesis upper T plus m asterisk upper N right-parenthesis right-parenthesis identical-to upper T m o d upper N](images/c03_2522.png), because adding  <math alttext="m asterisk upper N" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> ![m asterisk upper N](images/c03_2523.png) does not change the residue. Therefore, condition (a) holds.
    
     <math alttext="0 less-than-or-equal-to t less-than upper N question-mark" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>?</mo></mrow></math> ![0 less-than-or-equal-to t less-than upper N question-mark](images/c03_2524.png)(b) 
    
    From line 3, the returned result is either  <math alttext="t less-than upper N" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> ![t less-than upper N](images/c03_2525.png) or  <math alttext="t equals t minus upper N" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> ![t equals t minus upper N](images/c03_2526.png). Therefore, we need to prove that  <math alttext="t less-than 2 upper N" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> ![t less-than 2 upper N](images/c03_2527.png). From definition in line 1,  <math alttext="0 less-than-or-equal-to m less-than upper R" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow></math> ![0 less-than-or-equal-to m less-than upper R](images/c03_2528.png). Thus,  <math alttext="0 less-than-or-equal-to upper N asterisk m less-than upper N asterisk upper R" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow></math> ![0 less-than-or-equal-to upper N asterisk m less-than upper N asterisk upper R](images/c03_2529.png) By definition 3.44,  <math alttext="0 less-than-or-equal-to upper T less-than upper N asterisk upper R" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>T</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow></math> ![0 less-than-or-equal-to upper T less-than upper N asterisk upper R](images/c03_2530.png). Thus,  <math alttext="0 less-than-or-equal-to upper T plus upper N asterisk m less-than 2 asterisk upper N asterisk upper R" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>T</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow></math> ![0 less-than-or-equal-to upper T plus upper N asterisk m less-than 2 asterisk upper N asterisk upper R](images/c03_2531.png). Dividing the inequality by *R* yields  <math alttext="0 less-than-or-equal-to left-parenthesis upper T plus upper N asterisk m right-parenthesis slash upper R less-than 2 asterisk upper N" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> ![0 less-than-or-equal-to left-parenthesis upper T plus upper N asterisk m right-parenthesis slash upper R less-than 2 asterisk upper N](images/c03_2532.png). Thus, condition (b) holds.
    
     <math alttext="t" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi></math> ![t](images/c03_2533.png)(c) 
    
    Multiplying both sides in line 1 by *N* yields  <math alttext="upper N asterisk m equals upper N asterisk upper T asterisk upper N Superscript prime Baseline equals upper T asterisk left-parenthesis negative upper N asterisk upper N Superscript negative 1 Baseline right-parenthesis equals negative upper T m o d upper R" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>T</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>N</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>T</mi><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>N</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>T</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>R</mi></mrow></math> ![upper N asterisk m equals upper N asterisk upper T asterisk upper N Superscript prime Baseline equals upper T asterisk left-parenthesis negative upper N asterisk upper N Superscript negative 1 Baseline right-parenthesis equals negative upper T m o d upper R](images/c03_2534.png). Therefore, there exists some integer *k* such that  <math alttext="upper N asterisk m equals k asterisk upper R minus upper T" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></math> ![upper N asterisk m equals k asterisk upper R minus upper T](images/c03_2535.png) and hence  <math alttext="t equals StartFraction upper T plus m asterisk upper N Over upper R EndFraction equals StartFraction k asterisk upper R Over upper R EndFraction" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mi>R</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow><mi>R</mi></mfrac><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![t equals StartFraction upper T plus m asterisk upper N Over upper R EndFraction equals StartFraction k asterisk upper R Over upper R EndFraction](images/c03_2536.png) is an integer.
    
    □
    
2.  We need to prove that  <math alttext="c identical-to a asterisk b m o d upper N" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>b</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> ![c identical-to a asterisk b m o d upper N](images/c03_2537.png), where *c* denotes the result of the Montgomery multiplication. We proceed by substitution starting from the definition of *c*:
    
     <math alttext="c identical-to upper R upper E upper D upper C left-parenthesis c Superscript prime Baseline right-parenthesis identical-to c prime asterisk upper R Superscript negative 1 Baseline m o d upper N identical-to left-parenthesis upper R upper E upper D upper C left-parenthesis a overTilde asterisk b overTilde right-parenthesis right-parenthesis asterisk upper R Superscript negative 1 Baseline m o d upper N" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>R</mi><mi>E</mi><mi>D</mi><mi>C</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>c</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mi>c</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>N</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mi>E</mi><mi>D</mi><mi>C</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>a</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover><mo>\*</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>b</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> ![c identical-to upper R upper E upper D upper C left-parenthesis c Superscript prime Baseline right-parenthesis identical-to c prime asterisk upper R Superscript negative 1 Baseline m o d upper N identical-to left-parenthesis upper R upper E upper D upper C left-parenthesis a overTilde asterisk b overTilde right-parenthesis right-parenthesis asterisk upper R Superscript negative 1 Baseline m o d upper N](images/c03_2538.png)

***Problem*** ***3.18*** *(Proof of Gauss’s algorithm)*

Gauss’s algorithm is correct if and only if the returned value of *x* satisfies all the congruence equations. Recall that to apply the Chinese remainder theorem, the moduli in congruence equations must meet the following condition:

For  <math alttext="1 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than-or-equal-to k" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></math> ![1 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than-or-equal-to k](images/c03_2542.png),  <math alttext="n Subscript i" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![n Subscript i](images/c03_2543.png) is coprime with  <math alttext="n Subscript j" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![n Subscript j](images/c03_2544.png), for  <math alttext="i not-equals j" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>&#8800;</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></math> ![i not-equals j](images/c03_2545.png) and  <math alttext="1 less-than-or-equal-to j less-than-or-equal-to k" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></math> ![1 less-than-or-equal-to j less-than-or-equal-to k](images/c03_2546.png).

*Proof*:

By construction,  <math alttext="upper N Subscript i Baseline equals StartFraction product Underscript i equals 1 Overscript i equals k Endscripts n Subscript i Baseline Over n Subscript i Baseline EndFraction" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msubsup><mstyle displaystyle="true" mathsize="140%"><mo>&#8719;</mo></mstyle><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msubsup><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> ![upper N Subscript i Baseline equals StartFraction product Underscript i equals 1 Overscript i equals k Endscripts n Subscript i Baseline Over n Subscript i Baseline EndFraction](images/c03_2547.png), for  <math alttext="1 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than-or-equal-to k" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></math> ![1 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than-or-equal-to k](images/c03_2548.png). Thus,

1.  Since the  <math alttext="n Subscript i" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![n Subscript i](images/c03_2549.png)’s are pairwise coprime and  <math alttext="upper N Subscript i" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![upper N Subscript i](images/c03_2550.png) does not have a factor equal to  <math alttext="n Subscript i" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![n Subscript i](images/c03_2551.png),  <math alttext="GCD left-parenthesis upper N Subscript i Baseline comma n Subscript i Baseline right-parenthesis equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>GCD</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![GCD left-parenthesis upper N Subscript i Baseline comma n Subscript i Baseline right-parenthesis equals 1](images/c03_2552.png). ***Problem*** ***3.19*** (Proof of Lemma 3.8)

First, we need to prove that if *n* and *x* are integers such that  <math alttext="1 less-than x less-than n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>&#60;</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![1 less-than x less-than n](images/c03_2576.png) and  <math alttext="x Superscript 2 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![x Superscript 2 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d n](images/c03_2577.png), then *n* is composite.

*Proof*.  <math alttext="x Superscript 2 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d n right double arrow x Superscript 2 Baseline minus 1 identical-to 0 m o d n right double arrow left-parenthesis x plus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis x minus 1 right-parenthesis identical-to 0 m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8658;</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>0</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8658;</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>0</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![x Superscript 2 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d n right double arrow x Superscript 2 Baseline minus 1 identical-to 0 m o d n right double arrow left-parenthesis x plus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis x minus 1 right-parenthesis identical-to 0 m o d n](images/c03_2578.png). If  <math alttext="x not-equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8800;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![x not-equals 1](images/c03_2579.png) and  <math alttext="x not-equals n minus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8800;</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![x not-equals n minus 1](images/c03_2580.png), *n* must be composite because  <math alttext="left-parenthesis x plus 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis x plus 1 right-parenthesis](images/c03_2581.png) and  <math alttext="left-parenthesis x minus 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis x minus 1 right-parenthesis](images/c03_2582.png) are less than *n* and their product is a multiple of *n*. For example,  <math alttext="5 Superscript 2 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 24" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>24</mn></mrow></math> ![5 Superscript 2 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 24](images/c03_2583.png),  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 5 plus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis 5 minus 1 right-parenthesis identical-to 0 m o d 24" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>0</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>24</mn></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 5 plus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis 5 minus 1 right-parenthesis identical-to 0 m o d 24](images/c03_2584.png), and 24 is composite.

Second, let *n* and *a* be integers such that  <math alttext="normal upper G normal upper C normal upper D left-parenthesis a comma n right-parenthesis equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">G</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![normal upper G normal upper C normal upper D left-parenthesis a comma n right-parenthesis equals 1](images/c03_2585.png) and  <math alttext="a Superscript StartFraction n minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction Baseline CrossOut identical-to EndCrossOut plus-or-minus 1 m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup><menclose notation="updiagonalstrike"><mo>&#8801;</mo></menclose><mo>&#177;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![a Superscript StartFraction n minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction Baseline CrossOut identical-to EndCrossOut plus-or-minus 1 m o d n](images/c03_2586.png). Either  <math alttext="a Superscript n minus 1 Baseline CrossOut identical-to EndCrossOut 1 m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><menclose notation="updiagonalstrike"><mo>&#8801;</mo></menclose><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![a Superscript n minus 1 Baseline CrossOut identical-to EndCrossOut 1 m o d n](images/c03_2587.png) or <math alttext="a Superscript n minus 1 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![a Superscript n minus 1 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d n](images/c03_2588.png) holds.

By Fermat’s little theorem, if  <math alttext="a Superscript n minus 1 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![a Superscript n minus 1 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d n](images/c03_2589.png), then *n* must be composite.

 <math alttext="a Superscript n minus 1 Baseline identical-to 1 m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![a Superscript left-parenthesis n minus 1 right-parenthesis slash 2](images/c03_2592.png), which is different from  <math alttext="1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![1 m o d n](images/c03_2595.png). # 4   
Symmetric Ciphering  
Historical Ciphers

Shift and substitution ciphers have been used for written text transmission and dominated the art of secret writing for at least two millenniums (and maybe more). The most known historical ciphers in this category, include Caesar’s, Vigenere’s, affine, OTP, and Enigma ciphers. With the advent of computers, shift and substitution ciphering were abandoned, because it has become easy to break them. However, it is important to learn them since they had inspired the modern cryptography. The material below is mostly collected from \[[1](#c04.xhtml#c04-bib-0001)–[5](#c04.xhtml#c04-bib-0005)\].

## 4.1 Definitions

***Definition 4.1 Alphabet***: *it is a set of elements, which may be letters, words, or any other form of bit strings that are used to generate plaintexts and ciphertexts*.

In the sequel, the alphabet elements are either Latin letters or bits.

***Definition 4.2 Substitution cipher***: *it is a cipher in which an alphabet element is replaced by another alphabet element to yield a ciphertext*.

***Definition 4.3 Shift cipher***: *it is a special type of substitution cipher in which a letter is replaced by another letter located a few positions away*.

***Definition 4.4 Monoalphabetic cipher***: *it is a cipher in which the letters of the plaintext are mapped to ciphertext letters based on a single substitution key and each letter is always replaced by the same letter. The transformation is bijective*.

***Definition 4.5 Polyalphabetic cipher***: *it is a cipher, which makes use of multiple alphabets and a letter may be replaced by many other letters depending on its position in the plaintext. It makes use of multiple keys. The transformation is not bijective*.

***Definition 4.6 Information-theoretic secure cipher***: *a cipher is information-theoretic secure if it cannot be broken even if the adversary has unlimited computation resources*.

## 4.2 Caesar’s Cipher

One of the most known shift ciphers is Caesar’s cipher used in the Roman Empire to encrypt messages exchanged between Roma (i.e. the emperor and his attorneys) and roman armies around the world. At ancient Rome, the romans had an intelligence system comparable to the one in today’s USA.

A message to encrypt is a string of letters over an alphabet  <math alttext="script upper A" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="script">A</mi></math> ![script upper A](images/c04_1.png) of *m* letters. Each letter has an index in interval  <math alttext="left-bracket 1 comma m right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>m</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></math> ![left-bracket 1 comma m right-bracket](images/c04_2.png). Let  <math alttext="upper I n d left-parenthesis y right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>I</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![upper I n d left-parenthesis y right-parenthesis](images/c04_3.png) be a function that returns the index of a letter *y* in the alphabet  <math alttext="script upper A" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="script">A</mi></math> ![script upper A](images/c04_4.png) and  <math alttext="upper L e t left-parenthesis c right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper L e t left-parenthesis c right-parenthesis](images/c04_5.png), a function that returns the letter of index *c*. Caesar’s cipher may be formulated as follows:[¹](#c04.xhtml#c04-note-0001)

*Encryption*: given a key *k* ( <math alttext="k contains-as-member double-struck upper N comma k less-than m right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8715;</mo><mi>&#8469;</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>k</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> ![k contains-as-member double-struck upper N comma k less-than m right-parenthesis](images/c04_6.png) and *l* a letter to encrypt, the encryption is a shift right to yield the encrypted letter  <math alttext="l prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![l prime](images/c04_7.png). Formally:

 <math alttext="upper E n c left-parenthesis l right-parenthesis equals l prime equals upper L e t left-parenthesis script upper A left-parenthesis left-parenthesis upper I n d left-parenthesis l right-parenthesis plus k right-parenthesis m o d m right-parenthesis right-parenthesis period" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>c</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>l</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>l</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">A</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>I</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>l</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>m</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> ![upper E n c left-parenthesis l right-parenthesis equals l prime equals upper L e t left-parenthesis script upper A left-parenthesis left-parenthesis upper I n d left-parenthesis l right-parenthesis plus k right-parenthesis m o d m right-parenthesis right-parenthesis period](images/c04_8.png)

*Decryption*: It is a shift left. Formally,

Let  <math alttext="script upper A" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="script">A</mi></math> ![script upper A](images/c04_10.png) be the Latin alphabet,  <math alttext="m equals 26" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>26</mn></mrow></math> ![m equals 26](images/c04_11.png), and  <math alttext="k equals 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> ![k equals 3](images/c04_12.png).

Therefore, the encrypted message is  <math alttext="upper F upper D upper H upper V upper D upper U" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>F</mi><mi>D</mi><mi>H</mi><mi>V</mi><mi>D</mi><mi>U</mi></mrow></math> ![upper F upper D upper H upper V upper D upper U](images/c04_20.png).

The decryption is performed as follows:

 <math alttext="l prime Subscript i Baseline equals upper L e t left-parenthesis script upper A left-parenthesis left-parenthesis upper I n d left-parenthesis l Subscript i Baseline right-parenthesis minus 3 right-parenthesis m o d 26 right-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>l</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>'</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">A</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>I</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>l</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>26</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![l prime Subscript i Baseline equals upper L e t left-parenthesis script upper A left-parenthesis left-parenthesis upper I n d left-parenthesis l Subscript i Baseline right-parenthesis minus 3 right-parenthesis m o d 26 right-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c04_21.png), for  <math alttext="i equals 1 comma 2 ellipsis comma 26" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>26</mn></mrow></math> ![i equals 1 comma 2 ellipsis comma 26](images/c04_22.png). Therefore, the plaintext is the same as the original message.

*Caesar’s chipper security*

Caesar’s ciphering was very robust at Roman time. It required frequent changes of the secret (i.e. the key *k*) to prevent attacks. For example, during a secured mission that could not be jeopardized by enemies, a list of keys was transmitted to the governors of districts and then the keys were used for specific periods and for specific communicating entities (e.g. one key for each exchange between Roma and any other location in the empire).

Caesar’s cipher had been used for centuries because computer did not exist at that time. Unfortunately, Caesar’s cipher has two flaws. First, since there are only 26 letters in Latin alphabet, there exist 25 shifts (  <math alttext="k equals 0 or 26" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mtext>&#160;or&#160;</mtext><mn>26</mn></mrow></math> ![k equals 0 or 26](images/c04_23.png) results in no shift). Second, since frequency of letters in human readable texts is dependent on the language in use (e.g. “E” is more frequent than “X”) and since each letter is always encrypted with the same letter once the key is fixed, the distribution of letters in ciphertexts is the same as the one in plaintexts. Therefore, Caesar’s cipher is vulnerable to frequency-analysis attacks. Hence, with the event of computers, Caesar’s cipher can be easily broken either with brute-force attack or by frequency analysis (see Problem 4.1).

## 4.3 Affine Ciphers

In affine ciphers, each letter is encrypted using an affine substitution based on indices of letters in the alphabet. Formally:

*   Encryption:  <math alttext="upper E n c left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals a asterisk x plus b m o d m equals y" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>c</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>\*</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></math> ![upper E n c left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals a asterisk x plus b m o d m equals y](images/c04_24.png)[.]
*   Decryption:  <math alttext="upper D e c left-parenthesis y right-parenthesis equals a Superscript negative 1 Baseline left-parenthesis y minus b right-parenthesis m o d m equals x" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>D</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> ![upper D e c left-parenthesis y right-parenthesis equals a Superscript negative 1 Baseline left-parenthesis y minus b right-parenthesis m o d m equals x](images/c04_25.png).

where:

pair  <math alttext="left-parenthesis a comma b right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis a comma b right-parenthesis](images/c04_26.png) denotes the key of substitution

*m* denotes the number of letters in alphabet

 <math alttext="a Superscript negative 1 Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![a Superscript negative 1 Baseline](images/c04_27.png) is the multiplicative inverse of  <math alttext="a m o d m" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>m</mi></mrow></math> ![a m o d m](images/c04_28.png)

*l* denotes the letter in plaintext and *x*, its index in alphabet; i.e.  <math alttext="x equals upper I n d left-parenthesis l right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>I</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>l</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![x equals upper I n d left-parenthesis l right-parenthesis](images/c04_29.png)

 <math alttext="l prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![l prime](images/c04_30.png) denotes the letter in ciphertext and *y*, its index in alphabet; i.e.  <math alttext="l prime equals upper L e t left-parenthesis y right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>'</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![l prime equals upper L e t left-parenthesis y right-parenthesis](images/c04_31.png).

The intercept *b* can be any value in the interval  <math alttext="left-bracket 1 comma m minus 1 right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></math> ![left-bracket 1 comma m minus 1 right-bracket](images/c04_32.png). The decryption operation makes use of multiplicative inverse  <math alttext="a Superscript negative 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![a Superscript negative 1](images/c04_33.png). Therefore, not all values in  <math alttext="left-bracket 1 comma m minus 1 right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></math> ![left-bracket 1 comma m minus 1 right-bracket](images/c04_34.png) can be used for slope *a*. Indeed, *a* must be an element of  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript m Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>m</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript m Superscript asterisk](images/c04_35.png). Recall that an element *a* belongs to  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript m Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>m</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript m Superscript asterisk](images/c04_36.png) if and only if  <math alttext="upper G upper C upper D left-parenthesis m comma a right-parenthesis equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>G</mi><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![upper G upper C upper D left-parenthesis m comma a right-parenthesis equals 1](images/c04_37.png).

**Note**. Shift ciphers, including Caesar’s cipher, are affine ciphers with  <math alttext="a equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![a equals 0](images/c04_38.png).

**Example 4.2**

Let  <math alttext="script upper A" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="script">A</mi></math> ![script upper A](images/c04_39.png) be the Latin alphabet. Thus,  <math alttext="m equals 26" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>26</mn></mrow></math> ![m equals 26](images/c04_40.png).

 <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 26 Superscript asterisk Baseline equals StartSet 1 comma 3 comma 5 comma 7 comma 9 comma 11 comma 15 comma 17 comma 19 comma 21 comma 23 comma 25 EndSet period" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mrow><mn>26</mn></mrow><mo>\*</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>9</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>11</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>15</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>17</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>19</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>21</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>23</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>25</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 26 Superscript asterisk Baseline equals StartSet 1 comma 3 comma 5 comma 7 comma 9 comma 11 comma 15 comma 17 comma 19 comma 21 comma 23 comma 25 EndSet period](images/c04_41.png)

Therefore, the slope *a* can take distinct 12 values. For each element of  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 26 Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mrow><mn>26</mn></mrow><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 26 Superscript asterisk](images/c04_42.png) there exists a multiplicative inverse in  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 26 Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mrow><mn>26</mn></mrow><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 26 Superscript asterisk](images/c04_43.png) as shown in the following table:

![](images/c04_44.png)

Let  <math alttext="upper C upper A upper T" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>T</mi></mrow></math> ![upper C upper A upper T](images/c04_45.png) be the plaintext,  <math alttext="a equals 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![a equals 5](images/c04_46.png), and  <math alttext="b equals 7" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></math> ![b equals 7](images/c04_47.png).

The encryption is done as follows:

Resulting ciphertext is  <math alttext="upper V upper L upper C" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>V</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> ![upper V upper L upper C](images/c04_51.png). The decryption is done as follows:

*   First letter:

 <math alttext="x 1 equals 5 Superscript negative 1 Baseline left-parenthesis y 1 minus 7 right-parenthesis m o d 26 equals 21 left-parenthesis 22 minus 7 right-parenthesis m o d 26 equals 3" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>26</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>21</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>22</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>26</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> ![x 1 equals 5 Superscript negative 1 Baseline left-parenthesis y 1 minus 7 right-parenthesis m o d 26 equals 21 left-parenthesis 22 minus 7 right-parenthesis m o d 26 equals 3](images/c04_52.png) <math alttext="l 1 equals upper L e t left-parenthesis 3 right-parenthesis equals upper C period" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>l</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> ![l 1 equals upper L e t left-parenthesis 3 right-parenthesis equals upper C period](images/c04_53.png)

*   Second letter:

 <math alttext="x 2 equals 5 Superscript negative 1 Baseline left-parenthesis y 2 minus 7 right-parenthesis m o d 26 equals 21 left-parenthesis 12 minus 7 right-parenthesis m o d 26 equals 1" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>26</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>21</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>26</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![x 2 equals 5 Superscript negative 1 Baseline left-parenthesis y 2 minus 7 right-parenthesis m o d 26 equals 21 left-parenthesis 12 minus 7 right-parenthesis m o d 26 equals 1](images/c04_54.png) <math alttext="l 2 equals upper L e t left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis equals upper A period" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> ![l 2 equals upper L e t left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis equals upper A period](images/c04_55.png)

*   Third letter:

*Affine cipher security*

The total number of key combinations is  <math alttext="StartAbsoluteValue double-struck upper Z Subscript m Superscript asterisk Baseline EndAbsoluteValue asterisk m" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>m</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>\*</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow></math> ![StartAbsoluteValue double-struck upper Z Subscript m Superscript asterisk Baseline EndAbsoluteValue asterisk m](images/c04_58.png), where *m* denotes the cardinality of the alphabet and  <math alttext="StartAbsoluteValue double-struck upper Z Subscript m Superscript asterisk Baseline EndAbsoluteValue" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>m</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo>&#124;</mo></mrow></math> ![StartAbsoluteValue double-struck upper Z Subscript m Superscript asterisk Baseline EndAbsoluteValue](images/c04_59.png), the cardinality of the group  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript m Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>m</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript m Superscript asterisk](images/c04_60.png). For example, with Latin alphabet, the number of keys is  <math alttext="12 asterisk 26 equals 312" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>26</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>312</mn></mrow></math> ![12 asterisk 26 equals 312](images/c04_61.png). Even if an affine cipher provides more keys than Caesar’s cipher, it has the same flaws when computers are used in attacks.

## 4.4 Vigenere’s Cipher

To make attacks based on frequency analysis harder, polyalphabetic ciphers have been invented in the 16th century. One of the most famous polyalphabetic ciphers is the one invented by Blaise de Vigenere.

Vigenere’s cipher was proposed in the middle of the 16th century and it resisted all attempts to break it for three centuries. Vigenere’s cipher is an improvement of Caesar’s cipher. It makes use of several Caesar’s ciphers in sequence with different shift values. A table T, called Vigenere’s table, is defined as follows (see [Figure 4.1](#c04.xhtml#c04-fig-0001)): the first row is composed of the 26 letters of the Latin alphabet, the second row is one-position circular left shifting of the first row, …, the 26th row is one-position left circular shifting of the 25th row. Letters and table columns and rows are numbered from  <math alttext="0 to 25" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mtext>&#160;to&#160;</mtext><mn>25</mn></mrow></math> ![0 to 25](images/c04_62.png).

![Figure 4.1 Vigenere’s table.](images/c04f001.png)

[**Figure 4.1**](#c04.xhtml#rc04-fig-0001) Vigenere’s table.

*Encryption*:

1.  Before any encryption operation, the sender and receiver of message *M* must agree on a secret key word *k*.
2.  Key expansion *K*: the key word *k* is repeated until the size of the expanded key equals the size of the message *M* to encrypt.
3.  For each letter  <math alttext="upper M Subscript j Baseline left-parenthesis j equals 0 comma ellipsis comma l e n left-parenthesis upper M right-parenthesis minus 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![upper M Subscript j Baseline left-parenthesis j equals 0 comma ellipsis comma l e n left-parenthesis upper M right-parenthesis minus 1 right-parenthesis](images/c04_63.png) of message *M*, Vigenere’s table *T* is used for substitution as follows:

Let  <math alttext="upper I n d left-parenthesis upper M Subscript j Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>I</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper I n d left-parenthesis upper M Subscript j Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c04_64.png) be the index of letter  <math alttext="upper M Subscript j" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![upper M Subscript j](images/c04_65.png) and  <math alttext="upper I n d left-parenthesis upper K Subscript j Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>I</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper I n d left-parenthesis upper K Subscript j Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c04_66.png), the index of the *j*^(th) letter of the expanded key. Then, the encryption is

 <math alttext="upper E n c left-parenthesis upper M Subscript j Baseline right-parenthesis equals upper M prime Subscript j Baseline equals upper T left-parenthesis upper K Subscript j Baseline comma upper I n d left-parenthesis upper M Subscript j Baseline right-parenthesis right-parenthesis period" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>c</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>M</mi><mi>j</mi><mo>'</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mi>T</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>I</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> ![upper E n c left-parenthesis upper M Subscript j Baseline right-parenthesis equals upper M prime Subscript j Baseline equals upper T left-parenthesis upper K Subscript j Baseline comma upper I n d left-parenthesis upper M Subscript j Baseline right-parenthesis right-parenthesis period](images/c04_67.png)

*Decryption*:

For each letter  <math alttext="upper M prime Subscript j Baseline left-parenthesis j equals 0 comma ellipsis comma l e n left-parenthesis upper M prime right-parenthesis minus 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>M</mi><mi>j</mi><mo>'</mo></msubsup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![upper M prime Subscript j Baseline left-parenthesis j equals 0 comma ellipsis comma l e n left-parenthesis upper M prime right-parenthesis minus 1 right-parenthesis](images/c04_68.png) of the received message  <math alttext="upper M prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![upper M prime](images/c04_69.png), the decryption is performed as follows:

Go to raw  <math alttext="upper K Subscript j" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![upper K Subscript j](images/c04_70.png) of Vigenere’s table, locate the column of letter  <math alttext="upper M prime Subscript j" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>M</mi><mi>j</mi><mo>'</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![upper M prime Subscript j](images/c04_71.png) on raw  <math alttext="upper K Subscript j" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![upper K Subscript j](images/c04_72.png), say  <math alttext="c Subscript j" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![c Subscript j](images/c04_73.png). Then, use the letter  <math alttext="upper T left-parenthesis 0 comma c Subscript j Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>T</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper T left-parenthesis 0 comma c Subscript j Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c04_74.png).Formally,  <math alttext="upper D e c left-parenthesis upper M prime Subscript j right-parenthesis equals upper M Subscript j Baseline equals upper T left-parenthesis 0 comma upper C o l left-parenthesis upper K Subscript j Baseline comma upper M prime Subscript j right-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>D</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>M</mi><mi>j</mi><mo>'</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>T</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>l</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>M</mi><mi>j</mi><mo>'</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper D e c left-parenthesis upper M prime Subscript j right-parenthesis equals upper M Subscript j Baseline equals upper T left-parenthesis 0 comma upper C o l left-parenthesis upper K Subscript j Baseline comma upper M prime Subscript j right-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c04_75.png)

where  <math alttext="upper C o l left-parenthesis i comma l right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>l</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![upper C o l left-parenthesis i comma l right-parenthesis](images/c04_76.png) is a function that returns the column of letter *l* in raw *i* of table *T*.

The original version of Vigenere’s ciphering is based on a table (see [Figure 4.1](#c04.xhtml#c04-fig-0001)), because encryption and decryption were carried out by hand. With computers, the implementation of both operations does no more require the table. Indeed, Vigenere’s ciphering may be described without using a table as follows:

*   – Letters are ordered from  <math alttext="0 left-parenthesis upper A right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![0 left-parenthesis upper A right-parenthesis](images/c04_77.png) to  <math alttext="25 left-parenthesis upper Z right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>25</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![25 left-parenthesis upper Z right-parenthesis](images/c04_78.png).
*   – Encryption of *j*^(th) letter of message  <math alttext="upper M" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M](images/c04_79.png), denoted  <math alttext="upper M Subscript j Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![upper M Subscript j Baseline](images/c04_80.png), is:

 <math alttext="upper M prime Subscript j Baseline equals left-parenthesis upper M Subscript j Baseline plus upper K Subscript j Baseline right-parenthesis m o d 26" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>M</mi><mi>j</mi><mo>'</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>26</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![upper M prime Subscript j Baseline equals left-parenthesis upper M Subscript j Baseline plus upper K Subscript j Baseline right-parenthesis m o d 26](images/c04_81.png)( <math alttext="upper K Subscript j" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![upper K Subscript j](images/c04_82.png) is the *j*^(th) letter of the expanded key).

*   – Decryption of the *j*^(th) letter encrypted message  <math alttext="upper M prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![upper M prime](images/c04_83.png), denoted  <math alttext="upper M prime Subscript j" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>M</mi><mi>j</mi><mo>'</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![upper M prime Subscript j](images/c04_84.png), is:

 <math alttext="upper M Subscript j Baseline equals left-parenthesis upper M prime Subscript j Baseline minus upper K Subscript j Baseline right-parenthesis m o d 26 period" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><msub><mo>'</mo><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>&#8722;</mo><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>26</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> ![upper M Subscript j Baseline equals left-parenthesis upper M prime Subscript j Baseline minus upper K Subscript j Baseline right-parenthesis m o d 26 period](images/c04_85.png)

The second description of Vigenere’s cipher makes it an extension of Caesar’s cipher.
