**Example 5.1**

Let  <math alttext="b equals 100" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow></math> ![b equals 100](images/c05_223.png).

Any string of 100 bits is organized into four slices of 25 bits each. [Figure 5.4](#c05.xhtml#c05-fig-0004) shows the location of each bit on the four slices.

![Figure 5.4 Mapping of a 100-bit string to a state array.](images/c05f004.png)

[**Figure 5.4**](#c05.xhtml#rc05-fig-0004) Mapping of a 100-bit string to a state array.

##### *5.2.2.1.2 Step Mappings*

A round is composed of five step mappings (i.e. transformations) denoted by  <math alttext="theta comma rho comma pi comma chi" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#952;</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>&#961;</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>&#960;</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>&#967;</mi></mrow></math> ![theta comma rho comma pi comma chi](images/c05_224.png), and τ. With the exception of the mapping τ, the input *A* and output  <math alttext="upper A prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![upper A prime](images/c05_225.png) of step mappings are state arrays. Step mappings are defined as follows.

*Step mapping* θ

The effect of θ is to XOR each bit of the state with the parities of two column in the array. More formally, θ is specified as follows:

*   – For all pairs  <math alttext="left-parenthesis x comma z right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis x comma z right-parenthesis](images/c05_226.png) such that  <math alttext="0 less-than-or-equal-to x less-than 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![0 less-than-or-equal-to x less-than 5](images/c05_227.png) and  <math alttext="0 less-than-or-equal-to z less-than w" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow></math> ![0 less-than-or-equal-to z less-than w](images/c05_228.png) do:

 <math alttext="upper C left-bracket x comma z right-bracket equals upper A left-bracket x comma 0 comma z right-bracket circled-plus upper A left-bracket x comma 1 comma z right-bracket circled-plus upper A left-bracket x comma 2 comma z right-bracket circled-plus upper A left-bracket x comma 3 comma z right-bracket circled-plus upper A left-bracket x comma 4 comma z right-bracket" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>&#8853;</mo><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>&#8853;</mo><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper C left-bracket x comma z right-bracket equals upper A left-bracket x comma 0 comma z right-bracket circled-plus upper A left-bracket x comma 1 comma z right-bracket circled-plus upper A left-bracket x comma 2 comma z right-bracket circled-plus upper A left-bracket x comma 3 comma z right-bracket circled-plus upper A left-bracket x comma 4 comma z right-bracket](images/c05_229.png)

*   – For all pairs  <math alttext="left-parenthesis x comma z right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis x comma z right-parenthesis](images/c05_230.png) such that  <math alttext="0 less-than-or-equal-to x less-than 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![0 less-than-or-equal-to x less-than 5](images/c05_231.png) and  <math alttext="0 less-than-or-equal-to z less-than w" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow></math> ![0 less-than-or-equal-to z less-than w](images/c05_232.png) do:

 <math alttext="upper D left-bracket x comma z right-bracket equals upper C left-bracket left-parenthesis x minus 1 right-parenthesis m o d Baseline 5 comma z right-bracket circled-plus upper C left-bracket left-parenthesis x plus 1 right-parenthesis m o d Baseline 5 comma left-parenthesis z minus 1 right-parenthesis m o d w right-bracket" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>D</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>&#8853;</mo><mi>C</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>w</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper D left-bracket x comma z right-bracket equals upper C left-bracket left-parenthesis x minus 1 right-parenthesis m o d Baseline 5 comma z right-bracket circled-plus upper C left-bracket left-parenthesis x plus 1 right-parenthesis m o d Baseline 5 comma left-parenthesis z minus 1 right-parenthesis m o d w right-bracket](images/c05_233.png)

*   – For all triples  <math alttext="left-parenthesis x comma y comma z right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis x comma y comma z right-parenthesis](images/c05_234.png) such that  <math alttext="0 less-than-or-equal-to x less-than 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![0 less-than-or-equal-to x less-than 5](images/c05_235.png),  <math alttext="0 less-than-or-equal-to y less-than 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![0 less-than-or-equal-to y less-than 5](images/c05_236.png), and  <math alttext="0 less-than-or-equal-to z less-than w" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow></math> ![0 less-than-or-equal-to z less-than w](images/c05_237.png) do:

 <math alttext="upper A prime left-bracket x comma y comma z right-bracket equals upper A left-bracket x comma y comma z right-bracket circled-plus upper D left-bracket x comma z right-bracket" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>'</mo><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mi>D</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![upper A prime left-bracket x comma y comma z right-bracket equals upper A left-bracket x comma y comma z right-bracket circled-plus upper D left-bracket x comma z right-bracket](images/c05_238.png)

*Step mapping* ρ

The effect of ρ is to rotate the bits of each lane by a length, called offset, which depends on *x* and *y* coordinates of the lane. More formally, mapping ρ is specified as follows:

*   – For all *z* such that  <math alttext="0 less-than-or-equal-to z less-than-or-equal-to w" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow></math> ![0 less-than-or-equal-to z less-than-or-equal-to w](images/c05_239.png) do: <math alttext="upper A prime left-bracket 0 comma 0 comma z right-bracket equals upper A left-bracket 0 comma 0 comma z right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>A</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper A prime left-bracket 0 comma 0 comma z right-bracket equals upper A left-bracket 0 comma 0 comma z right-bracket](images/c05_240.png)

        – <math alttext="left-parenthesis x comma y right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis 1 comma 0 right-parenthesis" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis x comma y right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis 1 comma 0 right-parenthesis](images/c05_241.png)

*   – For  <math alttext="t equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![t equals 0](images/c05_242.png) to 23 do:

i) For *z* such that  <math alttext="0 z less-than w" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mi>z</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow></math> ![0 z less-than w](images/c05_243.png) do:  <math alttext="upper A prime left-bracket x comma y comma z right-bracket equals upper A left-bracket x comma y comma left-parenthesis z minus left-parenthesis t plus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis t plus 1 right-parenthesis slash 2 right-parenthesis m o d w right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>'</mo><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>w</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper A prime left-bracket x comma y comma z right-bracket equals upper A left-bracket x comma y comma left-parenthesis z minus left-parenthesis t plus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis t plus 1 right-parenthesis slash 2 right-parenthesis m o d w right-bracket](images/c05_244.png)

ii)  <math alttext="left-parenthesis x comma y right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis y comma left-parenthesis 2 x plus 3 y right-parenthesis m o d Baseline 5 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mn>5</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis x comma y right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis y comma left-parenthesis 2 x plus 3 y right-parenthesis m o d Baseline 5 right-parenthesis](images/c05_245.png)

*Step mapping* π

The effect of π is to rearrange the positions of the lanes. More formally, mapping π is specified as follows:

For all triples  <math alttext="left-parenthesis x comma y comma z right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis x comma y comma z right-parenthesis](images/c05_246.png) such that  <math alttext="0 less-than-or-equal-to x less-than 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![0 less-than-or-equal-to x less-than 5](images/c05_247.png),  <math alttext="0 less-than-or-equal-to y less-than 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![0 less-than-or-equal-to y less-than 5](images/c05_248.png), and  <math alttext="0 less-than-or-equal-to z less-than w" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow></math> ![0 less-than-or-equal-to z less-than w](images/c05_249.png) do:

 <math alttext="upper A prime left-bracket x comma y comma z right-bracket equals upper A left-bracket left-parenthesis x plus 3 y right-parenthesis m o d Baseline 5 comma y comma z right-bracket" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>'</mo><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper A prime left-bracket x comma y comma z right-bracket equals upper A left-bracket left-parenthesis x plus 3 y right-parenthesis m o d Baseline 5 comma y comma z right-bracket](images/c05_250.png)

*Step mapping* χ

The effect of χ is to XOR each bit with a nonlinear function. More formally, mapping χ is specified as follows:

For all triples  <math alttext="left-parenthesis x comma y comma z right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis x comma y comma z right-parenthesis](images/c05_251.png) such that  <math alttext="0 less-than-or-equal-to x less-than 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![0 less-than-or-equal-to x less-than 5](images/c05_252.png),  <math alttext="0 less-than-or-equal-to y less-than 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![0 less-than-or-equal-to y less-than 5](images/c05_253.png), and  <math alttext="0 less-than-or-equal-to z less-than normal w" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">w</mi></mrow></math> ![0 less-than-or-equal-to z less-than normal w](images/c05_254.png) do:

 <math alttext="upper A prime left-bracket x comma y comma z right-bracket equals upper A left-bracket x comma y comma z right-bracket circled-plus left-parenthesis upper A left-bracket left-parenthesis x plus 1 right-parenthesis m o d Baseline 5 comma y comma z right-bracket circled-plus 1 right-parenthesis logical-and left-parenthesis upper A left-bracket left-parenthesis x plus 2 right-parenthesis m o d Baseline 5 comma y comma z right-bracket right-parenthesis" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>'</mo><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>&#8853;</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8743;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper A prime left-bracket x comma y comma z right-bracket equals upper A left-bracket x comma y comma z right-bracket circled-plus left-parenthesis upper A left-bracket left-parenthesis x plus 1 right-parenthesis m o d Baseline 5 comma y comma z right-bracket circled-plus 1 right-parenthesis logical-and left-parenthesis upper A left-bracket left-parenthesis x plus 2 right-parenthesis m o d Baseline 5 comma y comma z right-bracket right-parenthesis](images/c05_255.png)

*Step mapping* τ

The effect of τ is to modify some of the bits of  <math alttext="upper L a n e left-parenthesis 0 comma 0 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>L</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper L a n e left-parenthesis 0 comma 0 right-parenthesis](images/c05_256.png) in a manner depending on the index of the round. The input of τ is a pair  <math alttext="left-parenthesis upper A comma i Subscript r Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>i</mi><mi>r</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis upper A comma i Subscript r Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c05_257.png), where *A* is a state array and  <math alttext="i Subscript r" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>i</mi><mi>r</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![i Subscript r](images/c05_258.png) a round index; its output is a state array  <math alttext="upper A prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![upper A prime](images/c05_259.png). More formally, mapping τ is specified as follows:

*   – For all triples  <math alttext="left-parenthesis x comma y comma z right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis x comma y comma z right-parenthesis](images/c05_260.png) such that  <math alttext="0 less-than-or-equal-to x less-than 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![0 less-than-or-equal-to x less-than 5](images/c05_261.png),  <math alttext="0 less-than-or-equal-to y less-than 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![0 less-than-or-equal-to y less-than 5](images/c05_262.png), and  <math alttext="0 less-than-or-equal-to z less-than w" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow></math> ![0 less-than-or-equal-to z less-than w](images/c05_263.png) do:  <math alttext="upper A prime left-bracket x comma y comma z right-bracket equals upper A left-bracket x comma y comma z right-bracket" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>'</mo><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper A prime left-bracket x comma y comma z right-bracket equals upper A left-bracket x comma y comma z right-bracket](images/c05_264.png)
    
*   –  <math alttext="upper R upper C equals 0 Superscript w" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mi>w</mi></msup></mrow></math> ![upper R upper C equals 0 Superscript w](images/c05_265.png) ( <math alttext="upper R upper C" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> ![upper R upper C](images/c05_266.png) is a string of *w* 0-bits)
*   –  <math alttext="l equals l o g 2 left-parenthesis b slash 25 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>l</mi><mi>o</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![l equals l o g 2 left-parenthesis b slash 25 right-parenthesis](images/c05_267.png)
*   – For *j*\=0 to *l* do:  <math alttext="upper R upper C left-bracket 2 Superscript j Baseline minus 1 right-bracket equals r c left-parenthesis j plus 7 i Subscript r Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mi>C</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>j</mi></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi><mi>c</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><msub><mi>i</mi><mi>r</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper R upper C left-bracket 2 Superscript j Baseline minus 1 right-bracket equals r c left-parenthesis j plus 7 i Subscript r Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c05_268.png)
*   – For all  <math alttext="z" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>z</mi></mrow></math> ![z](images/c05_269.png) such that  <math alttext="0 less-than-or-equal-to z less-than w" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow></math> ![0 less-than-or-equal-to z less-than w](images/c05_270.png) do:  <math alttext="upper A prime left-bracket 0 comma 0 comma z right-bracket equals upper A prime left-bracket 0 comma 0 comma z right-bracket circled-plus upper R upper C left-bracket z right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>'</mo><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>'</mo><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mi>R</mi><mi>C</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper A prime left-bracket 0 comma 0 comma z right-bracket equals upper A prime left-bracket 0 comma 0 comma z right-bracket circled-plus upper R upper C left-bracket z right-bracket](images/c05_271.png)

Function  <math alttext="r c left-parenthesis t right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>r</mi><mi>c</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![r c left-parenthesis t right-parenthesis](images/c05_272.png) is specified as follows:

*   – If  <math alttext="t m o d Baseline 255 equals 0 comma" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mn>255</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo></mrow></math> ![t m o d Baseline 255 equals 0 comma](images/c05_273.png) then return 1
*   –  <math alttext="upper R equals 10000000" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10000000</mn></mrow></math> ![upper R equals 10000000](images/c05_274.png) (*R* is an array of eight bits)
*   – For  <math alttext="i equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![i equals 1](images/c05_275.png) to 255 do:

  <math alttext="upper R equals 0 StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue upper R" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow></math> ![upper R equals 0 StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue upper R](images/c05_276.png)         <math alttext="upper R left-bracket 0 right-bracket equals upper R left-bracket 0 right-bracket circled-plus upper R left-bracket 8 right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> ![upper R left-bracket 0 right-bracket equals upper R left-bracket 0 right-bracket circled-plus upper R left-bracket 8 right-bracket](images/c05_277.png)

 <math alttext="upper R left-bracket 4 right-bracket equals upper R left-bracket 4 right-bracket upper R left-bracket 8 right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mrow><mo>\]</mo><mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow><mo>\[</mo></mrow><mn>4</mn><mrow><mo>\]</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi></mrow><mo>\[</mo></mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![upper R left-bracket 4 right-bracket equals upper R left-bracket 4 right-bracket upper R left-bracket 8 right-bracket](images/c05_278.png)    <math alttext="upper R left-bracket 6 right-bracket equals upper R left-bracket 6 right-bracket upper R left-bracket 8 right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>6</mn><mrow><mo>\]</mo><mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow><mo>\[</mo></mrow><mn>6</mn><mrow><mo>\]</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi></mrow><mo>\[</mo></mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![upper R left-bracket 6 right-bracket equals upper R left-bracket 6 right-bracket upper R left-bracket 8 right-bracket](images/c05_279.png)

 <math alttext="upper R equals upper T r u n c 8 left-bracket upper R right-bracket left-parenthesis keep the eight most minus left bits of upper R" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>T</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>u</mi><mi>n</mi><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>8</mn></msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>(</mo><mtext>keep&#160;the&#160;eight&#160;most</mtext><mo>&#8722;</mo><mtext>left&#160;bits&#160;of&#160;</mtext><mi>R</mi></mrow></math> ![upper R equals upper T r u n c 8 left-bracket upper R right-bracket left-parenthesis keep the eight most minus left bits of upper R](images/c05_280.png)

*   – Return *R*

##### *5.2.2.1.3 *Keccak\_p\[b, Nr\]* Permutation*

 <math alttext="upper K e c c a k bar p left-bracket b comma upper N Subscript r Baseline right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>K</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi><mo>\_</mo><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>r</mi></msub></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper K e c c a k bar p left-bracket b comma upper N Subscript r Baseline right-bracket](images/c05_281.png) permutation takes a string *S* of a bit-length of *b*, and a number of rounds  <math alttext="upper N Subscript r" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>r</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![upper N Subscript r](images/c05_282.png) and returns a bit string  <math alttext="upper S prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![upper S prime](images/c05_283.png) of the same length *b*. The permutation consists of  <math alttext="upper N Subscript r" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>r</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![upper N Subscript r](images/c05_284.png) rounds. More formally,  <math alttext="upper K e c c a k bar p left-bracket b comma upper N Subscript r Baseline right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>K</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi><mo>\_</mo><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>r</mi></msub></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper K e c c a k bar p left-bracket b comma upper N Subscript r Baseline right-bracket](images/c05_285.png) is specified as follows:

*   Convert the input bit string *S* into a state array *A*.
*    <math alttext="l equals l o g 2 left-parenthesis b slash 25 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>l</mi><mi>o</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![l equals l o g 2 left-parenthesis b slash 25 right-parenthesis](images/c05_286.png)
*   For  <math alttext="i Subscript r" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>i</mi><mi>r</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![i Subscript r](images/c05_287.png) =  <math alttext="12 plus 2 l minus upper N Subscript r" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>l</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>r</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![12 plus 2 l minus upper N Subscript r](images/c05_288.png) to  <math alttext="12 plus 2 l minus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>l</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![12 plus 2 l minus 1](images/c05_289.png) do:  <math alttext="upper A equals tau left-parenthesis chi left-parenthesis pi left-parenthesis rho left-parenthesis theta left-parenthesis upper A right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis comma i Subscript r Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>&#964;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>&#967;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>&#960;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>&#961;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>&#952;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>i</mi><mi>r</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper A equals tau left-parenthesis chi left-parenthesis pi left-parenthesis rho left-parenthesis theta left-parenthesis upper A right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis comma i Subscript r Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c05_290.png)
*   Convert the final state array *A* into a bit string  <math alttext="upper S prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![upper S prime](images/c05_291.png).

#### *5.2.2.1.4 Keccak\_f\[b\] Permutation*

 <math alttext="upper K e c c a k bar f left-bracket b right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>K</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi><mo>\_</mo><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper K e c c a k bar f left-bracket b right-bracket](images/c05_292.png) permutation is a specialization of the generic  <math alttext="upper K e c c a k bar p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>K</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi><mo>\_</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![upper K e c c a k bar p](images/c05_293.png) permutation, where the number of rounds  <math alttext="upper N Subscript r" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>r</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![upper N Subscript r](images/c05_294.png) is omitted, since it is fixed at 24.

 <math alttext="upper K e c c a k bar f left-bracket b right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>K</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi><mo>\_</mo><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper K e c c a k bar f left-bracket b right-bracket](images/c05_295.png) is equivalent to  <math alttext="upper K e c c a k bar p left-bracket b comma 12 plus 2 l o g 2 left-parenthesis b slash 25 right-parenthesis right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>K</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi><mo>\_</mo><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>l</mi><mi>o</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper K e c c a k bar p left-bracket b comma 12 plus 2 l o g 2 left-parenthesis b slash 25 right-parenthesis right-bracket](images/c05_296.png).

 <math alttext="upper K e c c a k bar p left-bracket 1600 comma 24 right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>K</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi><mo>\_</mo><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>1600</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>24</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper K e c c a k bar p left-bracket 1600 comma 24 right-bracket](images/c05_297.png) is the underlying permutation to all SHA-3 functions and it is equivalent to  <math alttext="upper K e c c a k bar f left-bracket 1600 right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>K</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi><mo>\_</mo><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>1600</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper K e c c a k bar f left-bracket 1600 right-bracket](images/c05_298.png).

#### 5.2.2.2 Sponge Construction

Sponge construction is a framework for specifying functions of binary data with arbitrary output length \[[3](#c05.xhtml#c05-bib-0003), [4](#c05.xhtml#c05-bib-0004)\]. The functions that the framework produces are called *sponge functions*. The latter are denoted by  <math alttext="upper S p o n g e left-bracket f comma upper P a d d i n g comma r right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>P</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>g</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper S p o n g e left-bracket f comma upper P a d d i n g comma r right-bracket](images/c05_299.png) where: *f* is a function that takes a string of length *b* and returns a string with the same length, *r* is called rate, and  <math alttext="upper P a d d i n g" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>g</mi></mrow></math> ![upper P a d d i n g](images/c05_300.png) is a padding rule.

A sponge function takes as inputs, a bit string *N* and an output bit-length *d*; and it returns a string *Z* of length <math alttext="d" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>d</mi></mrow></math> ![d](images/c05_301.png) (see [Figure 5.5](#c05.xhtml#c05-fig-0005)).

![Figure 5.5 Sponge construction.](images/c05f005.png)

[**Figure 5.5**](#c05.xhtml#rc05-fig-0005) Sponge construction.

In its generic form, given two inputs *x* and *m*,  <math alttext="upper P a d d i n g left-parenthesis x comma m right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![upper P a d d i n g left-parenthesis x comma m right-parenthesis](images/c05_302.png) returns a sequence of padding bits with a length such that  <math alttext="m plus l e n left-parenthesis upper P a d d i n g left-parenthesis x comma m right-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>P</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![m plus l e n left-parenthesis upper P a d d i n g left-parenthesis x comma m right-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c05_303.png) is a multiple of *x*. In sponge construction <math alttext="x equals r" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></math> ![x equals r](images/c05_304.png) and  <math alttext="m equals l e n left-parenthesis upper N right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![m equals l e n left-parenthesis upper N right-parenthesis](images/c05_305.png).

Bit string *N* is concatenated with the padding bits produced by  <math alttext="upper P a d d i n g" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>g</mi></mrow></math> ![upper P a d d i n g](images/c05_306.png) function to yield a sequence of bit strings  <math alttext="upper P 0 comma upper P 1 comma upper P 0 comma ellipsis comma upper P Subscript n minus 1 Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper P 0 comma upper P 1 comma upper P 0 comma ellipsis comma upper P Subscript n minus 1 Baseline](images/c05_307.png). Each bit string  <math alttext="upper P Subscript i Baseline comma 0 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than-or-equal-to n minus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![upper P Subscript i Baseline comma 0 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than-or-equal-to n minus 1](images/c05_308.png), has a fixed length of *r* bits. *n*, the number of strings, is equal to bit-length of padded input by *r*, i.e.  <math alttext="n equals left-parenthesis l e n left-parenthesis upper N right-parenthesis plus l e n left-parenthesis upper P a d d i n g left-parenthesis r comma l e n left-parenthesis upper N right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis slash r right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>P</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>)</mo><mo>)</mo><mo>/</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![n equals left-parenthesis l e n left-parenthesis upper N right-parenthesis plus l e n left-parenthesis upper P a d d i n g left-parenthesis r comma l e n left-parenthesis upper N right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis slash r right-parenthesis](images/c05_309.png). Notice that bit strings  <math alttext="upper P 0 comma upper P 1 comma upper P 0 comma ellipsis upper P Subscript n minus 1 Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper P 0 comma upper P 1 comma upper P 0 comma ellipsis upper P Subscript n minus 1 Baseline](images/c05_310.png) are equivalent to blocks *B*¹,  <math alttext="upper B squared" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math> ![upper B squared](images/c05_311.png)… in SHA-1 and SHA-2.

Sponge function is composed of two stages: *absorbing* and *squeezing*. In absorbing stage, the transformation of each bit string  <math alttext="upper P Subscript i" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![upper P Subscript i](images/c05_312.png),  <math alttext="1 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than-or-equal-to n minus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![1 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than-or-equal-to n minus 1](images/c05_313.png), is yielded by function *f* whose input is  <math alttext="upper P Subscript i" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![upper P Subscript i](images/c05_314.png) and the result of transformation of bit string  <math alttext="upper P Subscript i minus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper P Subscript i minus 1](images/c05_315.png). The bit string *S* yielded by the absorbing stage is used as input to the squeezing stage in which function *f* is applied *L* times and in each iteration, the *r* most-left bits of the result of function *f* are appended to a bit string *Z* initialized to empty string. The number of iterations of squeezing stage is  <math alttext="upper L equals left ceiling StartFraction d Over r EndFraction right ceiling" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>&#8968;</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mfrac></mrow><mo>&#8969;</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper L equals left ceiling StartFraction d Over r EndFraction right ceiling](images/c05_316.png).

The algorithm of  <math alttext="upper S p o n g e left-bracket f comma upper P a d d i n g comma r right-bracket left-parenthesis upper N comma d right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>P</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>g</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper S p o n g e left-bracket f comma upper P a d d i n g comma r right-bracket left-parenthesis upper N comma d right-parenthesis](images/c05_317.png) is specified as follows:

#### 5.2.2.3 SHA-3 Functions

When the sponge function is specialized for hashing, *N* represents the message, *d* the hash length, and *Z* the message digest. In SHA-3 hashing algorithms, the underlying function *f* is a  <math alttext="upper K e c c a k bar p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>K</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi><mo>\_</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![upper K e c c a k bar p](images/c05_331.png) permutation. Thus, the generic form of hashing functions produced by sponge construction is:

 <math alttext="upper H left-parenthesis upper N comma d right-parenthesis ModifyingBelow def With equals upper S p o n g e left-bracket upper K e c c a k bar p left-bracket b comma upper N Subscript r Baseline right-bracket comma upper P a d d i n g comma r right-bracket left-parenthesis upper N comma d right-parenthesis" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><munder><mrow><mtext>def</mtext></mrow><mo>=</mo></munder><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi><mo>\_</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo>\[</mo></mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mrow><mo>\]</mo><mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>P</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>g</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper H left-parenthesis upper N comma d right-parenthesis ModifyingBelow def With equals upper S p o n g e left-bracket upper K e c c a k bar p left-bracket b comma upper N Subscript r Baseline right-bracket comma upper P a d d i n g comma r right-bracket left-parenthesis upper N comma d right-parenthesis](images/c05_332.png)

*b*, the length of bit string size manipulated by  <math alttext="upper K e c c a k bar p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>K</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi><mo>\_</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![upper K e c c a k bar p](images/c05_333.png) permutation, is greater than *d*, the hash size.  <math alttext="c equals b minus r" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></math> ![c equals b minus r](images/c05_334.png) is called the capacity of the sponge function.

SHA-3 standard made the following choices:

*    <math alttext="b equals 1600" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1600</mn></mrow></math> ![b equals 1600](images/c05_335.png): the size of state arrays manipulated by mapping steps of Keccak-p permutation is 1600. The rationale of choice is that all SHA-3 variants have the same implementation support and 1600 is a multiple of 64 and 32; hence,  <math alttext="upper K e c c a k bar p left-bracket 1600 comma period right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>K</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi><mo>\_</mo><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>1600</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper K e c c a k bar p left-bracket 1600 comma period right-bracket](images/c05_336.png) favors 64-bit CPUs and remains efficient on 32-bit CPUs.
*    <math alttext="c equals 2 d" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>d</mi></mrow></math> ![c equals 2 d](images/c05_337.png): with such a capacity, there are no generic attacks with expected complexity below  <math alttext="2 Superscript d" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow></math> ![2 Superscript d](images/c05_338.png).
*    <math alttext="r equals 1600 minus 2 d" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1600</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>d</mi></mrow></math> ![r equals 1600 minus 2 d](images/c05_339.png): since by design  <math alttext="b equals r plus c" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></math> ![b equals r plus c](images/c05_340.png),  <math alttext="r equals 1600 minus 2 d" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1600</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>d</mi></mrow></math> ![r equals 1600 minus 2 d](images/c05_341.png).
*    <math alttext="upper N Subscript r Baseline equals 24" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>24</mn></mrow></math> ![upper N Subscript r Baseline equals 24](images/c05_342.png): 24 rounds are estimated sufficient to provide resistance against potential attacks.
*   SHA-3  <math alttext="upper P a d d i n g" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>g</mi></mrow></math> ![upper P a d d i n g](images/c05_343.png) function is labeled  <math alttext="quotation-mark p a d Baseline 10 asterisk 1 quotation-mark" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>"</mo><mi>p</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>d</mi><mn>10</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>"</mo></mrow></math> ![quotation-mark p a d Baseline 10 asterisk 1 quotation-mark](images/c05_344.png). It returns a string equal to  <math alttext="quotation-mark 1 StartAbsoluteValue StartAbsoluteValue 0 Superscript j Baseline EndAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 1 quotation-mark" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>"</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mn>0</mn><mi>j</mi></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow><mo>&#124;</mo></mrow><mo>&#124;</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mo>"</mo></mrow></math> ![quotation-mark 1 StartAbsoluteValue StartAbsoluteValue 0 Superscript j Baseline EndAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 1 quotation-mark](images/c05_345.png), where  <math alttext="j equals left-parenthesis left-parenthesis minus l e n left-parenthesis upper N right-parenthesis minus 2 right-parenthesis m o d r" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow></math> ![j equals left-parenthesis left-parenthesis minus l e n left-parenthesis upper N right-parenthesis minus 2 right-parenthesis m o d r](images/c05_346.png) and  <math alttext="0 Superscript j" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>0</mn><mi>j</mi></msup></mrow></math> ![0 Superscript j](images/c05_347.png) is a sequence of *j* 0-bits.  <math alttext="p a d Baseline 10 asterisk 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>d</mi><mn>10</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![p a d Baseline 10 asterisk 1](images/c05_348.png) is easy to specify and implement, while providing compliance regarding the randomness of padding bits.

Concrete sponge function model used to specify SHA-3 functions is labeled  <math alttext="upper K e c c a k left-bracket c right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>K</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper K e c c a k left-bracket c right-bracket](images/c05_349.png), where *c* is the capacity of the sponge function:

 <math alttext="upper K e c c a k left-bracket c right-bracket ModifyingBelow def With equals upper S p o n g e left-bracket upper K e c c a k bar p left-bracket 1600 comma 24 right-bracket comma p a d Baseline 10 asterisk 1 comma 1600 minus c right-bracket" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>K</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>\]</mo></mrow><munder><mrow><mtext>def</mtext></mrow><mo>=</mo></munder><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi><mo>\_</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo>\[</mo></mrow><mn>1600</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>24</mn><mrow><mo>\]</mo><mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>d</mi><mn>10</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1600</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper K e c c a k left-bracket c right-bracket ModifyingBelow def With equals upper S p o n g e left-bracket upper K e c c a k bar p left-bracket 1600 comma 24 right-bracket comma p a d Baseline 10 asterisk 1 comma 1600 minus c right-bracket](images/c05_350.png)

Given an input bit string *N* and an output length *d*,  <math alttext="upper K e c c a k left-bracket c right-bracket left-parenthesis upper N comma d right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>K</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper K e c c a k left-bracket c right-bracket left-parenthesis upper N comma d right-parenthesis](images/c05_351.png) produces a bit string of length *d*, which is a hash of *N*.

SHA-3 standard specified four hash functions based on sponge function whose capacity is the double of the hash bit-length:

*   SHA3-224  <math alttext="left-parenthesis upper M right-parenthesis equals upper K e c c a k left-bracket 448 right-bracket left-parenthesis upper M StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 01 comma 224 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>K</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>448</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>01</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>224</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis upper M right-parenthesis equals upper K e c c a k left-bracket 448 right-bracket left-parenthesis upper M StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 01 comma 224 right-parenthesis](images/c05_352.png)
*   SHA3-256  <math alttext="left-parenthesis upper M right-parenthesis equals upper K e c c a k left-bracket 512 right-bracket left-parenthesis upper M StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 01 comma 256 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>K</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>512</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>01</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>256</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis upper M right-parenthesis equals upper K e c c a k left-bracket 512 right-bracket left-parenthesis upper M StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 01 comma 256 right-parenthesis](images/c05_353.png)
*   SHA3-384  <math alttext="left-parenthesis upper M right-parenthesis equals upper K e c c a k left-bracket 768 right-bracket left-parenthesis upper M StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 01 comma 384 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>K</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>768</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>01</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>384</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis upper M right-parenthesis equals upper K e c c a k left-bracket 768 right-bracket left-parenthesis upper M StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 01 comma 384 right-parenthesis](images/c05_354.png)
*   SHA3-512  <math alttext="left-parenthesis upper M right-parenthesis equals upper K e c c a k left-bracket 1024 right-bracket left-parenthesis upper M StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 01 comma 512 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>K</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>1024</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>01</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>512</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis upper M right-parenthesis equals upper K e c c a k left-bracket 1024 right-bracket left-parenthesis upper M StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 01 comma 512 right-parenthesis](images/c05_355.png)

Notice the two additional paddings bits are appended to message *M* before launching the sponge function.

## 5.3 Message Authentication Codes

Message signature and message authentication codes (MACs) are the main applications of hash functions. Both mechanisms produce a key-based message digest for guaranteeing message integrity and authenticity. MACs differ from digital signatures as MAC values are both generated and verified using the same secret, while signatures may be generated by private keys and validated by public keys (see next chapters).

### 5.3.1 Objectives and Properties of MACs

A *message authentication code* (MAC) is a piece[^(11)](#c05.xhtml#c05-note-0011) of information associated with a message, which is used to authenticate message sender and to protect the integrity of message transmitted over an insecure network. MACs are used between two parties that share a secret. MAC algorithms have two parameters: a secrete key *k*, used to verify authenticity, and a hash function *H*, used to produce message digests (see [Figure 5.6](#c05.xhtml#c05-fig-0006)). A MAC system is composed of three components (or functions):

*   A key generation algorithm, which selects keys from the key space uniformly at random and periodically refreshed.
*   A tag generation algorithm, which returns a tag given the key and a message.
*   A verifying algorithm, which verifies the authenticity of the message given the key and the tag. If the hash computed by the receiver is identical to the received one, the message is accepted. Otherwise, it is rejected.

![Figure 5.6 Overall diagram of MAC algorithms.](images/c05f006.png)

[**Figure 5.6**](#c05.xhtml#rc05-fig-0006) Overall diagram of MAC algorithms.

This chapter focuses on the second component, i.e. generation of tags. The other components depend on the underlying cryptosystems either symmetric or asymmetric. In symmetric systems, the shared secret is used to encrypt and to sign. In public key cryptosystems, specific methods are used to generate private and public key and to generate signatures using hash functions and verifying them (see [Chapters 12](#c12.xhtml) and 13).

*MAC Properties*:

1.  P1: MAC systems should adapt to a large number of applications. Thus, they should accept arbitrary length of message, while producing a fixed length output.
2.  P2: preserve the integrity of message.
3.  P3: authenticate the message sender.

P1 and P2 properties are fulfilled by hash functions, while P3 is provided by using a shared secret key. It is worth noticing that MACs do not provide the property of non-repudiation assured by signatures, because any user who share the secret key can verify and generate MACs. In contrast to MAC, a digital signature is generated using the private key of a user. Since this private key is only accessible to its holder, a digital signature proves that a message was signed by none other than that private keyholder.

There exist two main standard categories of MACs:

1.  Hash function-based MACs, which are addressed in this chapter.
2.  Block cipher-based MACs, which are addressed in [Chapter 9](#c09.xhtml).

### 5.3.2 Hash Function-based MACs

The naïve, but simple, idea to designing MAC algorithms is to use the concatenation of key *k* and message *M* as input to the hash function leading to two design alternatives:

*    <math alttext="upper M upper A upper C left-parenthesis upper M comma k right-parenthesis equals upper H left-parenthesis k StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue upper M right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>C</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper M upper A upper C left-parenthesis upper M comma k right-parenthesis equals upper H left-parenthesis k StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue upper M right-parenthesis](images/c05_356.png), called secret prefix MAC.
*    <math alttext="upper M upper A upper C left-parenthesis upper M comma k right-parenthesis equals upper H left-parenthesis upper M StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue k right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>C</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper M upper A upper C left-parenthesis upper M comma k right-parenthesis equals upper H left-parenthesis upper M StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue k right-parenthesis](images/c05_357.png), called secret suffix MAC.

Secret prefix MACs, when used alone, are known to be vulnerable, while secrete suffix are not (see Problem 5.18). MAC algorithms used in practice, such as HMAC or KMAC, include additional mechanisms to provide secure MACs. Both HMAC and KMAC are called *keyed hash functions* and make use of a secret key, known as *MAC key*.

#### 5.3.2.1 HMAC

HMAC is the acronym for either *keyed-hash message authentication code* or *hash-based message authentication code*. HMAC was originally proposed by Bellare, Canetti, and Krawczyk \[[9](#c05.xhtml#c05-bib-0009)\] and then adopted by the IETF in 1997 \[[10](#c05.xhtml#c05-bib-0010)\]. HMAC is widely used in particular jointly with SHA-1 or SHA-2. Before being broken, MD5 also was widely used in HMAC implementations.

HMAC is a MAC family parameterized with the underlying hash function. HMAC instances are denoted HMAC-*H*, where *H* may be any hash function including SHA-1, MD5, SHA-256, SHA3-512, etc. HMAC takes two parameters *M*, the message, and *k*, the secrete key, and generates a digest  <math alttext="upper H upper M upper A upper C left-parenthesis upper M comma k right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>C</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper H upper M upper A upper C left-parenthesis upper M comma k right-parenthesis](images/c05_358.png) of a length of *n* bits, which is the same as the hash function output bit-length. HMAC can be used with any secret key length. However, secret keys with length less than the length of block size processed by the hash function are strongly discouraged, because they would decrease the security strength of the HMAC as a whole. [Figure 5.7](#c05.xhtml#c05-fig-0007) illustrates the diagram of HMAC. HMAC is a double hashing method to provide resistant MACs.

![Figure 5.7 HMAC diagram.](images/c05f007.png)

[**Figure 5.7**](#c05.xhtml#rc05-fig-0007) HMAC diagram.

 <math alttext="i k prime denotes the block yielded after XORing the expanded key k prime with i upper P a d" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>k</mi><mo>'</mo><mtext>&#160;denotes&#160;the&#160;block&#160;yielded&#160;after&#160;XORing&#160;the&#160;expanded&#160;key&#160;</mtext><mi>k</mi><mo>'</mo><mtext>&#160;with&#160;</mtext><mi>i</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow></math> ![i k prime denotes the block yielded after XORing the expanded key k prime with i upper P a d](images/c05_359.png) block.

 <math alttext="o k Superscript prime Baseline denotes the block yielded after XORing the expanded key k prime with o upper P a d" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>o</mi><msup><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mtext>&#160;denotes&#160;the&#160;block&#160;yielded&#160;after&#160;XORing&#160;the&#160;expanded&#160;key&#160;</mtext><mi>k</mi><mo>'</mo><mtext>&#160;with&#160;</mtext><mi>o</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow></math> ![o k Superscript prime Baseline denotes the block yielded after XORing the expanded key k prime with o upper P a d](images/c05_360.png) block.

 <math alttext="h Subscript left-parenthesis i right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![h Subscript left-parenthesis i right-parenthesis](images/c05_361.png) denotes the inner hash and  <math alttext="upper P left-parenthesis h Subscript left-parenthesis i right-parenthesis Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper P left-parenthesis h Subscript left-parenthesis i right-parenthesis Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c05_362.png), the block yielded after padding  <math alttext="h Subscript left-parenthesis i right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![h Subscript left-parenthesis i right-parenthesis](images/c05_363.png).

Given a message *M* and a secret key *k*, the yielded MAC is expressed as:

 <math alttext="upper H upper M upper A upper C left-parenthesis upper M comma k right-parenthesis equals upper H left-parenthesis left-parenthesis k prime o upper P a d right-parenthesis StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue left-parenthesis upper H left-parenthesis k prime i upper P a d StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue upper M right-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>C</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>o</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>i</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>d</mi><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper H upper M upper A upper C left-parenthesis upper M comma k right-parenthesis equals upper H left-parenthesis left-parenthesis k prime o upper P a d right-parenthesis StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue left-parenthesis upper H left-parenthesis k prime i upper P a d StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue upper M right-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c05_364.png)

which is computed with the following procedure:

 <math alttext="upper H upper M upper A upper C left-parenthesis upper M comma k right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>C</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper H upper M upper A upper C left-parenthesis upper M comma k right-parenthesis](images/c05_365.png) description

*Notations*:

*   – *M* is the message for which integrity and authentication are required.
*   – *n* and *L* denote the output bit-length and the block size of the underlying hash function *H*, respectively.

Then append zeros to the end of  <math alttext="upper H left-parenthesis k right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper H left-parenthesis k right-parenthesis](images/c05_379.png) and use the resulting bit-string as expanded key  <math alttext="k prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![k prime](images/c05_380.png) of a bit-length of *L* bits.
