In the encryption (resp. decryption) operation, the initial input state is added to the key words  <math alttext="upper K upper W 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>K</mi><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper K upper W 0](images/c07_378.png) to  <math alttext="upper K upper W 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>K</mi><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper K upper W 3](images/c07_379.png) (resp.  <math alttext="upper K upper W Subscript upper N r asterisk 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>K</mi><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mi>r</mi><mo>\*</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper K upper W Subscript upper N r asterisk 4](images/c07_380.png) to  <math alttext="upper K upper W Subscript upper N r asterisk 4 plus 3 Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>K</mi><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mi>r</mi><mo>\*</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> ![upper K upper W Subscript upper N r asterisk 4 plus 3 Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c07_381.png) before performing the first encryption (resp. decryption) round.

### 7.3.5 Key Expansion

Key expansion takes a key *K* of 128, 192, or 256 bits, and generates  <math alttext="upper N r plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>N</mi><mi>r</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![upper N r plus 1](images/c07_382.png) round keys grouped in a 4-byte-word array, denoted *W*. The total number of 4-byte words of *W* array is of  <math alttext="left-parenthesis upper N r plus 1 right-parenthesis asterisk 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mi>r</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>\*</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis upper N r plus 1 right-parenthesis asterisk 4](images/c07_383.png): four words are added to the initial state input and four words for each of the  <math alttext="upper N r" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>N</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow></math> ![upper N r](images/c07_384.png) rounds. The four words,  <math alttext="upper W left-bracket 4 upper R right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>W</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>R</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper W left-bracket 4 upper R right-bracket](images/c07_385.png),  <math alttext="upper W left-bracket 4 upper R plus 1 right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>W</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>R</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper W left-bracket 4 upper R plus 1 right-bracket](images/c07_386.png),  <math alttext="upper W left-bracket 4 upper R plus 2 right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>W</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>R</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper W left-bracket 4 upper R plus 2 right-bracket](images/c07_387.png), and  <math alttext="upper W left-bracket 4 upper R plus 3 right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>W</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>R</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper W left-bracket 4 upper R plus 3 right-bracket](images/c07_388.png), form the key of round *R*.

The round keys are computed recursively; i.e. the key of round *R* is computed from that of round  <math alttext="upper R minus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![upper R minus 1](images/c07_389.png). To simplify the key expansion description, we focus on a key length of 128 bits (i.e.  <math alttext="upper N k equals 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>N</mi><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></math> ![upper N k equals 4](images/c07_390.png)),[⁷](#c07.xhtml#c07-note-0007) which is illustrated by [Figure 7.16](#c07.xhtml#c07-fig-0016):

![Figure 7.16 Key expansion for a key-bit length of 128.](images/c07f016.png)

[**Figure 7.16**](#c07.xhtml#rc07-fig-0016) Key expansion for a key-bit length of 128.

*   Key *K* is mapped to a state of four words:  <math alttext="upper W left-bracket 0 right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>W</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper W left-bracket 0 right-bracket](images/c07_391.png),  <math alttext="upper W left-bracket 1 right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>W</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper W left-bracket 1 right-bracket](images/c07_392.png),  <math alttext="upper W left-bracket 2 right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>W</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper W left-bracket 2 right-bracket](images/c07_393.png),  <math alttext="upper W left-bracket 3 right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>W</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper W left-bracket 3 right-bracket](images/c07_394.png). Therefore, the first AddRo     undKey call in encryption and decryption adds the cipher key to initial block.
*   The words of the key of round *R* is computed as:

 <math alttext="upper W left-bracket 4 asterisk upper R right-bracket equals upper W left-bracket 4 left-parenthesis upper R minus 1 right-parenthesis right-bracket circled-plus g left-parenthesis upper W left-bracket 4 upper R minus 1 right-bracket right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>W</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>\*</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>W</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>&#8853;</mo><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>W</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>R</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper W left-bracket 4 asterisk upper R right-bracket equals upper W left-bracket 4 left-parenthesis upper R minus 1 right-parenthesis right-bracket circled-plus g left-parenthesis upper W left-bracket 4 upper R minus 1 right-bracket right-parenthesis](images/c07_395.png)

 <math alttext="upper W left-bracket 4 asterisk upper R plus j right-bracket equals upper W left-bracket 4 upper R plus j minus 1 right-bracket circled-plus upper W left-bracket 4 left-parenthesis upper R minus 1 right-parenthesis plus j right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>W</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>\*</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>W</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>R</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mi>W</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper W left-bracket 4 asterisk upper R plus j right-bracket equals upper W left-bracket 4 upper R plus j minus 1 right-bracket circled-plus upper W left-bracket 4 left-parenthesis upper R minus 1 right-parenthesis plus j right-bracket](images/c07_396.png), for  <math alttext="j equals 1 comma 2 comma 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> ![j equals 1 comma 2 comma 3](images/c07_397.png)

The function  <math alttext="g left-parenthesis upper Z right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![g left-parenthesis upper Z right-parenthesis](images/c07_398.png) has one-word input and output. It consists in three operations:

*    <math alttext="upper Z prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![upper Z prime](images/c07_399.png) is yielded using a one-byte left rotation of input *Z*
*   using the S-Box, substitute each byte of  <math alttext="upper Z prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![upper Z prime](images/c07_400.png) and output  <math alttext="upper Z prime prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>'</mo><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![upper Z prime prime](images/c07_401.png)
*   XOR  <math alttext="upper Z prime prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>'</mo><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![upper Z prime prime](images/c07_402.png) with a known round constant  <math alttext="upper R c o n left-bracket upper R n d right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>n</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper R c o n left-bracket upper R n d right-bracket](images/c07_403.png)

Therefore,  <math alttext="g left-parenthesis upper Z right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![g left-parenthesis upper Z right-parenthesis](images/c07_404.png) is defined by:  <math alttext="g left-parenthesis upper Z right-parenthesis ModifyingBelow Below ModifyingBelow def With bar With bar upper S u b upper B y t e s left-parenthesis upper L upper R o t a t e left-parenthesis upper Z right-parenthesis right-parenthesis circled-plus upper R c o n left-bracket upper R n d right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><munder accentunder="true"><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mtext>def</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext></mrow><mo stretchy="true">\_</mo></munder><mo stretchy="true">\_</mo></munder><mi>S</mi><mi>u</mi><mi>b</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>s</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mi>R</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>n</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![g left-parenthesis upper Z right-parenthesis ModifyingBelow Below ModifyingBelow def With bar With bar upper S u b upper B y t e s left-parenthesis upper L upper R o t a t e left-parenthesis upper Z right-parenthesis right-parenthesis circled-plus upper R c o n left-bracket upper R n d right-bracket](images/c07_405.png)

The  <math alttext="upper R c o n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper R c o n](images/c07_406.png) is an array, which associates one 4-byte constant word with each round *R* as follows:  <math alttext="upper R c o n left-bracket upper R right-bracket equals left-bracket x Superscript upper R minus 1 Baseline comma 00 comma 00 comma 00 right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>n</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>00</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>00</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>00</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper R c o n left-bracket upper R right-bracket equals left-bracket x Superscript upper R minus 1 Baseline comma 00 comma 00 comma 00 right-bracket](images/c07_407.png), where  <math alttext="x Superscript upper R minus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![x Superscript upper R minus 1](images/c07_408.png) denotes a modular exponentiation in the field (see Section 3.3.2). The three rightmost bytes of  <math alttext="upper R c o n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper R c o n](images/c07_409.png) are zeros and the leftmost bytes are given in [Table 7.11](#c07.xhtml#c07-tbl-0011).

![Table 7.11 Values of the leftmost byte of the constant vector Rcon.](images/c07_410.png)

[**Table 7.11**](#c07.xhtml#rc07-tbl-0011) Values of the leftmost byte of the constant vector Rcon.

Pseudocode below is a specification of the key expansion function for any value of  <math alttext="upper N k" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>N</mi><mi>k</mi></mrow></math> ![upper N k](images/c07_420.png) (4, 6, or 8).

*SubWord(Z)* is a function that takes a 4-byte input word *Z* and applies the S-Box to each of the four bytes to yield an output word  <math alttext="upper Z prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![upper Z prime](images/c07_437.png). *RotWord(Z)* is a function that takes a 4-byte input word  <math alttext="upper Z equals left-bracket upper Z 0 comma upper Z 1 comma upper Z 2 comma upper Z 3 right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Z</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Z</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper Z equals left-bracket upper Z 0 comma upper Z 1 comma upper Z 2 comma upper Z 3 right-bracket](images/c07_438.png) and outputs the permuted word  <math alttext="upper Z prime equals left-bracket upper Z 1 comma upper Z 2 comma upper Z 3 comma upper Z 0 right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>'</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Z</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Z</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper Z prime equals left-bracket upper Z 1 comma upper Z 2 comma upper Z 3 comma upper Z 0 right-bracket](images/c07_439.png). *Rcon(i)* is a constant array.

### 7.3.6 Mathematical Description of AES

AES computations are performed over the extension field  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>8</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 8](images/c07_440.png). Therefore, the design rationale and the proof of correctness of AES rely on mathematical notions. This section aims at describing AES operations using extension field computations. The proof of correctness of AES transformations is addressed in Problems 7.10 and 7.11.

The extension field  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>8</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 8](images/c07_441.png), also Galois field  <math alttext="upper G upper F left-parenthesis 2 Superscript 8 Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>G</mi><mi>F</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>8</mn></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper G upper F left-parenthesis 2 Superscript 8 Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c07_442.png), is the set of elements  <math alttext="StartSet 0 comma 1 comma ellipsis comma 255 EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>255</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></math> ![StartSet 0 comma 1 comma ellipsis comma 255 EndSet](images/c07_443.png); it is used to represent and process bytes in AES transformations. *We advise the reader to refer to chapter* [3](#c03.xhtml) *to learn the fundamentals of finite fields and to do some exercises included in that chapter*.

#### 7.3.6.1 Data Representation and Operations on Data

##### *7.3.6.1.1 Byte Representation and Operations on Bytes*

A byte *b* is a concatenation of eight bits  <math alttext="b 7 b 6 b 5 b 4 b 3 b 2 b 1 b 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>7</mn></msub><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>5</mn></msub><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![b 7 b 6 b 5 b 4 b 3 b 2 b 1 b 0](images/c07_444.png) and it is interpreted as an element of an extension field using a polynomial representation; i.e.  <math alttext="b left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals b 7 x Superscript 7 Baseline plus b 6 x Superscript 6 Baseline plus b 5 x Superscript 5 Baseline plus b 4 x Superscript 4 Baseline plus b 3 x cubed plus b 2 x squared plus b 1 x plus b 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>7</mn></msub><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>7</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>6</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>5</mn></msub><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>5</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![b left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals b 7 x Superscript 7 Baseline plus b 6 x Superscript 6 Baseline plus b 5 x Superscript 5 Baseline plus b 4 x Superscript 4 Baseline plus b 3 x cubed plus b 2 x squared plus b 1 x plus b 0](images/c07_445.png). A byte may be written in base 2 or in base 16. The notation used to write a constant in base 16 is  <math alttext="left-bracket period period right-bracket Subscript 16" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>..</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![left-bracket period period right-bracket Subscript 16](images/c07_446.png); for example  <math alttext="left-bracket 21 right-bracket Subscript 16" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>21</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![left-bracket 21 right-bracket Subscript 16](images/c07_447.png) represents the value 33 in base 10; and  <math alttext="left-bracket fd right-bracket Subscript 16" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mtext>fd</mtext></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![left-bracket fd right-bracket Subscript 16](images/c07_448.png) the value 253.

*   ***Byte addition***

Bytes are elements of the extension field  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>8</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 8](images/c07_449.png). Addition of elements of extension field  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>8</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 8](images/c07_450.png) is denoted ⊕, which is the bitwise XOR.

**Example 7.2**

Let  <math alttext="a equals 11011011 and b equals 11100011 Subscript 2 Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>11011011</mn><mtext>and&#160;</mtext><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mn>11100011</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![a equals 11011011 and b equals 11100011 Subscript 2 Baseline](images/c07_451.png) be two bytes in binary representation. In polynomial representation, we have:

 <math alttext="a left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 7 Baseline plus x Superscript 6 Baseline plus x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x cubed plus x plus 1 and b left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 7 Baseline plus x Superscript 6 Baseline plus x Superscript 5 Baseline plus x plus 1" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>7</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>6</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;and&#160;</mtext><mi>b</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>7</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>6</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>5</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![a left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 7 Baseline plus x Superscript 6 Baseline plus x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x cubed plus x plus 1 and b left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 7 Baseline plus x Superscript 6 Baseline plus x Superscript 5 Baseline plus x plus 1](images/c07_452.png)

In extension field  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>8</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 8](images/c07_453.png), the coefficients in the polynomials are binaries. Hence,  <math alttext="c equals a plus b" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></math> ![c equals a plus b](images/c07_454.png) is yielded by:  <math alttext="c left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals a left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis plus b left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 5 Baseline plus x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x cubed" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>5</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></math> ![c left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals a left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis plus b left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 5 Baseline plus x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x cubed](images/c07_455.png)

With the bitwise XOR operation:

 <math alttext="a circled-plus b equals left-parenthesis 11011011 Subscript 2 Baseline right-parenthesis circled-plus left-parenthesis 11100011 Subscript 2 Baseline right-parenthesis equals 00111000 Subscript 2" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8853;</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mrow><mn>11011011</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8853;</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mrow><mn>11100011</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mn>00111000</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![a circled-plus b equals left-parenthesis 11011011 Subscript 2 Baseline right-parenthesis circled-plus left-parenthesis 11100011 Subscript 2 Baseline right-parenthesis equals 00111000 Subscript 2](images/c07_456.png)

***Byte multiplication***

Byte multiplication, denoted •, is performed with the irreducible polynomial  <math alttext="m left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 8 Baseline plus x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x cubed plus x plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>8</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![m left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 8 Baseline plus x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x cubed plus x plus 1](images/c07_457.png). Notice that since the irreducible polynomial  <math alttext="m left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![m left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c07_458.png) is of degree 8, any multiplication of two bytes results in a value represented by a byte. Any element *b* and its inverse  <math alttext="b Superscript negative 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![b Superscript negative 1](images/c07_459.png) are both elements of  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>8</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 8](images/c07_460.png). The irreducible polynomial used in AES has a useful property, which makes it easy to implement the operations especially in hardware.

**Example 7.3**

Let  <math alttext="a equals 11011011 Subscript 2 Baseline and b equals 00000011 Subscript 2 Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mn>11011011</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mtext>&#160;and&#160;</mtext><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mn>00000011</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![a equals 11011011 Subscript 2 Baseline and b equals 00000011 Subscript 2 Baseline](images/c07_461.png) be two bytes in binary representation.

b](images/c07_462.png) is computed as follows:  <math alttext="StartLayout 1st Row c left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals a left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis asterisk b left-parenthesis x Let  <math alttext="a prime equals 10000111 Subscript 2 Baseline and b prime equals 01010110 Subscript 2 Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>'</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mn>10000111</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mtext>&#160;and&#160;</mtext><mi>b</mi><mo>'</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mn>01010110</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![a prime equals 10000111 Subscript 2 Baseline and b prime equals 01010110 Subscript 2 Baseline](images/c07_465.png) be two bytes in binary representation.

 <math alttext="c prime equals a prime bullet b prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>'</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>'</mo><mo>&#8226;</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![c prime equals a prime bullet b prime](images/c07_466.png) is computed as follows:

Notice that  <math alttext="b prime is the multiplicative inverse of prime m o d left-parenthesis x Superscript 8 Baseline plus x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x cubed plus x plus 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>'</mo><mtext>&#160;is&#160;the&#160;multiplicative&#160;inverse&#160;of&#160;</mtext><mo>'</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>8</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![b prime is the multiplicative inverse of prime m o d left-parenthesis x Superscript 8 Baseline plus x Superscript 4 Baseline plus x cubed plus x plus 1 right-parenthesis](images/c07_469.png).

##### *7.3.6.1.2 Word Representation and Operations on Words*

A 4-byte word can be represented as a polynomial of degree 3 with coefficients in  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>8</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 8](images/c07_470.png). More precisely, a word  <math alttext="upper A equals left-bracket upper A 0 comma upper A 1 comma upper A 2 comma upper A 3 right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper A equals left-bracket upper A 0 comma upper A 1 comma upper A 2 comma upper A 3 right-bracket](images/c07_471.png) is represented as a polynomial

 <math alttext="upper A left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals upper A 3 x cubed plus upper A 2 x squared plus upper A 1 x plus upper A 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper A left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals upper A 3 x cubed plus upper A 2 x squared plus upper A 1 x plus upper A 0](images/c07_472.png), where  <math alttext="upper A Subscript i equals 0 comma 1 comma 2 comma 3 Baseline element-of upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 8 Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8712;</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>8</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper A Subscript i equals 0 comma 1 comma 2 comma 3 Baseline element-of upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 8 Baseline](images/c07_473.png).

*   ***Word addition***

The addition of two words  <math alttext="upper A equals left-bracket upper A 0 comma upper A 1 comma upper A 2 comma upper A 3 right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper A equals left-bracket upper A 0 comma upper A 1 comma upper A 2 comma upper A 3 right-bracket](images/c07_474.png) and  <math alttext="upper B equals left-bracket upper B 0 comma upper B 1 comma upper B 2 comma upper B 3 right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper B equals left-bracket upper B 0 comma upper B 1 comma upper B 2 comma upper B 3 right-bracket](images/c07_475.png) is yielded by the bitwise XOR of their coefficients. More precisely,  <math alttext="upper C equals upper A plus upper B" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow></math> ![upper C equals upper A plus upper B](images/c07_476.png) is yielded as follows:

 <math alttext="upper C equals left-bracket upper A 0 circled-plus upper B 0 comma upper A 1 circled-plus upper B 1 comma upper A 2 circled-plus upper B 2 comma upper A 3 circled-plus upper B 3 right-bracket" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper C equals left-bracket upper A 0 circled-plus upper B 0 comma upper A 1 circled-plus upper B 1 comma upper A 2 circled-plus upper B 2 comma upper A 3 circled-plus upper B 3 right-bracket](images/c07_477.png)

Alternatively, we can write:  <math alttext="upper C left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis upper A 3 circled-plus upper B 3 right-parenthesis x cubed plus left-parenthesis upper A 2 circled-plus upper B 2 right-parenthesis x squared plus left-parenthesis upper A 1 circled-plus upper B 1 right-parenthesis x plus left-parenthesis upper A 0 circled-plus upper B 0 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper C left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis upper A 3 circled-plus upper B 3 right-parenthesis x cubed plus left-parenthesis upper A 2 circled-plus upper B 2 right-parenthesis x squared plus left-parenthesis upper A 1 circled-plus upper B 1 right-parenthesis x plus left-parenthesis upper A 0 circled-plus upper B 0 right-parenthesis](images/c07_478.png).

*   ***Word multiplication***

Word multiplication is not used in AES transformations. Rather, the modular product of words, denoted ⊗, is used instead. The modular product of two words  <math alttext="upper A equals left-bracket upper A 0 comma upper A 1 comma upper A 2 comma upper A 3 right-bracket and upper B equals left-bracket upper B 0 comma upper B 1 comma upper B 2 comma upper B 3 right-bracket comma upper D equals upper A upper B" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;and&#160;</mtext><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>B</mi></mrow></math> ![upper A equals left-bracket upper A 0 comma upper A 1 comma upper A 2 comma upper A 3 right-bracket and upper B equals left-bracket upper B 0 comma upper B 1 comma upper B 2 comma upper B 3 right-bracket comma upper D equals upper A upper B](images/c07_479.png) is computed in two steps:

*   2) Reduce the polynomial  <math alttext="upper C left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper C left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c07_482.png):

 <math alttext="upper C left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper C left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c07_483.png) is a polynomial of degree 6 and does not represent a 4-byte word. That is why a reduction with a polynomial of degree 4 is required. More precisely, the polynomial  <math alttext="x Superscript 4 Baseline plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![x Superscript 4 Baseline plus 1](images/c07_484.png) is used in AES:

**Notes**

1.  The polynomial  <math alttext="x Superscript 4 Baseline plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![x Superscript 4 Baseline plus 1](images/c07_490.png) is not an irreducible polynomial, because it has 1 as a root. Thus, the multiplicative inverse does not exist for some elements  <math alttext="m o d x Superscript 4 plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![m o d x Superscript 4 plus 1](images/c07_491.png). However, it is not important, because AES makes use of only two polynomials that both have inverses: 
    *   – Polynomial  <math alttext="upper A left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals left-bracket 03 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x cubed plus left-bracket 01 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x squared plus left-bracket 01 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x plus left-bracket 02 right-bracket Subscript 16" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>03</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>01</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>01</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>02</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper A left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals left-bracket 03 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x cubed plus left-bracket 01 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x squared plus left-bracket 01 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x plus left-bracket 02 right-bracket Subscript 16](images/c07_492.png) is used in MixColumns; and its inverse is  <math alttext="upper A left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals left-bracket 0 normal b right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x cubed plus left-bracket 0 normal d right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x squared plus left-bracket 09 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x plus left-bracket 0 normal e right-bracket Subscript 16" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>09</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper A left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals left-bracket 0 normal b right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x cubed plus left-bracket 0 normal d right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x squared plus left-bracket 09 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x plus left-bracket 0 normal e right-bracket Subscript 16](images/c07_493.png). One can easily check that  <math alttext="upper A left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis asterisk upper A left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 1 m o d left-parenthesis x Superscript 4 Baseline plus 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo><mi>A</mi><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper A left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis asterisk upper A left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 1 m o d left-parenthesis x Superscript 4 Baseline plus 1 right-parenthesis](images/c07_494.png).
    *   – Polynomial  <math alttext="upper A left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x cubed" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></math> ![upper A left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x cubed](images/c07_495.png) is used in key expansion; and its inverse is  <math alttext="upper A left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals x" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> ![upper A left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals x](images/c07_496.png), because  <math alttext="x cubed asterisk x m o d left-parenthesis x Superscript 4 Baseline plus 1 right-parenthesis equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>\*</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![x cubed asterisk x m o d left-parenthesis x Superscript 4 Baseline plus 1 right-parenthesis equals 1](images/c07_497.png).
2.  AES selected the polynomial  <math alttext="x Superscript 4 Baseline plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![x Superscript 4 Baseline plus 1](images/c07_498.png), due to its simplicity of reduction. Indeed, it provides the following reduction:  <math alttext="x Superscript i Baseline m o d left-parenthesis x Superscript 4 Baseline plus 1 right-parenthesis equals x Superscript i m o d Baseline 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![x Superscript i Baseline m o d left-parenthesis x Superscript 4 Baseline plus 1 right-parenthesis equals x Superscript i m o d Baseline 4](images/c07_499.png).

Thus,  <math alttext="left-bracket 11 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline bullet left-bracket cd right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline equals left-bracket normal a Baseline 9 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>11</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub><mo>&#8226;</mo><msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mtext>cd</mtext></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![left-bracket 11 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline bullet left-bracket cd right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline equals left-bracket normal a Baseline 9 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline](images/c07_519.png).

Therefore,  <math alttext="upper C Superscript left-parenthesis 1 asterisk 2 right-parenthesis Baseline left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals left-bracket 72 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x Superscript 6 Baseline plus left-bracket 34 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x Superscript 5 Baseline plus left-bracket normal a Baseline 9 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x cubed" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mtext>\*</mtext><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>72</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>6</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>34</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>5</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></math> ![upper C Superscript left-parenthesis 1 asterisk 2 right-parenthesis Baseline left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals left-bracket 72 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x Superscript 6 Baseline plus left-bracket 34 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x Superscript 5 Baseline plus left-bracket normal a Baseline 9 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x cubed](images/c07_520.png)

*   – Reduce the polynomial  <math alttext="upper C Superscript left-parenthesis 1 asterisk 2 right-parenthesis Baseline left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mtext>\*</mtext><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper C Superscript left-parenthesis 1 asterisk 2 right-parenthesis Baseline left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c07_521.png):

 <math alttext="upper C Superscript left-parenthesis 1 asterisk 2 right-parenthesis Baseline left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis m o d left-parenthesis x Superscript 4 Baseline plus 1 right-parenthesis equals left-bracket normal a Baseline 9 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x cubed plus left-bracket 72 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x squared plus left-bracket 34 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mtext>\*</mtext><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>72</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>34</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> ![upper C Superscript left-parenthesis 1 asterisk 2 right-parenthesis Baseline left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis m o d left-parenthesis x Superscript 4 Baseline plus 1 right-parenthesis equals left-bracket normal a Baseline 9 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x cubed plus left-bracket 72 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x squared plus left-bracket 34 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x](images/c07_522.png)

#### 7.3.6.2 SubBytes and InvSubBytes Transformations

SubBytes is a nonlinear[⁹](#c07.xhtml#c07-note-0009) transformation, which operates independently on each byte of the state using the S-Box; InvSubBytes is its inverse, which makes use of the InvS-Box. Both boxes are 16×16byte arrays. Row and column indexes, denoted *x* (4 bits) and *y* (4 bits), of a box cell form a byte  <math alttext="x StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue y" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></math> ![x StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue y](images/c07_524.png), which is an element of the extension field  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>8</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 8](images/c07_525.png).

*Construction of S-Box*

Let *a* denote the concatenation of the row and column indexes of an S-Box cell.  <math alttext="b prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![b prime](images/c07_526.png), the content of the S-Box cell indexed[^(10)](#c07.xhtml#c07-note-0010) by *a*, is computed in two steps as follows:

*   Take  <math alttext="b" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow></math> ![b](images/c07_527.png), the multiplicative inverse of *a* in the extension field  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>8</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 8](images/c07_528.png); that is,  <math alttext="b equals a Superscript negative 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![b equals a Superscript negative 1](images/c07_529.png) Since the element 00 has no multiplicative inverse in any extension field, AES authors made an exception and mapped 00 to itself.
*   Apply the following affine transformation to the element  <math alttext="b comma for 0 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than 8 comma to yield b prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;for&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>0</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;to&#160;yield&#160;</mtext><mi>b</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![b comma for 0 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than 8 comma to yield b prime](images/c07_530.png) such as:

 <math alttext="b prime Subscript i Baseline equals b Subscript i Baseline circled-plus b Subscript left-parenthesis i plus 4 right-parenthesis m o d Baseline 8 Baseline circled-plus b Subscript left-parenthesis i plus 5 right-parenthesis m o d Baseline 8 Baseline circled-plus b Subscript left-parenthesis i plus 6 right-parenthesis m o d Baseline 8 Baseline circled-plus b Subscript left-parenthesis i plus 7 right-parenthesis m o d Baseline 8 Baseline circled-plus c Subscript i Baseline comma" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>b</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>'</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mn>8</mn></mrow></msub><mo>&#8853;</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mn>8</mn></mrow></msub><mo>&#8853;</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mn>8</mn></mrow></msub><mo>&#8853;</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mn>8</mn></mrow></msub><mo>&#8853;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo></mrow></math> ![b prime Subscript i Baseline equals b Subscript i Baseline circled-plus b Subscript left-parenthesis i plus 4 right-parenthesis m o d Baseline 8 Baseline circled-plus b Subscript left-parenthesis i plus 5 right-parenthesis m o d Baseline 8 Baseline circled-plus b Subscript left-parenthesis i plus 6 right-parenthesis m o d Baseline 8 Baseline circled-plus b Subscript left-parenthesis i plus 7 right-parenthesis m o d Baseline 8 Baseline circled-plus c Subscript i Baseline comma](images/c07_531.png)(7.1) 

where *c* is a constant with the value  <math alttext="left-bracket 63 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline equals 01100011 Subscript 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>63</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mn>01100011</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![left-bracket 63 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline equals 01100011 Subscript 2](images/c07_532.png).

Computing inverses in  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>8</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 8](images/c07_533.png) results in a nonlinear byte substitution, which makes AES resistant against some forms of cryptanalysis attacks.

**Example 7.5**

*   –  <math alttext="upper S bar upper B o x left-parenthesis 0 comma 0 right-parenthesis equals left-bracket 63 right-bracket Subscript 16" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>\_</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>63</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper S bar upper B o x left-parenthesis 0 comma 0 right-parenthesis equals left-bracket 63 right-bracket Subscript 16](images/c07_534.png), because:

*   o The inverse of  <math alttext="a equals 00 is b equals 00" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>00</mn><mtext>&#160;is&#160;</mtext><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>00</mn></mrow></math> ![a equals 00 is b equals 00](images/c07_535.png) (by AES design)
*   o By ([7.1](#c07.xhtml#c07-disp-0001)),  <math alttext="b prime Subscript i Baseline equals c Subscript i Baseline period Since c equals left-bracket 63 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline comma b prime equals left-bracket 63 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>b</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>'</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>.</mo><mtext>&#160;Since&#160;</mtext><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>63</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>b</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>63</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![b prime Subscript i Baseline equals c Subscript i Baseline period Since c equals left-bracket 63 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline comma b prime equals left-bracket 63 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline](images/c07_536.png). 
    *   –  <math alttext="upper S bar upper B o x left-parenthesis 8 comma 7 right-parenthesis equals 17" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>\_</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>17</mn></mrow></math> ![upper S bar upper B o x left-parenthesis 8 comma 7 right-parenthesis equals 17](images/c07_537.png), because:

*   o In extension field  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>8</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 8](images/c07_538.png), the inverse of  <math alttext="a equals 87" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>87</mn></mrow></math> ![a equals 87](images/c07_539.png) is  <math alttext="b equals 56" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>56</mn></mrow></math> ![b equals 56](images/c07_540.png)
*   o By ([7.1](#c07.xhtml#c07-disp-2001)):

*Construction of InvS-Box*

The InvS-Box is constructed in the inverse order of that of the S-Box; it is obtained by the inverse of the affine transformation used to construct the S-Box and then, by computing the multiplicative inverse.

Let α denote the concatenation of the row and column indexes of an InvS-Box cell.  <math alttext="beta prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#946;</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![beta prime](images/c07_543.png), the content of the InvS-Box cell indexed by α, is computed in two steps as follows:

*   Apply the following affine transformation to the element α, for  <math alttext="0 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></math> ![0 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than 8](images/c07_544.png), to yield

 <math alttext="alpha prime Subscript i Baseline equals alpha Subscript left-parenthesis i plus 2 right-parenthesis m o d Baseline 8 Baseline circled-plus alpha Subscript left-parenthesis i plus 5 right-parenthesis m o d Baseline 8 Baseline circled-plus alpha Subscript left-parenthesis i plus 7 right-parenthesis m o d Baseline 8 Baseline circled-plus d Subscript i Baseline comma" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#945;</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>'</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mn>8</mn></mrow></msub><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mn>8</mn></mrow></msub><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mrow><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mn>8</mn></mrow></msub><mo>&#8853;</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo></mrow></math> ![alpha prime Subscript i Baseline equals alpha Subscript left-parenthesis i plus 2 right-parenthesis m o d Baseline 8 Baseline circled-plus alpha Subscript left-parenthesis i plus 5 right-parenthesis m o d Baseline 8 Baseline circled-plus alpha Subscript left-parenthesis i plus 7 right-parenthesis m o d Baseline 8 Baseline circled-plus d Subscript i Baseline comma](images/c07_545.png)(7.3) 

where *d* is a constant with a value of  <math alttext="05 Subscript 16 Baseline equals 00000101 Subscript 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mrow><mn>05</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mn>00000101</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![05 Subscript 16 Baseline equals 00000101 Subscript 2](images/c07_546.png).

*   Take  <math alttext="beta prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#946;</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![beta prime](images/c07_547.png), the multiplicative inverse of  <math alttext="alpha prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#945;</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![alpha prime](images/c07_548.png) in the extension field  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>8</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 8](images/c07_549.png); that is,  <math alttext="beta prime equals alpha Superscript prime negative 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#946;</mi><mo>'</mo><mo>=</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><msup><mi>&#945;</mi><mrow><mtext>'</mtext><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![beta prime equals alpha Superscript prime negative 1](images/c07_550.png).

**Note**. The elements of the S-Box and their inverses are constants; thus, they are computed one time and stored in two tables.

#### 7.3.6.3 **ShiftRows** and **InvShiftRows** Transformations

In ShiftRows and InvShiftRows, the row 0 of the state is not shifted, while the others are left-shifted using ShiftRows and right-shifted using InvShiftRows. Therefore, for any state  <math alttext="upper S comma upper I n v upper S h i f t upper R o w s left-parenthesis upper S h i f t upper R o w s left-parenthesis upper S right-parenthesis right-parenthesis equals upper S" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>I</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>v</mi><mi>S</mi><mi>h</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>f</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>w</mi><mi>s</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mi>h</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>f</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>w</mi><mi>s</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>S</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow></math> ![upper S comma upper I n v upper S h i f t upper R o w s left-parenthesis upper S h i f t upper R o w s left-parenthesis upper S right-parenthesis right-parenthesis equals upper S](images/c07_552.png).

#### 7.3.6.4 **MixColumns** and **InvMixColumns** Transformations

In the MixColumns transformation, each column of the state is considered as a polynomial of degree 4 with coefficients in the extension field  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>8</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript 8](images/c07_553.png) and multiplied modulo the polynomial  <math alttext="x Superscript 4 Baseline plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![x Superscript 4 Baseline plus 1](images/c07_554.png) by a fixed polynomial  <math alttext="a left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals left-bracket 03 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x cubed plus left-bracket 01 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x squared plus left-bracket 01 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x plus left-bracket 02 right-bracket Subscript 16" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>03</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>01</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>01</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>02</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![a left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals left-bracket 03 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x cubed plus left-bracket 01 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x squared plus left-bracket 01 right-bracket Subscript 16 Baseline x plus left-bracket 02 right-bracket Subscript 16](images/c07_555.png). Thus, a state *S* is mapped to  <math alttext="upper S prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![upper S prime](images/c07_556.png), such that:  <math alttext="upper S prime left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals upper S left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis circled-plus a left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>S</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8853;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper S prime left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals upper S left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis circled-plus a left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c07_557.png), which can be written as a matrix multiplication, for each column  <math alttext="c semicolon 0 less-than-or-equal-to c less-than 4 comma" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>0</mn><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8804;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>c</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#60;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo></mrow></math> ![c semicolon 0 less-than-or-equal-to c less-than 4 comma](images/c07_558.png) as follows:

From the four equalities above, we observe that each byte in a column *c* of the input state *S* is replaced by twice that byte, plus three times the next byte, plus the byte that comes next, and plus the byte that follows in the column.

#### 7.3.6.5 AddRoundKey Transformation

AddRoundKey is an XOR operation between a state and the round key; it is its inverse.

### 7.3.7 Security of AES

Although AES was introduced in 2001, all the threats against the AES cipher remain theoretical, because of their time complexity, which remains beyond the ability of any computer system to handle. This would last for a long time. In particular, differential and linear cryptanalyses have been used to design attacks against AES; however, their time complexity is just an optimization of that of brute-force attack. Such attacks will be addressed in [Chapter 11](#c11.xhtml).

A major known risk to AES encryption comes from side-channel attacks. Rather than attempting brute-force or cryptanalysis-based attacks, side-channel attacks are aimed at collecting information about what a computing device does when it is performing cryptographic operations (e.g. AES permutations, substitutions, etc.). Some side-channel attacks have been proposed and took advantage of some specific hardware or software implementations. To our knowledge, the most recent side-channel attack against AES was proposed in \[[8](#c07.xhtml#c07-bib-0008)\]. The attack targeted AES used in OpenSSL and made strong assumptions: i) the attacker is hosted on the same processor as the attacked system and both share the same processor cache, ii) the attacker can pre-empt the victim while it is encrypting or decrypting, iii) a few blocks of plaintext or ciphertext are known. Under such assumptions, the proposed attack runs in less than a minute. In conclusion, security experts still consider that AES is secure when implemented properly.

***Exercise 7.1***

Consider the first round of the Feistel cipher encryption. Which part of the plaintext is encrypted at the end of the round?

***Exercise 7.2***

***Exercise 7.3***

***Exercise 7.5***

2.  What is the output of the first round of DEA when the plaintext and the key are both all ones?

## 7.4.2 Solutions to Exercises and Problems

***Exercise* *7.1***

Operations performed in the first round are  <math alttext="upper L upper E 1 equals upper R upper E 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>L</mi><msub><mi>E</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>R</mi><msub><mi>E</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper L upper E 1 equals upper R upper E 0](images/c07_622.png) and  <math alttext="upper R upper E 1 equals upper L upper E 0 circled-plus upper F left-parenthesis upper R upper E 0 comma upper K 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>R</mi><msub><mi>E</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>L</mi><msub><mi>E</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>&#8853;</mo><mi>F</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><msub><mi>E</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>K</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper R upper E 1 equals upper L upper E 0 circled-plus upper F left-parenthesis upper R upper E 0 comma upper K 1 right-parenthesis](images/c07_623.png).

The right half is used in the round function *F*, but it does not change and it is directly copied in the left part of the input to the second round.

The left half is XORed with the output of the round function *F* and the transformation result is copied in the right part of the input to the second round. Therefore, only the left part of the plaintext is encrypted in the first round.

***Exercise* *7.3***

DEA key length is of 56 bits; hence, there exist  <math alttext="2 Superscript 56" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>56</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![2 Superscript 56](images/c07_652.png) distinct keys. DEA block length is of 64 bits; hence, there exist  <math alttext="2 Superscript 64" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>64</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![2 Superscript 64](images/c07_653.png) distinct plaintext blocks and  <math alttext="2 Superscript 64" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>64</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![2 Superscript 64](images/c07_654.png) distinct ciphertext blocks. For one key, a plaintext *x* maps to a ciphertext *y* with a probability of  <math alttext="StartFraction 1 Over 2 Superscript 64 Baseline EndFraction" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>64</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> ![StartFraction 1 Over 2 Superscript 64 Baseline EndFraction](images/c07_655.png).

For  <math alttext="2 Superscript 56" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>56</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![2 Superscript 56](images/c07_656.png) distinct keys, a plaintext *x* maps to a ciphertext *y* with a probability of  <math alttext="StartFraction 1 Over 2 Superscript 64 Baseline EndFraction asterisk 2 Superscript 56 Baseline equals StartFraction 1 Over 256 EndFraction" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>64</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>\*</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>56</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>256</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> ![StartFraction 1 Over 2 Superscript 64 Baseline EndFraction asterisk 2 Superscript 56 Baseline equals StartFraction 1 Over 256 EndFraction](images/c07_657.png).

1.     Applying the initial permutation to *B* yields a 64 zero-bit string. Therefore, the input of the first round is the same than *B*; i.e.  <math alttext="upper L 0 equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![upper L 0 equals 0](images/c07_684.png) and  <math alttext="upper R 0 equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![upper R 0 equals 0](images/c07_685.png).

***Exercise 7.6***

All blocks  <math alttext="upper C Subscript i" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![upper C Subscript i](images/c07_727.png) and  <math alttext="upper D Subscript i" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![upper D Subscript i](images/c07_728.png),  <math alttext="i equals 1 comma ellipsis 16" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow></math> ![i equals 1 comma ellipsis 16](images/c07_729.png), used in the key schedule function are 28-bit blocks.  <math alttext="upper N upper L upper R" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>N</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>R</mi></mrow></math> ![upper N upper L upper R](images/c07_730.png) ([Table 7.8](#c07.xhtml#c07-tbl-0008)) vector determines the number of positions to rotate both  <math alttext="upper C Subscript i" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![upper C Subscript i](images/c07_731.png) and  <math alttext="upper D Subscript i" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![upper D Subscript i](images/c07_732.png) for each round *i*. At 16^(th) round, the value of  <math alttext="upper C 16" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper C 16](images/c07_733.png) (resp.  <math alttext="upper D 16" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper D 16](images/c07_734.png)) is the initial value  <math alttext="upper C 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper C 0](images/c07_735.png) (resp.  <math alttext="upper D 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper D 0](images/c07_736.png)), which has been left-rotated by a total number of positions equal to the sum of elements of vector  <math alttext="upper N upper L upper R" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>N</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>R</mi></mrow></math> ![upper N upper L upper R](images/c07_737.png) (i.e.  <math alttext="4 asterisk 1 plus 12 asterisk 2 equals 28" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>28</mn></mrow></math> ![4 asterisk 1 plus 12 asterisk 2 equals 28](images/c07_738.png)). Thus, if you left-rotate  <math alttext="upper C 16" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper C 16](images/c07_739.png) (resp.  <math alttext="upper D 16" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper D 16](images/c07_740.png)) by one position, you get  <math alttext="upper C 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper C 1](images/c07_741.png) (resp.  <math alttext="upper D 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper D 1](images/c07_742.png)). Notice that  <math alttext="upper C 0 equals upper C 16" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper C 0 equals upper C 16](images/c07_743.png) and  <math alttext="upper D 0 equals upper D 16" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper D 0 equals upper D 16](images/c07_744.png).

***Exercise 7.7***

Let  <math alttext="upper S b left-parenthesis upper S Subscript r comma c Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mi>b</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper S b left-parenthesis upper S Subscript r comma c Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c07_745.png) denote the substitution of byte  <math alttext="upper S Subscript r comma c" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper S Subscript r comma c](images/c07_746.png) (i.e. the byte of state *S* at row *r* and column *c*) using the S-Box. The result of ShiftRows (SubBytes (S)) is given on the left of [Figure 7.17](#c07.xhtml#c07-fig-0017) and that of SubBytes(ShiftRows(S)) on the right. The results are the same. Thus, SubBytes and ShiftRows can be applied in either order in the AES encryption.

![Figure 7.17 ShiftRows and SubBytes can be used in any order.](images/c07f017.png)

[**Figure 7.17**](#c07.xhtml#rc07-fig-0017) ShiftRows and SubBytes can be used in any order.
