If parameter  <math alttext="b equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![b equals 0](images/c10_363.png), then every plaintext  <math alttext="m 0 Superscript i" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mn>0</mn><mi>i</mi></msubsup></mrow></math> ![m 0 Superscript i](images/c10_364.png) is encrypted and a ciphertext  <math alttext="c Subscript i Baseline equals epsilon Subscript upper K Baseline left-parenthesis m 0 Superscript i Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mn>0</mn><mi>i</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![c Subscript i Baseline equals epsilon Subscript upper K Baseline left-parenthesis m 0 Superscript i Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c10_365.png) is returned; and if  <math alttext="b equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![b equals 1](images/c10_366.png), then every plaintext  <math alttext="m 1 Superscript i" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mn>1</mn><mi>i</mi></msubsup></mrow></math> ![m 1 Superscript i](images/c10_367.png) is encrypted and a ciphertext  <math alttext="c Subscript i Baseline equals epsilon Subscript upper K Baseline left-parenthesis m 1 Superscript i Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mn>1</mn><mi>i</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![c Subscript i Baseline equals epsilon Subscript upper K Baseline left-parenthesis m 1 Superscript i Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c10_368.png) is returned. The game for the adversary, is to guess which plaintext  <math alttext="m 0 Superscript i" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mn>0</mn><mi>i</mi></msubsup></mrow></math> ![m 0 Superscript i](images/c10_369.png) (the left) or  <math alttext="m 1 Superscript i" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mn>1</mn><mi>i</mi></msubsup></mrow></math> ![m 1 Superscript i](images/c10_370.png) (the right) has been encrypted.

The advantage that an adversary  <math alttext="upper A Subscript upper C upper P upper A" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>C</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>A</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper A Subscript upper C upper P upper A](images/c10_371.png) can get is the difference between the probability that the adversary outputs 1 if it thinks that its queries have been processed with  <math alttext="b equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![b equals 1](images/c10_372.png), while it is effectively true and the probability that it outputs 1 if it thinks that its queries have been processed with  <math alttext="b equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![b equals 1](images/c10_373.png), while it is false. Formally, the advantage of adversary  <math alttext="upper A Subscript upper C upper P upper A" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>C</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>A</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper A Subscript upper C upper P upper A](images/c10_374.png) is defined by:

In other words, the adversary advantage is measured in terms of the difference between the probabilities to guess which plaintexts have been encrypted, the left or the right ones. In a CCA security analysis session, in addition to  <math alttext="q Subscript e" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![q Subscript e](images/c10_379.png) encryption queries, the adversary submits  <math alttext="q Subscript d" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![q Subscript d](images/c10_380.png) decryption queries each of the form of a bit-string  <math alttext="y Subscript i" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![y Subscript i](images/c10_381.png),  <math alttext="i equals 1 comma ellipsis comma q Subscript d Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![i equals 1 comma ellipsis comma q Subscript d Baseline](images/c10_382.png), under the assumption that  <math alttext="y Subscript i" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![y Subscript i](images/c10_383.png) has not been previously returned by the encryption oracle  <math alttext="epsilon Subscript upper K" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![epsilon Subscript upper K](images/c10_384.png). Otherwise, the adversary will obviously win the game. Then, if  <math alttext="y Subscript i" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![y Subscript i](images/c10_385.png) is a valid ciphertext, the decryption oracle returns a plaintext  <math alttext="m Subscript i Baseline equals script upper D Subscript upper K Baseline left-parenthesis y Subscript i Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="script">D</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![m Subscript i Baseline equals script upper D Subscript upper K Baseline left-parenthesis y Subscript i Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c10_386.png). Otherwise, it returns a null symbol ⊥. Using the chosen ciphertexts and received plaintexts, the adversary has to guess which value is used for parameter *b*.

### 10.3.2 Some Bounds of Security of Block Cipher Modes of Operation

Below are given some bounds proven in literature. They are very useful to understand why the number of plaintexts encrypted with the same key is limited, in order to not compromise the security. It is worth noticing that the security analysis has mainly focused on CBC and CTR modes for two reasons: they are the most used in practice and the security of OFB and CFB modes may be inferred from those of CBC and CTR.

*Security under chosen-plaintext attack*

To simplify the bound definitions, we assume that the plaintext bit-length is a multiple of *n*, the block length of the underlying block cipher. In \[[2](#c10.xhtml#c10-bib-0002), [5](#c10.xhtml#c10-bib-0005), [7](#c10.xhtml#c10-bib-0007)\], the following security bounds are proved, where *q* is the total number[⁵](#c10.xhtml#c10-note-0005) of *n*\-bit blocks encrypted using the block cipher *E* under the same key and  <math alttext="mu Subscript e" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>&#956;</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![mu Subscript e](images/c10_396.png) is the total number of bits encrypted with CBC or CTR such that  <math alttext="mu Subscript e Baseline equals n asterisk q" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>&#956;</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> ![mu Subscript e Baseline equals n asterisk q](images/c10_397.png). Notice that  <math alttext="q Subscript e" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![q Subscript e](images/c10_398.png) is at most *q* and it has no impact on the following bounds.

*CBC mode* (if the IV is randomly selected and unpredictable by adversary):

*CTR mode* (if the initial counter value is randomly chosen):

Inequalities ([10.4](#c10.xhtml#c10-disp-0004)) and ([10.5](#c10.xhtml#c10-disp-0005)) state that the adversary advantage attacking the CBC or CTR modes, under CPA, is at most the advantage when attacking the underlying block cipher *E*, if it is modeled as a PRF, plus a quantity that depends on the number of encrypted blocks. Notice that CTR mode has a better security bound. If the underlying block cipher is secure and the number of encrypted blocks is low, then both CBC and CTR modes are secure.

**Example 10.4**

Using the TDES security bound ([10.1](#c10.xhtml#c10-disp-0001)), given the maximum number of blocks to encrypt under CBC over TDES, the CBC-adversary advantage β can be yielded as follows:

*Security under Chosen-Ciphertext Attack*

CCA attacks are powerful enough to break all the modes of operation of block ciphers including CBC, CFB, OFB, and CTR. As far as we know, only XTS-AES was proven to be a strong PRP (i.e. it is secure under CCA attacks). In \[[8](#c10.xhtml#c10-bib-0008)\], the following bound is proven regarding the XTS-AES:

 <math alttext="upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper X upper T upper S minus upper A upper E upper S Superscript c c a Baseline left-parenthesis t comma q right-parenthesis 2 asterisk upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper A upper E upper S Superscript p r p minus c c a Baseline left-parenthesis t prime comma q right-parenthesis plus StartFraction q squared Over 2 Superscript 128 Baseline EndFraction" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>D</mi><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>X</mi><mi>T</mi><mi>S</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>E</mi><mi>S</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>D</mi><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>E</mi><mi>S</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>'</mo><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>q</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>128</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> ![upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper X upper T upper S minus upper A upper E upper S Superscript c c a Baseline left-parenthesis t comma q right-parenthesis 2 asterisk upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper A upper E upper S Superscript p r p minus c c a Baseline left-parenthesis t prime comma q right-parenthesis plus StartFraction q squared Over 2 Superscript 128 Baseline EndFraction](images/c10_413.png)(10.6) 

where *q* denotes the total number of encryption and decryption queries. *t* and  <math alttext="t prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![t prime](images/c10_414.png) are the maximum computation times of adversaries attacking XTS-AES;  <math alttext="t prime equals t plus upper O left-parenthesis q right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>O</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![t prime equals t plus upper O left-parenthesis q right-parenthesis](images/c10_415.png). *O*(*q*) denotes “in order of q”.

Below are two examples of CCAs against CTR and CBC modes.

1. The probability that the random permutation oracle returns a bit string that differs from *B* by a single bit at a known position is  <math alttext="1 slash 2 Superscript n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow></math> ![1 slash 2 Superscript n](images/c10_430.png). Thus, CCA-adversary advantage is close to 1.

The probability that the random permutation oracle returns a bit string that differs from *B* by a single bit at a known position is  <math alttext="1 slash 2 Superscript n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow></math> ![1 slash 2 Superscript n](images/c10_445.png). Thus, CCA-adversary advantage is close to 1.

## 10.4 Security Analysis of Authenticity-only Schemes

Authenticity-only schemes, which include CMAC, GMAC, and HMAC, aim to generate and verify MACs. Therefore, the security analysis of such schemes focuses on authenticity. Authenticity modes of operation, which include CMAC and GMAC standards, are presented in [Chapter 9](#c09.xhtml). HMAC is another way to provide authenticity guarantees by using hash functions and not block ciphers; it is presented in Section 5.3.2.1.

### 10.4.1 Generic Models for Security Analysis of Authenticity Schemes

The main objective of security analysis models of MAC modes is to find bounds on the probability that an adversary can infer some useful information on the MAC modes in order to forge valid tags (i.e. the adversary is able to apply existential forgery attack). Recall that MAC modes aim to authenticate the origin of messages and not to make the information confidential. Therefore, the main purpose of MAC mode security evaluation focuses only on tag forgery. There exist two models of MAC security analysis, one focuses on tag forgery and the other on the MAC function indistinguishability.

#### 10.4.1.1 Game for Tag Forgery Analysis

The basic security analysis model of MAC modes is an oracle with two components: MAC generation and MAC verification (see [Figure 10.3](#c10.xhtml#c10-fig-0003)). In the initialization step, a key *K* is uniformly selected at random from the key space  <math alttext="script upper K equals StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript k" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">K</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mi>k</mi></msup></mrow></math> ![script upper K equals StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript k](images/c10_446.png), where *k* is the key bit-length. Then, the adversary selects a message  <math alttext="upper M element-of StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8712;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><msup><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo></msup></mrow></math> ![upper M element-of StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript asterisk](images/c10_447.png) and queries the MAC generation component to produce a valid tag  <math alttext="upper T equals upper F Subscript upper K Baseline left-parenthesis upper M right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper T equals upper F Subscript upper K Baseline left-parenthesis upper M right-parenthesis](images/c10_448.png), where *F* is the MAC mode under analysis. The tag generation query operation is repeated[⁶](#c10.xhtml#c10-note-0006) several times. Then, using the collected tags, the adversary tries to forge a tag  <math alttext="upper T prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![upper T prime](images/c10_449.png) for some message  <math alttext="upper M prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![upper M prime](images/c10_450.png) that has never been submitted to the tag generation component, and queries the MAC verification component to check if tag  <math alttext="upper T prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![upper T prime](images/c10_451.png) is valid or not; the oracle returns 1 if the tag is valid and 0 otherwise. The tag verification query operation is repeated several times, until the adversary succeeds in forging a tag or stops.

![Figure 10.3 Generic oracle for MAC mode security analysis.](images/c10f003.png)

[**Figure 10.3**](#c10.xhtml#rc10-fig-0003) Generic oracle for MAC mode security analysis.

Given a MAC mode *F* (such as CMAC, GMAC, or HMAC), the maximum probability of forging a valid tag by an adversary  <math alttext="script upper A" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="script">A</mi></math> ![script upper A](images/c10_452.png) is referred to as adversary *mac*\-*advantage* and it is denoted  <math alttext="upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper F Superscript m a c Baseline left-parenthesis script upper A right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>D</mi><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="script">A</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper F Superscript m a c Baseline left-parenthesis script upper A right-parenthesis](images/c10_453.png). The resources used by an adversary to forge a tag, by querying the oracle, are represented in terms of the number of tag generation queries, denoted  <math alttext="q Subscript g e n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mi>g</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![q Subscript g e n](images/c10_454.png), and that of tag verification queries, denoted  <math alttext="q Subscript v e r" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mi>v</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![q Subscript v e r](images/c10_455.png). The probability of attack success depends on the number of queries; the higher the number of queries, the higher the probability of success. The computation time *t* required to perform encryptions ( <math alttext="upper E n c Subscript upper K" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mi>n</mi><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![upper E n c Subscript upper K](images/c10_456.png)), decryptions ( <math alttext="upper D e c Subscript upper K" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>D</mi><mi>e</mi><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![upper D e c Subscript upper K](images/c10_457.png)), and tag verifications to answer all the queries is of paramount importance, because it indicates if the attack is computationally feasible or not under the expected probability.

 <math alttext="upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper F Superscript m a c Baseline left-parenthesis t comma q Subscript g e n Baseline plus q Subscript v e r Baseline comma right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>D</mi><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mi>g</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mi>v</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper F Superscript m a c Baseline left-parenthesis t comma q Subscript g e n Baseline plus q Subscript v e r Baseline comma right-parenthesis](images/c10_458.png) denotes the probability of tag forgery over all adversaries that ask at most *t* calls[⁷](#c10.xhtml#c10-note-0007) to the underlying block cipher,  <math alttext="q Subscript g e n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mi>g</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![q Subscript g e n](images/c10_459.png) queries to the MAC generation component, and  <math alttext="q Subscript v e r" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mi>v</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![q Subscript v e r](images/c10_460.png) queries to the MAC-verification component with a maximum of μ bits per query. Formally,

 <math alttext="probability left-bracket upper K left-arrow Overscript upper R Endscripts script upper K semicolon script upper A Superscript upper F Super Subscript upper K Superscript Baseline right double arrow 1 right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mover><mo>&#8592;</mo><mi>R</mi></mover><mi mathvariant="script">K</mi><mo>;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi mathvariant="script">A</mi><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow></msup><mo>&#8658;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![probability left-bracket upper K left-arrow Overscript upper R Endscripts script upper K semicolon script upper A Superscript upper F Super Subscript upper K Superscript Baseline right double arrow 1 right-bracket](images/c10_464.png) means the probability that the adversary  <math alttext="script upper A" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="script">A</mi></math> ![script upper A](images/c10_465.png) receives 1 (i.e. it succeeds in forging a tag  <math alttext="upper T prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![upper T prime](images/c10_466.png) and a message  <math alttext="upper M prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![upper M prime](images/c10_467.png) such that  <math alttext="upper T prime equals upper F Subscript upper K Baseline left-parenthesis upper M prime right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>'</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper T prime equals upper F Subscript upper K Baseline left-parenthesis upper M prime right-parenthesis](images/c10_468.png)).

#### 10.4.1.2 Game for MAC Indistinguishability

With the exception of GMAC, all the MAC modes presented in this book are pseudo random functions (PRFs). Thus, a MAC mode *F* is a PRF  <math alttext="upper F colon StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript k Baseline times StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript asterisk Baseline right-arrow StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript upper T l e n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>:</mo><msup><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mi>k</mi></msup><mo>&#215;</mo><msup><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo></msup><mo>&#8594;</mo><msup><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>T</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![upper F colon StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript k Baseline times StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript asterisk Baseline right-arrow StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript upper T l e n](images/c10_470.png), where *k* and  <math alttext="upper T l e n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>T</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper T l e n](images/c10_471.png) denote the key and tag bit-lengths, respectively.

Then, the security analysis of a MAC mode *F* may be measured as the maximum advantage that an adversary  <math alttext="script upper A" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="script">A</mi></math> ![script upper A](images/c10_472.png) can obtain when trying to distinguish between the oracle of *F* and a random function. Following the same idea of indistinguishability of function and permutation families introduced in [Section 10.1.2](#c10.xhtml#c10-sec-02002) (see [Figure 10.1](#c10.xhtml#c10-fig-0001)), the principle of MAC indistinguishability is to give the adversary access to two oracles:

1.  First oracle denoted  <math alttext="upper F Subscript upper K" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript upper K](images/c10_473.png): uniformly select a key *K* at random from key space  <math alttext="script upper K" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="script">K</mi></math> ![script upper K](images/c10_474.png) and then process adversary queries with the function  <math alttext="upper F Subscript upper K" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript upper K](images/c10_475.png).
2.  Second oracle φ: select at random a function φ from the set  <math alttext="phi colon StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript asterisk Baseline right-arrow StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript upper T l e n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#981;</mi><mo>:</mo><msup><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo></msup><mo>&#8594;</mo><msup><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>T</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![phi colon StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript asterisk Baseline right-arrow StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript upper T l e n](images/c10_476.png) of all random functions that take an input from the message space ℳ and return a  <math alttext="upper T l e n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>T</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper T l e n](images/c10_477.png)\-bit string. Then, all adversary queries are processed with function φ.

Before processing the adversary queries, the challenger uniformly selects at random a parameter  <math alttext="b element-of StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8712;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![b element-of StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet](images/c10_478.png). If  <math alttext="b equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![b equals 1](images/c10_479.png), the adversary is given access to the oracle  <math alttext="upper F Subscript upper K" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript upper K](images/c10_480.png); and it receives a valid tag  <math alttext="upper T equals upper F Subscript upper K Baseline left-parenthesis upper M right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper T equals upper F Subscript upper K Baseline left-parenthesis upper M right-parenthesis](images/c10_481.png) for any input message *M*. If  <math alttext="b equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![b equals 0](images/c10_482.png), it is given access the oracle of φ; and it receives a random  <math alttext="upper T l e n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>T</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper T l e n](images/c10_483.png)\-bit string for any input message *M*. Then, the adversary asks with a set of messages selected (according to some strategy) from the message domain ℳ. Then, it receives either a set of valid tags or a set of random  <math alttext="upper T l e n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>T</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper T l e n](images/c10_484.png)\-bit strings. Notice that we are talking about chosen-plaintext-attacks. Making exploitation of the received answers, the adversary is requested to guess which oracle is used.

The adversary advantage of a MAC *F* as a PRF is its ability to distinguish between a MAC function and a random function. The advantage is measured in terms of the difference between the probability it outputs 1 while it has access to oracle of  <math alttext="upper F Subscript upper K" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript upper K](images/c10_485.png) (i.e. probability of a correct guess) and the probability it outputs 1 while it has access to a random function oracle (i.e. probability of a wrong guess). Using the same notations as in [Section 10.1.2](#c10.xhtml#c10-sec-02002), the advantage of adversary  <math alttext="script upper A" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="script">A</mi></math> ![script upper A](images/c10_486.png) attacking a MAC *F* as a PRF is defined by:

The maximum advantage over all adversaries with computation time at most *t* and submitting at most *q* plaintexts with a total of μ bits is defined by:

 <math alttext="upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper F Superscript p r f Baseline left-parenthesis t comma q comma mu right-parenthesis equals Overscript d e f Endscripts max Underscript script upper A Endscripts upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper F Superscript p r f Baseline left-parenthesis script upper A right-parenthesis" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>D</mi><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>f</mi></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>&#956;</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>f</mi></mrow></mover><munder><mrow><mi>max</mi></mrow><mi mathvariant="script">A</mi></munder><mi>A</mi><mi>D</mi><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>f</mi></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="script">A</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper F Superscript p r f Baseline left-parenthesis t comma q comma mu right-parenthesis equals Overscript d e f Endscripts max Underscript script upper A Endscripts upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper F Superscript p r f Baseline left-parenthesis script upper A right-parenthesis](images/c10_488.png)

It is commonly accepted that if function family *F* is secure as a PRF (i.e. *F* is indistinguishable from a random function), it is secure as a MAC (i.e. attacker cannot forge tags, which are validated by MAC *F*). That fact is formalized by the following relationship proven in \[[5](#c10.xhtml#c10-bib-0005)\]:

 <math alttext="upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper F Superscript m a c Baseline left-parenthesis t comma q comma mu right-parenthesis less-than-or-equal-to upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper F Superscript p r f Baseline left-parenthesis t prime comma q right-parenthesis plus StartFraction 1 Over 2 Superscript upper T l e n Baseline EndFraction" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>D</mi><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>&#956;</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>D</mi><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>f</mi></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>'</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>T</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> ![upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper F Superscript m a c Baseline left-parenthesis t comma q comma mu right-parenthesis less-than-or-equal-to upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper F Superscript p r f Baseline left-parenthesis t prime comma q right-parenthesis plus StartFraction 1 Over 2 Superscript upper T l e n Baseline EndFraction](images/c10_489.png)(10.7) 

where:

*q* is the number of queries; *t* and  <math alttext="t prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![t prime](images/c10_490.png) denote the computation times of adversary attacking *F* as a MAC or as a PRF, respectively.  <math alttext="t prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></math> ![t prime](images/c10_491.png) exceeds *t* with an amount in order of  <math alttext="upper T l e n plus d" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>T</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></math> ![upper T l e n plus d](images/c10_492.png), where *d* is the bit-length of plaintext. Notice that  <math alttext="StartFraction 1 Over 2 Superscript upper T l e n Baseline EndFraction" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>T</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> ![StartFraction 1 Over 2 Superscript upper T l e n Baseline EndFraction](images/c10_493.png) is added in ([10.7](#c10.xhtml#c10-disp-0007)), because even a perfect PRF (i.e.  <math alttext="upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper F Superscript p r f Baseline left-parenthesis ellipsis right-parenthesis equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>D</mi><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>f</mi></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper F Superscript p r f Baseline left-parenthesis ellipsis right-parenthesis equals 0](images/c10_494.png)), there is a probability of  <math alttext="StartFraction 1 Over 2 Superscript upper T l e n Baseline EndFraction" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>T</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> ![StartFraction 1 Over 2 Superscript upper T l e n Baseline EndFraction](images/c10_495.png) that the adversary can randomly choose a valid tag and submit a query, and then receives 1 (i.e. the tag is valid) from the tag verifier.

The maximum adversary advantage to forge a tag is called the *maximum forgery probability*.

### 10.4.2 Some Security Bounds for MAC Schemes

#### 10.4.2.1 Security Bounds for CMAC

CMAC mode is modeled as a PRF:  <math alttext="upper C upper M upper A upper C colon StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript k Baseline times StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript asterisk Baseline right-arrow StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript upper T l e n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>:</mo><msup><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mi>k</mi></msup><mo>&#215;</mo><msup><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo></msup><mo>&#8594;</mo><msup><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>T</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![upper C upper M upper A upper C colon StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript k Baseline times StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript asterisk Baseline right-arrow StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript upper T l e n](images/c10_496.png). It operates above a block cipher *E*. Since *E* is PRP, the adversary advantage includes a PRP advantage. As far as we know, the security of CMAC and its variants are the most addressed in literature. Below are some useful proven bounds on CMAC tag forgery probability; in the three bounds, *n* denotes the block cipher bit-length:

 <math alttext="upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper C upper M upper A upper C Superscript p r f Baseline left-parenthesis t comma q comma m right-parenthesis less-than-or-equal-to StartFraction l asterisk q squared Over 2 Superscript n Baseline EndFraction asterisk left-parenthesis 12 plus StartFraction 64 asterisk l cubed Over 2 Superscript n Baseline EndFraction right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>D</mi><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>C</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>C</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>f</mi></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8804;</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>q</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>64</mn><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>l</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper C upper M upper A upper C Superscript p r f Baseline left-parenthesis t comma q comma m right-parenthesis less-than-or-equal-to StartFraction l asterisk q squared Over 2 Superscript n Baseline EndFraction asterisk left-parenthesis 12 plus StartFraction 64 asterisk l cubed Over 2 Superscript n Baseline EndFraction right-parenthesis](images/c10_499.png) \[[2](#c10.xhtml#c10-bib-0002)\]

where: *q* denotes the total number of tag generation and verification queries.  <math alttext="sigma" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#963;</mi></mrow></math> ![sigma](images/c10_501.png) denotes the total number of blocks of all the *q* queries. *l* denotes the maximum number of blocks per query. In the tag verification query, one block contains the forged tag. In \[[9](#c10.xhtml#c10-bib-0009)\],  <math alttext="q prime equals sigma plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>&#963;</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![q prime equals sigma plus 1](images/c10_502.png) and  <math alttext="t prime equals t plus upper O left-parenthesis sigma right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>O</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>&#963;</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![t prime equals t plus upper O left-parenthesis sigma right-parenthesis](images/c10_503.png). *O*(*σ*) means “in order of *σ*”.

**Example 10.5**

In AES-CMAC standard, it is recommended to limit the key to no more than  <math alttext="2 Superscript 48" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>48</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![2 Superscript 48](images/c10_504.png) messages for general-purpose applications and to no more than  <math alttext="2 Superscript 48" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>48</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![2 Superscript 48](images/c10_505.png) blocks if a higher confidence in security is required. The  <math alttext="upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper E Superscript p r p Baseline left-parenthesis t prime comma q prime right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>D</mi><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mi>E</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>p</mi></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>'</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper E Superscript p r p Baseline left-parenthesis t prime comma q prime right-parenthesis](images/c10_506.png) is negligible, if the number of blocks  <math alttext="q prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![q prime](images/c10_507.png) is at most  <math alttext="2 Superscript 48" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>48</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![2 Superscript 48](images/c10_508.png). The third bound of forgery probability may be reduced to  <math alttext="StartFraction 4 asterisk sigma asterisk q Over 2 Superscript n Baseline EndFraction" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>\*</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>&#963;</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> ![StartFraction 4 asterisk sigma asterisk q Over 2 Superscript n Baseline EndFraction](images/c10_509.png), because the second factor is very small.

*   – If each of  <math alttext="2 Superscript 48" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>48</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![2 Superscript 48](images/c10_510.png) messages is  <math alttext="1 upper G" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;G</mtext></mrow></math> ![1 upper G](images/c10_511.png) bytes in length, then
    
     <math alttext="q equals 2 Superscript 48" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>48</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![q equals 2 Superscript 48](images/c10_512.png),  <math alttext="sigma equals left-parenthesis StartFraction 2 Superscript 30 Baseline Over 16 EndFraction right-parenthesis asterisk 2 Superscript 48 Baseline equals 2 Superscript 74" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#963;</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>30</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>48</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>74</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![sigma equals left-parenthesis StartFraction 2 Superscript 30 Baseline Over 16 EndFraction right-parenthesis asterisk 2 Superscript 48 Baseline equals 2 Superscript 74](images/c10_513.png).
    
    The best advantage bound is  <math alttext="upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper C upper M upper A upper C Superscript p r f Baseline left-parenthesis t comma q comma sigma right-parenthesis less-than-or-equal-to StartFraction 5 asterisk 2 Superscript 74 Baseline asterisk 2 Superscript 48 Baseline Over 2 Superscript 128 Baseline EndFraction equals five-sixty-fourths" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>D</mi><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>C</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>C</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>f</mi></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>&#963;</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8804;</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>\*</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>74</mn></mrow></msup><mo>\*</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>48</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>128</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mrow><mn>64</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> ![upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper C upper M upper A upper C Superscript p r f Baseline left-parenthesis t comma q comma sigma right-parenthesis less-than-or-equal-to StartFraction 5 asterisk 2 Superscript 74 Baseline asterisk 2 Superscript 48 Baseline Over 2 Superscript 128 Baseline EndFraction equals five-sixty-fourths](images/c10_514.png), which is a weak security.
    
*   – If each of  <math alttext="2 Superscript 48" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>48</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![2 Superscript 48](images/c10_515.png) messages is 16 bytes in length, then
    
     <math alttext="q equals 2 Superscript 48" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>48</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![q equals 2 Superscript 48](images/c10_516.png),  <math alttext="sigma equals left-parenthesis StartFraction 16 Over 16 EndFraction right-parenthesis asterisk 2 Superscript 48 Baseline equals 2 Superscript 48" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#963;</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>48</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>48</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![sigma equals left-parenthesis StartFraction 16 Over 16 EndFraction right-parenthesis asterisk 2 Superscript 48 Baseline equals 2 Superscript 48](images/c10_517.png).
    
    The best advantage bound is  <math alttext="upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper C upper M upper A upper C Superscript p r f Baseline left-parenthesis t comma q comma sigma right-parenthesis less-than-or-equal-to StartFraction 5 asterisk 2 Superscript 48 Baseline asterisk 2 Superscript 48 Baseline Over 2 Superscript 128 Baseline EndFraction equals StartFraction 5 Over 2 Superscript 32 Baseline EndFraction" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>D</mi><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>C</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>C</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>f</mi></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>&#963;</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8804;</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>\*</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>48</mn></mrow></msup><mo>\*</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>48</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>128</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>32</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> ![upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper C upper M upper A upper C Superscript p r f Baseline left-parenthesis t comma q comma sigma right-parenthesis less-than-or-equal-to StartFraction 5 asterisk 2 Superscript 48 Baseline asterisk 2 Superscript 48 Baseline Over 2 Superscript 128 Baseline EndFraction equals StartFraction 5 Over 2 Superscript 32 Baseline EndFraction](images/c10_518.png), which is a strong security.
    
*   – If each of  <math alttext="2 Superscript 32" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>32</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![2 Superscript 32](images/c10_519.png) messages is  <math alttext="1 upper G" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;G</mtext></mrow></math> ![1 upper G](images/c10_520.png) bytes in length, then

    The best advantage bound is  <math alttext="upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper C upper M upper A upper C Superscript p r f Baseline left-parenthesis t comma q comma sigma right-parenthesis less-than-or-equal-to StartFraction 5 asterisk 2 Superscript 58 Baseline asterisk 2 Superscript 32 Baseline Over 2 Superscript 128 Baseline EndFraction equals StartFraction 5 Over 2 Superscript 38 Baseline EndFraction" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>D</mi><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>C</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>C</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>f</mi></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>&#963;</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8804;</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>\*</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>58</mn></mrow></msup><mo>\*</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>32</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>128</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>38</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> ![upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper C upper M upper A upper C Superscript p r f Baseline left-parenthesis t comma q comma sigma right-parenthesis less-than-or-equal-to StartFraction 5 asterisk 2 Superscript 58 Baseline asterisk 2 Superscript 32 Baseline Over 2 Superscript 128 Baseline EndFraction equals StartFraction 5 Over 2 Superscript 38 Baseline EndFraction](images/c10_523.png), which is a very strong security.
    

#### 10.4.2.2 Security Bounds for HMAC

Hash functions and HMAC are presented in Section 3.5.2.1. HMAC is a family of MAC schemes parameterized with a cryptographic hash function. HMAC instances are denoted HMAC\_*H*, where *H* may be any hash function including SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA3-512, etc. HMAC does not make use of any block cipher; its security relies on the underlying hash function. A MAC of a message <math alttext="upper M" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M](images/c10_524.png) is computed as follows:

 <math alttext="upper H upper M upper A upper C minus upper H left-parenthesis upper K comma upper M right-parenthesis equals upper H left-parenthesis left-parenthesis upper K prime circled-plus o upper P a d right-parenthesis StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue left-parenthesis upper H left-parenthesis upper K Superscript prime Baseline circled-plus i upper P a d StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue upper M right-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>K</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>o</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>K</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>&#8853;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>i</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>d</mi><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper H upper M upper A upper C minus upper H left-parenthesis upper K comma upper M right-parenthesis equals upper H left-parenthesis left-parenthesis upper K prime circled-plus o upper P a d right-parenthesis StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue left-parenthesis upper H left-parenthesis upper K Superscript prime Baseline circled-plus i upper P a d StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue upper M right-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c10_525.png)(10.8) 

where *H* is the underlying hash function,  <math alttext="upper K prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>K</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></math> ![upper K prime](images/c10_526.png) an expanded key derived from a master key *K*, and  <math alttext="o upper P a d" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>o</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow></math> ![o upper P a d](images/c10_527.png) and  <math alttext="i upper P a d" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow></math> ![i upper P a d](images/c10_528.png) are constant bit strings.

*H* function takes any bit string (with length multiple of 8) and returns a bit string (called digest) of fixed length  <math alttext="upper H l e n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper H l e n](images/c10_529.png). Function *H* splits up a message into blocks of a fixed length *b*, which is a parameter of *H* (e.g.  <math alttext="b equals 512" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>512</mn></mrow></math> ![b equals 512](images/c10_530.png) for SHA-1 and  <math alttext="b equals 1024" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1024</mn></mrow></math> ![b equals 1024](images/c10_531.png) for SHA-512) and iterates[⁸](#c10.xhtml#c10-note-0008) over them with a compression function *h*. A compression function *h* is basic hash function that takes a single *b*\-bit block and a chaining parameter (which may be an IV or the tag of the previous block) and returns a  <math alttext="upper H l e n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper H l e n](images/c10_532.png)\-bit tag; i.e. *h* is a map:  <math alttext="h colon StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript upper H l e n Baseline times StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript b Baseline right-arrow StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript upper H l e n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>:</mo><msup><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></msup><mo>&#215;</mo><msup><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mi>b</mi></msup><mo>&#8594;</mo><msup><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![h colon StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript upper H l e n Baseline times StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript b Baseline right-arrow StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript upper H l e n](images/c10_533.png). Any HMAC variant is a function, i.e.

 <math alttext="upper H upper M upper A upper C minus upper H colon upper H upper M upper A upper C minus upper H colon StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript k Baseline times StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript asterisk Baseline right-arrow StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript upper H l e n" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>H</mi><mo>:</mo><mi>H</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>H</mi><mo>:</mo><msup><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mi>k</mi></msup><mo>&#215;</mo><msup><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo></msup><mo>&#8594;</mo><msup><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![upper H upper M upper A upper C minus upper H colon upper H upper M upper A upper C minus upper H colon StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript k Baseline times StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript asterisk Baseline right-arrow StartSet 0 comma 1 EndSet Superscript upper H l e n](images/c10_534.png)

where *k* denotes the key bit-length and  <math alttext="upper H l e n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper H l e n](images/c10_535.png) the tag bit-length (e.g.  <math alttext="upper H l e n equals 160" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>160</mn></mrow></math> ![upper H l e n equals 160](images/c10_536.png) if  <math alttext="upper H equals" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>=</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![upper H equals](images/c10_537.png) SHA-1,  <math alttext="upper H l e n equals 256" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>256</mn></mrow></math> ![upper H l e n equals 256](images/c10_538.png) if  <math alttext="upper H equals" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>=</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![upper H equals](images/c10_539.png) is SHA-256, and  <math alttext="upper H l e n equals 512" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>512</mn></mrow></math> ![upper H l e n equals 512](images/c10_540.png) if *H* is SHA3-512).

HMAC security relies on i) the security of the key derivation key (KDF), which computes  <math alttext="upper K prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![upper K prime](images/c10_541.png) from *K* and ii) on the security of the underlying hash function *H*. The KDF used in standard HMAC is a PRG (pseudorandom generator). Therefore, the first condition is omitted when analyzing the security of standard HMAC.

In \[[11](#c10.xhtml#c10-bib-0011)\], Bellare proved that HMAC is a PRF under the sole assumption that the compression function of the underlying hash function is a PRF. Standard hash families SHA-1 and SHA-2 (including SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512, SHA-512/224, and SHA-512/256) are iterated hash functions and are considered as secure PRFs. SHA-3 is a based on the Keccak permutation and it also is considered as a secure hash function.

Under the assumption that the underlying compression function is a PRF, Bellare proposed the following bound:

xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>h</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![t Subscript h](images/c10_558.png) is the time for one computation of *h*.

It is worth noticing that the bound mentioned above is a simplified one of a more accurate bound proposed in \[[6](#c10.xhtml#c10-bib-0006)\], which adds an advantage of any adversary that attacks the dual function of compression *h*.  <math alttext="h overbar" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>&#175;</mo></mover></math> ![h overbar](images/c10_559.png) is a dual function of *h* is defined by  <math alttext="ModifyingAbove h With bar left-parenthesis x comma y right-parenthesis equals h left-parenthesis y comma x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>&#175;</mo></mover><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![ModifyingAbove h With bar left-parenthesis x comma y right-parenthesis equals h left-parenthesis y comma x right-parenthesis](images/c10_560.png).

## 10.5 Generic Models for Security Analysis of Authenticated-Encryption Modes

### 10.5.1 Generic Modeling of Security of AEAD Modes

Authenticated-encryption modes (i.e. CCM, GCM, and AES-GCM-SIV) are presented in [Chapter 9](#c09.xhtml). The security analysis of authenticated-encryption modes focuses both on privacy and on authenticity. Therefore, security analyses of privacy (see [section 10.3](#c10.xhtml#c10-sec-01004)) and authenticity (see [Section 10.4](#c10.xhtml#c10-sec-01005)) are used to provide bounds for CCM, GCM, and AES-GCM-SIV. Recall that an authenticated-encryption mode takes a plaintext, an associated data, and an IV and it returns a pair ciphertext‒tag. Thus, an authenticated-encryption *F* can be defined by a function:

 <math alttext="upper F colon script upper K times script upper N times double-struck upper A times German script upper M right-arrow script upper C" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>:</mo><mi mathvariant="script">K</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi mathvariant="script">N</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi mathvariant="double-struck">A</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi mathvariant="fraktur">&#8499;</mi><mo>&#8594;</mo><mi mathvariant="script">C</mi></mrow></math> ![upper F colon script upper K times script upper N times double-struck upper A times German script upper M right-arrow script upper C](images/c10_561.png)

where  <math alttext="script upper K" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="script">K</mi></math> ![script upper K](images/c10_562.png) denotes the key space,  <math alttext="script upper N" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="script">N</mi></math> ![script upper N](images/c10_563.png) the IV space,  <math alttext="double-struck upper A" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="double-struck">A</mi></math> ![double-struck upper A](images/c10_564.png) the associated data space,  <math alttext="German script upper M" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="fraktur">&#8499;</mi></math> ![German script upper M](images/c10_565.png) the plaintext space, and the  <math alttext="script upper C" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi mathvariant="script">C</mi></mrow></math> ![script upper C](images/c10_566.png) ciphertext-tag space.

The authenticated decryption is defined by:

 <math alttext="upper F Superscript negative 1 Baseline colon script upper K times script upper N times double-struck upper A times script upper C German script upper M union Superscript zero width space Baseline left-brace up-tack right-brace" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>F</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>:</mo><mi mathvariant="script">K</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi mathvariant="script">N</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi mathvariant="double-struck">A</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi mathvariant="script">C</mi><mi mathvariant="fraktur">&#8499;</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><msup><mstyle displaystyle="true" mathsize="140%"><mo>&#8746;</mo></mstyle><mtext>&#8203;</mtext></msup><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mrow><mo>{</mo><mo>&#8869;</mo><mo>}</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![upper F Superscript negative 1 Baseline colon script upper K times script upper N times double-struck upper A times script upper C German script upper M union Superscript zero width space Baseline left-brace up-tack right-brace](images/c10_567.png)

where ⊥ denotes that the input ciphertext is invalid and the returned result is undefined.

Using the same notations as in previous sections, the privacy advantage and authenticity advantage of an adversary attacking an authenticated-encryption *F*, over block cipher *E*, are defined by:

 <math alttext="2 Superscript negative 47" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>47</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![2 Superscript negative 47](images/c10_568.png) <math alttext="upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper F left-bracket upper E right-bracket Superscript m a c Baseline left-parenthesis script upper A right-parenthesis equals Overscript d e f Endscripts probability left-bracket upper K left-arrow Overscript upper R Endscripts script upper K semicolon script upper A Superscript upper F Super Subscript upper K Superscript comma upper F Super Subscript upper K Super Superscript negative 1 Superscript Baseline right double arrow 1 right-bracket" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>D</mi><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>F</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mi>E</mi><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="script">A</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>f</mi></mrow></mover><mi>Pr</mi><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mover><mo>&#8592;</mo><mi>R</mi></mover><mi mathvariant="script">K</mi><mo>;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi mathvariant="script">A</mi><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mi>K</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></msup><mo>&#8658;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper A upper D upper V Subscript upper F left-bracket upper E right-bracket Superscript m a c Baseline left-parenthesis script upper A right-parenthesis equals Overscript d e f Endscripts probability left-bracket upper K left-arrow Overscript upper R Endscripts script upper K semicolon script upper A Superscript upper F Super Subscript upper K Superscript comma upper F Super Subscript upper K Super Superscript negative 1 Superscript Baseline right double arrow 1 right-bracket](images/c10_569.png)

### 10.5.2 Some Security Bounds for CCM, GCM, and AES-GCM-SIV

#### 10.5.2.1 Bounds for CCM

#### 10.5.2.2 Bounds for GCM

The first bounds on GCM privacy and authenticity were proposed by D. A. McGrew and J. Viega, the authors of GMAC, in \[[13](#c10.xhtml#c10-bib-0013)\], but in \[[14](#c10.xhtml#c10-bib-0014)\], the authors showed that the proof was invalid in some cases and proposed other bounds with a larger security bound roughly by a factor of  <math alttext="2 Superscript 22" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>22</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![2 Superscript 22](images/c10_579.png), then optimized bounds were proposed in \[[14](#c10.xhtml#c10-bib-0014)\].

where:

*q* denotes the number of queries (either MAC generation or verification queries);

 <math alttext="q Subscript upper E" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>E</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![q Subscript upper E](images/c10_588.png) and  <math alttext="q Subscript upper D" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>D</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![q Subscript upper D](images/c10_589.png) are the numbers of encryption and decryption queries, respectively;

 <math alttext="l Subscript p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>l</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![l Subscript p](images/c10_590.png) is total number of plaintext bits;

 <math alttext="l Subscript upper I upper V" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>l</mi><mrow><mi>I</mi><mi>V</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![l Subscript upper I upper V](images/c10_591.png) is the maximum bit-length of the IV; *l* is the maximum number of input bits (of ciphertext and associated data) for any query;

*t* and  <math alttext="t prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![t prime](images/c10_592.png) are computation times of GMAC and PRP *E* adversaries, respectively;

 <math alttext="q prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![q prime](images/c10_593.png) is the total number of blocks processed by the block cipher *E*.

#### 10.5.2.3 Some Bounds for AES-GCM-SIV Security

AES-GCM-SIV is the strongest authenticated-encryption mode. It is expected to become dominating AEAD mode in the future. AES-GCM-SIV is a nonce-misuse-resistant algorithm at some extent. That is, the nonce cannot repeat indefinitely without jeopardizing the security of the encryption system. In \[[15](#c10.xhtml#c10-bib-0015)\], the authors of AES-GCM-SIV proved the following bound:

 <math alttext="upper Q Subscript upper D Superscript i" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi></msubsup></mrow></math> ![upper Q Subscript upper D Superscript i](images/c10_598.png) ( <math alttext="i equals 1 comma ellipsis comma upper N" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> ![i equals 1 comma ellipsis comma upper N](images/c10_599.png)) denotes the number of decryption queries using the nonce *i*; thus,  <math alttext="upper Q Subscript upper D Baseline equals StartSet upper Q Subscript upper D Superscript 1 Baseline comma ellipsis comma upper Q Subscript upper D Superscript upper N Baseline EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>D</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi>D</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi>D</mi><mi>N</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper Q Subscript upper D Baseline equals StartSet upper Q Subscript upper D Superscript 1 Baseline comma ellipsis comma upper Q Subscript upper D Superscript upper N Baseline EndSet](images/c10_600.png);

 <math alttext="upper B m a x equals max Underscript i equals 1 comma ellipsis comma upper N Endscripts left-parenthesis upper B Superscript i Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mi>max</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper B m a x equals max Underscript i equals 1 comma ellipsis comma upper N Endscripts left-parenthesis upper B Superscript i Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c10_601.png), where  <math alttext="upper B Superscript i" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi></msup></mrow></math> ![upper B Superscript i](images/c10_602.png) denotes the number of blocks encrypted or decrypted using nonce *i*. If all messages are of the same length, then  <math alttext="upper B m a x equals max Underscript i equals 1 comma ellipsis comma upper N Endscripts left-parenthesis upper Q Subscript upper E Superscript i Baseline plus upper Q Subscript upper D Superscript i Baseline right-parenthesis asterisk 2 Superscript m" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mi>max</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi>E</mi><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow></math> ![upper B m a x equals max Underscript i equals 1 comma ellipsis comma upper N Endscripts left-parenthesis upper Q Subscript upper E Superscript i Baseline plus upper Q Subscript upper D Superscript i Baseline right-parenthesis asterisk 2 Superscript m](images/c10_603.png);  <math alttext="2 Superscript m" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow></math> ![2 Superscript m](images/c10_604.png) denotes the length (in blocks) of the longest message.

Gueron and Lindell’s bound is proved under the assumptions that: i) that the number of queries *N* is at most  <math alttext="2 Superscript 64" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>64</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![2 Superscript 64](images/c10_605.png), ii) the advantage when attacking AES is negligible, iii) no associated data is included in queries, and iv)  <math alttext="2 Superscript m Baseline asterisk sigma-summation Underscript i Overscript upper N Endscripts upper Q Subscript upper D Superscript i Baseline less-than StartFraction upper N asterisk upper B m a x squared Over 2 EndFraction" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></msup><mo>\*</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msubsup><mo>&#8721;</mo><mi>i</mi><mi>N</mi></msubsup></mstyle><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo>&#60;</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></math> ![2 Superscript m Baseline asterisk sigma-summation Underscript i Overscript upper N Endscripts upper Q Subscript upper D Superscript i Baseline less-than StartFraction upper N asterisk upper B m a x squared Over 2 EndFraction](images/c10_606.png).
