    The integer  <math alttext="upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline minus upper M" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline minus upper M](images/c12_148.png) is a multiple of *p* and *q*. Since *p* and *q* are primes, there exists a positive integer *f* such that  <math alttext="upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline minus upper M equals f asterisk p asterisk q" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline minus upper M equals f asterisk p asterisk q](images/c12_149.png). It results that  <math alttext="upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline minus upper M" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline minus upper M](images/c12_150.png) also is a multiple of  <math alttext="n equals p asterisk q" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>\*</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> ![n equals p asterisk q](images/c12_151.png). Consequently,  <math alttext="upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d n identical-to upper M m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>M</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d n identical-to upper M m o d n](images/c12_152.png).
    
2.  Case 2: *M* is coprime with *p* and not with *q*.

Since *q* is a prime number, *M* is either 0 or a multiple of *q* (i.e.  <math alttext="upper M identical-to 0 m o d q" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>0</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M identical-to 0 m o d q](images/c12_153.png)). By the modular arithmetic exponentiation rule, we have:

 <math alttext="upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d q identical-to left-parenthesis 0 right-parenthesis Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d q identical-to 0 m o d q identical-to upper M m o d q" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>0</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>M</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d q identical-to left-parenthesis 0 right-parenthesis Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d q identical-to 0 m o d q identical-to upper M m o d q](images/c12_154.png)

Since *M* is coprime with *p*, by Fermat’s little theorem,

 <math alttext="upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d p identical-to upper M asterisk left-parenthesis upper M Superscript left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript k left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline m o d p identical-to upper M asterisk left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis Superscript k left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline m o d p" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d p identical-to upper M asterisk left-parenthesis upper M Superscript left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript k left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline m o d p identical-to upper M asterisk left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis Superscript k left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline m o d p](images/c12_155.png)

The integer  <math alttext="upper M Superscript e d Baseline minus upper M" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8722;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M Superscript e d Baseline minus upper M](images/c12_156.png) is a multiple of *p* and *q*. Since *p* and *q* are primes and  <math alttext="n equals p asterisk q" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>=</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>\*</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> ![n equals p asterisk q](images/c12_157.png),  <math alttext="upper M Superscript e d Baseline minus zero width space upper M" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8722;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#8203;</mtext><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M Superscript e d Baseline minus zero width space upper M](images/c12_158.png) also is a multiple of  <math alttext="upper M Superscript e d Baseline minus zero width space upper M" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8722;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#8203;</mtext><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M Superscript e d Baseline minus zero width space upper M](images/c12_159.png). Consequently,  <math alttext="upper M Superscript e d Baseline identical-to upper M m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>M</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M Superscript e d Baseline identical-to upper M m o d n](images/c12_160.png).□

### 12.2.4 RSA Security

Aiming to recover the confidential messages, adversaries need to disclose *d*, the private key of the recipient. By definition of RSA scheme:  <math alttext="d asterisk e identical-to 1 m o d phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>&#981;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![d asterisk e identical-to 1 m o d phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis](images/c12_161.png). If an adversary could find  <math alttext="phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#981;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis](images/c12_162.png), then he/she could compute *d* and recover the plaintext. However, if  <math alttext="n equals p asterisk q" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> ![n equals p asterisk q](images/c12_163.png) is a product of two primes, computing  <math alttext="phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#981;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis](images/c12_164.png) is equivalent to factoring *n*.

Factoring the RSA modulus *n* is a particular case of the following well-known problem, which is known to be computationally infeasible for large integers:

In case of RSA, the number of integers, which are coprime with *n* is  <math alttext="left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis](images/c12_167.png), which is derived from Euler’s totient theorem (Theorem 3.1).

Given *n*, finding *p* and *q* may be solved by naïvely checking all pairs  <math alttext="p prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></math> ![p prime](images/c12_168.png) and  <math alttext="q prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></math> ![q prime](images/c12_169.png) in the range  <math alttext="left-bracket 3 period period left-parenthesis n minus 1 right-parenthesis right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>..</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></math> ![left-bracket 3 period period left-parenthesis n minus 1 right-parenthesis right-bracket](images/c12_170.png) to find the pair whose product is equal to *n*. Thus, the number of tries (in case of brute-force attack) is very high when large primes are used. Another approach is to pick randomly an integer and test if it is a factor of *n*. Given that there exist  <math alttext="phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#981;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis](images/c12_171.png) integers that are coprime with *n*, the probability to pick an integer that divides *n* is  <math alttext="1 minus StartFraction phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis Over n EndFraction" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>&#981;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>n</mi></mfrac></mrow></math> ![1 minus StartFraction phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis Over n EndFraction](images/c12_172.png); with large prime numbers *p* and *q*, such probability is almost zero.

As far as we know and under the current known attacks, RSA security relies on the difficulty to factorize the modulus. No algorithm has been published that can factorize all integers in polynomial time. The general number field sieve (GNFS) is the most efficient algorithm for factoring (very) large integer; its correctness is considered in \[[3](#c12.xhtml#c12-bib-0003)\]. The GNFS has a time complexity of:

 <math alttext="e x p left-parenthesis left-parenthesis left-parenthesis StartFraction 64 Over 9 EndFraction right-parenthesis Superscript one-third Baseline plus o left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis right-parenthesis left-parenthesis left-parenthesis l n n right-parenthesis Superscript one-third Baseline left-parenthesis l n l n n right-parenthesis Superscript two-thirds Baseline right-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>64</mn></mrow><mn>9</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>o</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>l</mi><mi>n</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo><msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup><mo>(</mo><mi>l</mi><mi>n</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>l</mi><mi>n</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo><msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![e x p left-parenthesis left-parenthesis left-parenthesis StartFraction 64 Over 9 EndFraction right-parenthesis Superscript one-third Baseline plus o left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis right-parenthesis left-parenthesis left-parenthesis l n n right-parenthesis Superscript one-third Baseline left-parenthesis l n l n n right-parenthesis Superscript two-thirds Baseline right-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c12_173.png)

Such a complexity makes the factorization computationally infeasible for very large numbers. That is the reason why the RSA requires the selection of large prime numbers *p* and *q* to generate the keys. If both *p* and *q* are not large enough, there exists an efficient algorithm, called Lenstra’s elliptic-curve factorization method, which makes use of elliptic curves (discussed in [Chapter 13](#c13.xhtml)), with a time complexity of  <math alttext="e x p left-parenthesis StartRoot l o g left-parenthesis p right-parenthesis asterisk l o g left-parenthesis l o g left-parenthesis p right-parenthesis right-parenthesis EndRoot right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mi>l</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo><mi>l</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![e x p left-parenthesis StartRoot l o g left-parenthesis p right-parenthesis asterisk l o g left-parenthesis l o g left-parenthesis p right-parenthesis right-parenthesis EndRoot right-parenthesis](images/c12_174.png), where *p* is the smallest factor of the number to factorize. To thwart attacks based on Lenstra’s algorithm, it is recommended to use both RSA primes of a bit-length in magnitude of 1000 or more.

For readers interested in prime numbers, the list of 10 000 first prime numbers and the top ten prime numbers are available at: [https://tk5.org](https://tk5.org).

Just for curiosity, the largest prime number was discovered in 2018; it is  <math alttext="2 Superscript 82 589 933 Baseline minus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>82</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>589</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>933</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8722;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![2 Superscript 82 589 933 Baseline minus 1](images/c12_175.png) (it has 24 862 048 decimal digits).

When the value of the modulus *n* is not large, some RSA-S[⁵](#c12.xhtml#c12-note-0005) had been cracked: RSA-576 cracked in 2003, RSA-640 in 2005, and RSA-768 in 2009. However, it should be noticed that much computation resources were monopolized to crack RSA. Cryptanalysts used either special multiprocessors or clusters interconnected via Internet. For example, RSA-640 was cracked with the equivalent of almost 200 years of computing on a single core 2.2 GHz and RSA-768 with the equivalent of almost 2000 years of computing on a single core 2.2 GHz.

No RSA-S with  <math alttext="upper S ampersand gt semicolon 768" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#38;gt;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>768</mn></mrow></math> ![upper S ampersand gt semicolon 768](images/c12_176.png) has been cracked yet. RSA-2048 is recommended and currently widely used. In conclusion, RSA is considered secure when used with large primes (made of 1024 or more bits). Therefore, users may continue using RA for years before the RSA-2048 would be broken.

**Note**. It is not yet formally proven that the only way to disclose RSA-encrypted message is by factoring the modulus *n*.

### 12.2.5 Optimal Asymmetric Encryption Padding (OAEP)

Low public-key exponent values may make the system vulnerable to some attacks, if the system is not complying with security implementation guidelines. For example, the same message encrypted three times with exponent  <math alttext="normal e equals 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> ![normal e equals 3](images/c12_177.png) and three pairwise coprime moduli can be recovered (see Problem 12.1). Another example of incorrect use of RSA is to send messages represented by low values (see Problem 12.5).

A countermeasure has been proposed by Bellare and Rogaway \[[4](#c12.xhtml#c12-bib-0004)\] to address vulnerabilities raised by low values. The proposed method is called Optimal Asymmetric Encryption Padding (OAEP). When implemented, the OAEP enables to use any public-key exponent greater than 2 and any message value less than the modulus. Since 2016, the OAEP support is required to provide security to new applications \[[5](#c12.xhtml#c12-bib-0005)\].

Message encoding is a way to message formatting before the RSA encryption is applied. Therefore, short messages are extended with padding data and then encrypted at a high level of security (see [Figure 12.3](#c12.xhtml#c12-fig-0003)). RSA-OAEP is the combination of basic RSA and OAEP.

![Figure 12.3 OAEP encryption diagram.](images/c12f003.png)

[**Figure 12.3**](#c12.xhtml#rc12-fig-0003) OAEP encryption diagram.

![Figure 12.4 PSS encoding method of RSA-PSS.](images/c12f004.png)

[**Figure 12.4**](#c12.xhtml#rc12-fig-0004) PSS encoding method of RSA-PSS.

RSA-OAEP is parameterized by the choice of a hash function  <math alttext="upper H left-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>(</mo><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![upper H left-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c12_178.png) and a mask generation function  <math alttext="upper G left-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>(</mo><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![upper G left-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c12_179.png). In current RSA cryptosystems, OAEP mainly makes use of SHA-256, SHA-384, and SHA-512. Any mask generation function used in RSA-OAEP shall be deterministic (i.e. the output is fully determined by the input). Mask generation function takes a byte string of variable length and returns a string of the desired length. The output should be pseudorandom (i.e. given a part of the output but not the input, it should be infeasible to predict another part of the output). At the time of writing this chapter, only one mask generation function is specified by the RSA standards, which is labeled MGF1. The latter is a hash function. Thus, in current RSA-OAEP cryptosystems, the encoding is based on hash functions; a single hash function may be used for both parameters  <math alttext="upper H left-parenthesis right-parenthesis and upper G left-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>(</mo><mo>)</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>and&#160;</mtext><mi>G</mi><mo>(</mo><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![upper H left-parenthesis right-parenthesis and upper G left-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c12_180.png) or two distinct hash functions may be used. Below is the description of the RSA-OAEP cryptosystem \[[5](#c12.xhtml#c12-bib-0005)\].

*   *RSA-OAEP set up*
    
    *   Select a hash function  <math alttext="upper H left-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>(</mo><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![upper H left-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c12_181.png) with output of  <math alttext="h upper L e n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>h</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![h upper L e n](images/c12_182.png) bytes.
    *   Select a mask generation function  <math alttext="upper G left-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>(</mo><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![upper G left-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c12_183.png) with output of  <math alttext="m a s k upper L e n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![m a s k upper L e n](images/c12_184.png) bytes.
    *   The identity[⁶](#c12.xhtml#c12-note-0006) of the selected functions shall be known to both parties.
*   *RSA-OAEP encoding*
    
    *   Let *k* denote the length (in bytes) of the modulus *n* and  <math alttext="m upper L e n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![m upper L e n](images/c12_185.png) denote the length of the message *M* to encrypt. Message length  <math alttext="m upper L e n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![m upper L e n](images/c12_186.png) is bounded:  <math alttext="m upper L e n less-than-or-equal-to k minus 2 asterisk h upper L e n minus 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mi>h</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![m upper L e n less-than-or-equal-to k minus 2 asterisk h upper L e n minus 2](images/c12_187.png) (because padding bytes and hashes are concatenated with the original message before encryption).
    *   Select a string label *L* associated with the message *M*. In the version PKCS #1 v2.2, *L* is the empty string.
    *   Compute:  <math alttext="upper H left-parenthesis upper L right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>L</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper H left-parenthesis upper L right-parenthesis](images/c12_188.png), the hash associated with the label *L*.
    *   Generate a padding string  <math alttext="upper P upper S" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>S</mi></mrow></math> ![upper P upper S](images/c12_189.png) formed by  <math alttext="k minus m upper L e n minus 2 asterisk h upper L e n minus 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mi>h</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![k minus m upper L e n minus 2 asterisk h upper L e n minus 2](images/c12_190.png) zero-bytes. The length of string  <math alttext="upper P upper S" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>S</mi></mrow></math> ![upper P upper S](images/c12_191.png) may be zero.
    *   Make concatenation:  <math alttext="upper P upper M equals upper H left-parenthesis upper L right-parenthesis parallel-to upper P upper S parallel-to 0 normal x Baseline 01 parallel-to upper M" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>L</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8741;</mo><mi>P</mi><mi>S</mi><mo>&#8741;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>0</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mn>01</mn><mo>&#8741;</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> ![upper P upper M equals upper H left-parenthesis upper L right-parenthesis parallel-to upper P upper S parallel-to 0 normal x Baseline 01 parallel-to upper M](images/c12_192.png). ( <math alttext="0 normal x Baseline 01" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mn>01</mn></mrow></math> ![0 normal x Baseline 01](images/c12_193.png) denotes a byte with value 1).
    *   Generate a random string  <math alttext="s e e d" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>s</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow></math> ![s e e d](images/c12_194.png) of length  <math alttext="h upper L e n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>h</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![h upper L e n](images/c12_195.png) bytes.
    *   Compute:  <math alttext="m a s k e d upper P upper M equals upper P upper M circled-plus upper G left-parenthesis s e e d comma k minus h upper L e n minus 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>P</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>P</mi><mi>M</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>G</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>h</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![m a s k e d upper P upper M equals upper P upper M circled-plus upper G left-parenthesis s e e d comma k minus h upper L e n minus 1 right-parenthesis](images/c12_196.png).
    *   Compute:  <math alttext="m a s k e d upper S e e d equals s e e d circled-plus upper G left-parenthesis m a s k e d upper P upper M comma h upper L e n right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>S</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>s</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>G</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![m a s k e d upper S e e d equals s e e d circled-plus upper G left-parenthesis m a s k e d upper P upper M comma h upper L e n right-parenthesis](images/c12_197.png)
    *   Make concatenation:  <math alttext="upper E upper M equals 0 normal x Baseline 00 parallel-to m a s k e d upper S e e d parallel-to m a s k e d upper P upper M" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mn>00</mn><mo>&#8741;</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>S</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mo>&#8741;</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> ![upper E upper M equals 0 normal x Baseline 00 parallel-to m a s k e d upper S e e d parallel-to m a s k e d upper P upper M](images/c12_198.png) The length of the encoded message  <math alttext="upper E upper M" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> ![upper E upper M](images/c12_199.png) is *k* (i.e. the modulus length in bytes).
*   *RSA-OAEP encryption*
    
    *   Encryption:  <math alttext="upper C identical-to upper E upper M Superscript normal e Baseline m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>E</mi><msup><mi>M</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper C identical-to upper E upper M Superscript normal e Baseline m o d n](images/c12_200.png) (*e* is the public key exponent and  <math alttext="upper E upper M" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> ![upper E upper M](images/c12_201.png) is the output of the OAEP encoding operation).
*   *RSA-OAEP decryption*
    
    *   Decryption:  <math alttext="upper E upper M identical-to upper C Superscript d Baseline m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mi>C</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper E upper M identical-to upper C Superscript d Baseline m o d n](images/c12_202.png) (*d* is the private key and *C*, the ciphertext)
    *   OAEP decoding (assuming no error in the coding step)
        
        *   Let  <math alttext="upper E upper M period m a s k e d upper S e e d" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>.</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>S</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow></math> ![upper E upper M period m a s k e d upper S e e d](images/c12_203.png) and  <math alttext="upper E upper M period m a s k e d upper P upper M" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>.</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> ![upper E upper M period m a s k e d upper P upper M](images/c12_204.png) denote the values of the fields  <math alttext="m a s k e d upper S e e d" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>S</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow></math> ![m a s k e d upper S e e d](images/c12_205.png) and  <math alttext="m a s k e d upper P upper M" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> ![m a s k e d upper P upper M](images/c12_206.png), respectively, in the byte string  <math alttext="upper E upper M" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> ![upper E upper M](images/c12_207.png)
        *   Compute:  <math alttext="s e e d equals upper E upper M period m a s k e d upper S e e d circled-plus upper G left-parenthesis upper E upper M period m a s k e d upper P upper M comma h upper L e n right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>s</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>E</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>.</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>S</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>G</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>E</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>.</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![s e e d equals upper E upper M period m a s k e d upper S e e d circled-plus upper G left-parenthesis upper E upper M period m a s k e d upper P upper M comma h upper L e n right-parenthesis](images/c12_208.png)
        *   Compute:  <math alttext="upper P upper M equals upper E upper M period m a s k e d upper P upper M circled-plus upper G left-parenthesis s e e d comma k minus h upper L e n minus 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>E</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>.</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>M</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>G</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>h</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper P upper M equals upper E upper M period m a s k e d upper P upper M circled-plus upper G left-parenthesis s e e d comma k minus h upper L e n minus 1 right-parenthesis](images/c12_209.png)
        *   Extract *M* from  <math alttext="upper P upper M" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> ![upper P upper M](images/c12_210.png) byte string.

**Example 12.3** In the example, byte values are represented in decimal.

*   – RSA modulus and key selection 
    *   6 is the minimum length to form an OAEP message with one data byte, one padding byte, two one-byte hashes, and two constant bytes (see [Figure 12.3](#c12.xhtml#c12-fig-0003)). Therefore, the length of the RSA-OAEP modulus *n* should be of six bytes at least.
    *    <math alttext="p equals 32 452 843" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>452</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>843</mn></mrow></math> ![p equals 32 452 843](images/c12_211.png) and  <math alttext="q equals 1 000 003" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>003</mn></mrow></math> ![q equals 1 000 003](images/c12_212.png) are two primes such that  <math alttext="n equals p asterisk q equals 32 452 940 358 529" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>32</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>452</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>940</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>358</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>529</mn></mrow></math> ![n equals p asterisk q equals 32 452 940 358 529](images/c12_213.png) has a length of six bytes.
    *   Public key exponent selection:  <math alttext="e equals 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![e equals 5](images/c12_214.png)
    *   Private key selection:  <math alttext="d equals 6 490 581 381 137" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>490</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>581</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>381</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>137</mn></mrow></math> ![d equals 6 490 581 381 137](images/c12_215.png)
*   – Hash and mask generation functions and padding string 
    *   To make the computations easy to check without a specialized library, let  <math alttext="upper H left-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>(</mo><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![upper H left-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c12_216.png) be the identity function and  <math alttext="upper G left-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>(</mo><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![upper G left-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c12_217.png) the one-byte-left rotation function that returns the most-right byte(s).
    *   Let *L* be one-byte string with decimal value 65. A single byte is hashed. Hence,  <math alttext="h upper L e n equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>h</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![h upper L e n equals 1](images/c12_218.png).
*   – OAEP encoding
    
    *   Let *M* be one-byte message with decimal value 10.
    *   A single padding zero-byte is included in the OAEP message.
    *    <math alttext="upper P upper M equals upper H left-parenthesis upper L right-parenthesis StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue upper P upper S StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 0 normal x Baseline 01 StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue upper M equals 65 StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 00 StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 01 StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 10" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>L</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>P</mi><mi>S</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>0</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mn>01</mn><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>65</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>00</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>01</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>10</mn></mrow></math> ![upper P upper M equals upper H left-parenthesis upper L right-parenthesis StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue upper P upper S StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 0 normal x Baseline 01 StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue upper M equals 65 StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 00 StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 01 StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 10](images/c12_219.png).
    *   Let  <math alttext="s e e d" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>s</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow></math> ![s e e d](images/c12_220.png) be 21.
    *    <math alttext="m a s k e d upper P upper M equals upper P upper M circled-plus upper G left-parenthesis s e e d comma k minus h upper L e n minus 1 right-parenthesis equals upper P upper M circled-plus upper G left-parenthesis 21 comma 4 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>P</mi><mi>M</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>G</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>h</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>P</mi><mi>M</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>G</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>21</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![m a s k e d upper P upper M equals upper P upper M circled-plus upper G left-parenthesis s e e d comma k minus h upper L e n minus 1 right-parenthesis equals upper P upper M circled-plus upper G left-parenthesis 21 comma 4 right-parenthesis](images/c12_221.png)
        
         <math alttext="upper G left-parenthesis 21 comma 4 right-parenthesis equals 00 parallel-to 00 parallel-to 21 parallel-to 00" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>21</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>=</mo><mn>00</mn><mo>&#8741;</mo><mn>00</mn><mo>&#8741;</mo><mn>21</mn><mo>&#8741;</mo><mn>00</mn></mrow></math> ![upper G left-parenthesis 21 comma 4 right-parenthesis equals 00 parallel-to 00 parallel-to 21 parallel-to 00](images/c12_222.png)
        
         <math alttext="upper P upper M circled-plus upper G left-parenthesis 21 comma 4 right-parenthesis equals 65 parallel-to 00 parallel-to 20 parallel-to 10" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>M</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>G</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>21</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>=</mo><mn>65</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8741;</mo><mn>00</mn><mo>&#8741;</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>&#8741;</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></math> ![upper P upper M circled-plus upper G left-parenthesis 21 comma 4 right-parenthesis equals 65 parallel-to 00 parallel-to 20 parallel-to 10](images/c12_223.png)

xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>S</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>s</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>G</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ### 12.2.6 RSA Signature

RSA signature scheme is specified in two standards: ANSI standard X9.31 \[[6](#c12.xhtml#c12-bib-0006)\] and RFC 8017 \[[5](#c12.xhtml#c12-bib-0005)\]. In the ANSI standard, it is called RSA DSA (digital signature algorithm) and RSASSA (Signature Scheme with Appendix) in RFC 8017. There exist some detail differences between the standards, which makes implementations non-interoperable. In the sequel, the focus is on the common principles of RSA signature scheme in both standards.

RSA digital signature is computed with a private key *d* and a hash function  <math alttext="upper H left-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>(</mo><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![upper H left-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c12_243.png) and it is verified with the public key  <math alttext="left-parenthesis e comma n right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis e comma n right-parenthesis](images/c12_244.png). A signature key pair  <math alttext="left-parenthesis left-parenthesis e comma n right-parenthesis comma d right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis left-parenthesis e comma n right-parenthesis comma d right-parenthesis](images/c12_245.png) shall be used only for signing and not for other purposes.

The standards specify three choices for the size of the modulus *n*: 1024, 2048, and 3072 bits. The standards recommend that the modulus size and the hash output size must be the same unless an agreement had been made between participating entities to use a stronger hash function.

#### 12.2.6.1 RSA Signature Generation

The signature of message *M* is generated as follows:

Compute the message hash:  <math alttext="h equals upper H left-parenthesis upper M right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![h equals upper H left-parenthesis upper M right-parenthesis](images/c12_246.png)

Encrypt the hash:  <math alttext="s identical-to h Superscript d Baseline m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>s</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![s identical-to h Superscript d Baseline m o d n](images/c12_247.png), *s* is the signature

Send the following items to the verifier

*    <math alttext="left-parenthesis upper M comma s right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis upper M comma s right-parenthesis](images/c12_248.png): message and its signature
*    <math alttext="left-parenthesis e comma n right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis e comma n right-parenthesis](images/c12_249.png): signer’s public-key
*    <math alttext="upper H left-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>(</mo><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![upper H left-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c12_250.png): identity of the hash function

#### 12.2.6.2 RSA Signature Verification

The intended recipient, or any other party (since the message content is not encrypted), verifies the signature to determine the authenticity of the message.

Before signature verification, the verifier should receive and accept signer’s public-key and the identity of the hash function. Upon reception of a message  <math alttext="upper M prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![upper M prime](images/c12_251.png) and its signature  <math alttext="s prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![s prime](images/c12_252.png), the verification is as follows:

*   Compute the hash of the received message:  <math alttext="h prime equals upper H left-parenthesis upper M prime right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>'</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![h prime equals upper H left-parenthesis upper M prime right-parenthesis](images/c12_253.png)
*   Signature decryption:  <math alttext="h left-parenthesis s prime right-parenthesis Superscript e Baseline identical-to m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>h</mi><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>e</mi></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![h left-parenthesis s prime right-parenthesis Superscript e Baseline identical-to m o d n](images/c12_254.png)
*   Verification: if  <math alttext="h prime equals h" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></math> ![h prime equals h](images/c12_255.png), the signature is valid. Otherwise, reject the message.

As for message encryption, in order to increase the efficiency of signature generation and verification, the public key exponents  <math alttext="e equals 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> ![e equals 3](images/c12_256.png) and  <math alttext="e equals 65537" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>65537</mn></mrow></math> ![e equals 65537](images/c12_257.png) are commonly used.

#### 12.2.6.3 Probabilistic Signature Scheme (PSS)

In the PKCS#1 standard, two signature methods are specified: RSASSA-PSS and RSASSA-PKCS1-v1\_5. RSASSA-PKCS1-v1\_5 and RSA-PKCS1-v1\_5 are used interchangeably; and RSASSA-PSS and RSA-PSS also are used interchangeably. RSA-PKCS#1 method is no more recommended; and current and future RSA signature systems are required to use RSA-PSS method.

RSA-PSS method is expected to provide a higher level of security to prevent attacks, which try to discover private keys from intercepted signed messages. The PSS method is similar to the OAEP method introduced in the previous section. PSS is based on adding random padding information to the original message before generating the signature. Below is the description of RSA-PSS.

*   *RSA-PSS set up*
    
    *   Select a hash function  <math alttext="upper H left-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>(</mo><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![upper H left-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c12_258.png) with output of  <math alttext="h upper L e n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>h</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![h upper L e n](images/c12_259.png) bytes.
    *   Select a mask generation function  <math alttext="upper G left-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>(</mo><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![upper G left-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c12_260.png) with output of  <math alttext="m a s k upper L e n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![m a s k upper L e n](images/c12_261.png) bytes. In the current version of the RSA signature standards, it is recommended that the function  <math alttext="upper G left-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>(</mo><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![upper G left-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c12_262.png) is the same as the hash function  <math alttext="left-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c12_263.png).
    *   Select a salt length  <math alttext="s upper L e n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>s</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![s upper L e n](images/c12_264.png). A salt is a random byte string added to the original message. The salt string used in RSA-PSS and the seed string used in RSA-OAEP ([section 12.2.5](#c12.xhtml#c12-sec-02006)) have the same role, which is creating randomness in messages. Therefore, that the same message content results in distinct messages when encrypted or signed.
    *   The identity of the selected functions and the salt length shall be known to both parties.
*   *RSA-PSS encoding* (see [Figure 12.4](#c12.xhtml#c12-fig-0004))
    
    *   Let *k* denote the length (in bytes) of the modulus *n*. *k* also is the length of signature *s*. Let *M* be the message to sign.
    *   Compute:  <math alttext="m upper H a s h equals upper H left-parenthesis upper M right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>H</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![m upper H a s h equals upper H left-parenthesis upper M right-parenthesis](images/c12_265.png), the hash associated with the message *M*.
    *   Generate a random string  <math alttext="s a l t" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>s</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> ![s a l t](images/c12_266.png) of length  <math alttext="s upper L e n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>s</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![s upper L e n](images/c12_267.png) bytes.
    *   Make concatenations and hashing: 
        *    <math alttext="upper P upper H s a l t equals left-parenthesis 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 right-parenthesis parallel-to m upper H a s h parallel-to s a l t" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>H</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>00</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>00</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>00</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>00</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>00</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>00</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>00</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>00</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8741;</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>H</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>h</mi><mo>&#8741;</mo><mi>s</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> ![upper P upper H s a l t equals left-parenthesis 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 right-parenthesis parallel-to m upper H a s h parallel-to s a l t](images/c12_268.png).  <math alttext="upper P upper H s a l t" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>H</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> ![upper P upper H s a l t](images/c12_269.png) is a byte string with length of  <math alttext="8 plus h upper L e n plus s upper L e n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>h</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>s</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![8 plus h upper L e n plus s upper L e n](images/c12_270.png) bytes.
        *    <math alttext="upper H a s h equals upper H left-parenthesis upper P upper H s a l t right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>H</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper H a s h equals upper H left-parenthesis upper P upper H s a l t right-parenthesis](images/c12_271.png)
        *   Generate a string  <math alttext="upper P upper S" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>S</mi></mrow></math> ![upper P upper S](images/c12_272.png) consisting of  <math alttext="k minus s upper L e n minus h upper L e n minus 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>s</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>h</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![k minus s upper L e n minus h upper L e n minus 2](images/c12_273.png) zero bytes.  <math alttext="upper P upper S" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>S</mi></mrow></math> ![upper P upper S](images/c12_274.png) may be the empty string.
        *    <math alttext="upper P s a l t equals upper P upper S parallel-to 0 normal x Baseline 01 parallel-to s a l t" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>P</mi><mi>S</mi><mo>&#8741;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>0</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mn>01</mn><mo>&#8741;</mo><mi>s</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> ![upper P s a l t equals upper P upper S parallel-to 0 normal x Baseline 01 parallel-to s a l t](images/c12_275.png) (the length of  <math alttext="upper P s a l t" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> ![upper P s a l t](images/c12_276.png) is  <math alttext="k minus h upper L e n minus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>h</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![k minus h upper L e n minus 1](images/c12_277.png))
        *    <math alttext="m a s k e d upper P s a l t equals upper P s a l t circled-plus upper G left-parenthesis upper H a s h comma k minus h upper L e n minus 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>P</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>t</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>G</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>h</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![m a s k e d upper P s a l t equals upper P s a l t circled-plus upper G left-parenthesis upper H a s h comma k minus h upper L e n minus 1 right-parenthesis](images/c12_278.png)
        *    <math alttext="upper E upper H equals m a s k e d upper P s a l t parallel-to upper H a s h parallel-to 0 normal x b c" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mi>H</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8741;</mo><mi>H</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>h</mi><mo>&#8741;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>0</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mi>b</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></math> ![upper E upper H equals m a s k e d upper P s a l t parallel-to upper H a s h parallel-to 0 normal x b c](images/c12_279.png)
            
             <math alttext="upper E upper H" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mi>H</mi></mrow></math> ![upper E upper H](images/c12_280.png) is the encoded hash and  <math alttext="0 normal x b c" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mi>b</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></math> ![0 normal x b c](images/c12_281.png) is a byte with hexadecimal value  <math alttext="b c" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></math> ![b c](images/c12_282.png).
            
    *   *RSA-PSS signature generation* 
        *    <math alttext="s" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>s</mi></mrow></math> ![s](images/c12_283.png)≡ <math alttext="upper E upper H Superscript d Baseline m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><msup><mi>H</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper E upper H Superscript d Baseline m o d n](images/c12_284.png) (*d* is the private key and  <math alttext="upper E upper H" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mi>H</mi></mrow></math> ![upper E upper H](images/c12_285.png) is the output of the encoding operation)
    *   *RSA-PSS signature verification* 
        *   Receive the domain parameters (including:  <math alttext="upper H left-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>(</mo><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![upper H left-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c12_286.png) and  <math alttext="upper G left-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>(</mo><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![upper G left-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c12_287.png) identities and salt length), signer’s public key  <math alttext="left-parenthesis e comma n right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis e comma n right-parenthesis](images/c12_288.png), and a message *M* and its signature *s*.
        *   Signature decryption:  <math alttext="upper E upper H identical-to s Superscript normal e Baseline m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mi>H</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper E upper H identical-to s Superscript normal e Baseline m o d n](images/c12_289.png)
        *   Signature decoding and verification 
            *   Compute the hash of received message:  <math alttext="m upper H a s h equals upper H left-parenthesis upper M right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>H</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![m upper H a s h equals upper H left-parenthesis upper M right-parenthesis](images/c12_290.png)
            *   From  <math alttext="upper E upper H" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mi>H</mi></mrow></math> ![upper E upper H](images/c12_291.png) extract  <math alttext="upper E upper H period m a s k e d upper P s a l t" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mi>H</mi><mo>.</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> ![upper E upper H period m a s k e d upper P s a l t](images/c12_292.png) and  <math alttext="upper E upper H period upper H a s h" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mi>H</mi><mo>.</mo><mi>H</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></math> ![upper E upper H period upper H a s h](images/c12_293.png).
            *    <math alttext="upper P s a l t equals upper E upper H period m a s k e d upper P s a l t circled-plus upper G left-parenthesis upper E upper H period upper H a s h comma k minus h upper L e n minus 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>E</mi><mi>H</mi><mo>.</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>t</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mi>G</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>E</mi><mi>H</mi><mo>.</mo><mi>H</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>h</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper P s a l t equals upper E upper H period m a s k e d upper P s a l t circled-plus upper G left-parenthesis upper E upper H period upper H a s h comma k minus h upper L e n minus 1 right-parenthesis](images/c12_294.png)
            *   Extract  <math alttext="s a l t" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>s</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> ![s a l t](images/c12_295.png) value from  <math alttext="upper P s a l t" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> ![upper P s a l t](images/c12_296.png).
            *   Let  <math alttext="upper P upper H s a l t" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>H</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> ![upper P upper H s a l t](images/c12_297.png) be a string formed as follows:
                
                 <math alttext="left-parenthesis 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 right-parenthesis parallel-to m upper H a s h parallel-to s a l t period" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>00</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>00</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>00</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>00</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>00</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>00</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>00</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>00</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>&#8741;</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>H</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>h</mi><mo>&#8741;</mo><mi>s</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>.</mo></math> ![left-parenthesis 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 right-parenthesis parallel-to m upper H a s h parallel-to s a l t period](images/c12_298.png)
                
            *   Compute the hash of  <math alttext="upper P upper H s a l t" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>H</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> ![upper P upper H s a l t](images/c12_299.png):  <math alttext="upper H a s h Superscript prime Baseline equals upper H left-parenthesis upper P upper H s a l t right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>H</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper H a s h Superscript prime Baseline equals upper H left-parenthesis upper P upper H s a l t right-parenthesis](images/c12_300.png)
            *   If  <math alttext="upper H a s h Superscript prime Baseline equals upper E upper H period upper H a s h" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>E</mi><mi>H</mi><mo>.</mo><mi>H</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></math> ![upper H a s h Superscript prime Baseline equals upper E upper H period upper H a s h](images/c12_301.png), then the signature is valid. Otherwise, it is not valid.

**Example 12.4** In the example, byte values are represented in decimal.

*   – Consider the following RSA parameters: 
    *    <math alttext="p equals 702 613" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>702</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>613</mn></mrow></math> ![p equals 702 613](images/c12_302.png) and  <math alttext="q equals 1 000 003" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>003</mn></mrow></math> ![q equals 1 000 003](images/c12_303.png).
    *    <math alttext="n equals p asterisk q equals 702 615 107 839" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>702</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>615</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>107</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>839</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![n equals p asterisk q equals 702 615 107 839](images/c12_304.png) has a length of five bytes.
    *    <math alttext="k equals 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![k equals 5](images/c12_305.png), *k* is the byte length of modulus *n*.
    *   Public key exponent selection:  <math alttext="e equals 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![e equals 5](images/c12_306.png).
    *   Private key selection:  <math alttext="d equals 140 522 681 045" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>140</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>522</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>681</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>045</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![d equals 140 522 681 045](images/c12_307.png).
*   – Hash and mask generation functions

As in example 12.3, to make the computations easy to check without a specialized library, let  <math alttext="upper H left-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>(</mo><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![upper H left-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c12_308.png) be the identity function and  <math alttext="upper G left-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>(</mo><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![upper G left-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c12_309.png) the one-byte-left rotation function that returns the most-right byte(s). Let the hash output length be 1 (i.e.  <math alttext="h upper L e n equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>h</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![h upper L e n equals 1](images/c12_310.png)).

*   – To use a modulus with length of six bytes, and without loss of generality, the string of eight zeros in  <math alttext="upper P upper H s a l t" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>H</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> ![upper P upper H s a l t](images/c12_311.png) is removed and the padding string  <math alttext="upper P upper S" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>S</mi></mrow></math> ![upper P upper S](images/c12_312.png) is the empty string.
*   – PSS encoding 
    *   Let *M* be one-byte message with decimal value 10.
    *    <math alttext="upper H left-parenthesis 10 right-parenthesis equals 10" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></math> ![upper H left-parenthesis 10 right-parenthesis equals 10](images/c12_313.png)
    *   Let  <math alttext="s a l t equals 77" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>s</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>77</mn></mrow></math> ![s a l t equals 77](images/c12_314.png) (a random value of one byte length)
    *    <math alttext="upper P upper H s a l t equals 10 StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 77" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>H</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>77</mn></mrow></math> ![upper P upper H s a l t equals 10 StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 77](images/c12_315.png) <math alttext="upper H a s h equals upper H left-parenthesis upper P upper H s a l t right-parenthesis equals 10 StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 77" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>H</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>77</mn></mrow></math> ![upper H a s h equals upper H left-parenthesis upper P upper H s a l t right-parenthesis equals 10 StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 77](images/c12_316.png)
    *    <math alttext="upper P upper S" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>S</mi></mrow></math> ![upper P upper S](images/c12_317.png) consists of the empty string
    *    <math alttext="upper P s a l t equals 01 StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 77" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>01</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>77</mn></mrow></math> ![upper P s a l t equals 01 StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 77](images/c12_318.png)

    *    <math alttext="upper P s a l t equals upper E upper H period m a s k e d upper P s a l t circled-plus upper G left-parenthesis upper E upper H period upper H a s h comma k minus h upper L e n minus 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>E</mi><mi>H</mi><mo>.</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>t</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8853;</mo><mi>G</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>E</mi><mi>H</mi><mo>.</mo><mi>H</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>h</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper P s a l t equals upper E upper H period m a s k e d upper P s a l t circled-plus upper G left-parenthesis upper E upper H period upper H a s h comma k minus h upper L e n minus 1 right-parenthesis](images/c12_333.png)
        
         <math alttext="equals left-parenthesis 76 StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 71 right-parenthesis circled-plus left-parenthesis 77 StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 10 right-parenthesis equals 01 StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 77" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>76</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>71</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>&#8853;</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>77</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>10</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>01</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>77</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![equals left-parenthesis 76 StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 71 right-parenthesis circled-plus left-parenthesis 77 StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 10 right-parenthesis equals 01 StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue 77](images/c12_334.png)
