Thus,  <math alttext="d equals negative 23" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>23</mn></mrow></math> ![d equals negative 23](images/c12_781.png). In modulo 60,  <math alttext="d equals 37" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>37</mn></mrow></math> ![d equals 37](images/c12_782.png).

***Exercise 12.4***

Let RSA parameters be  <math alttext="p equals 101" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>=</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>101</mn></mrow></math> ![p equals 101](images/c12_783.png), <math alttext="q equals 113" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>q</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>=</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>113</mn></mrow></math> ![q equals 113](images/c12_784.png), and  <math alttext="e equals 6747" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>e</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>=</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>6747</mn></mrow></math> ![e equals 6747](images/c12_785.png).

Since RSA parameters *p*, *q*, and *e* are known, it is easy to find the private key *d* and then decrypt the ciphertext.

1.  Find the secret key using the Extended Euclidean algorithm

RSA modulus  <math alttext="n equals 101 asterisk 113 equals 11413" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>101</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>113</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>11413</mn></mrow></math> ![n equals 101 asterisk 113 equals 11413](images/c12_786.png) and  <math alttext="phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis equals 100 asterisk 112 equals 11200" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>112</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>11200</mn></mrow></math> ![phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis equals 100 asterisk 112 equals 11200](images/c12_787.png)

By definition of RSA private key:  <math alttext="d asterisk 6747 identical-to 1 m o d 11200" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>\*</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>6747</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>11200</mn></mrow></math> ![d asterisk 6747 identical-to 1 m o d 11200](images/c12_788.png).

The Extended Euclidean algorithm is used to find *x* and *y* such that  <math alttext="a x plus b y equals GCD left-parenthesis a comma b right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mtext>GCD</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![a x plus b y equals GCD left-parenthesis a comma b right-parenthesis](images/c12_789.png).

Let  <math alttext="a equals 11200" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>11200</mn></mrow></math> ![a equals 11200](images/c12_790.png) and  <math alttext="b equals 6747" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6747</mn></mrow></math> ![b equals 6747](images/c12_791.png).

By definition of RSA public key,  <math alttext="GCD left-parenthesis 11200 comma 6747 right-parenthesis equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>GCD</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>11200</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>6747</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![GCD left-parenthesis 11200 comma 6747 right-parenthesis equals 1](images/c12_792.png).

Application of the Extended Euclidean algorithm:

 <math alttext="11200 equals 6747 asterisk 1 plus 4453" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>11200</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>6747</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4453</mn></mrow></math> ![11200 equals 6747 asterisk 1 plus 4453](images/c12_793.png)

 <math alttext="6747 equals 4453 asterisk 1 plus 2294" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>6747</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>4453</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2294</mn></mrow></math> ![6747 equals 4453 asterisk 1 plus 2294](images/c12_794.png)

 <math alttext="4453 equals 2294 asterisk 1 plus 2159" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>4453</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2294</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2159</mn></mrow></math> ![4453 equals 2294 asterisk 1 plus 2159](images/c12_795.png)

 <math alttext="2294 equals 2159 asterisk 1 plus 135" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>2294</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2159</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>135</mn></mrow></math> ![2294 equals 2159 asterisk 1 plus 135](images/c12_796.png)

 <math alttext="2159 equals 135 asterisk 15 plus 134" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>2159</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>135</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>134</mn></mrow></math> ![2159 equals 135 asterisk 15 plus 134](images/c12_797.png)

 <math alttext="135 equals 134 asterisk 1 plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>135</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>134</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![135 equals 134 asterisk 1 plus 1](images/c12_798.png)

Now, do the inverse calculations to retrieve *x* and *y* such that <math alttext="11200 x plus 6747 y equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>11200</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>6747</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![11200 x plus 6747 y equals 1](images/c12_799.png)

  <math alttext="1 equals 135 minus 134" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>135</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>134</mn></mrow></math> ![1 equals 135 minus 134](images/c12_800.png)

  <math alttext="equals left-parenthesis 2294 minus 2159 right-parenthesis minus left-parenthesis 2159 minus 15 asterisk left-parenthesis 2294 minus 2159 right-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>2294</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2159</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>2159</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>2294</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2159</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![equals left-parenthesis 2294 minus 2159 right-parenthesis minus left-parenthesis 2159 minus 15 asterisk left-parenthesis 2294 minus 2159 right-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c12_801.png)

  <math alttext="equals left-parenthesis 2294 right-parenthesis minus 2 asterisk 2159 plus left-parenthesis 15 asterisk left-parenthesis 2294 minus 2159 right-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>2294</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>2159</mn><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>15</mn><mo>\*</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>2294</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2159</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![equals left-parenthesis 2294 right-parenthesis minus 2 asterisk 2159 plus left-parenthesis 15 asterisk left-parenthesis 2294 minus 2159 right-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c12_802.png)

  <math alttext="equals 16 asterisk left-parenthesis 2294 right-parenthesis plus left-parenthesis negative 17 right-parenthesis asterisk left-parenthesis 2159 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>2294</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>17</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>\*</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>2159</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![equals 16 asterisk left-parenthesis 2294 right-parenthesis plus left-parenthesis negative 17 right-parenthesis asterisk left-parenthesis 2159 right-parenthesis](images/c12_803.png)

  <math alttext="equals 33 asterisk left-parenthesis 6747 minus 4453 right-parenthesis minus 17 asterisk left-parenthesis 4453 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>33</mn><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>6747</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>4453</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>17</mn><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>4453</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![equals 33 asterisk left-parenthesis 6747 minus 4453 right-parenthesis minus 17 asterisk left-parenthesis 4453 right-parenthesis](images/c12_804.png)

  <math alttext="equals 11200 asterisk left-parenthesis negative 50 right-parenthesis plus 6747 asterisk left-parenthesis 83 right-parenthesis equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>11200</mn><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>6747</mn><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>83</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![equals 11200 asterisk left-parenthesis negative 50 right-parenthesis plus 6747 asterisk left-parenthesis 83 right-parenthesis equals 1](images/c12_805.png)

Section 3.3.1.3.2 shows that when  <math alttext="GCD left-parenthesis a comma b right-parenthesis equals a x plus b y" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>GCD</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow></math> ![GCD left-parenthesis a comma b right-parenthesis equals a x plus b y](images/c12_806.png) is solved with *a* prime and  <math alttext="GCD left-parenthesis a comma b right-parenthesis equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>GCD</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![GCD left-parenthesis a comma b right-parenthesis equals 1](images/c12_807.png), *y* represents  <math alttext="b Superscript negative 1 Baseline m o d a" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>a</mi></mrow></math> ![b Superscript negative 1 Baseline m o d a](images/c12_808.png).

Therefore, the secret key is  <math alttext="d equals 83" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>83</mn></mrow></math> ![d equals 83](images/c12_809.png).

2) Decryption of the ciphertext 5859 using the right-to-left exponentiation method.

 <math alttext="normal upper C equals 5859" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5859</mn></mrow></math> ![normal upper C equals 5859](images/c12_810.png)

Decryption:  <math alttext="upper M identical-to 5859 Superscript 83 Baseline m o d 11413" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mn>5859</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>83</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>11413</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![upper M identical-to 5859 Superscript 83 Baseline m o d 11413](images/c12_811.png)

The exponent  <math alttext="83 equals 64 plus 16 plus 2 plus 1 equals 2 Superscript 6 Baseline plus 2 Superscript 4 Baseline plus 2 Superscript 1 Baseline plus 2 Superscript 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>83</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>6</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>1</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>0</mn></msup></mrow></math> ![83 equals 64 plus 16 plus 2 plus 1 equals 2 Superscript 6 Baseline plus 2 Superscript 4 Baseline plus 2 Superscript 1 Baseline plus 2 Superscript 0](images/c12_812.png)

Thus, the right-to-left binary exponentiation runs seven iterations. <math alttext="upper L equals 7 comma k 6 equals 1 comma k 5 equals 0 comma k 4 equals 0 comma k 3 equals 0 comma k 2 equals 0 comma k 1 equals 1 comma k 0 equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>k</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>k</mi><mn>5</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>k</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>k</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>k</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>k</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>k</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![upper L equals 7 comma k 6 equals 1 comma k 5 equals 0 comma k 4 equals 0 comma k 3 equals 0 comma k 2 equals 0 comma k 1 equals 1 comma k 0 equals 1](images/c12_813.png)

Check: one can easily do computations (using a program of the right-to-left binary exponentiation method) to confirm that:

*    <math alttext="1 identical-to 9192 Superscript 112 Baseline m o d 11413" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mn>9192</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>112</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>11413</mn></mrow></math> ![1 identical-to 9192 Superscript 112 Baseline m o d 11413](images/c12_822.png) and  <math alttext="5859 identical-to 9192 Superscript 27 Baseline m o d 11413" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>5859</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mrow><mn>9192</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>27</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>11413</mn></mrow></math> ![5859 identical-to 9192 Superscript 27 Baseline m o d 11413](images/c12_823.png)
    
    Thus, encrypting the plaintext 9192 with the public key 6747 results in  <math alttext="upper C identical-to 9192 Superscript 6747 Baseline m o d 11413 identical-to 9192 Superscript 60 asterisk 112 plus 27 Baseline m o d 11413 equals 5859" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mn>9192</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>6747</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>11413</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mn>9192</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>60</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>112</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>27</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>11413</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>5859</mn></mrow></math> ![upper C identical-to 9192 Superscript 6747 Baseline m o d 11413 identical-to 9192 Superscript 60 asterisk 112 plus 27 Baseline m o d 11413 equals 5859](images/c12_824.png).
    

***Exercise 12.5***

Let  <math alttext="p equals 37" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>37</mn></mrow></math> ![p equals 37](images/c12_825.png),  <math alttext="p equals 131" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>131</mn></mrow></math> ![p equals 131](images/c12_826.png),  <math alttext="d equals 3343" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3343</mn></mrow></math> ![d equals 3343](images/c12_827.png), and  <math alttext="upper C equals 1819" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1819</mn></mrow></math> ![upper C equals 1819](images/c12_828.png).

The plaintext *M* is such that  <math alttext="upper M identical-to 1819 Superscript 3343 Baseline m o d 37 asterisk 131" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mn>1819</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>3343</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>37</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>131</mn></mrow></math> ![upper M identical-to 1819 Superscript 3343 Baseline m o d 37 asterisk 131](images/c12_829.png) and by Lemma 3.2,  <math alttext="upper M identical-to 1819 Superscript 3343 Baseline m o d 37" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mn>1819</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>3343</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>37</mn></mrow></math> ![upper M identical-to 1819 Superscript 3343 Baseline m o d 37](images/c12_830.png) and  <math alttext="upper M identical-to 1819 Superscript 3343 Baseline m o d 131" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mn>1819</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>3343</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>131</mn></mrow></math> ![upper M identical-to 1819 Superscript 3343 Baseline m o d 131](images/c12_831.png).

To find the plaintext *M* using the CRT-based RSA decryption, we proceed as follows:

*   Reduce the bases of congruences:
    
     <math alttext="1819 equals 37 asterisk 49 plus 6 equals 131 asterisk 13 plus 116" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1819</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>37</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>49</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>131</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>13</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>116</mn></mrow></math> ![1819 equals 37 asterisk 49 plus 6 equals 131 asterisk 13 plus 116](images/c12_832.png)
    
     <math alttext="upper C Subscript p Baseline identical-to 1819 m o d 37 identical-to 6" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1819</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>37</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></math> ![upper C Subscript p Baseline identical-to 1819 m o d 37 identical-to 6](images/c12_833.png)
    
     <math alttext="upper C Subscript q Baseline identical-to 1819 m o d 131 identical-to 116" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1819</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>131</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>116</mn></mrow></math> ![upper C Subscript q Baseline identical-to 1819 m o d 131 identical-to 116](images/c12_834.png)
    
*   Reduce the exponents:
    
     <math alttext="3343 equals 92 asterisk left-parenthesis 37 minus 1 right-parenthesis plus 31 equals 25 asterisk left-parenthesis 131 minus 1 right-parenthesis plus 93" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>3343</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>92</mn><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>37</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>31</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>131</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>93</mn></mrow></math> ![3343 equals 92 asterisk left-parenthesis 37 minus 1 right-parenthesis plus 31 equals 25 asterisk left-parenthesis 131 minus 1 right-parenthesis plus 93](images/c12_835.png)
    
     <math alttext="d Subscript p Baseline equals 3343 m o d left-parenthesis 37 minus 1 right-parenthesis equals 31" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>3343</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>37</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>31</mn></mrow></math> ![d Subscript p Baseline equals 3343 m o d left-parenthesis 37 minus 1 right-parenthesis equals 31](images/c12_836.png)
    
     <math alttext="d Subscript q Baseline equals 3343 m o d left-parenthesis 131 minus 1 right-parenthesis equals 93" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>3343</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>131</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>93</mn></mrow></math> ![d Subscript q Baseline equals 3343 m o d left-parenthesis 131 minus 1 right-parenthesis equals 93](images/c12_837.png)
    
*   Exponentiation in  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 37" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>&#8484;</mi><mrow><mn>37</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 37](images/c12_838.png) and  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z 131" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>&#8484;</mi><mrow><mn>131</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z 131](images/c12_839.png):
    
     <math alttext="upper M Subscript p Baseline equals upper C Subscript p Superscript d Super Subscript p Superscript Baseline m o d p equals 6 Superscript 31 Baseline m o d 37 identical-to 31" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mi>p</mi><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>6</mn><mrow><mn>31</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>37</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>31</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![upper M Subscript p Baseline equals upper C Subscript p Superscript d Super Subscript p Superscript Baseline m o d p equals 6 Superscript 31 Baseline m o d 37 identical-to 31](images/c12_840.png)
    
     <math alttext="upper M Subscript q Baseline equals upper C Subscript q Superscript d Super Subscript q Superscript Baseline m o d q equals 116 Superscript 93 Baseline m o d 131 identical-to 30" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mi>q</mi><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>q</mi></msub></mrow></msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mn>116</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>93</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>131</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow></math> ![upper M Subscript q Baseline equals upper C Subscript q Superscript d Super Subscript q Superscript Baseline m o d q equals 116 Superscript 93 Baseline m o d 131 identical-to 30](images/c12_841.png)
    
*   CRT-based solution to decryption

2) What is the solution to  <math alttext="5 Superscript k Baseline identical-to 35 m o d 97" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mi>k</mi></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>35</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>97</mn></mrow></math> ![5 Superscript k Baseline identical-to 35 m o d 97](images/c12_859.png)?

With the help of a python program, powers of 5 from 1 to 95 have been computed.  <math alttext="k equals 32" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow></math> ![k equals 32](images/c12_860.png) is the solution to the DLP. The result can be easily checked with the modular exponentiation[^(19)](#c12.xhtml#c12-note-0019) as follows:

 <math alttext="5 squared identical-to 25 m o d 97" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>25</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>97</mn></mrow></math> ![5 squared identical-to 25 m o d 97](images/c12_861.png)        <math alttext="5 Superscript 4 Baseline identical-to 25 squared m o d 97 equals 43" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mrow><mn>25</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>97</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>43</mn></mrow></math> ![5 Superscript 4 Baseline identical-to 25 squared m o d 97 equals 43](images/c12_862.png)

 <math alttext="5 Superscript 16 Baseline identical-to 43 Superscript 4 Baseline m o d 97 equals 36" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mn>43</mn></mrow><mn>4</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>97</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>36</mn></mrow></math> ![5 Superscript 16 Baseline identical-to 43 Superscript 4 Baseline m o d 97 equals 36](images/c12_863.png)    <math alttext="5 Superscript 32 Baseline identical-to 36 squared m o d 97 equals 35" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mrow><mn>32</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mrow><mn>36</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>97</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>35</mn></mrow></math> ![5 Superscript 32 Baseline identical-to 36 squared m o d 97 equals 35](images/c12_864.png)

    <math alttext="s 2 equals left-parenthesis 57 minus 9 asterisk 18 right-parenthesis asterisk 17 Superscript negative 1 Baseline m o d 30 equals left-parenthesis 57 minus 9 asterisk 18 right-parenthesis asterisk 23 m o d 30 equals 15" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>57</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>18</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo><msup><mrow><mn>17</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>30</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>57</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>18</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo><mn>23</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>30</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow></math> ![s 2 equals left-parenthesis 57 minus 9 asterisk 18 right-parenthesis asterisk 17 Superscript negative 1 Baseline m o d 30 equals left-parenthesis 57 minus 9 asterisk 18 right-parenthesis asterisk 23 m o d 30 equals 15](images/c12_874.png)

Verification of  <math alttext="upper M 1 equals 25" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow></math> ![upper M 1 equals 25](images/c12_875.png) and its signature  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 20 comma 5 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>20</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>5</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 20 comma 5 right-parenthesis](images/c12_876.png):

    <math alttext="v equals upper P u Subscript upper B Superscript r Baseline asterisk r Superscript s Baseline m o d p equals left-parenthesis 8 Superscript 20 Baseline asterisk 20 Superscript 5 Baseline right-parenthesis m o d 31 equals 25" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow><mi>B</mi><mi>r</mi></msubsup><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mi>s</mi></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mn>8</mn><mrow><mn>20</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></msup><mo>\*</mo><msup><mrow><mn>20</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>31</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow></math> ![v equals upper P u Subscript upper B Superscript r Baseline asterisk r Superscript s Baseline m o d p equals left-parenthesis 8 Superscript 20 Baseline asterisk 20 Superscript 5 Baseline right-parenthesis m o d 31 equals 25](images/c12_877.png)

    <math alttext="g Superscript upper M Baseline m o d p equals 7 Superscript 25 Baseline m o d 31 equals 25" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>M</mi></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>7</mn><mrow><mn>25</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>31</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow></math> ![g Superscript upper M Baseline m o d p equals 7 Superscript 25 Baseline m o d 31 equals 25](images/c12_878.png)

    <math alttext="v equals g Superscript upper M Baseline m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>M</mi></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![v equals g Superscript upper M Baseline m o d p](images/c12_879.png) is satisfied; thus, the signature is valid.

Verification of  <math alttext="upper M 2 equals 57" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>57</mn></mrow></math> ![upper M 2 equals 57](images/c12_880.png) and its signature  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 18 comma 15 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>18</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>15</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 18 comma 15 right-parenthesis](images/c12_881.png):

    <math alttext="v equals upper P u Subscript upper B Superscript r Baseline asterisk r Superscript s Baseline m o d p equals left-parenthesis 8 Superscript 18 Baseline asterisk 18 Superscript 15 Baseline right-parenthesis m o d 31 equals 16" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow><mi>B</mi><mi>r</mi></msubsup><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mi>s</mi></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mn>8</mn><mrow><mn>18</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></msup><mo>\*</mo><msup><mrow><mn>18</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>15</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>31</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow></math> ![v equals upper P u Subscript upper B Superscript r Baseline asterisk r Superscript s Baseline m o d p equals left-parenthesis 8 Superscript 18 Baseline asterisk 18 Superscript 15 Baseline right-parenthesis m o d 31 equals 16](images/c12_882.png)

    <math alttext="g Superscript upper M Baseline m o d p equals 7 Superscript 57 Baseline m o d 31 equals 16" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>M</mi></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>7</mn><mrow><mn>57</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>31</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow></math> ![g Superscript upper M Baseline m o d p equals 7 Superscript 57 Baseline m o d 31 equals 16](images/c12_883.png)

    <math alttext="v equals g Superscript upper M Baseline m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>M</mi></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![v equals g Superscript upper M Baseline m o d p](images/c12_884.png) is satisfied; thus, the signature is valid.

***Problem 12.1***

1.  If  <math alttext="e equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![e equals 1](images/c12_885.png), then the encryption becomes  <math alttext="upper C identical-to upper M Superscript 1 Baseline m o d n equals upper M" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mi>M</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> ![upper C identical-to upper M Superscript 1 Baseline m o d n equals upper M](images/c12_886.png). Thus, with  <math alttext="e equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![e equals 1](images/c12_887.png), the plaintext and ciphertext are identical; no confidentiality is assured.
    
    If  <math alttext="e equals 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![e equals 2](images/c12_888.png), then  <math alttext="d asterisk e identical-to 1 m o d phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>&#981;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![d asterisk e identical-to 1 m o d phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis](images/c12_889.png) becomes  <math alttext="2 asterisk d identical-to 1 m o d phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>&#981;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![2 asterisk d identical-to 1 m o d phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis](images/c12_890.png). Since *p* and *q* are primes,  <math alttext="phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#981;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis](images/c12_891.png) is divisible by 2 and consequently, there is no *d* such that  <math alttext="2 asterisk d" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></math> ![2 asterisk d](images/c12_892.png) and  <math alttext="phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#981;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis](images/c12_893.png) are coprime. In other words,  <math alttext="upper G upper C upper D left-parenthesis 2 comma phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis right-parenthesis not-equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>G</mi><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>&#981;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8800;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![upper G upper C upper D left-parenthesis 2 comma phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis right-parenthesis not-equals 1](images/c12_894.png). Therefore, the multiplicative inverse of  <math alttext="2 m o d phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>&#981;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![2 m o d phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis](images/c12_895.png) does not exist.
    
2.  Let *M* be a message, which is encrypted three times with the same public-key exponent  <math alttext="e equals 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> ![e equals 3](images/c12_896.png) and with three distinct moduli, which are pairwise coprime. For example, the public keys are ( <math alttext="e equals 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> ![e equals 3](images/c12_897.png),  <math alttext="n 1 equals 5 asterisk 11" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>11</mn></mrow></math> ![n 1 equals 5 asterisk 11](images/c12_898.png)), ( <math alttext="e equals 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> ![e equals 3](images/c12_899.png),  <math alttext="n 2 equals 23 asterisk 29" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>23</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>\*</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>29</mn></mrow></math> ![n 2 equals 23 asterisk 29](images/c12_900.png)), and  <math alttext="left-parenthesis e equals 3 comma n 3 equals 41 asterisk 101 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>41</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>\*</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>101</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis e equals 3 comma n 3 equals 41 asterisk 101 right-parenthesis](images/c12_901.png). The ciphertexts are as follows:
    
       <math alttext="upper C 1 identical-to upper M cubed m o d n 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>M</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper C 1 identical-to upper M cubed m o d n 1](images/c12_902.png)    <math alttext="upper C 2 identical-to upper M cubed m o d n 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>M</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![upper C 2 identical-to upper M cubed m o d n 2](images/c12_903.png)    <math alttext="upper C 3 identical-to upper M cubed m o d n 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>M</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![upper C 3 identical-to upper M cubed m o d n 3](images/c12_904.png)
    
    Let *x* be  <math alttext="upper M cubed" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></math> ![upper M cubed](images/c12_905.png). By substitution:
    
       <math alttext="x identical-to upper C 1 m o d n 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![x identical-to upper C 1 m o d n 1](images/c12_906.png)    <math alttext="x identical-to upper C 2 m o d n 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![x identical-to upper C 2 m o d n 2](images/c12_907.png)    <math alttext="x identical-to upper C 3 m o d n 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![x identical-to upper C 3 m o d n 3](images/c12_908.png)
    
    Then, by transformation (with  <math alttext="k 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![k 1](images/c12_909.png),  <math alttext="k 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![k 2](images/c12_910.png), and  <math alttext="k 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![k 3](images/c12_911.png) positive integers):
    
       <math alttext="x equals upper C 1 plus k 1 asterisk n 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>\*</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![x equals upper C 1 plus k 1 asterisk n 1](images/c12_912.png)    <math alttext="x equals upper C 2 plus k 2 asterisk n 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>\*</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![x equals upper C 2 plus k 2 asterisk n 2](images/c12_913.png)    <math alttext="x equals upper C 3 plus k 3 asterisk n 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>\*</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![x equals upper C 3 plus k 3 asterisk n 3](images/c12_914.png)
    
    Let us take an example with  <math alttext="upper M equals 13" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>13</mn></mrow></math> ![upper M equals 13](images/c12_915.png) and the suggested public keys. The ciphertexts are:
    
        <math alttext="upper C 1 identical-to 13 cubed m o d left-parenthesis 5 asterisk 11 right-parenthesis equals 52" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mrow><mn>13</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>11</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>52</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![upper C 1 identical-to 13 cubed m o d left-parenthesis 5 asterisk 11 right-parenthesis equals 52](images/c12_916.png)    <math alttext="upper C 2 identical-to 13 cubed m o d left-parenthesis 23 asterisk 29 right-parenthesis equals 196" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mn>13</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>23</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>29</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>196</mn></mrow></math> ![upper C 2 identical-to 13 cubed m o d left-parenthesis 23 asterisk 29 right-parenthesis equals 196](images/c12_917.png)
    
        <math alttext="upper C 3 identical-to 13 cubed m o d left-parenthesis 41 asterisk 101 right-parenthesis equals 2197" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mn>13</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>41</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>101</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2197</mn></mrow></math> ![upper C 3 identical-to 13 cubed m o d left-parenthesis 41 asterisk 101 right-parenthesis equals 2197](images/c12_918.png)
    
    The linear equation system to solve is as follows:
    
        <math alttext="x equals 52 plus k 1 asterisk left-parenthesis 5 asterisk 11 right-parenthesis" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>52</mn><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>11</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![x equals 52 plus k 1 asterisk left-parenthesis 5 asterisk 11 right-parenthesis](images/c12_919.png)
    
        <math alttext="x equals 196 plus k 2 asterisk left-parenthesis 23 asterisk 29 right-parenthesis" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>196</mn><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>23</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>29</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![x equals 196 plus k 2 asterisk left-parenthesis 23 asterisk 29 right-parenthesis](images/c12_920.png)
    
        <math alttext="x equals 2197 plus k 3 asterisk left-parenthesis 41 asterisk 101 right-parenthesis" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2197</mn><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>41</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>101</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![x equals 2197 plus k 3 asterisk left-parenthesis 41 asterisk 101 right-parenthesis](images/c12_921.png)
    

Since the moduli  <math alttext="n 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![n 1](images/c12_922.png),  <math alttext="n 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![n 2](images/c12_923.png), and  <math alttext="n 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![n 3](images/c12_924.png) are pairwise coprime, and any ciphertext is less than the modulus (i.e.  <math alttext="upper C Subscript i Baseline less-than n Subscript i Baseline comma i equals 1 comma 2 comma 3 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>&#60;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![upper C Subscript i Baseline less-than n Subscript i Baseline comma i equals 1 comma 2 comma 3 right-parenthesis](images/c12_925.png), by the Chinese remainder theorem, there exists one and only one value of *x* to fulfill the equation system.

There exist multiple methods to solve linear equation systems. The solution to the problem is  <math alttext="k 1 equals 39" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>39</mn></mrow></math> ![k 1 equals 39](images/c12_926.png),  <math alttext="k 2 equals 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> ![k 2 equals 3](images/c12_927.png),  <math alttext="k 3 equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![k 3 equals 0](images/c12_928.png). Consequently,  <math alttext="x equals 2197" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2197</mn></mrow></math> ![x equals 2197](images/c12_929.png) and  <math alttext="RootIndex 3 StartRoot 2197 EndRoot equals 13" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mroot><mrow><mn>2197</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></mroot><mo>=</mo><mn>13</mn></mrow></math> ![RootIndex 3 StartRoot 2197 EndRoot equals 13](images/c12_930.png). Thus, the message can be recovered from the known ciphertexts and public keys.

***Problem 12.2***

Let *e*, *d*, and *n* be the RSA public and private key and modulus, respectively.

RSA is correct if the decryption of a ciphertext  <math alttext="upper C equals upper M Superscript e Baseline m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>M</mi><mi>e</mi></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper C equals upper M Superscript e Baseline m o d n](images/c12_931.png) returns the original plaintext *M*. Formally, the following must hold:

 <math alttext="left-parenthesis upper M Superscript e Baseline m o d n right-parenthesis Superscript d Baseline identical-to upper M m o d n equals upper M comma for-all upper M less-than-or-equal-to n minus 1" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mi>e</mi></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>M</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8704;</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis upper M Superscript e Baseline m o d n right-parenthesis Superscript d Baseline identical-to upper M m o d n equals upper M comma for-all upper M less-than-or-equal-to n minus 1](images/c12_932.png)(a) 

Modular arithmetic rule (see Lemma 3.1) states that:

 <math alttext="a Superscript d Baseline m o d n identical-to left-parenthesis a m o d n right-parenthesis Superscript d Baseline m o d n" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![a Superscript d Baseline m o d n identical-to left-parenthesis a m o d n right-parenthesis Superscript d Baseline m o d n](images/c12_933.png)(b) 

Replacing *a* by  <math alttext="upper M Superscript e Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mi>e</mi></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![upper M Superscript e Baseline](images/c12_934.png) in (b) yields:

 <math alttext="upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d n identical-to left-parenthesis upper M Superscript e Baseline m o d n right-parenthesis Superscript d Baseline m o d n" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mi>e</mi></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d n identical-to left-parenthesis upper M Superscript e Baseline m o d n right-parenthesis Superscript d Baseline m o d n](images/c12_935.png)(c) 

Therefore, we need to prove that  <math alttext="upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d n identical-to upper M m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>M</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d n identical-to upper M m o d n](images/c12_936.png).

By definition of RSA, *p* and *q* are primes and *n* is equal to  <math alttext="p asterisk q" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> ![p asterisk q](images/c12_937.png). By statements 2 and 3,  <math alttext="phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis equals phi left-parenthesis p right-parenthesis asterisk phi left-parenthesis q right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis asterisk left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#981;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>&#981;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo><mi>&#981;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis equals phi left-parenthesis p right-parenthesis asterisk phi left-parenthesis q right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis asterisk left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis](images/c12_938.png).

By definition of RSA public and private keys:  <math alttext="e asterisk d identical-to 1 m o d left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis period" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> ![e asterisk d identical-to 1 m o d left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis period](images/c12_939.png)

Thus, there exists a positive integer *k* such that  <math alttext="e asterisk d equals 1 plus k asterisk left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![e asterisk d equals 1 plus k asterisk left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis](images/c12_940.png)

By substitution:

   <math alttext="upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d n identical-to upper M Superscript 1 plus k asterisk left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline m o d n identical-to upper M asterisk upper M Superscript k asterisk left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline m o d n" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d n identical-to upper M Superscript 1 plus k asterisk left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline m o d n identical-to upper M asterisk upper M Superscript k asterisk left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline m o d n](images/c12_941.png)

   <math alttext="identical-to upper M asterisk upper M Superscript k asterisk phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis Baseline m o d n" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>&#981;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![identical-to upper M asterisk upper M Superscript k asterisk phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis Baseline m o d n](images/c12_942.png)

By Euler’s theorem:  <math alttext="upper M asterisk upper M Superscript k asterisk phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis Baseline m o d n identical-to upper M asterisk 1 Superscript k Baseline m o d n equals upper M" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>&#981;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mn>1</mn><mi>k</mi></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M asterisk upper M Superscript k asterisk phi left-parenthesis n right-parenthesis Baseline m o d n identical-to upper M asterisk 1 Superscript k Baseline m o d n equals upper M](images/c12_943.png)

***Problem 12.3***

Let *e*, *d*, and *n* be the RSA public and private key and modulus, respectively.

Formally, the following must hold:

 <math alttext="left-parenthesis upper M Superscript e Baseline m o d n right-parenthesis Superscript d Baseline identical-to upper M m o d n equals upper M comma for-all upper M less-than-or-equal-to n minus 1" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mi>e</mi></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>M</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8704;</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis upper M Superscript e Baseline m o d n right-parenthesis Superscript d Baseline identical-to upper M m o d n equals upper M comma for-all upper M less-than-or-equal-to n minus 1](images/c12_945.png)(a) 

Modular arithmetic rule (see Lemma 3.1) states that:

Replacing *a* by  <math alttext="upper M Superscript e Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mi>e</mi></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![upper M Superscript e Baseline](images/c12_947.png) in (b) yields:

 <math alttext="upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d n identical-to left-parenthesis upper M Superscript e Baseline m o d n right-parenthesis Superscript d Baseline m o d n" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mi>e</mi></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d n identical-to left-parenthesis upper M Superscript e Baseline m o d n right-parenthesis Superscript d Baseline m o d n](images/c12_948.png)(c) 

By definition of RSA keys:  <math alttext="e asterisk d identical-to 1 m o d left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![e asterisk d identical-to 1 m o d left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis](images/c12_949.png). Thus, there exists an integer *k* such that:  <math alttext="e asterisk d equals 1 plus k left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![e asterisk d equals 1 plus k left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis](images/c12_950.png)

By substitution:  <math alttext="upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d n identical-to upper M Superscript 1 plus k left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d n identical-to upper M Superscript 1 plus k left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline m o d n](images/c12_951.png)

 <math alttext="identical-to upper M asterisk left-parenthesis upper M Superscript left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript k left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline m o d n identical-to upper M asterisk left-parenthesis upper M Superscript left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript k left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline m o d n" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>M</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>\*</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>\*</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![identical-to upper M asterisk left-parenthesis upper M Superscript left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript k left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline m o d n identical-to upper M asterisk left-parenthesis upper M Superscript left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript k left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline m o d n](images/c12_952.png)

We need to prove that:  <math alttext="upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d n identical-to upper M m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>M</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d n identical-to upper M m o d n](images/c12_953.png)

Since  <math alttext="upper M less-than n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M less-than n](images/c12_954.png) and *n* is a product of two primes *p* and *q*, *M* can have common dividers with *p* or with *q*, but not with both. Hence, three cases are to consider:

Case 1: *M* is coprime with *p* and with *q*.

Case 2: *M* is coprime with *p* but not with *q*.

Case 3: *M* is coprime with *q* but not with *p*.

Cases 2 and 3 are identical from the proof point of view.

1.  Case 1: *M* is coprime with *p* and with *q*

By Fermat’s little theorem:

 <math alttext="left-parenthesis upper M Superscript left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript k left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline identical-to 1 m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis upper M Superscript left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript k left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline identical-to 1 m o d p](images/c12_955.png)

 <math alttext="left-parenthesis upper M Superscript left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript k left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline identical-to 1 m o d q" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis upper M Superscript left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript k left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline identical-to 1 m o d q](images/c12_956.png)

Multiplying by *M* both congruences above yield the following congruence equation system:

 <math alttext="upper S equals left-brace StartLayout 1st Row upper M identical-to upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d p 2nd Row upper M identical-to upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d q EndLayout" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtable><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>q</mi></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper S equals left-brace StartLayout 1st Row upper M identical-to upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d p 2nd Row upper M identical-to upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d q EndLayout](images/c12_957.png)

The Chinese theorem states that: if *k* integer numbers  <math alttext="n Subscript i Baseline comma i equals 1 comma ellipsis comma k" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></math> ![n Subscript i Baseline comma i equals 1 comma ellipsis comma k](images/c12_958.png) are pairwise coprime and greater than 1, and if *k* numbers  <math alttext="a 1 comma ellipsis comma a Subscript k Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![a 1 comma xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>&#60;</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![0 less-than-or-equal-to a
