Overscript i equals k Endscripts n Subscript i" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msubsup><mo>&#8719;</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mstyle></mrow></math> ![0 less-than-or-equal-to x less-than product Underscript i equals 1 Overscript i equals k Endscripts n Subscript i](images/c12_961.png) such that  <math alttext="x identical-to a Subscript i Baseline m o d n Subscript i" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![x identical-to a Subscript i Baseline m o d n Subscript i](images/c12_962.png) for every  <math alttext="i i n left-parenthesis 1 comma ellipsis comma k right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![i i n left-parenthesis 1 comma ellipsis comma k right-parenthesis](images/c12_963.png). By Gauss’s algorithm (see Section 3.3.4),

 <math alttext="x identical-to left-parenthesis sigma-summation Underscript i equals 1 Overscript k Endscripts left-parenthesis a Subscript i Baseline asterisk upper N Subscript i Baseline asterisk upper N Subscript i Superscript negative 1 Baseline right-parenthesis right-parenthesis m o d upper N" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true" mathsize="140%"><munderover><mo>&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>k</mi></munderover></mstyle><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>\*</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>\*</mo><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> ![x identical-to left-parenthesis sigma-summation Underscript i equals 1 Overscript k Endscripts left-parenthesis a Subscript i Baseline asterisk upper N Subscript i Baseline asterisk upper N Subscript i Superscript negative 1 Baseline right-parenthesis right-parenthesis m o d upper N](images/c12_964.png)(d) 

In system *S*, the Chinese remainder theorem parameters are as follows:

 <math alttext="k equals 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![k equals 2](images/c12_965.png),  <math alttext="a 1 equals a 2 equals upper M Superscript e asterisk d" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![a 1 equals a 2 equals upper M Superscript e asterisk d](images/c12_966.png),  <math alttext="n 1 equals p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![n 1 equals p](images/c12_967.png),  <math alttext="n 2 equals q" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> ![n 2 equals q](images/c12_968.png), and  <math alttext="x equals upper M" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> ![x equals upper M](images/c12_969.png).

Computations in Gauss’ algorithm yield:

 <math alttext="upper N equals p q" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> ![upper N equals p q](images/c12_970.png),  <math alttext="upper N 1 equals q" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> ![upper N 1 equals q](images/c12_971.png),  <math alttext="upper N 2 equals p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![upper N 2 equals p](images/c12_972.png),  <math alttext="upper N 1 Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals q Superscript negative 1 Baseline m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>q</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![upper N 1 Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals q Superscript negative 1 Baseline m o d p](images/c12_973.png), and  <math alttext="upper N 2 Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals p Superscript negative 1 Baseline m o d q" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> ![upper N 2 Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals p Superscript negative 1 Baseline m o d q](images/c12_974.png)

By substitution of system *S* parameters in equality (d):

 <math alttext="upper M identical-to upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline asterisk left-parenthesis q asterisk left-parenthesis q Superscript negative 1 Baseline m o d p right-parenthesis plus p asterisk left-parenthesis p Superscript negative 1 Baseline m o d q right-parenthesis right-parenthesis m o d p q" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>q</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M identical-to upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline asterisk left-parenthesis q asterisk left-parenthesis q Superscript negative 1 Baseline m o d p right-parenthesis plus p asterisk left-parenthesis p Superscript negative 1 Baseline m o d q right-parenthesis right-parenthesis m o d p q](images/c12_975.png)(e) 

To fulfill congruence equation (e), the following must hold:

 <math alttext="1 identical-to left-parenthesis q asterisk left-parenthesis q Superscript negative 1 Baseline m o d p right-parenthesis plus p asterisk left-parenthesis p Superscript negative 1 Baseline m o d q right-parenthesis right-parenthesis m o d p q" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>q</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> ![1 identical-to left-parenthesis q asterisk left-parenthesis q Superscript negative 1 Baseline m o d p right-parenthesis plus p asterisk left-parenthesis p Superscript negative 1 Baseline m o d q right-parenthesis right-parenthesis m o d p q](images/c12_976.png)(f) 

Congruence (f) is true by the lemma provided in this problem. Therefore,

 <math alttext="upper M identical-to upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d p q" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M identical-to upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d p q](images/c12_977.png), which proves the correctness of RSA decryption.

*   2) Case 2: *M* is coprime with *p* but not with *q*

Since *q* is a prime number, *M* is either 0 or a multiple of *q* (i.e.  <math alttext="upper M Baseline 0 m o d q" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mn>0</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M Baseline 0 m o d q](images/c12_978.png)). By the modular arithmetic exponentiation rule, we have:

 <math alttext="upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d q identical-to left-parenthesis 0 right-parenthesis Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d q identical-to 0 m o d q identical-to upper M m o d q" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>0</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>M</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d q identical-to left-parenthesis 0 right-parenthesis Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d q identical-to 0 m o d q identical-to upper M m o d q](images/c12_979.png)

Since *M* is coprime with *p*, by Fermat’s little theorem:

 <math alttext="upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d p identical-to upper M asterisk left-parenthesis upper M Superscript left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript k left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline m o d p upper M asterisk left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis Superscript k left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline m o d p equals upper M" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>\*</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M Superscript e asterisk d Baseline m o d p identical-to upper M asterisk left-parenthesis upper M Superscript left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript k left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline m o d p upper M asterisk left-parenthesis 1 right-parenthesis Superscript k left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis Baseline m o d p equals upper M](images/c12_980.png)

The integer  <math alttext="upper M Superscript e d Baseline minus upper M" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M Superscript e d Baseline minus upper M](images/c12_981.png) is a multiple of *p* and *q*. Since *p* and *q* are primes and  <math alttext="n equals p asterisk q" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> ![n equals p asterisk q](images/c12_982.png),  <math alttext="upper M Superscript e d Baseline minus upper M" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M Superscript e d Baseline minus upper M](images/c12_983.png) also is a multiple of *n*. Therefore,  <math alttext="upper M Superscript e d Baseline identical-to upper M m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>M</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M Superscript e d Baseline identical-to upper M m o d n](images/c12_985.png), which proves the correctness of RSA decryption.

***Problem 12.4***

1.  The ciphertext 75 was obtained using  <math alttext="n equals 437" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>437</mn></mrow></math> ![n equals 437](images/c12_986.png) and  <math alttext="e equals 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> ![e equals 3](images/c12_987.png). Since the plaintext is supposed to be a value between 3 and 10, we have to check a maximum of eight alternatives:
    
    If the valid plaintext is 3, then  <math alttext="3 cubed mod 437 identical-to 27" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;mod&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>437</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>27</mn></mrow></math> ![3 cubed mod 437 identical-to 27](images/c12_988.png).
    
    If the valid plaintext is 4, then  <math alttext="4 cubed mod 437 identical-to 64" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;mod&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>437</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>64</mn></mrow></math> ![4 cubed mod 437 identical-to 64](images/c12_989.png).
    
    If the valid plaintext is 5, then  <math alttext="5 cubed mod 437 identical-to 125" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;mod</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>437</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>125</mn></mrow></math> ![5 cubed mod 437 identical-to 125](images/c12_990.png).
    
    If the valid plaintext is 6, then  <math alttext="6 cubed mod 437 identical-to 216" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>6</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;mod&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>437</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>216</mn></mrow></math> ![6 cubed mod 437 identical-to 216](images/c12_991.png).
    
    If the valid plaintext is 7, then  <math alttext="7 cubed mod 437 identical-to 343" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>7</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;mod</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>437</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>343</mn></mrow></math> ![7 cubed mod 437 identical-to 343](images/c12_992.png).
    
    If the valid plaintext is 8, then  <math alttext="8 cubed mod 437 identical-to 75" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>8</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;mod</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>437</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>75</mn></mrow></math> ![8 cubed mod 437 identical-to 75](images/c12_993.png).
    
    Thus, the valid plaintext is 8.
    
2.  We know that  <math alttext="516107 squared identical-to 7 m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>516107</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![516107 squared identical-to 7 m o d n](images/c12_994.png) and  <math alttext="187722 squared identical-to 2 squared asterisk 7 m o d n period" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>187722</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>\*</mo><mn>7</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> ![187722 squared identical-to 2 squared asterisk 7 m o d n period](images/c12_995.png) Use this information to factor *n*. By multiplication and substitution,
    
     <math alttext="4 asterisk 516107 squared identical-to 4 asterisk 7 m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>\*</mo><msup><mrow><mn>516107</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>4</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>7</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![4 asterisk 516107 squared identical-to 4 asterisk 7 m o d n](images/c12_996.png)
    
     <math alttext="4 asterisk 516107 squared minus 2 squared asterisk 7 identical-to m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>\*</mo><msup><mrow><mn>516107</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>\*</mo><mn>7</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![4 asterisk 516107 squared minus 2 squared asterisk 7 identical-to m o d n](images/c12_997.png)
    
     <math alttext="4 asterisk 516107 squared minus 187722 squared identical-to 0 m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>\*</mo><msup><mrow><mn>516107</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mrow><mn>187722</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>0</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![4 asterisk 516107 squared minus 187722 squared identical-to 0 m o d n](images/c12_998.png)
    
     <math alttext="left-parenthesis 2 asterisk 516107 right-parenthesis squared minus 187722 squared identical-to 0 m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>516107</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mrow><mn>187722</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>0</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 2 asterisk 516107 right-parenthesis squared minus 187722 squared identical-to 0 m o d n](images/c12_999.png)
    
     <math alttext="left-parenthesis 2 asterisk 516107 plus 187722 right-parenthesis asterisk left-parenthesis 2 asterisk 516107 minus 187722 right-parenthesis identical-to 0 m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>516107</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>187722</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>516107</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>187722</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>0</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 2 asterisk 516107 plus 187722 right-parenthesis asterisk left-parenthesis 2 asterisk 516107 minus 187722 right-parenthesis identical-to 0 m o d n](images/c12_1000.png)
    

Thus, factorization of *n* is found.

***Problem 12.5***

Having  <math alttext="e equals 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> ![e equals 3](images/c12_1001.png), any message *M* is encrypted as  <math alttext="upper C identical-to upper M cubed m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>M</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper C identical-to upper M cubed m o d n](images/c12_1002.png).

If *M* is in the range of  <math alttext="3 ellipsis 9" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>3</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>&#8230;</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn></mrow></math> ![3 ellipsis 9](images/c12_1003.png),  <math alttext="3 cubed less-than-or-equal-to upper M cubed less-than-or-equal-to 9 cubed" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>&#8804;</mo><msup><mi>M</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>&#8804;</mo><msup><mn>9</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></math> ![3 cubed less-than-or-equal-to upper M cubed less-than-or-equal-to 9 cubed](images/c12_1004.png) and the modulus *n* is large, then

 <math alttext="upper M cubed equals left-parenthesis upper M cubed m o d n right-parenthesis plus 0 asterisk n" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>M</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>\*</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M cubed equals left-parenthesis upper M cubed m o d n right-parenthesis plus 0 asterisk n](images/c12_1005.png)

Given  <math alttext="upper C identical-to upper M cubed m o d upper N" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>M</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> ![upper C identical-to upper M cubed m o d upper N](images/c12_1006.png), there is a unique solution to *M*, if  <math alttext="upper M cubed equals left-parenthesis upper M cubed m o d n right-parenthesis plus 0 asterisk n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>M</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>\*</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M cubed equals left-parenthesis upper M cubed m o d n right-parenthesis plus 0 asterisk n](images/c12_1007.png), which is  <math alttext="RootIndex 3 StartRoot upper C EndRoot" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mroot><mi>C</mi><mn>3</mn></mroot></mrow></math> ![RootIndex 3 StartRoot upper C EndRoot](images/c12_1008.png).

For example,  <math alttext="n equals 41 asterisk 101" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>41</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>101</mn></mrow></math> ![n equals 41 asterisk 101](images/c12_1009.png) and  <math alttext="upper M equals 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![upper M equals 5](images/c12_1010.png) yield  <math alttext="upper C equals 5 cubed equals 125 equals 125 plus 0 asterisk n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>125</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>125</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>\*</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper C equals 5 cubed equals 125 equals 125 plus 0 asterisk n](images/c12_1011.png).

Therefore,  <math alttext="RootIndex 3 StartRoot 125 EndRoot equals 5" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mroot><mrow><mn>125</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></mroot><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math> ![RootIndex 3 StartRoot 125 EndRoot equals 5](images/c12_1012.png).

***Problem 12.6***

RSA signature scheme does not protect against stolen public keys. It assumes that a higher level mechanism (i.e. authentication) is used jointly with RSA signature.

***Problem 12.7***

Recall that RSA signature is the modular exponentiation of the hash of the message to sign. Given two messages  <math alttext="upper M 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper M 1](images/c12_1013.png) and  <math alttext="upper M 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper M 2](images/c12_1014.png) and their signatures  <math alttext="s 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![s 1](images/c12_1015.png) and  <math alttext="s 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![s 2](images/c12_1016.png), the adversary may start with the following computations:

 <math alttext="left-parenthesis s 1 asterisk s 2 right-parenthesis m o d n identical-to left-parenthesis upper H left-parenthesis upper M 1 right-parenthesis Superscript d Baseline asterisk upper H left-parenthesis upper M 2 right-parenthesis Superscript d Baseline right-parenthesis m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>\*</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>)</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi></msup><mo>\*</mo><mi>H</mi><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis s 1 asterisk s 2 right-parenthesis m o d n identical-to left-parenthesis upper H left-parenthesis upper M 1 right-parenthesis Superscript d Baseline asterisk upper H left-parenthesis upper M 2 right-parenthesis Superscript d Baseline right-parenthesis m o d n](images/c12_1017.png) (*d* is the private key)

 <math alttext="left-parenthesis s 1 asterisk s 2 right-parenthesis m o d n identical-to left-parenthesis upper H left-parenthesis upper M 1 right-parenthesis asterisk upper H left-parenthesis upper M 2 right-parenthesis right-parenthesis Superscript d Baseline m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>\*</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>)</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis s 1 asterisk s 2 right-parenthesis m o d n identical-to left-parenthesis upper H left-parenthesis upper M 1 right-parenthesis asterisk upper H left-parenthesis upper M 2 right-parenthesis right-parenthesis Superscript d Baseline m o d n](images/c12_1018.png)

 <math alttext="left-parenthesis s 1 asterisk s 2 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>\*</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis s 1 asterisk s 2 right-parenthesis](images/c12_1019.png) could be the forged signature. To do so, the adversary must find a message  <math alttext="upper M prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![upper M prime](images/c12_1020.png), such that  <math alttext="upper H left-parenthesis upper M prime right-parenthesis equals upper H left-parenthesis upper M 1 right-parenthesis asterisk upper H left-parenthesis upper M 2 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper H left-parenthesis upper M prime right-parenthesis equals upper H left-parenthesis upper M 1 right-parenthesis asterisk upper H left-parenthesis upper M 2 right-parenthesis](images/c12_1021.png). However, he/she has to find the message associated with the given hash. Such an attack is referred to as preimage attack, which is known to be computationally infeasible, because hash functions are one-way functions.

***Problem 12.8***

Recall that an existential forgery attack means the adversary can generate a pair composed by a message and its signature without controlling the message content.

Suppose that Bob signed two messages  <math alttext="upper M 1 equals 25" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow></math> ![upper M 1 equals 25](images/c12_1022.png) and  <math alttext="upper M 2 equals 57" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>57</mn></mrow></math> ![upper M 2 equals 57](images/c12_1023.png) and produced two signatures:  <math alttext="s 1 identical-to 25 Superscript d Baseline m o d 119" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mrow><mn>25</mn></mrow><mi>d</mi></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>119</mn></mrow></math> ![s 1 identical-to 25 Superscript d Baseline m o d 119](images/c12_1024.png) and  <math alttext="s 1 identical-to 57 Superscript d Baseline m o d 119" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mrow><mn>57</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>119</mn></mrow></math> ![s 1 identical-to 57 Superscript d Baseline m o d 119](images/c12_1025.png).

Then,  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 25 comma s 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 25 comma s 1 right-parenthesis](images/c12_1026.png) and  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 57 comma s 2 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>57</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 57 comma s 2 right-parenthesis](images/c12_1027.png) are sent to Alice.

Eve intercepts  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 25 comma s 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 25 comma s 1 right-parenthesis](images/c12_1028.png) and  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 57 comma s 2 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>57</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 57 comma s 2 right-parenthesis](images/c12_1029.png) and she knows Bob’s public key  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 5 comma 119 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>119</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 5 comma 119 right-parenthesis](images/c12_1030.png). Then, an existential attack may consist in sending  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 25 asterisk 57 comma s 1 asterisk s 2 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>57</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>\*</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 25 asterisk 57 comma s 1 asterisk s 2 right-parenthesis](images/c12_1031.png) to Alice. Notice that Eve just multiplies the values she received.

Upon reception of  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 25 asterisk 57 s 1 asterisk s 2 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>57</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>\*</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 25 asterisk 57 s 1 asterisk s 2 right-parenthesis](images/c12_1032.png), Alice verifies signature as follows:

 <math alttext="left-parenthesis s 1 asterisk s 1 right-parenthesis Superscript e Baseline m o d 119 identical-to left-parenthesis left-parenthesis 25 asterisk 57 right-parenthesis Superscript d Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript e Baseline m o d 119 identical-to 25 asterisk 57" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>\*</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>e</mi></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>119</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>57</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>e</mi></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>119</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>25</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>57</mn></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis s 1 asterisk s 1 right-parenthesis Superscript e Baseline m o d 119 identical-to left-parenthesis left-parenthesis 25 asterisk 57 right-parenthesis Superscript d Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript e Baseline m o d 119 identical-to 25 asterisk 57](images/c12_1033.png)

Therefore, the received forged signed message is accepted by Alice. However, notice that Eve cannot control the content of the forged message.

By Textbook RSA signature of message  <math alttext="upper M prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![upper M prime](images/c12_1037.png):

***Problem 12.10***

1.  *x* is a (very) low value compared to *y*. If the public key has a low value, its corresponding private key has a high value and vice versa.
2.  Let *M* and *C* denote the plaintext and ciphertext respectively. Let  <math alttext="t Subscript e n c" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![t Subscript e n c](images/c12_1044.png) denote the number of iterations of the encryption operation and  <math alttext="t Subscript d e c" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![t Subscript d e c](images/c12_1045.png) that of the decryption operation. Recall that the right-to-left binary exponentiation method computes  <math alttext="a Superscript k Baseline m o d b" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>b</mi></mrow></math> ![a Superscript k Baseline m o d b](images/c12_1046.png) within  <math alttext="left ceiling l o g 2 k right ceiling" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8968;</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mi>o</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>&#8969;</mo></mrow></math> ![left ceiling l o g 2 k right ceiling](images/c12_1047.png) square-and-multiply iterations.

If *x* is the public key and *y* the private key, then

 <math alttext="t Subscript e n c Baseline equals left ceiling l o g 2 x right ceiling" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>&#8968;</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mi>o</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>&#8969;</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![t Subscript e n c Baseline equals left ceiling l o g 2 x right ceiling](images/c12_1048.png) and  <math alttext="t Subscript d e c Baseline equals left ceiling l o g 2 y right ceiling" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>&#8968;</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mi>o</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>&#8969;</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![t Subscript d e c Baseline equals left ceiling l o g 2 y right ceiling](images/c12_1049.png).

If *y* is the public key and *x* the private key, then

 <math alttext="t Subscript e n c Baseline equals left ceiling l o g 2 y right ceiling" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>&#8968;</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mi>o</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>&#8969;</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![t Subscript e n c Baseline equals left ceiling l o g 2 y right ceiling](images/c12_1050.png) and  <math alttext="t Subscript d e c Baseline equals left ceiling l o g 2 x right ceiling" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>&#8968;</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mi>o</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>&#8969;</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![t Subscript d e c Baseline equals left ceiling l o g 2 x right ceiling](images/c12_1051.png).

Therefore, the sum of  <math alttext="t Subscript e n c Baseline plus t Subscript d e c" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![t Subscript e n c Baseline plus t Subscript d e c](images/c12_1052.png) is the same, if the public and private keys are swapped.

There is no gain in terms of the sum of RSA operation times, if we choose low values as private keys.

*   3\. If the adversary knows the public key *e* and the modulus *n* and suspects that the private key *d* is less than 100, he/she tries decryption with, at most, 98 candidate private keys and produces 98 candidate plaintexts among which the known plaintext is used to validate the private key recovery. Keys 1 and 2 are not tested, because key 1 is the identity and 2 is not coprime with  <math alttext="phi left-parenthesis p q right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![phi left-parenthesis p q right-parenthesis](images/c12_1053.png), which is even. Let *D* be the recovered private key. The adversary finds a candidate value matching  <math alttext="phi left-parenthesis p q right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![phi left-parenthesis p q right-parenthesis](images/c12_1054.png) and then checks it regarding RSA parameters as follows:

Starting from  <math alttext="lamda equals n minus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#955;</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![lamda equals n minus 1](images/c12_1055.png), because  <math alttext="phi left-parenthesis p q right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![phi left-parenthesis p q right-parenthesis](images/c12_1056.png) is not far from *n*, and until *p* and *q* are recovered, check decreasing values of λ:

*   If  <math alttext="upper G upper C upper D left-parenthesis e asterisk upper D comma lamda right-parenthesis not-equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>G</mi><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>D</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>&#955;</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8800;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![upper G upper C upper D left-parenthesis e asterisk upper D comma lamda right-parenthesis not-equals 1](images/c12_1057.png), try the next value of λ.
*   If  <math alttext="GCD left-parenthesis e asterisk upper D comma lamda right-parenthesis equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>GCD</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>D</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>&#955;</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![GCD left-parenthesis e asterisk upper D comma lamda right-parenthesis equals 1](images/c12_1058.png), suppose that  <math alttext="lamda equals phi left-parenthesis p q right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#955;</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![lamda equals phi left-parenthesis p q right-parenthesis](images/c12_1059.png). Then check:

 <math alttext="n equals p q" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> ![n equals p q](images/c12_1060.png) and  <math alttext="lamda equals left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis equals p q minus p minus q plus 1 equals n minus p minus q plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#955;</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![lamda equals left-parenthesis p minus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis q minus 1 right-parenthesis equals p q minus p minus q plus 1 equals n minus p minus q plus 1](images/c12_1061.png)

 <math alttext="right double arrow p equals StartFraction n Over q EndFraction equals n minus lamda negative q plus 1 right double arrow StartFraction n Over q EndFraction plus q equals n minus lamda plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8658;</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>n</mi><mi>q</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>&#955;</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8658;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mfrac><mi>n</mi><mi>q</mi></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>&#955;</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![right double arrow p equals StartFraction n Over q EndFraction equals n minus lamda negative q plus 1 right double arrow StartFraction n Over q EndFraction plus q equals n minus lamda plus 1](images/c12_1062.png)

 <math alttext="right double arrow q squared minus q left-parenthesis n minus lamda plus 1 right-parenthesis plus n equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8658;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>q</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>q</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>&#955;</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![right double arrow q squared minus q left-parenthesis n minus lamda plus 1 right-parenthesis plus n equals 0](images/c12_1063.png)

 <math alttext="quotation-mark n minus lamda plus 1 quotation-mark" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>"</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>&#955;</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>"</mo></mrow></math> ![quotation-mark n minus lamda plus 1 quotation-mark](images/c12_1064.png) is a constant. If the solutions to the second-degree equation above are integers, a pair  <math alttext="left-parenthesis p comma q right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis p comma q right-parenthesis](images/c12_1065.png) is found. Then, check if all RSA parameters are consistent (i.e.  <math alttext="e asterisk upper D identical-to 1 m o d phi left-parenthesis p q right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>D</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![e asterisk upper D identical-to 1 m o d phi left-parenthesis p q right-parenthesis](images/c12_1066.png)). If not consistent, then try the next value of λ.

Example (just the final attempts of attack are given): assume the private key  <math alttext="d equals 13" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>13</mn></mrow></math> ![d equals 13](images/c12_1067.png) has been recovered using a known pair of plaintext–ciphertext. The modulus,  <math alttext="n equals 1009 asterisk 1013" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1009</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>1013</mn></mrow></math> ![n equals 1009 asterisk 1013](images/c12_1068.png), and public key,  <math alttext="e equals 78469" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>78469</mn></mrow></math> ![e equals 78469](images/c12_1069.png), are known to the adversary.

After some attempts,  <math alttext="lamda equals 1020096" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#955;</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1020096</mn></mrow></math> ![lamda equals 1020096](images/c12_1070.png), which meets  <math alttext="78469 asterisk 13 identical-to 1 m o d 1020096" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>78469</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>\*</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>13</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1020096</mn></mrow></math> ![78469 asterisk 13 identical-to 1 m o d 1020096](images/c12_1071.png), is found.

Make substitutions in the second degree equation above:

 <math alttext="q squared minus q left-parenthesis 1009 asterisk 1013 minus 102096 plus 1 right-parenthesis plus 1009 asterisk 1013" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>q</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>q</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1009</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>1013</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>102096</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1009</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>1013</mn></mrow></math> ![q squared minus q left-parenthesis 1009 asterisk 1013 minus 102096 plus 1 right-parenthesis plus 1009 asterisk 1013](images/c12_1072.png)

 <math alttext="equals q squared minus 2022 q plus 1022117" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>q</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2022</mn><mi>q</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1022117</mn></mrow></math> ![equals q squared minus 2022 q plus 1022117](images/c12_1073.png)

The solutions to equation are  <math alttext="q equals 1009" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1009</mn></mrow></math> ![q equals 1009](images/c12_1074.png) and  <math alttext="q equals 1013" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1013</mn></mrow></math> ![q equals 1013](images/c12_1075.png), which means that the primes are recovered.

*   4\. Let *m* be the bit-length of the private key. Given a pair of plaintext–ciphertext, each tested private key  <math alttext="k element-of left-bracket 3 comma 2 Superscript m Baseline minus 1 right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![k element-of left-bracket 3 comma 2 Superscript m Baseline minus 1 right-bracket](images/c12_1076.png) requires  <math alttext="left ceiling l o g 2 k right ceiling" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8968;</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mi>o</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>&#8969;</mo></mrow></math> ![left ceiling l o g 2 k right ceiling](images/c12_1077.png) RLBEM iterations. To test all the private keys in range  <math alttext="left-bracket 3 comma 2 Superscript m Baseline minus 1 right-bracket" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></math> ![left-bracket 3 comma 2 Superscript m Baseline minus 1 right-bracket](images/c12_1078.png),  <math alttext="sigma-summation Underscript i equals 3 Overscript 2 Superscript m Baseline minus 1 Endscripts left ceiling l o g 2 i right ceiling equals sigma-summation Underscript k equals 3 Overscript m Endscripts left-parenthesis k asterisk 2 Superscript k minus 1 Baseline right-parenthesis minus left-parenthesis m minus 1 right-parenthesis plus 3 equals 2 Superscript m Baseline left-parenthesis m minus 1 right-parenthesis minus m" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msubsup><mo>&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo>&#8968;</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mi>o</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo>&#8969;</mo><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msubsup><mo>&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow></mstyle></mrow></mstyle></mrow></math> minus 1 right-parenthesis minus m](images/c12_1079.png). RLBEM iterations are needed (the proof of the formula is addressed below). Therefore, to make infeasible a plaintext brute-force attack with a capacity of  <math alttext="2 Superscript upper Omega" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>&#937;</mi></msup></mrow></math> ![2 Superscript upper Omega](images/c12_1080.png) iterations,  <math alttext="2 Superscript m Baseline left-parenthesis m minus 1 right-parenthesis minus m greater-than-or-equal-to 2 Superscript upper Omega" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>m</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8805;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>&#937;</mi></msup></mrow></math> ![2 Superscript m Baseline left-parenthesis m minus 1 right-parenthesis minus m greater-than-or-equal-to 2 Superscript upper Omega](images/c12_1081.png), i.e approximately  <math alttext="m left ceiling l o g 2 m right ceiling greater-than-or-equal-to upper Omega" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo>&#8968;</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mi>o</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>m</mi></mrow><mo>&#8969;</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8805;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>&#937;</mi></mrow></math> ![m left ceiling l o g 2 m right ceiling greater-than-or-equal-to upper Omega](images/c12_1082.png).
*   5\. As a conclusion, the use of low-value RSA private keys is insecure. Therefore, they are prohibited in RSA cryptosystems.

*Proof*:  <math alttext="sigma-summation Underscript i equals 3 Overscript 2 Superscript m Baseline minus 1 Endscripts left ceiling l o g 2 i right ceiling equals sigma-summation Underscript k equals 3 Overscript m Endscripts left-parenthesis k asterisk 2 Superscript k minus 1 Baseline right-parenthesis minus left-parenthesis m minus 1 right-parenthesis plus 3 equals 2 Superscript m Baseline left-parenthesis m minus 1 right-parenthesis minus m" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msubsup><mo>&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo>&#8968;</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mi>o</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo>&#8969;</mo><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msubsup><mo>&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow></mstyle></mrow></mstyle></mrow></math> ![sigma-summation Underscript i equals 3 Overscript 2 Superscript m Baseline minus 1 Endscripts left ceiling l o g 2 i right ceiling equals sigma-summation Underscript k equals 3 Overscript m Endscripts left-parenthesis k asterisk 2 Superscript k minus 1 Baseline right-parenthesis minus left-parenthesis m minus 1 right-parenthesis plus 3 equals 2 Superscript m Baseline left-parenthesis m minus 1 right-parenthesis minus m](images/c12_1083.png)

Proof by recurrence that  <math alttext="sigma-summation Underscript k equals 2 Overscript m Endscripts left-parenthesis k asterisk 2 Superscript k minus 1 Baseline right-parenthesis equals 2 Superscript m Baseline left-parenthesis m minus 1 right-parenthesis minus 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msubsup><mo>&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mstyle></mrow></math> ![sigma-summation Underscript k equals 2 Overscript m Endscripts left-parenthesis k asterisk 2 Superscript k minus 1 Baseline right-parenthesis equals 2 Superscript m Baseline left-parenthesis m minus 1 right-parenthesis minus 4](images/c12_1101.png)

Now, assume that the equality holds for  <math alttext="m equals n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![m equals n](images/c12_1106.png) ( <math alttext="n ampersand gt semicolon 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#38;gt;</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> ![n ampersand gt semicolon 3](images/c12_1107.png)) and and equation (a) becomes  <math alttext="m equals n plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![m equals n plus 1](images/c12_1108.png):

Therefore,  <math alttext="sigma-summation Underscript i equals 2 Overscript 2 Superscript m Baseline minus 1 Endscripts left ceiling l o g 2 i right ceiling equals sigma-summation Underscript k equals 2 Overscript m Endscripts left-parenthesis k asterisk 2 Superscript k minus 1 Baseline right-parenthesis equals 2 Superscript m Baseline left-parenthesis m minus 1 right-parenthesis minus 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msubsup><mo>&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo>&#8968;</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mi>o</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo>&#8969;</mo></mrow></mstyle><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msubsup><mo>&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mstyle></mrow></math> ![sigma-summation Underscript i equals 2 Overscript 2 Superscript m Baseline minus 1 Endscripts left ceiling l o g 2 i right ceiling equals sigma-summation Underscript k equals 2 Overscript m Endscripts left-parenthesis k asterisk 2 Superscript k minus 1 Baseline right-parenthesis equals 2 Superscript m Baseline left-parenthesis m minus 1 right-parenthesis minus 4](images/c12_1111.png).

Finally,  <math alttext="sigma-summation Underscript i equals 3 Overscript 2 Superscript m Baseline minus 1 Endscripts left ceiling l o g 2 i right ceiling equals 2 Superscript m Baseline left-parenthesis m minus 1 right-parenthesis minus m" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msubsup><mo>&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo>&#8968;</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mi>o</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo>&#8969;</mo></mrow></mstyle><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow></math> ![sigma-summation Underscript i equals 3 Overscript 2 Superscript m Baseline minus 1 Endscripts left ceiling l o g 2 i right ceiling equals 2 Superscript m Baseline left-parenthesis m minus 1 right-parenthesis minus m](images/c12_1112.png).□

***Problem 12.11***

1.  Let  <math alttext="upper C 1 identical-to left-parenthesis upper M 1 right-parenthesis Superscript e Baseline m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>e</mi></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper C 1 identical-to left-parenthesis upper M 1 right-parenthesis Superscript e Baseline m o d n](images/c12_1113.png) and  <math alttext="upper C 2 identical-to left-parenthesis upper M 2 right-parenthesis Superscript e Baseline m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>e</mi></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper C 2 identical-to left-parenthesis upper M 2 right-parenthesis Superscript e Baseline m o d n](images/c12_1114.png) be two ciphertexts.

 <math alttext="upper C 1 asterisk upper C 2 m o d n identical-to left-parenthesis left-parenthesis upper M 1 Superscript e Baseline m o d n right-parenthesis asterisk left-parenthesis upper M 2 Superscript e Baseline m o d n right-parenthesis right-parenthesis m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>\*</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>M</mi><mn>1</mn><mi>e</mi></msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>M</mi><mn>2</mn><mi>e</mi></msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper C 1 asterisk upper C 2 m o d n identical-to left-parenthesis left-parenthesis upper M 1 Superscript e Baseline m o d n right-parenthesis asterisk left-parenthesis upper M 2 Superscript e Baseline m o d n right-parenthesis right-parenthesis m o d n](images/c12_1115.png)

 <math alttext="identical-to upper M 1 Superscript e Baseline asterisk upper M 2 Superscript e Baseline m o d n identical-to left-parenthesis upper M 1 asterisk upper M 2 right-parenthesis Superscript e Baseline m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8801;</mo><msubsup><mi>M</mi><mn>1</mn><mi>e</mi></msubsup><mo>\*</mo><msubsup><mi>M</mi><mn>2</mn><mi>e</mi></msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>\*</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>e</mi></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![identical-to upper M 1 Superscript e Baseline asterisk upper M 2 Superscript e Baseline m o d n identical-to left-parenthesis upper M 1 asterisk upper M 2 right-parenthesis Superscript e Baseline m o d n](images/c12_1116.png)

Therefore, the product of two RSA ciphertexts is equal to the encryption of the product of the two respective plaintexts.

*   Assume that Eve has intercepted a ciphertext sent by Alice. Let be  <math alttext="upper C identical-to upper M Subscript s e c Superscript e Baseline m o d" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><msubsup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi></msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow></math> ![upper C identical-to upper M Subscript s e c Superscript e Baseline m o d](images/c12_1117.png) be the ciphertext known to Eve.  <math alttext="upper M Subscript s e c" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper M Subscript s e c](images/c12_1118.png) is the plaintext to recover by Eve. The attack may be designed as follows: 
    *   Eve chooses an arbitrary plaintext  <math alttext="x element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript n Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8712;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![x element-of double-struck upper Z Subscript n Superscript asterisk](images/c12_1119.png), then computes  <math alttext="upper C Subscript a r b Baseline identical-to x Superscript e Baseline asterisk upper C m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>e</mi></msup><mo>\*</mo><mi>C</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper C Subscript a r b Baseline identical-to x Superscript e Baseline asterisk upper C m o d n](images/c12_1120.png)
    *   Eve sends the ciphertext  <math alttext="upper C Subscript a r b" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper C Subscript a r b](images/c12_1121.png) to Bob as a pretext to check if he owns the private key associated with the public key  <math alttext="left-parenthesis e comma n right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis e comma n right-parenthesis](images/c12_1122.png).

***Problem 12.12***

1\. In general, the right-to-left binary exponentiation method (RLBEM) requires  <math alttext="left ceiling l o g 2 k right ceiling" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8968;</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mi>o</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>&#8969;</mo></mrow></math> ![left ceiling l o g 2 k right ceiling](images/c12_1141.png) iterations to find *x* such that  <math alttext="x identical-to a Superscript k Baseline m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![x identical-to a Superscript k Baseline m o d n](images/c12_1142.png), given *a*, *k*, and *n*. RLBEM iteration is composed of a test, two modular multiplications, and a one-bit-shift.

1.  If only the modular multiplication matters, the encryption time is  <math alttext="2 asterisk left ceiling l o g 2 zero width space e right ceiling asterisk m squared asterisk c comma" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>&#8968;</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mi>o</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mtext>&#8203;</mtext><mi>e</mi></mrow><mo>&#8969;</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>\*</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo></mrow></math> ![2 asterisk left ceiling l o g 2 zero width space e right ceiling asterisk m squared asterisk c comma](images/c12_1143.png) where *m* denotes the bit-length modulus *n*. *c* is a constant that depends on the underlying implementation and hardware.

If the bit-length of the modulus *n* multiplied by a factor of δ, the encryption time is increased by a factor of <math alttext="StartFraction 2 asterisk left ceiling l o g 2 left-parenthesis 2 Superscript 16 Baseline plus 1 right-parenthesis right ceiling asterisk left-parenthesis delta asterisk m right-parenthesis squared asterisk normal c Over 2 asterisk left ceiling l o g 2 *   2\. Modulus 4092 is  <math alttext="4 asterisk 1024" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>1024</mn></mrow></math> ![4 asterisk 1024](images/c12_1145.png). With  <math alttext="delta equals 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#948;</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></math> ![delta equals 4](images/c12_1146.png), by substitution in the formula above, the ratio of the encryption time increase is  <math alttext="delta squared equals 16" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>&#948;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow></math> ![delta squared equals 16](images/c12_1147.png). It is worth noticing that increasing the security level of an RSA cryptosystem comes with a significant computation time increase.

***Problem 12.13***

1.   <math alttext="100 000 007" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>100</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>007</mn></mrow></math> ![100 000 007](images/c12_1148.png) is prime. Thus,  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript 100 000 007 Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mrow><mn>100</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>007</mn></mrow><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript 100 000 007 Superscript asterisk](images/c12_1149.png) has  <math alttext="100 000 006" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>100</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>000</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>006</mn></mrow></math> ![100 000 006](images/c12_1150.png) elements, which is close to  <math alttext="10 Superscript 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mn>8</mn></msup></mrow></math> ![10 Superscript 8](images/c12_1151.png). Therefore, in case of a brute-force attack, approximately  <math alttext="10 Superscript 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mn>8</mn></msup></mrow></math> ![10 Superscript 8](images/c12_1152.png) powers of the generator should be computed and tested. Consequently, the worst computation time is  <math alttext="1 asterisk 10 Superscript 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>\*</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mn>8</mn></msup></mrow></math> ![1 asterisk 10 Superscript 8](images/c12_1153.png) μs (i.e. 100 seconds), which is not deterrent for attackers.
2.  If the length of *p* is 90 bits and *p* is prime, then  <math alttext="double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msubsup><mi>&#8484;</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>\*</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> ![double-struck upper Z Subscript p Superscript asterisk](images/c12_1154.png) has approximately  <math alttext="2 Superscript 90" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>90</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![2 Superscript 90](images/c12_1155.png) elements. Consequently, the worst computation time is  <math alttext="1 asterisk 2 Superscript 90 Baseline mu s equals left-parenthesis 2 Superscript 10 Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript 9 Baseline mu s equals 1024 Superscript 9 Baseline mu s almost-equals 10 Superscript 27" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>\*</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>90</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#956;s</mtext><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>9</mn></msup><mtext>&#956;s</mtext><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mn>1024</mn></mrow><mn>9</mn></msup><mtext>&#956;s</mtext><mo>&#8776;</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>27</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![1 asterisk 2 Superscript 90 Baseline mu s equals left-parenthesis 2 Superscript 10 Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript 9 Baseline mu s equals 1024 Superscript 9 Baseline mu s almost-equals 10 Superscript 27](images/c12_1156.png) seconds!

Therefore, Brute-force attack is computationally infeasible if the group cardinality is large.

***Problem 12.14***

Recall that the shared secret key is computed in DHKE protocol as follows:
