Thus,  <math alttext="upper S Subscript upper A Baseline equals upper S Subscript upper B Baseline equals h asterisk upper I m p upper S i g Subscript upper B Baseline asterisk upper I m p upper S i g Subscript upper A Baseline dot upper G" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>B</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>I</mi><mi>m</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>S</mi><mi>i</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>B</mi></msub><mo>\*</mo><mi>I</mi><mi>m</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>S</mi><mi>i</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>G</mi></mrow></math> ![upper S Subscript upper A Baseline equals upper S Subscript upper B Baseline equals h asterisk upper I m p upper S i g Subscript upper B Baseline asterisk upper I m p upper S i g Subscript upper A Baseline dot upper G](images/c13_466.png); i.e. both parties generate the same secret.□

### 13.5.5 Elliptic-Curve Digital-Signature Algorithm (ECDSA)

At the time of writing this chapter, most SSL/TLS certificates are still being signed with RSA keys. However, since the early 2010s, many certificate authorities are involved in the deployment of ECDSA as a new and performant algorithm to digital signature and most modern signature-service clients have implemented support for ECDSA. The latter will probably become the standard in public key industry. The ECDSA is composed of three processes \[[14](#c13.xhtml#c13-bib-0014)\]:

*   Setup process
*   Signature generation process
*   Signature verification process

#### 13.5.5.1 Setup Process

Let us consider Alice and Bob as two parties in communication. Alice has a message *M* to send to Bob. That is, Alice is the *signer* and Bob the *verifier*. In the setup process, the elliptic curve domain parameters (see [Section 13.5.2](#c13.xhtml#c13-sec-1030)) and the hash function are selected by the signer. ECDSA works on the hash of the message, rather than on the message itself. SHA-256 and SHA-512 are currently recommended by security standards.

Alice makes use of the selected elliptic curve domain parameters to generate a key pair  <math alttext="left-parenthesis upper P r Subscript upper A Baseline comma upper P u Subscript upper A Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>P</mi><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>P</mi><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis upper P r Subscript upper A Baseline comma upper P u Subscript upper A Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c13_467.png), where  <math alttext="upper P r Subscript upper A" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![upper P r Subscript upper A](images/c13_468.png) is Alice’s private key, which is a random integer in  <math alttext="StartSet 1 comma ellipsis comma n minus 1 EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></math> ![StartSet 1 comma ellipsis comma n minus 1 EndSet](images/c13_469.png), and  <math alttext="upper P u Subscript upper A Baseline equals upper P r Subscript upper A Baseline dot upper G" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>P</mi><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>G</mi></mrow></math> ![upper P u Subscript upper A Baseline equals upper P r Subscript upper A Baseline dot upper G](images/c13_470.png) is her public key; *G* is the base point.

#### 13.5.5.2 ECDSA Signature Generation

The signature generation (also called *signing process*) is done by Alice, the signer, as follows:

1.  Generate a new ephemeral key pair  <math alttext="left-parenthesis k comma upper Q right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Q</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis k comma upper Q right-parenthesis](images/c13_471.png) as follows: 
    *   Pick a cryptographically secure random[⁷](#c13.xhtml#c13-note-0007) integer  <math alttext="k such that 0 less-than k less-than n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>k</mi><mtext>&#160;such&#160;that&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>0</mn><mo>&#60;</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![k such that 0 less-than k less-than n](images/c13_472.png). *n* is the order of the base point *G*.
    *   Calculate point  <math alttext="upper Q equals k dot upper G" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>G</mi></mrow></math> ![upper Q equals k dot upper G](images/c13_473.png);  <math alttext="left-parenthesis x Subscript upper Q Baseline comma y Subscript upper Q Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>Q</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>Q</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis x Subscript upper Q Baseline comma y Subscript upper Q Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c13_474.png) are the coordinates of EC point *Q*.
2.  Calculate  <math alttext="r equals x Subscript upper Q Baseline m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>Q</mi></msub><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![r equals x Subscript upper Q Baseline m o d n](images/c13_475.png).
3.  If  <math alttext="r equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![r equals 0](images/c13_476.png), return to step 1 and try again.
4.  Compute the message digest[⁸](#c13.xhtml#c13-note-0008)  <math alttext="upper H equals h a s h left-parenthesis upper M right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>h</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper H equals h a s h left-parenthesis upper M right-parenthesis](images/c13_477.png), where  <math alttext="h a s h left-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>h</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> ![h a s h left-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c13_478.png) is the hash function selected by the signer.
5.  Calculate  <math alttext="s equals k Superscript negative 1 Baseline asterisk left-parenthesis upper H plus r asterisk upper P r Subscript upper A Baseline right-parenthesis m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>P</mi><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![s equals k Superscript negative 1 Baseline asterisk left-parenthesis upper H plus r asterisk upper P r Subscript upper A Baseline right-parenthesis m o d n](images/c13_479.png).  <math alttext="k Superscript negative 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ![k Superscript negative 1](images/c13_480.png) is the multiplicative inverse of *k* in the underlying finite field. Notice that, in order to optimize computation time, the signature relates to the hash of the message and not to the entire message.
6.  If  <math alttext="s equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![s equals 0](images/c13_481.png), then return to step 1 and try again.[⁹](#c13.xhtml#c13-note-0009)
7.  The pair  <math alttext="left-parenthesis r comma s right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis r comma s right-parenthesis](images/c13_482.png) is the signature of message *M*.

#### 13.5.5.3 ECDSA Signature Verification

Assume that Bob has received, from Alice, the followings items:

*   Domain parameters selected by Alice, the public key of Alice  <math alttext="upper P u Subscript upper A" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![upper P u Subscript upper A](images/c13_483.png), and the identity of the hash function
*   Message  <math alttext="upper M prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![upper M prime](images/c13_484.png) and its signature  <math alttext="left-parenthesis r prime comma s prime right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>'</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis r prime comma s prime right-parenthesis](images/c13_485.png).

The signature verification process is as follows:

1.  If  <math alttext="r prime not-an-element-of StartSet 1 comma ellipsis comma n minus 1 EndSet or s prime not-an-element-of StartSet 1 comma ellipsis comma n minus 1 EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8713;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;or&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8713;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![r prime not-an-element-of StartSet 1 comma ellipsis comma n minus 1 EndSet or s prime not-an-element-of StartSet 1 comma ellipsis comma n minus 1 EndSet](images/c13_486.png), stop the verification, because the signature pair is invalid regarding the signature generation procedure.
2.  Compute the message digest  <math alttext="upper H prime equals h a s h left-parenthesis upper M prime right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>'</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>h</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper H prime equals h a s h left-parenthesis upper M prime right-parenthesis](images/c13_487.png)
3.  Compute  <math alttext="upper U 1 equals upper H prime left-parenthesis s prime right-parenthesis Superscript negative 1 Baseline m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>H</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>n</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![upper U 1 equals upper H prime left-parenthesis s prime right-parenthesis Superscript negative 1 Baseline m o d n](images/c13_488.png) and  <math alttext="upper U 2 equals r prime left-parenthesis s prime right-parenthesis Superscript negative 1 Baseline m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper U 2 equals r prime left-parenthesis s prime right-parenthesis Superscript negative 1 Baseline m o d n](images/c13_489.png).
4.  Compute the EC point  <math alttext="upper R equals left-parenthesis x Subscript upper R Baseline comma y Subscript upper R Baseline right-parenthesis equals upper U 1 dot upper G plus upper U 2 dot upper P u Subscript upper A Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>G</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>P</mi><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![upper R equals left-parenthesis x Subscript upper R Baseline comma y Subscript upper R Baseline right-parenthesis equals upper U 1 dot upper G plus upper U 2 dot upper P u Subscript upper A Baseline](images/c13_490.png).
5.  If  <math alttext="x Subscript upper R Baseline m o d n equals r prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![x Subscript upper R Baseline m o d n equals r prime](images/c13_491.png), the signature is valid. Otherwise, it is invalid.

**Example 13.7** Many online tools provide services for playing with ECDSA. The domain parameters of recommended EC are listed in \[[10](#c13.xhtml#c13-bib-0010)\]. As far as we know, the most used elliptic curve in EC-based digital signature systems is labeled P-256; its equation is  <math alttext="y squared equals x cubed minus 3 x plus b m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![y squared equals x cubed minus 3 x plus b m o d p](images/c13_492.png) over prime field *F[p]*. Notice that parameter *a* is −3; and parameter *b* should be selected prior starting signing process.

The domain parameters of the EC P-256 are as follows:

*p* = 15792089210356248762697446949407573530086143415290314195533631308867097853951

*n* = 115792089210356248762697446949407573529996955224135760342422259061068512044369

*b* = 5ac635d8 aa3a93e7 b3ebbd55 769886bc 651d06b0 cc53b0f6 3bce3c3e 27d2604b

*x[G]* = 6b17d1f2 e12c4247 f8bce6e5 63a440f2 77037d81 2deb33a0 f4a13945 d898c296

*y[G]* = 4fe342e2 fe1a7f9b 8ee7eb4a 7c0f9e16 2bce3357 6b315ece cbb64068 37bf51f5

The following scenario is provided using *8gwifi.org* tool.

1.  Select P-256 as elliptic curve.
2.  The randomly produced private key looks like this:
    
    ```
    -----BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY-----
    MHQCAQEEIFqqEkIem0YXpT1WBsUjXGH/flXMLbScdBNbrOzP4zCWoAcGBSuBBAAKoUQDQgAERVFoufpWA1h1d7f1Y+DneelWWmoGI5EWuMeDN/xu/Z2UWk1DQ+rXAxCE/Eo1gFb5gpHB1uTNwreW2Ft+4YXUbQ==
    -----END EC PRIVATE KEY-----
    ```
    
3.  The randomly produced public key looks like this:
    
    ```
    -----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----
    MFYwEAYHKoZIzj0CAQYFK4EEAAoDQgAERVFoufpWA1h1d7f1Y+DneelWWmoGI5EWuMeDN/xu/Z2UWk1DQ+rXAxCE/Eo1gFb5gpHB1uTNwreW2Ft+4YXUbQ==
    -----END PUBLIC KEY-----
    ```
    
4.  Message = “Hello ECDSA users”.
5.  Signature looks like this:
    
    ```
    MEYCIQCtK/+15PFcTIqDJA21qIocPTCkOCF4SIJ3gLzIh0TdvgIhAMV3egIYolvZmPhwOsAuHAjLFvOfssso79tQ9MvI4NSD
    ```
    

#### 13.5.5.4 Correctness of ECDSA Algorithm

ECDSA is correct if and only if both following conditions hold:

*   C1: If Bob receives the correct message *M* and its signature  <math alttext="left-parenthesis r comma s right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis r comma s right-parenthesis](images/c13_493.png), then the result is “Valid signature”.
*   C2: If Bob receives either an incorrect message or an incorrect signature, then the result is “Invalid”.

To address both conditions, we start from step 4 in signature verification. Since ECs are cyclic groups modulo the order of the EC,  <math alttext="m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![m o d n](images/c13_494.png) is omitted in the following proof.

*   *Condition C1*

If Bob receives the valid data, then:  <math alttext="upper M prime equals upper M" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> ![upper M prime equals upper M](images/c13_495.png),  <math alttext="left-parenthesis r prime comma s Superscript prime Baseline right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis r comma s right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis r prime comma s Superscript prime Baseline right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis r comma s right-parenthesis](images/c13_496.png), and  <math alttext="upper H prime equals upper H" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>H</mi></mrow></math> ![upper H prime equals upper H](images/c13_497.png). Using the definition of  <math alttext="upper P u Subscript upper A" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![upper P u Subscript upper A](images/c13_498.png),  <math alttext="upper U 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper U 1](images/c13_499.png), and  <math alttext="upper U 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper U 2](images/c13_500.png), we can write:

upper A Baseline dot upper G 2nd Row equals left-parenthesis upper H asterisk s Superscript negative 1 Baseline plus r asterisk s Superscript negative 1 Baseline dot upper P r Subscript upper A Baseline right-parenthesis dot upper G equals s Superscript negative 1 Baseline asterisk left-parenthesis upper H plus r asterisk upper P r Subscript upper A Baseline right-parenthesis dot upper G EndLayout" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mtable><mtr><mtd><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>G</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>P</mi><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>G</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>P</mi><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>G</mi></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>P</mi><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>P</mi><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>G</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable></math> By definition (step 5 in Signature generation):  <math alttext="s equals k Superscript negative 1 Baseline left-parenthesis upper H plus r asterisk upper P r Subscript upper A Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>P</mi><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![s equals k Superscript negative 1 Baseline left-parenthesis upper H plus r asterisk upper P r Subscript upper A Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c13_502.png).

For any element *z* in a finite field:  <math alttext="z asterisk z Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![z asterisk z Superscript negative 1 Baseline equals 1](images/c13_503.png). We can write:

 <math alttext="StartLayout 1st Row k asterisk s equals k asterisk k Superscript negative 1 Baseline left-parenthesis upper H plus r asterisk upper P r Subscript upper A Baseline right-parenthesis equals upper H plus r asterisk upper P r Subscript upper A Baseline right-parenthesis 2nd Row right double arrow k equals s Superscript negative 1 Baseline asterisk left-parenthesis upper H plus r asterisk upper P r Subscript upper A Baseline right-parenthesis EndLayout" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mtable columnalign="left"><mtr><mtd><mi>k</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>P</mi><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>H</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>P</mi><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mo>&#8658;</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>P</mi><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></math> ![StartLayout 1st Row k asterisk s equals k asterisk k Superscript negative 1 Baseline left-parenthesis upper H plus r asterisk upper P r Subscript upper A Baseline right-parenthesis equals upper H plus r asterisk upper P r Subscript upper A Baseline right-parenthesis 2nd Row right double arrow k equals s Superscript negative 1 Baseline asterisk left-parenthesis upper H plus r asterisk upper P r Subscript upper A Baseline right-parenthesis EndLayout](images/c13_504.png)

We substitute  <math alttext="s Superscript negative 1 Baseline asterisk left-parenthesis upper H plus r asterisk upper P r Subscript upper A Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>s</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>\*</mo><mi>P</mi><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![s Superscript negative 1 Baseline asterisk left-parenthesis upper H plus r asterisk upper P r Subscript upper A Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c13_505.png) by *k* in our last definition of *R*:

 <math alttext="upper R equals s Superscript negative 1 Baseline left-parenthesis upper H plus r dot upper P r Subscript upper A Baseline right-parenthesis dot upper G equals k dot upper G" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>r</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>P</mi><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>G</mi></mrow></math> ![upper R equals s Superscript negative 1 Baseline left-parenthesis upper H plus r dot upper P r Subscript upper A Baseline right-parenthesis dot upper G equals k dot upper G](images/c13_506.png)

 <math alttext="upper R equals k dot upper G" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>G</mi></mrow></math> ![upper R equals k dot upper G](images/c13_507.png) is the same point as  <math alttext="upper Q equals k dot upper G" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>G</mi></mrow></math> ![upper Q equals k dot upper G](images/c13_508.png) (step 1 in Signature generation). Consequently, ECDSA verification result is correct when the received message and its signature are valid.

*   *Condition C2*

If Bob received an incorrect message, then:  <math alttext="upper H prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![upper H prime](images/c13_509.png)≠  <math alttext="upper H" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi></mrow></math> ![upper H](images/c13_510.png).

If Bob received an incorrect signature, then:  <math alttext="left-parenthesis s comma r right-parenthesis not-equals left-parenthesis s prime comma r Superscript prime Baseline right-parenthesis period" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>&#8800;</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mtext>s</mtext><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>r</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis s comma r right-parenthesis not-equals left-parenthesis s prime comma r Superscript prime Baseline right-parenthesis period](images/c13_511.png) There are three cases to check:

stretchy="false">\[</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>\*</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>&#948;</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>G</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>G</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo>\[</mo><mrow><msup><mi>s</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>\*</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>&#948;</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>G</mi></mrow><mo>\]</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper R equals left-bracket s Superscript negative 1 Baseline left-parenthesis upper H plus r dot upper P r Subscript upper A Baseline right-parenthesis dot upper G right-bracket plus left-bracket s Superscript negative 1 Baseline asterisk delta dot upper G right-bracket equals left-bracket k dot upper G right-bracket plus left-bracket s Superscript negative 1 Baseline asterisk delta dot upper G right-bracket](images/c13_521.png)

Point *R* calculated by Bob differs from point  <math alttext="upper Q equals k dot upper G" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>G</mi></mrow></math> ![upper Q equals k dot upper G](images/c13_522.png) (step 1 in Signature generation). If the hash function has a sufficient level of security strength, there is a very negligible probability that  <math alttext="s Superscript negative 1 Baseline asterisk delta dot upper G equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>s</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>\*</mo><mi>&#948;</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![s Superscript negative 1 Baseline asterisk delta dot upper G equals 0](images/c13_523.png). Thus, the result of ECDSA is “Invalid”, which is a correct decision.□

### 13.5.6 Edwards Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (EdDSA)

When the digital signature is produced using an Edwards curve, it is referred to as *Edwards curve digital signature* and denoted EdDSA. Edwards curve model is introduced in [Section 13.2.4](#c13.xhtml#c13-sec-1015). EdDSA signatures are recommended, because they are efficient (in terms of computation time) compared to traditional ECDSA signatures.

As in traditional ECs, domain parameters must be selected before generating and verifying EdDSA signatures. Domain parameters of Edwards ECs are the following:

*   *p*: prime.
*   *a* and *d*: the coefficients of the Edwards curve equation  <math alttext="y squared plus a x squared equals 1 plus d x squared y squared m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![y squared plus a x squared equals 1 plus d x squared y squared m o d p](images/c13_524.png). Both coefficients are elements in *F[p]*.
*    <math alttext="upper G equals left-parenthesis x Subscript upper G Baseline comma y Subscript upper G Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>G</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>G</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper G equals left-parenthesis x Subscript upper G Baseline comma y Subscript upper G Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c13_525.png): base point.
*   *n*: order of base point *G*.
*   *h*: cofactor associated with the base point:  <math alttext="h equals StartFraction StartAbsoluteValue upper E left-parenthesis upper F p right-parenthesis EndAbsoluteValue Over n EndFraction" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mrow><mi>E</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>F</mi><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&#124;</mo></mrow><mi>n</mi></mfrac></mrow></math> ![h equals StartFraction StartAbsoluteValue upper E left-parenthesis upper F p right-parenthesis EndAbsoluteValue Over n EndFraction](images/c13_526.png).

Edwards25519 and Edwards448 curves make use of the hash functions SHA-512 and SHAKE256,[^(10)](#c13.xhtml#c13-note-0010) respectively.

#### 13.5.6.1 EdDSA Key Pair Generation

Let *b* denote the bit-length of the private key.  <math alttext="b equals 256" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>256</mn></mrow></math> ![b equals 256](images/c13_527.png), when Edwards25519 curve is used; and  <math alttext="b equals 456" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>456</mn></mrow></math> ![b equals 456](images/c13_528.png), when Edwards448 curve is used.

1.  Pick a cryptographically secure random[^(11)](#c13.xhtml#c13-note-0011) integer *k* of *b* bits.
2.  Compute the private key hash *H*:
    
    *   For Edwards25519 curve:  <math alttext="upper H equals upper S upper H upper A soft hyphen 512 left-parenthesis k right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>S</mi><mi>H</mi><mi>A</mi><mo>&#173;</mo><mn>512</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper H equals upper S upper H upper A soft hyphen 512 left-parenthesis k right-parenthesis](images/c13_529.png)
    *   For Edwards448 curve:  <math alttext="upper H equals upper S upper H upper A upper K upper E Baseline 256 left-parenthesis k comma 912 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>S</mi><mi>H</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>K</mi><mi>E</mi><mn>256</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>912</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper H equals upper S upper H upper A upper K upper E Baseline 256 left-parenthesis k comma 912 right-parenthesis](images/c13_530.png)
        
3.  Let  <math alttext="left-parenthesis h 0 comma h 1 comma ellipsis comma h Subscript 2 b minus 1 Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>b</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis h 0 comma h 1 comma ellipsis comma h Subscript 2 b minus 1 Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c13_531.png) denote the  <math alttext="2 b" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>b</mi></mrow></math> ![2 b](images/c13_532.png) bits of the key hash *H*. Let  <math alttext="upper H 1 equals left-parenthesis h 0 comma h 1 comma ellipsis comma h Subscript b minus 1 Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper H 1 equals left-parenthesis h 0 comma h 1 comma ellipsis comma h Subscript b minus 1 Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c13_533.png) and  <math alttext="upper H 2 equals left-parenthesis h Subscript b Baseline comma h Subscript b plus 1 Baseline comma ellipsis comma h Subscript 2 b minus 1 Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>b</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper H 2 equals left-parenthesis h Subscript b Baseline comma h Subscript b plus 1 Baseline comma ellipsis comma h Subscript 2 b minus 1 Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c13_534.png); i.e.  <math alttext="upper H 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper H 1](images/c13_535.png) and  <math alttext="upper H 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper H 2](images/c13_536.png) are the first and second halves of  <math alttext="upper H left-parenthesis k right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper H left-parenthesis k right-parenthesis](images/c13_537.png), respectively.
4.  Generate the public key *Q*:
    
    *   For Edwards25519: set  <math alttext="h 0 equals h 1 equals h 2 equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![h 0 equals h 1 equals h 2 equals 0](images/c13_538.png);  <math alttext="h Subscript b minus 2 Baseline equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![h Subscript b minus 2 Baseline equals 1](images/c13_539.png);  <math alttext="h Subscript b minus 1 Baseline equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![h Subscript b minus 1 Baseline equals 0](images/c13_540.png). Then, set *t* to the modified  <math alttext="upper H 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper H 1](images/c13_541.png); i.e.  <math alttext="t equals left-parenthesis 0 comma 0 comma 0 comma h 3 comma ellipsis comma h Subscript b minus 3 Baseline comma 1 comma 0 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![t equals left-parenthesis 0 comma 0 comma 0 comma h 3 comma ellipsis comma h Subscript b minus 3 Baseline comma 1 comma 0 right-parenthesis](images/c13_542.png)
    *   For Edwards448: set  <math alttext="h 0 equals h 1 equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![h 0 equals h 1 equals 0](images/c13_543.png);  <math alttext="h Subscript b minus 9 Baseline equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![h Subscript b minus 9 Baseline equals 1](images/c13_544.png); and  <math alttext="h Subscript i Baseline equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![h Subscript i Baseline equals 0](images/c13_545.png), for  <math alttext="b minus 8 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than-or-equal-to b minus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>i</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8804;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>b</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![b minus 8 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than-or-equal-to b minus 1](images/c13_546.png). Then, set *t* to the modified  <math alttext="upper H 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper H 1](images/c13_547.png); i.e.  <math alttext="t equals left-parenthesis 0 comma 0 comma h 2 comma ellipsis comma h Subscript b minus 10 Baseline comma 1 comma 0 comma 0 ellipsis comma 0 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![t equals left-parenthesis 0 comma 0 comma h 2 comma ellipsis comma h Subscript b minus 10 Baseline comma 1 comma 0 comma 0 ellipsis comma 0 right-parenthesis](images/c13_548.png)
    *   Encode  <math alttext="t colon s equals upper B i t upper S t r i n g upper T o upper I n t e g e r left-parenthesis t right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>:</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>S</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>T</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>I</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>r</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![t colon s equals upper B i t upper S t r i n g upper T o upper I n t e g e r left-parenthesis t right-parenthesis](images/c13_549.png)
    *    <math alttext="upper Q equals s dot upper G" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>&#8901;</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow></math> ![upper Q equals s dot upper G](images/c13_550.png) # multiplication of point *G* by a scalar *s*
    *   Encode[^(12)](#c13.xhtml#c13-note-0012)  <math alttext="upper Q equals upper Q Subscript e n c Baseline equals upper E n c o d e upper P o i n t left-parenthesis upper Q comma b right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>=</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>c</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext></mrow></msub><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>=</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>E</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> ![upper Q equals upper Q Subscript e n c Baseline equals upper E n c o d e upper P o i n t left-parenthesis upper Q comma b right-parenthesis](images/c13_551.png)
5.  Encoded public key  <math alttext="upper Q Subscript e n c" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>c</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper Q Subscript e n c](images/c13_552.png) is sent either along with the signed message or separately.

Using steps 4.1 (or 4.2) and 4.3 in key-pair generation procedure, we can see that integer *s* has the three (or two) least significant bits at 0. Let us focus on the Edwards25519 curve (the same apply to the second curve). We can write *s* as  <math alttext="s equals s prime asterisk 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>s</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>=</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>\*</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>8</mn></mrow></math> ![s equals s prime asterisk 8](images/c13_553.png), where  <math alttext="s prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></math> ![s prime](images/c13_554.png) the rightmost  <math alttext="b minus 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8722;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> ![b minus 3](images/c13_555.png) bits of *s*. 8 is the cofactor of the Edwards2219 curve. Notice that  <math alttext="s prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></math> ![s prime](images/c13_556.png) is distinct from 0, because it has at least a 1-bit. Then, in step 4.4, the public key is computed as  <math alttext="upper Q equals s dot upper G" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>&#8901;</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow></math> ![upper Q equals s dot upper G](images/c13_557.png). By substitution:  <math alttext="upper Q equals left-parenthesis 8 asterisk s Superscript prime Baseline right-parenthesis dot upper G equals 8 dot left-parenthesis s prime dot upper G right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>=</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>\*</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8901;</mo><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>&#8901;</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>&#8901;</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper Q equals left-parenthesis 8 asterisk s Superscript prime Baseline right-parenthesis dot upper G equals 8 dot left-parenthesis s prime dot upper G right-parenthesis](images/c13_558.png). By Lemma 13.1, *Q* is point of prime order *n*. Therefore, the legitimate signer makes use of public key with an order of *n*.

#### 13.5.6.2 EdDSA Signature Generation

The signature of a message *M* is of a bit-length of  <math alttext="2 b" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>b</mi></mrow></math> ![2 b](images/c13_559.png); it is composed of two equal-length parts, *R* and *S* computed as follows:

1.  Compute the private-key hash *H*: 
    *   For Edwards25519 curve:  <math alttext="upper H equals upper S upper H upper A soft hyphen 512 left-parenthesis k right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>S</mi><mi>H</mi><mi>A</mi><mo>&#173;</mo><mn>512</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper H equals upper S upper H upper A soft hyphen 512 left-parenthesis k right-parenthesis](images/c13_560.png)
    *   For Edwards448 curve:  <math alttext="upper H equals upper S upper H upper A upper K upper E Baseline 256 left-parenthesis k comma 912 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>S</mi><mi>H</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>K</mi><mi>E</mi><mn>256</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>912</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper H equals upper S upper H upper A upper K upper E Baseline 256 left-parenthesis k comma 912 right-parenthesis](images/c13_561.png)
2.  Let  <math alttext="left-parenthesis h 0 comma h 1 comma ellipsis comma h Subscript 2 b minus 1 Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>b</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis h 0 comma h 1 comma ellipsis comma h Subscript 2 b minus 1 Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c13_562.png) denote the  <math alttext="2 b" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>b</mi></mrow></math> ![2 b](images/c13_563.png) bits of the key hash *H*. Let  <math alttext="upper H 1 equals left-parenthesis h 0 comma h 1 comma ellipsis comma h Subscript b minus 1 Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper H 1 equals left-parenthesis h 0 comma h 1 comma ellipsis comma h Subscript b minus 1 Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c13_564.png) and  <math alttext="upper H 2 equals left-parenthesis h Subscript b Baseline comma h Subscript b plus 1 Baseline comma ellipsis comma h Subscript 2 b minus 1 Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>b</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper H 2 equals left-parenthesis h Subscript b Baseline comma h Subscript b plus 1 Baseline comma ellipsis comma h Subscript 2 b minus 1 Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c13_565.png).
3.  Compute the part *R* of the signature using  <math alttext="upper H 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper H 2](images/c13_566.png), the second half of the key hash: 
    *   For Edwards25519:  <math alttext="r equals upper S upper H upper A soft hyphen 512 left-parenthesis upper H 2 StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue upper M right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>S</mi><mi>H</mi><mi>A</mi><mo>&#173;</mo><mn>512</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> ![r equals upper S upper H upper A soft hyphen 512 left-parenthesis upper H 2 StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue upper M right-parenthesis](images/c13_567.png)
    *   For Edwards448:  <math alttext="r equals upper S upper H upper A upper K upper E Baseline 256 left-parenthesis upper A p p e n d e d upper D a t a parallel-to upper H 2 parallel-to upper M comma 912 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>S</mi><mi>H</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>K</mi><mi>E</mi><mn>256</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>D</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8741;</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>&#8741;</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>912</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![r equals upper S upper H upper A upper K upper E Baseline 256 left-parenthesis upper A p p e n d e d upper D a t a parallel-to upper H 2 parallel-to upper M comma 912 right-parenthesis](images/c13_568.png), where
        
         <math alttext="upper A p p e n d e d upper D a t a equals quotation-mark upper S i g upper E d Baseline 448 quotation-mark StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue o c t e t left-parenthesis 0 right-parenthesis StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue o c t e t left-parenthesis l e n left-parenthesis c o n t e x t right-parenthesis right-parenthesis StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue c o n t e x t" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>D</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>"</mo><mi>S</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>E</mi><mi>d</mi><mn>448</mn><mo>"</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>o</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>o</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>c</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> ![upper A p p e n d e d upper D a t a equals quotation-mark upper S i g upper E d Baseline 448 quotation-mark StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue o c t e t left-parenthesis 0 right-parenthesis StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue o c t e t left-parenthesis l e n left-parenthesis c o n t e x t right-parenthesis right-parenthesis StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue c o n t e x t](images/c13_569.png)
        
         <math alttext="o c t e t left-parenthesis a right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>o</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![o c t e t left-parenthesis a right-parenthesis](images/c13_570.png) denotes an octet with a value *a*;  <math alttext="c o n t e x t" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> ![c o n t e x t](images/c13_571.png)[^(13)](#c13.xhtml#c13-note-0013) denotes a bit-string known to the signer and the verifier; by default,  <math alttext="c o n t e x t" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> ![c o n t e x t](images/c13_572.png) is the empty string.
        
         <math alttext="upper S upper H upper A upper K upper E Baseline 256 left-parenthesis upper I n p u t upper D a t a comma 912 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mi>H</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>K</mi><mi>E</mi><mn>256</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>I</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>u</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>D</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>912</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper S upper H upper A upper K upper E Baseline 256 left-parenthesis upper I n p u t upper D a t a comma 912 right-parenthesis](images/c13_573.png) produces a hash of 456 bits.
        
    *   Compute point  <math alttext="upper R prime equals r prime dot upper G" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>'</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>'</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>G</mi></mrow></math> ![upper R prime equals r prime dot upper G](images/c13_574.png), where  <math alttext="r prime equals upper B i t upper S t r i n g upper T o upper I n t e g e r left-parenthesis r right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>S</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>T</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>I</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>r</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![r prime equals upper B i t upper S t r i n g upper T o upper I n t e g e r left-parenthesis r right-parenthesis](images/c13_575.png). Then, encode point  <math alttext="upper R prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![upper R prime](images/c13_576.png) as a *b*\-bit-string  <math alttext="upper R equals upper E n c o d e upper P o i n t left-parenthesis upper R prime comma b right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>E</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>'</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper R equals upper E n c o d e upper P o i n t left-parenthesis upper R prime comma b right-parenthesis](images/c13_577.png)
4.  Compute the part *S* of the signature using  <math alttext="upper H 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper H 1](images/c13_578.png), the first half of the key hash
    
    *   For Edwards25519: set  <math alttext="h 0 equals h 1 equals h 2 equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![h 0 equals h 1 equals h 2 equals 0](images/c13_579.png);  <math alttext="h Subscript b minus 2 Baseline equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![h Subscript b minus 2 Baseline equals 1](images/c13_580.png);  <math alttext="h Subscript b minus 1 Baseline equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![h Subscript b minus 1 Baseline equals 0](images/c13_581.png). Then, set *t* to the modified  <math alttext="h equals StartFraction StartAbsoluteValue upper E left-parenthesis upper F p right-parenthesis EndAbsoluteValue Over n EndFraction" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mrow><mi>E</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>F</mi><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&#124;</mo></mrow><mi>n</mi></mfrac></mrow></math> ![h equals StartFraction StartAbsoluteValue upper E left-parenthesis upper F p right-parenthesis EndAbsoluteValue Over n EndFraction](images/c13_582.png); i.e.  <math alttext="t equals left-parenthesis 0 comma 0 comma 0 comma h 3 comma ellipsis comma h Subscript b minus 3 Baseline comma 1 comma 0 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![t equals left-parenthesis 0 comma 0 comma 0 comma h 3 comma ellipsis comma h Subscript b minus 3 Baseline comma 1 comma 0 right-parenthesis](images/c13_583.png)
    *   For Edwards448: set  <math alttext="h 0 equals h 1 equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![h 0 equals h 1 equals 0](images/c13_584.png);  <math alttext="h Subscript b minus 9 Baseline equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![h Subscript b minus 9 Baseline equals 1](images/c13_585.png); and  <math alttext="h Subscript i Baseline equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![h Subscript i Baseline equals 0](images/c13_586.png), for  <math alttext="b minus 8 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than-or-equal-to b minus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![b minus 8 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than-or-equal-to b minus 1](images/c13_587.png). Then, set *t* to the modified  <math alttext="upper H 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> ![upper H 1](images/c13_588.png); i.e.  <math alttext="t equals left-parenthesis 0 comma 0 comma h 2 comma ellipsis comma h Subscript b minus 10 Baseline comma 1 comma 0 comma 0 ellipsis comma 0 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![t equals left-parenthesis 0 comma 0 comma h 2 comma ellipsis comma h Subscript b minus 10 Baseline comma 1 comma 0 comma 0 ellipsis comma 0 right-parenthesis](images/c13_589.png)
    *   Encode  <math alttext="t colon s equals upper B i t upper S t r i n g upper T o upper I n t e g e r left-parenthesis t right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>:</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>S</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>T</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>I</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>r</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![t colon s equals upper B i t upper S t r i n g upper T o upper I n t e g e r left-parenthesis t right-parenthesis](images/c13_590.png)([^(14)](#c13.xhtml#c13-note-0014))
    *   For Edwards25519:  <math alttext="upper W equals upper S upper H upper A soft hyphen 512 left-parenthesis upper R parallel-to upper Q Subscript e n c Baseline parallel-to upper M right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>W</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>S</mi><mi>H</mi><mi>A</mi><mo>&#173;</mo><mn>512</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>&#8741;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo>&#8741;</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper W equals upper S upper H upper A soft hyphen 512 left-parenthesis upper R parallel-to upper Q Subscript e n c Baseline parallel-to upper M right-parenthesis](images/c13_591.png)
    *   For Edwards448:  <math alttext="upper W equals upper S upper H upper A upper K upper E Baseline 256 left-parenthesis upper A p p e n d e d upper D a t a StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue upper R StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue upper Q Subscript e n c Baseline StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue upper M comma 912 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>W</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>S</mi><mi>H</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>K</mi><mi>E</mi><mn>256</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>D</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>a</mi><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>912</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> ![upper W equals upper S upper H upper A upper K upper E Baseline 256 left-parenthesis upper A p p e n d e d upper D a t a StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue upper R StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue upper Q Subscript e n c Baseline StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue upper M comma 912 right-parenthesis](images/c13_592.png)
    *    <math alttext="v equals left-parenthesis r prime plus upper B i t upper S t r i n g upper T o upper I n t e g e r left-parenthesis upper W right-parenthesis asterisk s right-parenthesis m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>'</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>S</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>T</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>I</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>r</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![v equals left-parenthesis r prime plus upper B i t upper S t r i n g upper T o upper I n t e g e r left-parenthesis upper W right-parenthesis asterisk s right-parenthesis m o d n](images/c13_593.png)
        
        Encode  <math alttext="v colon upper S equals upper I n t e g e r upper T o upper B i t upper S t r i n g left-parenthesis v comma b right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>:</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>I</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>T</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>S</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![v colon upper S equals upper I n t e g e r upper T o upper B i t upper S t r i n g left-parenthesis v comma b right-parenthesis](images/c13_594.png)
        
5.  The EdDSA signature is  <math alttext="upper S i g equals upper R StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue upper S" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow></math> ![upper S i g equals upper R StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue upper S](images/c13_595.png)

#### 13.5.6.3 EdDSA Signature Verification

Let  <math alttext="h equals StartFraction StartAbsoluteValue upper E left-parenthesis upper F p right-parenthesis EndAbsoluteValue Over n EndFraction" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mrow><mi>E</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>F</mi><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&#124;</mo></mrow><mi>n</mi></mfrac></mrow></math> ![m](images/c13_596.png) denote the signed message and  <math alttext="upper S i g" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>g</mi></mrow></math> ![upper S i g](images/c13_597.png), its signature. Domain parameters and the signer public-key  <math alttext="upper Q Subscript e n c" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper Q Subscript e n c](images/c13_598.png), are known to the verifier. The signature verification process is as follows:

1.  Data decoding: 
    *   Decode the signer public key  <math alttext="upper Q Subscript e n c" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper Q Subscript e n c](images/c13_599.png) to an EC point *Q*.
    *   Decode the first half of the signature  <math alttext="upper S i g" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>g</mi></mrow></math> ![upper S i g](images/c13_600.png) to a point  <math alttext="upper R prime" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow></math> ![upper R prime](images/c13_601.png).
    *   Decode the second half of the signature  <math alttext="upper S i g" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>g</mi></mrow></math> ![upper S i g](images/c13_602.png) to an integer *v*. If  <math alttext="v less-than n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![v less-than n](images/c13_603.png) continue the verification. Otherwise, reject the received message.
2.  Compute the hash: 
    *    <math alttext="upper D a t a upper T o upper H a s h equals upper E n c o d e upper P o i n t left-parenthesis upper R prime right-parenthesis parallel-to upper Q Subscript e n c Baseline parallel-to upper M" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>D</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>T</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>H</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>E</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>'</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8741;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo>&#8741;</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> ![upper D a t a upper T o upper H a s h equals upper E n c o d e upper P o i n t left-parenthesis upper R prime right-parenthesis parallel-to upper Q Subscript e n c Baseline parallel-to upper M](images/c13_604.png)
    *   For Edwards25519:  <math alttext="u equals upper S upper H upper A soft hyphen 512 left-parenthesis upper D a t a upper T o upper H a s h right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>S</mi><mi>H</mi><mi>A</mi><mo>&#173;</mo><mn>512</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>D</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>T</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>H</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![u equals upper S upper H upper A soft hyphen 512 left-parenthesis upper D a t a upper T o upper H a s h right-parenthesis](images/c13_605.png)
    *   For Edwards448:  <math alttext="u equals upper S upper H upper A upper K upper E Baseline 256 left-parenthesis upper A p p e n d e d upper D a t a StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue upper D a t a upper T o upper H a s h comma 912 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>S</mi><mi>H</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>K</mi><mi>E</mi><mn>256</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>D</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>a</mi><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>D</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>T</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>H</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>912</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> ![u equals upper S upper H upper A upper K upper E Baseline 256 left-parenthesis upper A p p e n d e d upper D a t a StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue upper D a t a upper T o upper H a s h comma 912 right-parenthesis](images/c13_606.png), where  <math alttext="upper A p p e n d e d upper D a t a" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>D</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>a</mi></mrow></math> ![upper A p p e n d e d upper D a t a](images/c13_607.png) has the same content than that in Signature generation; i.e.  <math alttext="upper A p p e n d e d upper D a t a equals quotation-mark upper S i g upper E d Baseline 448 quotation-mark StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue o c t e t left-parenthesis 0 right-parenthesis StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue o c t e t left-parenthesis l e n left-parenthesis c o n t e x t right-parenthesis right-parenthesis StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue c o n t e x t" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>D</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>"</mo><mi>S</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>E</mi><mi>d</mi><mn>448</mn><mo>"</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>o</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>o</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>c</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> ![upper A p p e n d e d upper D a t a equals quotation-mark upper S i g upper E d Baseline 448 quotation-mark StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue o c t e t left-parenthesis 0 right-parenthesis StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue o c t e t left-parenthesis l e n left-parenthesis c o n t e x t right-parenthesis right-parenthesis StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue c o n t e x t](images/c13_608.png)
        
         <math alttext="t equals upper B i t upper S upper T r i n g upper T o upper I n t e g e r left-parenthesis u right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>S</mi><mi>T</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>T</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>I</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>r</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![t equals upper B i t upper S upper T r i n g upper T o upper I n t e g e r left-parenthesis u right-parenthesis](images/c13_609.png)
        
3.  Check: 
    *   For Edwards25519:  <math alttext="c equals log Subscript 2 Baseline left-parenthesis h right-parenthesis equals 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mi>log</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> ![c equals log Subscript 2 Baseline left-parenthesis h right-parenthesis equals 3](images/c13_610.png);  <math alttext="h equals 8" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></math> ![h equals 8](images/c13_611.png) is the cofactor of Edwards25519.
    *   For Edwards448:  <math alttext="c equals log Subscript 2 Baseline left-parenthesis h right-parenthesis equals 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mi>log</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![c equals log Subscript 2 Baseline left-parenthesis h right-parenthesis equals 2](images/c13_612.png);  <math alttext="h equals 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></math> ![h equals 4](images/c13_613.png) is the cofactor of Edwards448.
    *   If  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 2 Superscript c Baseline asterisk v right-parenthesis dot upper G equals 2 Superscript c Baseline dot upper R prime plus left-parenthesis 2 Superscript c Baseline asterisk t right-parenthesis dot upper Q" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>c</mi></msup><mo>\*</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&#8901;</mo><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>c</mi></msup><mo>&#8901;</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>'</mo><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>c</mi></msup><mo>\*</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&#8901;</mo><mi>Q</mi></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 2 Superscript c Baseline asterisk v right-parenthesis dot upper G equals 2 Superscript c Baseline dot upper R prime plus left-parenthesis 2 Superscript c Baseline asterisk t right-parenthesis dot upper Q](images/c13_614.png), then accept message *M*, else reject it.

*   *Proof of EdDSA correctness*

To simplify the proof of correctness of the EdDSA scheme, omit the conversion between integers and bit-strings and use a hash function  <math alttext="upper H a s h" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>H</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></math> ![upper H a s h](images/c13_615.png) that can be either SHA-512 or SHAKE256.

*   – From key-pair generation procedure, we have:  <math alttext="upper Q equals s dot upper G" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>&#8901;</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow></math> ![upper Q equals s dot upper G](images/c13_616.png)
*   – From the signature generation procedure we have:
    
        <math alttext="r equals upper H a s h left-parenthesis upper H 2 StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue upper M right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>H</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#124;</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> ![r equals upper H a s h left-parenthesis upper H 2 StartAbsoluteValue EndAbsoluteValue upper M right-parenthesis](images/c13_617.png)
    
        <math alttext="t equals upper H a s h left-parenthesis upper R parallel-to upper Q Subscript e n c Baseline parallel-to upper M right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>H</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>&#8741;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo>&#8741;</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![t equals upper H a s h left-parenthesis upper R parallel-to upper Q Subscript e n c Baseline parallel-to upper M right-parenthesis](images/c13_618.png)
    
        <math alttext="upper R prime equals r dot upper G" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>'</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>G</mi></mrow></math> ![upper R prime equals r dot upper G](images/c13_619.png)
    
        <math alttext="upper S equals v equals left-parenthesis r plus upper H a s h left-parenthesis upper R parallel-to upper Q Subscript e n c Baseline parallel-to upper M right-parenthesis asterisk s right-parenthesis m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>H</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>&#8741;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo>&#8741;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>\*</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![upper S equals v equals left-parenthesis r plus upper H a s h left-parenthesis upper R parallel-to upper Q Subscript e n c Baseline parallel-to upper M right-parenthesis asterisk s right-parenthesis m o d n](images/c13_620.png)
    
*   – Since the base point *G* has an order of *n*, we omit the  <math alttext="m o d n" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> ![m o d n](images/c13_621.png) in *S*. Indeed, for any positive integers *a* and *b*, such that  <math alttext="b less-than" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>&#60;</mo></mrow></math> ![b less-than](images/c13_622.png), we have:

*   – Make substitutions in the left part of the equality in the step 3 of the signature verification procedure:
