***Exercise 13.2*** Given the EC  <math alttext="upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus 4 x plus 20" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>:</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow></math> ![upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus 4 x plus 20](images/c13_944.png) over the finite field  <math alttext="upper F 29" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mn>29</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F 29](images/c13_945.png), point  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 8 comma 19 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>19</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 8 comma 19 right-parenthesis](images/c13_946.png) is one of the generators of  <math alttext="upper E left-parenthesis upper F 29 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mn>29</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper E left-parenthesis upper F 29 right-parenthesis](images/c13_947.png). The check is as follows:

Let *P* denote the point  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 8 comma 19 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>19</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 8 comma 19 right-parenthesis](images/c13_948.png). The multiples of *P* are:

![](images/c13_949.png)

Thus, point  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 8 comma 19 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>19</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 8 comma 19 right-parenthesis](images/c13_987.png) is a generator of the elliptic curve  <math alttext="upper E left-parenthesis upper F 29 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mn>29</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper E left-parenthesis upper F 29 right-parenthesis](images/c13_988.png).

***Exercise 13.3*** To be on an elliptic curve  <math alttext="upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus a x plus b m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>:</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus a x plus b m o d p](images/c13_989.png),  <math alttext="x cubed plus a x plus b" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></math> ![x cubed plus a x plus b](images/c13_990.png) must be a quadratic residue. Euler’s criterion (Theorem 3.7) states that given integers *a* and *p*, such that  <math alttext="p ampersand gt semicolon 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#38;gt;</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![p ampersand gt semicolon 2](images/c13_991.png) and *a* and *p* are coprime,  <math alttext="a Superscript StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction Baseline identical-to 1 m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![a Superscript StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction Baseline identical-to 1 m o d p](images/c13_992.png), if there exists *r* such that  <math alttext="r squared identical-to a m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mi>a</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![r squared identical-to a m o d p](images/c13_993.png) and  <math alttext="a Superscript StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction Baseline identical-to negative 1 m o d zero width space p comma" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#8203;</mtext><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo></mrow></math> ![a Superscript StartFraction p minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction Baseline identical-to negative 1 m o d zero width space p comma](images/c13_994.png) otherwise.

Let *E* be an elliptic curve given by  <math alttext="y squared equals x cubed plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![y squared equals x cubed plus 1](images/c13_995.png) over finite field  <math alttext="upper F 103" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mn>103</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F 103](images/c13_996.png).

1.  Does  <math alttext="y squared equals left-parenthesis 2 right-parenthesis cubed plus 1 m o d 103" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>103</mn></mrow></math> ![y squared equals left-parenthesis 2 right-parenthesis cubed plus 1 m o d 103](images/c13_997.png) has a solution?
    
     <math alttext="9 Superscript StartFraction 103 minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction Baseline m o d 103 equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>9</mn><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>103</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>103</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![9 Superscript StartFraction 103 minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction Baseline m o d 103 equals 1](images/c13_998.png)  # (a tool of modular exponentiation is needed).
    
    By Euler’s criterion, there exists an integer *y* such that  <math alttext="y squared equals left-parenthesis 2 right-parenthesis cubed plus 1 m o d 103" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>103</mn></mrow></math> ![y squared equals left-parenthesis 2 right-parenthesis cubed plus 1 m o d 103](images/c13_999.png).
    
    It is easy to find  <math alttext="y squared equals 9 m o d 103" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>103</mn></mrow></math> ![y squared equals 9 m o d 103](images/c13_1000.png).  <math alttext="y equals plus-or-minus 3" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>&#177;</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> ![y equals plus-or-minus 3](images/c13_1001.png) is a solution.
    
    Hence,  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 2 comma 3 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 2 comma 3 right-parenthesis](images/c13_1002.png) and  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 2 comma 100 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>100</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 2 comma 100 right-parenthesis](images/c13_1003.png) are points of the curve  <math alttext="upper E left-parenthesis upper F 103 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mn>103</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper E left-parenthesis upper F 103 right-parenthesis](images/c13_1004.png).
    
2.  Does  <math alttext="y squared equals left-parenthesis 4 right-parenthesis cubed plus 1 m o d 103" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>103</mn></mrow></math> ![y squared equals left-parenthesis 4 right-parenthesis cubed plus 1 m o d 103](images/c13_1005.png) has a solution?
    
     <math alttext="65 Superscript StartFraction 103 minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction Baseline m o d 103 equals 102 equals negative 1 m o d 103" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>65</mn></mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>103</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>103</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>102</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>103</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![65 Superscript StartFraction 103 minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction Baseline m o d 103 equals 102 equals negative 1 m o d 103](images/c13_1006.png)
    
    By Euler’s criterion, there is no integer *y* such that  <math alttext="y squared equals left-parenthesis 4 right-parenthesis cubed plus 1 m o d 103" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>103</mn></mrow></math> ![y squared equals left-parenthesis 4 right-parenthesis cubed plus 1 m o d 103](images/c13_1007.png).
    
    Therefore, no point with coordinate  <math alttext="x equals 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></math> ![x equals 4](images/c13_1008.png) is on the elliptic curve  <math alttext="upper E left-parenthesis upper F 103 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mn>103</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper E left-parenthesis upper F 103 right-parenthesis](images/c13_1009.png).
    

***Exercise 13.4***

1.  Let  <math alttext="upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus x plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>:</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus x plus 1](images/c13_1010.png) be an elliptic curve over field  <math alttext="upper F 103" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mn>103</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F 103](images/c13_1011.png). Given *x*\-coordinate, to find the *y*\-coordinate, we need to find square roots. 
    *    <math alttext="x equals 0 right double arrow y squared identical-to 1 m o d 103" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8658;</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>103</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![x equals 0 right double arrow y squared identical-to 1 m o d 103](images/c13_1012.png)⇒  <math alttext="y equals plus-or-minus 1 m o d 103" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>&#177;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>103</mn></mrow></math> ![y equals plus-or-minus 1 m o d 103](images/c13_1013.png). Hence, points are  <math alttext="upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus 4 x plus 20" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>:</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow></math> ![upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus 4 x plus 20](images/c13_1014.png) and  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 0 comma 102 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>102</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 0 comma 102 right-parenthesis](images/c13_1015.png).
    *    <math alttext="x equals 11 identical-to 11 cubed plus 11 plus 1 m o d 103 identical-to 4 m o d 103" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mn>11</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>103</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>4</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>103</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![x equals 11 identical-to 11 cubed plus 11 plus 1 m o d 103 identical-to 4 m o d 103](images/c13_1016.png)⇒ <math alttext="y equals plus-or-minus 2 m o d 103" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>&#177;</mo><mn>2</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>103</mn></mrow></math> ![y equals plus-or-minus 2 m o d 103](images/c13_1017.png). Hence, points are:  <math alttext="upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus 4 x plus 20" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>:</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow></math> ![upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus 4 x plus 20](images/c13_1018.png) and  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 11 comma 101 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>11</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>101</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 11 comma 101 right-parenthesis](images/c13_1019.png).
    *    <math alttext="x equals 73 right double arrow y squared identical-to 73 cubed plus 73 plus 1 m o d 103 identical-to 60 m o d 103" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>73</mn><mo>&#8658;</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mn>73</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>73</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>103</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>60</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>103</mn></mrow></math> ![x equals 73 right double arrow y squared identical-to 73 cubed plus 73 plus 1 m o d 103 identical-to 60 m o d 103](images/c13_1020.png)
        
        In this case, there is no easy way to find the square roots. More work is needed. By Euler’s criterion (Theorem 3.7), 60 is a square residue, because  <math alttext="upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus 4 x plus 20" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>:</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow></math> ![upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus 4 x plus 20](images/c13_1021.png). Thus, a square root exists. Since  <math alttext="103 identical-to 3 m o d 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>103</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>3</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>4</mn></mrow></math> ![103 identical-to 3 m o d 4](images/c13_1022.png), by Lemma 3.5,  <math alttext="y identical-to plus-or-minus left-parenthesis 60 Superscript StartFraction 103 plus 1 Over 4 EndFraction Baseline right-parenthesis m o d 103 identical-to plus-or-minus 36 m o d 103" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mo>&#177;</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>60</mn></mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>103</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>103</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mo>&#177;</mo><mn>36</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>103</mn></mrow></math> ![y identical-to plus-or-minus left-parenthesis 60 Superscript StartFraction 103 plus 1 Over 4 EndFraction Baseline right-parenthesis m o d 103 identical-to plus-or-minus 36 m o d 103](images/c13_1023.png). Hence, points are  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 73 comma 36 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>73</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>36</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 73 comma 36 right-parenthesis](images/c13_1024.png) and  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 73 comma 67 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>73</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>67</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 73 comma 67 right-parenthesis](images/c13_1025.png).
        
2.  Let  <math alttext="upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus x plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>:</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus x plus 1](images/c13_1026.png) be an elliptic curve over field  <math alttext="upper F 101" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mn>101</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F 101](images/c13_1027.png).
    
    *    <math alttext="x equals 0 right double arrow y squared identical-to 1 m o d 101" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8658;</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>101</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow></math> ![x equals 0 right double arrow y squared identical-to 1 m o d 101](images/c13_1028.png)⇒  <math alttext="y equals plus-or-minus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>&#177;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![y equals plus-or-minus 1](images/c13_1029.png). Thus, points are:  <math alttext="upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus 4 x plus 20" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>:</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow></math> ![upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus 4 x plus 20](images/c13_1030.png) and  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 0 comma 100 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>100</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 0 comma 100 right-parenthesis](images/c13_1031.png).
    *    <math alttext="upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus 4 x plus 20" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>:</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow></math> ![upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus 4 x plus 20](images/c13_1032.png) ⇒  <math alttext="y equals plus-or-minus 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>&#177;</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></math> ![y equals plus-or-minus 4](images/c13_1033.png). Hence, points are:  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 8 comma 4 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 8 comma 4 right-parenthesis](images/c13_1034.png) and  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 8 comma 97 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>97</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 8 comma 97 right-parenthesis](images/c13_1035.png).
    *    <math alttext="x equals 100 right double arrow y squared identical-to 100 cubed plus 100 plus 1 m o d 101" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8658;</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mn>100</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>101</mn></mrow></math> ![x equals 100 right double arrow y squared identical-to 100 cubed plus 100 plus 1 m o d 101](images/c13_1036.png)
        
    
     <math alttext="y squared identical-to 100 cubed m o d 101 identical-to left-parenthesis negative 1 right-parenthesis cubed m o d 101 identical-to negative 1 m o d 101 identical-to 100 m o d 101" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mn>100</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>101</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>101</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>101</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>100</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>101</mn></mrow></math> ![y squared identical-to 100 cubed m o d 101 identical-to left-parenthesis negative 1 right-parenthesis cubed m o d 101 identical-to negative 1 m o d 101 identical-to 100 m o d 101](images/c13_1037.png)
    
    ⇒  <math alttext="y equals plus-or-minus 10" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>&#177;</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></math> ![y equals plus-or-minus 10](images/c13_1038.png). Hence, points are  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 100 comma 10 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>10</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 100 comma 10 right-parenthesis](images/c13_1039.png) and  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 100 comma 91 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>91</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 100 comma 91 right-parenthesis](images/c13_1040.png).
    
    *    <math alttext="x equals 57" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>57</mn></mrow></math> ![x equals 57](images/c13_1041.png) ⇒  <math alttext="y squared identical-to 17 m o d 101" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>17</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>101</mn></mrow></math> ![y squared identical-to 17 m o d 101](images/c13_1042.png).
    
    In this case, there is no easy way to find the roots. More work is needed. By Euler’s criterion, 17 is a square residue, because  <math alttext="17 Superscript StartFraction 101 minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 101" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>17</mn></mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>101</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>101</mn></mrow></math> ![17 Superscript StartFraction 101 minus 1 Over 2 EndFraction Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 101](images/c13_1043.png). Thus, a square root exists. Since  <math alttext="101 identical-to 1 m o d 4" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>101</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>4</mn></mrow></math> ![101 identical-to 1 m o d 4](images/c13_1044.png), Tonelli-Shanks algorithm (see Section 3.3.5.1) can be used to find the square roots.
    
    The steps of Tonelli-Shanks algorithm are as follows:
    
     <math alttext="101 equals 2 squared asterisk 25 plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>101</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>\*</mo><mn>25</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![101 equals 2 squared asterisk 25 plus 1](images/c13_1045.png). Hence,  <math alttext="upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus 4 x plus 20" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>:</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow></math> ![upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus 4 x plus 20](images/c13_1046.png) and  <math alttext="q equals 25" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow></math> ![q equals 25](images/c13_1047.png).
    
    Find a square nonresidue modulo  <math alttext="101 colon u equals 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>101</mn><mo>:</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![101 colon u equals 2](images/c13_1048.png) is a square nonresidue.
    
    Initialization:  <math alttext="m equals 2" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> ![m equals 2](images/c13_1049.png);  <math alttext="c equals 2 Superscript 25 Baseline m o d 101 equals 10" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>25</mn></mrow></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>101</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></math> ![c equals 2 Superscript 25 Baseline m o d 101 equals 10](images/c13_1050.png)
    
     <math alttext="t equals 17 Superscript 25 Baseline m o d 101 equals 100" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mn>17</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>25</mn></mrow></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>101</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow></math> ![t equals 17 Superscript 25 Baseline m o d 101 equals 100](images/c13_1051.png); R  <math alttext="equals 17 Superscript left-parenthesis 25 plus 1 right-parenthesis slash 2 Baseline m o d 101 equals 65" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mn>17</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>101</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>65</mn></mrow></math> ![equals 17 Superscript left-parenthesis 25 plus 1 right-parenthesis slash 2 Baseline m o d 101 equals 65](images/c13_1052.png)
    
    Loop:
    
    Iteration 1:
    
    1.   <math alttext="100 Superscript 2 Super Superscript 1 Superscript Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 101" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>100</mn></mrow><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>1</mn></msup></mrow></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>101</mn></mrow></math> ![100 Superscript 2 Super Superscript 1 Superscript Baseline identical-to 1 m o d 101](images/c13_1053.png). Hence,  <math alttext="k equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![k equals 1](images/c13_1054.png)
    2.   <math alttext="b identical-to 10 Superscript 2 Super Superscript m minus k minus 1 Superscript Baseline m o d 101 identical-to 10 Superscript 2 Super Superscript 0 Superscript Baseline m o d 101 equals 10" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>101</mn><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>0</mn></msup></mrow></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>101</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></math> ![b identical-to 10 Superscript 2 Super Superscript m minus k minus 1 Superscript Baseline m o d 101 identical-to 10 Superscript 2 Super Superscript 0 Superscript Baseline m o d 101 equals 10](images/c13_1055.png)
    3.   <math alttext="m equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![m equals 1](images/c13_1056.png)
    4.   <math alttext="c identical-to 10 squared m o d 101 equals 100" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>101</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow></math> ![c identical-to 10 squared m o d 101 equals 100](images/c13_1057.png)
    5.   <math alttext="t identical-to 100 asterisk 10 squared m o d 101 equals 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>\*</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>101</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![t identical-to 100 asterisk 10 squared m o d 101 equals 1](images/c13_1058.png)
    6.   <math alttext="upper R identical-to 65 asterisk 10 m o d 101 equals 44" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>65</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>10</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>101</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>44</mn></mrow></math> ![upper R identical-to 65 asterisk 10 m o d 101 equals 44](images/c13_1059.png)
    
    Iteration 2:
    
    *   vii)  <math alttext="t identical-to 1 m o d 101" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8801;</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>101</mn></mrow></math> ![t identical-to 1 m o d 101](images/c13_1060.png). Hence, stop and return  <math alttext="r equals 44" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>44</mn></mrow></math> ![r equals 44](images/c13_1061.png)
    
    Check:  <math alttext="left-parenthesis plus-or-minus 44 right-parenthesis squared equals 17 m o d 101" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>&#177;</mo><mn>44</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>17</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>101</mn></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis plus-or-minus 44 right-parenthesis squared equals 17 m o d 101](images/c13_1062.png).
    
    Therefore, points are:  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 57 comma 44 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>57</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>44</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 57 comma 44 right-parenthesis](images/c13_1063.png) and  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 57 comma 57 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>57</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>57</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 57 comma 57 right-parenthesis](images/c13_1064.png).
    

***Exercise 13.5***

1.  In general, to find all points over an elliptic curve  <math alttext="upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus a x plus b m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>:</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus a x plus b m o d p](images/c13_1065.png), we need to check for each coordinate  <math alttext="x element-of upper F Subscript p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></math> ![x element-of upper F Subscript p](images/c13_1066.png), if  <math alttext="u equals x cubed plus a x plus b m o d p" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> ![u equals x cubed plus a x plus b m o d p](images/c13_1067.png) is a square residue. We make use of Euler’s criterion (Theorem 3.7) to check if an integer *u* is a square root  <math alttext="upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus 4 x plus 20" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>:</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow></math> ![upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus 4 x plus 20](images/c13_1068.png). Then, for each square residue, we compute the square root (i.e. *y*). The following table gives the results of calculations. The number of points is  <math alttext="27 plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>27</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![27 plus 1](images/c13_1069.png) ( <math alttext="plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![plus 1](images/c13_1070.png) to count the point to infinity).

![](images/c13_1071.png)

*   2) The value calculated by Theorem 13.2 is:
    
     <math alttext="number-sign upper E left-parenthesis upper F Subscript p Baseline right-parenthesis equals 23 plus 1 plus sigma-summation Overscript zero width space Endscripts Underscript x element-of upper F Subscript p Baseline Endscripts left-parenthesis StartFraction x cubed plus a x plus b Over p EndFraction right-parenthesis equals 23 plus 1 plus 4 equals 28 period" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>#</mo><mi>E</mi><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>23</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><msup><mstyle displaystyle="true" mathsize="140%"><mo>&#8721;</mo></mstyle><mtext>&#8203;</mtext></msup></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mi>p</mi></mfrac></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>23</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>28</mn><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> ![number-sign upper E left-parenthesis upper F Subscript p Baseline right-parenthesis equals 23 plus 1 plus sigma-summation Overscript zero width space Endscripts Underscript x element-of upper F Subscript p Baseline Endscripts left-parenthesis StartFraction x cubed plus a x plus b Over p EndFraction right-parenthesis equals 23 plus 1 plus 4 equals 28 period](images/c13_1099.png)
    
    The sum of Legendre’s symbol associated with *x*\-coordinates in  <math alttext="upper F 23" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mn>23</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F 23](images/c13_1100.png) is given by the sum of the values in the third column. Therefore, we checked the correctness of Theorem 13.2. For formal proof of Theorem 13.1, see Problem 13.5.
    

***Exercise 13.6***

Since  <math alttext="upper E left-parenthesis upper F Subscript 2 squared Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> ![upper E left-parenthesis upper F Subscript 2 squared Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c13_1147.png) has seven points plus the point to infinity, its order is  <math alttext="upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus 4 x plus 20" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>:</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow></math> ![upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus 4 x plus 20](images/c13_1148.png).

Therefore, every point  <math alttext="upper P element-of upper E left-parenthesis upper F Subscript 2 squared Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi>E</mi><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> ![upper P element-of upper E left-parenthesis upper F Subscript 2 squared Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c13_1149.png), such that  <math alttext="8 dot upper P equals script upper O" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>8</mn><mo>&#8901;</mo><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="script">O</mi></mrow></math> ![8 dot upper P equals script upper O](images/c13_1150.png) is a generator of  <math alttext="upper E left-parenthesis upper F Subscript 2 squared Baseline right-parenthesis period" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> ![upper E left-parenthesis upper F Subscript 2 squared Baseline right-parenthesis period](images/c13_1151.png)

The elliptic curve has equation  <math alttext="upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus 4 x plus 20" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>:</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow></math> ![upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus 4 x plus 20](images/c13_1152.png); thus,  <math alttext="a equals 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> ![a equals 0](images/c13_1153.png)[.]

The field  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 squared" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 squared](images/c13_1154.png) has a reduction polynomial  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x squared plus x plus 1" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x squared plus x plus 1](images/c13_1155.png) and a generator  <math alttext="g equals x" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> ![g equals x](images/c13_1156.png).

The elements, in binary representation, of  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 squared" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 squared](images/c13_1157.png) are  <math alttext="StartSet 00 comma 01 comma 10 comma 11 EndSet" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>00</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>01</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow></math> ![StartSet 00 comma 01 comma 10 comma 11 EndSet](images/c13_1158.png); they are all powers of the generator  <math alttext="g equals x" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> ![g equals x](images/c13_1159.png) under the reduction polynomial  <math alttext="left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x squared plus x plus 1 colon" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>:</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x squared plus x plus 1 colon](images/c13_1160.png)

 <math alttext="g Superscript 4 Baseline identical-to x Superscript 4 Baseline m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 1 Baseline m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis 10 right-parenthesis" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>g</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![g Superscript 4 Baseline identical-to x Superscript 4 Baseline m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 1 Baseline m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis 10 right-parenthesis](images/c13_1165.png)

 <math alttext="g Superscript 5 Baseline identical-to x Superscript 5 Baseline m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 1 Baseline plus 1 m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis 11 right-parenthesis" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>g</mi><mn>5</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>5</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>11</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![g Superscript 5 Baseline identical-to x Superscript 5 Baseline m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals x Superscript 1 Baseline plus 1 m o d f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis 11 right-parenthesis](images/c13_1166.png)

Representation of elements as powers of the field generator *g* is very useful for point addition calculation. The coordinates of points are represented as powers of *g*. Remember that addition of two elements of  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 squared" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 squared](images/c13_1167.png) is a bitwise XOR operation and the multiplication is the remainder modulo the reduction polynomial  <math alttext="f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis](images/c13_1168.png).

Let point  <math alttext="upper P equals" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo></mrow></math> ![upper P equals](images/c13_1171.png)  <math alttext="left-parenthesis x Subscript p Baseline comma y Subscript p Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis x Subscript p Baseline comma y Subscript p Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c13_1172.png) denote the point to check.

1.  Check of point  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 1 comma 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 1 comma 1 right-parenthesis](images/c13_1173.png)
    
    First, calculate point  <math alttext="upper Q equals" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo></mrow></math> ![upper Q equals](images/c13_1174.png)  <math alttext="left-parenthesis x Subscript q Baseline comma y Subscript q Baseline right-parenthesis equals 2 dot upper P equals 2 dot left-parenthesis 1 comma 1 right-parenthesis equals 2 dot left-parenthesis g Superscript 0 Baseline comma g Superscript 0 Baseline right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>q</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>&#8901;</mo><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>&#8901;</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>&#8901;</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>g</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>g</mi><mn>0</mn></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis x Subscript q Baseline comma y Subscript q Baseline right-parenthesis equals 2 dot upper P equals 2 dot left-parenthesis 1 comma 1 right-parenthesis equals 2 dot left-parenthesis g Superscript 0 Baseline comma g Superscript 0 Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c13_1175.png) using the point doubling formulas, i.e.:
    
     <math alttext="lamda equals x Subscript upper P Baseline plus StartFraction y Subscript upper P Baseline Over x Subscript upper P Baseline EndFraction" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>&#955;</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>P</mi></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>P</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> ![lamda equals x Subscript upper P Baseline plus StartFraction y Subscript upper P Baseline Over x Subscript upper P Baseline EndFraction](images/c13_1176.png)     <math alttext="x Subscript 2 upper P Baseline equals lamda squared plus lamda plus a" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>P</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>&#955;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>&#955;</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></math> ![x Subscript 2 upper P Baseline equals lamda squared plus lamda plus a](images/c13_1177.png)     <math alttext="y Subscript 2 upper P Baseline equals x Subscript upper P Baseline squared plus left-parenthesis lamda plus 1 right-parenthesis x Subscript 2 upper P Baseline" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>P</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>P</mi></msub><msup><mrow><mtext>&#160;</mtext></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>&#955;</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>P</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![y Subscript 2 upper P Baseline equals x Subscript upper P Baseline squared plus left-parenthesis lamda plus 1 right-parenthesis x Subscript 2 upper P Baseline](images/c13_1178.png)

     <math alttext="x Subscript 2 upper P Baseline equals left-parenthesis 00 right-parenthesis squared plus left-parenthesis 00 right-parenthesis plus 0 equals left-parenthesis 00 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>P</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>00</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>00</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>00</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![x Subscript 2 upper P Baseline equals left-parenthesis 00 right-parenthesis squared plus left-parenthesis 00 right-parenthesis plus 0 equals left-parenthesis 00 right-parenthesis](images/c13_1180.png)     <math alttext="y Subscript 2 upper P Baseline equals left-parenthesis g Superscript 0 Baseline right-parenthesis squared plus left-parenthesis left-parenthesis 00 right-parenthesis plus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis 00 right-parenthesis equals g Superscript 0" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>P</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>g</mi><mn>0</mn></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>00</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>00</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mn>0</mn></msup></mrow></math> ![y Subscript 2 upper P Baseline equals left-parenthesis g Superscript 0 Baseline right-parenthesis squared plus left-parenthesis left-parenthesis 00 right-parenthesis plus 1 right-parenthesis left-parenthesis 00 right-parenthesis equals g Superscript 0](images/c13_1181.png)

***Exercise 13.7***

1.  Find points of the elliptic curve  <math alttext="upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus 2 x plus 2 m o d 17" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>:</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>17</mn></mrow></math> ![upper E colon y squared equals x cubed plus 2 x plus 2 m o d 17](images/c13_1236.png)
    
    First, compute the quadric residues  <math alttext="m o d 17" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>17</mn></mrow></math> ![m o d 17](images/c13_1237.png)

2.  Theorem 13.1 (Hasse’s theorem) bounds the cardinality of an elliptic curve as follows:
    
     <math alttext="StartAbsoluteValue number-sign upper E left-parenthesis upper F Subscript q Baseline right-parenthesis minus q minus 1 EndAbsoluteValue less-than-or-equal-to 2 StartRoot q EndRoot" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mrow><mo>#</mo><mi>E</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>q</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#8804;</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mi>q</mi></msqrt></mrow></math> ![StartAbsoluteValue number-sign upper E left-parenthesis upper F Subscript q Baseline right-parenthesis minus q minus 1 EndAbsoluteValue less-than-or-equal-to 2 StartRoot q EndRoot](images/c13_1269.png). In this exercise  <math alttext="upper E left-parenthesis upper F Subscript q Baseline right-parenthesis equals 19" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>q</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>19</mn></mrow></math> ![upper E left-parenthesis upper F Subscript q Baseline right-parenthesis equals 19](images/c13_1270.png) and  <math alttext="q equals 17" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>17</mn></mrow></math> ![q equals 17](images/c13_1271.png).
    
     <math alttext="StartAbsoluteValue 19 minus 17 minus 1 EndAbsoluteValue less-than-or-equal-to 2 StartRoot 17 EndRoot" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mrow><mn>19</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>17</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>&#124;</mo><mo>&#8804;</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mrow><mn>17</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow></math> ![StartAbsoluteValue 19 minus 17 minus 1 EndAbsoluteValue less-than-or-equal-to 2 StartRoot 17 EndRoot](images/c13_1272.png). Therefore, Hasse’s theorem is satisfied.
    
    When an elliptic curve is defined over a prime finite field, theorem 13.2 provides an accurate value of the cardinality of the elliptic curve as follows:
    
     <math alttext="number-sign upper E left-parenthesis upper F Subscript p Baseline right-parenthesis equals p plus 1 plus sigma-summation Underscript x element-of upper F Subscript p Baseline Endscripts left-parenthesis StartFraction x cubed plus a x plus b Over p EndFraction right-parenthesis" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>#</mo><mi>E</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msub><mo>&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mi>p</mi></mfrac></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mstyle></mrow></math> ![number-sign upper E left-parenthesis upper F Subscript p Baseline right-parenthesis equals p plus 1 plus sigma-summation Underscript x element-of upper F Subscript p Baseline Endscripts left-parenthesis StartFraction x cubed plus a x plus b Over p EndFraction right-parenthesis](images/c13_1273.png)(a)

     <math alttext="1 squared identical-to 1 m o d 17" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>1</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>17</mn></mrow></math> ![1 squared identical-to 1 m o d 17](images/c13_1294.png)         <math alttext="6 squared identical-to 2 m o d 17" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>6</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mn>2</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>17</mn></mrow></math> ![6 squared identical-to 2 m o d 17](images/c13_1295.png)      <math alttext="3 squared identical-to 9 m o d 17" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mo>&#8801;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>9</mn><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>17</mn></mrow></math> ![3 squared identical-to 9 m o d 17](images/c13_1296.png)

    Make substitution in (a):  <math alttext="number-sign upper E left-parenthesis upper F Subscript p Baseline right-parenthesis equals 17 plus 1 plus 1 equals 19" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>#</mo><mi>E</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>17</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>19</mn></mrow></math> ![number-sign upper E left-parenthesis upper F Subscript p Baseline right-parenthesis equals 17 plus 1 plus 1 equals 19](images/c13_1299.png).
    

***Exercise 13.8*** Let  <math alttext="upper E left-parenthesis upper F 179 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mn>179</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper E left-parenthesis upper F 179 right-parenthesis](images/c13_1300.png) be an elliptic curve with equation  <math alttext="y squared equals x cubed plus 2 x plus 7" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn></mrow></math> ![y squared equals x cubed plus 2 x plus 7](images/c13_1301.png).

Find an EC point to map the message  <math alttext="upper M equals 11" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>11</mn></mrow></math> ![upper M equals 11](images/c13_1302.png) assuming that  <math alttext="upper K equals 10" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></math> ![upper K equals 10](images/c13_1303.png).

 <math alttext="upper K equals 10" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></math> ![upper K equals 10](images/c13_1304.png) ⇒ any message *M* to map should be such that:  <math alttext="0 less-than-or-equal-to upper M less-than left floor StartFraction 179 Over 10 EndFraction right floor minus 1 equals 16" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mrow><mo>&#8970;</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>179</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>&#8971;</mo></mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow></math> ![0 less-than-or-equal-to upper M less-than left floor StartFraction 179 Over 10 EndFraction right floor minus 1 equals 16](images/c13_1305.png).

Let the message to map be 11 ⇒  <math alttext="10 asterisk 11 less-than-or-equal-to x less-than 10 asterisk left-parenthesis 11 plus 1 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>&#60;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>10</mn><mo>\*</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>11</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![10 asterisk 11 less-than-or-equal-to x less-than 10 asterisk left-parenthesis 11 plus 1 right-parenthesis](images/c13_1306.png).

There are three points that fulfill equation  <math alttext="y squared identical-to left-parenthesis x cubed plus 2 x plus 7 right-parenthesis m o d 179" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&#8801;</mo><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>7</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>179</mn></mrow></math> ![y squared identical-to left-parenthesis x cubed plus 2 x plus 7 right-parenthesis m o d 179](images/c13_1307.png):

 <math alttext="left-parenthesis 110 cubed plus 2 asterisk 110 plus 7 right-parenthesis m o d 179 equals 2 squared m o d 179" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>110</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>110</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>179</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>179</mn></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 110 cubed plus 2 asterisk 110 plus 7 right-parenthesis m o d 179 equals 2 squared m o d 179](images/c13_1308.png). Thus, point  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 110 comma 2 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>110</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 110 comma 2 right-parenthesis](images/c13_1309.png) is a mapping solution.

 <math alttext="left-parenthesis 111 cubed plus 2 asterisk 111 plus 7 right-parenthesis m o d 179 equals 11 squared m o d 179" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>111</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>111</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>179</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mn>11</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>179</mn></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 111 cubed plus 2 asterisk 111 plus 7 right-parenthesis m o d 179 equals 11 squared m o d 179](images/c13_1310.png). Thus, point  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 111 comma 11 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>111</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>11</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 111 comma 11 right-parenthesis](images/c13_1311.png) is a mapping solution.

 <math alttext="112 cubed plus 2 asterisk 112 plus 7 right-parenthesis m o d 179 equals 3 squared m o d 179" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>112</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>\*</mo><mn>112</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>179</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>179</mn></mrow></math> ![112 cubed plus 2 asterisk 112 plus 7 right-parenthesis m o d 179 equals 3 squared m o d 179](images/c13_1312.png). Thus, point  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 111 comma 3 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>111</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 111 comma 3 right-parenthesis](images/c13_1313.png) is a mapping solution.

***Problem 13.1***

1.  Representation of 128 in power of 2 results in:  <math alttext="128 dot upper P equals 2 left-parenthesis 2 left-parenthesis 2 left-parenthesis 2 left-parenthesis 2 left-parenthesis 2 left-parenthesis 2 dot upper P right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>128</mn><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>P</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![128 dot upper P equals 2 left-parenthesis 2 left-parenthesis 2 left-parenthesis 2 left-parenthesis 2 left-parenthesis 2 left-parenthesis 2 dot upper P right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c13_1314.png). Under Left-to-right point multiplication algorithm, seven point doublings are used. More generally, when *k* is a power of 2 (i.e.  <math alttext="k equals 2 Superscript m" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow></math> ![k equals 2 Superscript m](images/c13_1315.png)), *m* point doublings are used to compute  <math alttext="k dot upper P" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8901;</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> ![k dot upper P](images/c13_1316.png).
2.  There are different alternatives to calculate  <math alttext="127 dot upper P" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>127</mn><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> ![127 dot upper P](images/c13_1317.png) among which the following ones: 
    1.   <math alttext="127 dot upper P" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>127</mn><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> ![127 dot upper P](images/c13_1318.png) is rewritten as  <math alttext="127 dot upper P equals left-parenthesis 128 minus 1 right-parenthesis dot upper P equals 128 dot upper P minus upper P" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>127</mn><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>128</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>128</mn><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>P</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> ![127 dot upper P equals left-parenthesis 128 minus 1 right-parenthesis dot upper P equals 128 dot upper P minus upper P](images/c13_1319.png). Under binary representation multiplication method, seven point doublings and one addition are used. *–P* is the negative of point *P. –P* coordinates depend on the underlying field:  <math alttext="minus left-parenthesis x comma y right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis x comma negative y right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![minus left-parenthesis x comma y right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis x comma negative y right-parenthesis](images/c13_1320.png) if the field is prime and  <math alttext="minus left-parenthesis x comma y right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis x comma x plus y right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![minus left-parenthesis x comma y right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis x comma x plus y right-parenthesis](images/c13_1321.png) if the field is an extension one (i.e. of the form  <math alttext="upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript m" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ![upper F Subscript 2 Sub Superscript m](images/c13_1322.png)).
    2.   <math alttext="127 dot upper P equals" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>127</mn><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo></mrow></math> ![127 dot upper P equals](images/c13_1323.png)  <math alttext="left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 63 right-parenthesis right-parenthesis dot upper P equals left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 31 right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis dot upper P" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>63</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>31</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> ![left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 63 right-parenthesis right-parenthesis dot upper P equals left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 31 right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis dot upper P](images/c13_1324.png)
        
         <math alttext="equals left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 15 right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis dot upper P" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>15</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> ![equals left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 15 right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis dot upper P](images/c13_1325.png)
        
         <math alttext="equals left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 7 right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis upper P" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> ![equals left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 7 right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis upper P](images/c13_1326.png)
        
         <math alttext="equals left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis dot upper P" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> ![equals left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 left-parenthesis 1 plus 2 right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis dot upper P](images/c13_1327.png)
        
         <math alttext="equals left-parenthesis upper P plus 2 dot left-parenthesis upper P plus 2 dot left-parenthesis upper P plus 2 dot left-parenthesis upper P plus 2 dot left-parenthesis upper P plus 2 dot left-parenthesis upper P plus 2 dot upper P right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>(</mo><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>P</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![equals left-parenthesis upper P plus 2 dot left-parenthesis upper P plus 2 dot left-parenthesis upper P plus 2 dot left-parenthesis upper P plus 2 dot left-parenthesis upper P plus 2 dot left-parenthesis upper P plus 2 dot upper P right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c13_1328.png)
        

Thereby, calculation of  <math alttext="127 dot upper P" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mn>127</mn><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mo>&#8901;</mo><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mtext>&#8201;</mtext><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> ![127 dot upper P](images/c13_1329.png) requires six doublings and six additions.

***Problem 13.2***

1.  In the left-to-right binary method for point multiplication, scalar *k* is represented as a bit string with *r* bits such that  <math alttext="k equals left-parenthesis k Subscript r minus 1 Baseline k Subscript r minus 2 Baseline ellipsis k 0 right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>k</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>&#8230;</mo><mtext>&#160;</mtext><msub><mi>k</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> ![k equals left-parenthesis k Subscript r minus 1 Baseline k Subscript r minus 2 Baseline ellipsis k 0 right-parenthesis](images/c13_1330.png). The number of iterations is *r*. Therefore, the complexity of the method is  <math alttext="upper O left-parenthesis l o g 2 left-parenthesis k right-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>O</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mi>o</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper O left-parenthesis l o g 2 left-parenthesis k right-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c13_1331.png).
2.  In the recursive method for point multiplication, scalar *k* is divided by 2 until it reaches 0 or 1. Therefore, the number of iterations is in  <math alttext="upper O left-parenthesis l o g 2 left-parenthesis k right-parenthesis right-parenthesis" display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>O</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mi>o</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> ![upper O left-parenthesis l o g 2 left-parenthesis k right-parenthesis right-parenthesis](images/c13_1332.png).
